# 4.12 Memory Architecture Philosophy

Memory is the most fragile subsystem in browser video editors.

The architecture must support:

* 4K60 recording.
* Multiple hour recordings.
* Live preview.
* AI analysis.
* Export.
* Undo history.

without exhausting browser memory.

## Golden Memory Rules

1. Video pixels are never duplicated unless absolutely necessary.
2. Every transferable object has exactly one owner.
3. GPU textures are pooled.
4. Memory pools are bounded.
5. Workers release ownership immediately after processing.
6. Long recordings stream to disk continuously.

Memory ownership is stricter than object ownership.

---

# 4.13 Browser Memory Budget

The scheduler operates within configurable budgets.

## Target Budgets

| Resource            | Soft Limit | Hard Limit |
| ------------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| JavaScript Heap     | 512 MB     | 1 GB       |
| GPU Texture Pool    | 256 MB     | 512 MB     |
| Active VideoFrames  | 16         | 32         |
| Active ImageBitmaps | 32         | 64         |
| Shared Buffers      | 64 MB      | 128 MB     |
| Recording Buffer    | 128 MB     | 256 MB     |

Crossing a hard limit triggers degradation.

---

## Memory Zones

```text id="1mb5tv"
Browser Process
│
├── JS Heap
├── GPU Memory
├── Shared Memory
├── IndexedDB
└── Browser Encoder Buffers
```

Each zone has independent monitoring.

---

# 4.14 Memory Ownership Model

Every runtime resource belongs to exactly one owner.

## Ownership States

```text id="x1x6l5"
Created
   │
Owned
   │
Transferred
   │
Consumed
   │
Released
   │
Disposed
```

Resources never return to previous owners.

---

## Ownership Contract

```typescript id="aaxynm"
interface MemoryOwnedResource {

    id:string;

    ownerWorker:string;

    createdAt:number;

    transferred:boolean;

}
```

Ownership transfer invalidates previous owner.

---

# 4.15 VideoFrame Lifecycle

VideoFrame is the most expensive runtime object.

## Lifecycle

```text id="8szl4w"
TrackProcessor
     │
VideoFrame Created
     │
Timestamp Assigned
     │
Transferred to Vision
     │
Converted to ImageBitmap
     │
VideoFrame Closed
```

VideoFrames should exist for milliseconds only.

---

## Capture Rules

* Capture Worker creates VideoFrame.
* Timestamp assigned immediately.
* Queue insertion.
* Ownership transferred.
* `close()` called after transfer.

---

## VideoFrame Lifetime Budget

| Stage             | Lifetime Target |
| ----------------- | --------------- |
| Capture Queue     | Under 8 ms      |
| Vision Transfer   | Under 5 ms      |
| Bitmap Conversion | Under 3 ms      |
| Total Lifetime    | Under 20 ms     |

Never retain VideoFrames for preview history.

---

## VideoFrame Metadata

```typescript id="5jlwmx"
interface RuntimeVideoFrame {

    frameId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    durationUs:number;

    width:number;

    height:number;

    colorSpace:string;

    rotation:number;

}
```

Metadata survives after VideoFrame disposal.

---

# 4.16 ImageBitmap Lifecycle

ImageBitmap is optimized for worker communication.

## Lifecycle

```text id="jl5ejk"
VideoFrame
    │
createImageBitmap()
    │
Transfer
    │
Vision Processing
    │
OCR Processing
    │
Gemini Sampling
    │
Bitmap Closed
```

Bitmaps replace VideoFrames for analysis.

---

## Bitmap Ownership

Owner chain:

Capture Worker → Vision Worker → OCR Worker → Gemini Worker.

Only one owner exists at a time.

---

## Bitmap Lifetime Budget

| Stage            | Target                |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Vision Detection | Under 10 ms           |
| OCR              | Under 30 ms           |
| Gemini Sampling  | Until upload finishes |
| Total Lifetime   | Under 250 ms          |

After Gemini upload, bitmap is released.

---

# 4.17 Transferable Ownership Rules

Transferable objects avoid memory copies.

## Allowed Transferables

| Object          | Strategy |
| --------------- | -------- |
| VideoFrame      | Transfer |
| ImageBitmap     | Transfer |
| AudioData       | Transfer |
| ArrayBuffer     | Transfer |
| OffscreenCanvas | Transfer |
| MessagePort     | Transfer |

No structured clone for large pixel data.

---

## Ownership Example

```text id="8zhz8z"
Capture Worker

   owns VideoFrame

        │ Transfer

Vision Worker

   owns VideoFrame

        │ Convert

Vision Worker

   owns ImageBitmap

        │ Transfer

OCR Worker
```

Old owner must discard reference immediately.

---

## Invalid Ownership

Never:

* share VideoFrame references.
* clone ImageBitmap.
* duplicate ArrayBuffers unnecessarily.

Violating ownership increases memory dramatically.

---

# 4.18 SharedArrayBuffer Strategy

SharedArrayBuffer is optional acceleration.

Used only for synchronization.

## Use Cases

* Playback clock.
* Frame counters.
* Audio playback position.
* Scheduler metrics.
* Timeline playhead.

Never store pixels inside SharedArrayBuffer.

---

## Shared Memory Layout

```text id="wzwlz0"
SharedArrayBuffer

│

├── Playback Clock

├── Audio Clock

├── Render Tick

├── Scheduler State

└── Worker Flags
```

Tiny shared state only.

---

## Playback Clock Structure

```typescript id="9xbgur"
interface PlaybackClock {

    currentTimestampUs:number;

    playing:boolean;

    playbackRate:number;

}
```

Updated atomically.

---

## Shared Memory Synchronization

Uses Atomics.

Allowed operations:

* load
* store
* add
* wait
* notify

No busy loops.

---

# 4.19 Ring Buffer Architecture

Realtime systems use ring buffers instead of growing arrays.

## Why Ring Buffers?

* Constant memory.
* No reallocations.
* Predictable latency.

---

## Frame Ring Buffer

```text id="l2z2s5"
HEAD

 │

Frame1

Frame2

Frame3

Frame4

Frame5

 │

TAIL
```

Old entries overwritten after consumption.

---

## Ring Buffer Rules

* Fixed capacity.
* Head advances on write.
* Tail advances on read.
* Occupancy tracked.

---

## Ring Buffer Contract

```typescript id="qstgtw"
interface RingBuffer<T> {

    push(item:T):boolean;

    pop():T|undefined;

    size:number;

    capacity:number;

}
```

Used heavily inside Capture Worker.

---

## Ring Buffers Used By

| Worker  | Buffer          |
| ------- | --------------- |
| Capture | VideoFrames     |
| Audio   | AudioData       |
| Preview | Render Requests |
| Cursor  | Cursor Samples  |
| Vision  | Detection Queue |

---

# 4.20 GPU Texture Pool

GPU textures are expensive allocations.

Never allocate textures every frame.

## Pool Lifecycle

```text id="ktdxja"
Acquire Texture

      │

Render Pass

      │

Release Texture

      │

Return To Pool
```

Pool owns reusable textures.

---

## Pool Rules

* Resolution buckets.
* LRU eviction.
* Maximum pool size.
* Idle cleanup.

---

## Texture Buckets

| Bucket | Resolution |
| ------ | ---------- |
| Small  | Under 720p |
| Medium | 1080p      |
| Large  | 1440p      |
| XL     | 4K         |

Separate pools reduce fragmentation.

---

## Texture Pool Contract

```typescript id="euhpbj"
interface GPUTexturePool {

    acquire(width:number,height:number):GPUTexture;

    release(texture:GPUTexture):void;

    evictIdle():void;

}
```

---

# 4.21 Long Recording Memory Management

Long recordings cannot remain in RAM.

## Recording Strategy

```text id="pynozs"
Frames

  │

Chunk Buffer

  │

Encoder

  │

IndexedDB

  │

Buffer Cleared
```

Memory stays constant.

---

## Chunk Flush Rules

Flush when:

* 5 seconds elapsed.
* 128 MB reached.
* Recording paused.
* Recording stopped.

Never wait until recording ends.

---

## Chunk Verification

Each chunk stores checksum.

Used for crash recovery.

---

## Streaming Window

During preview:

Only nearby chunks stay decoded.

Window example:

* Previous chunk.
* Current chunk.
* Next chunk.

Everything else unloaded.

---

# 4.22 Memory Pressure Detection

Browser exposes approximate memory.

Scheduler observes:

* heap usage
* texture usage
* queue depth
* chunk buffer size

---

## Pressure Levels

| State    | Behavior                  |
| -------- | ------------------------- |
| Normal   | Full quality              |
| Elevated | Reduce OCR frequency      |
| High     | Pause Gemini sampling     |
| Critical | Flush buffers immediately |

Recording quality never changes.

---

## Pressure Recovery

When memory decreases:

* Resume Gemini.
* Resume OCR.
* Resume thumbnails.

Gradual recovery.

---

# 4.23 Garbage Collection Strategy

Do not rely on browser GC.

Manual cleanup is mandatory.

## Manual Cleanup Targets

* VideoFrames
* ImageBitmaps
* GPU textures
* Audio buffers
* OffscreenCanvas contexts
* AbortControllers

---

## Cleanup Pipeline

```text id="pcbhw4"
Frame Consumed

      │

Release Ownership

      │

Close Resource

      │

Return Pool Object

      │

Eligible For GC
```

Objects become collectible quickly.

---

## Idle Cleanup

Runs during:

* playback pause
* idle editor
* export completion
* project close

Never during recording.

---

# 4.24 Memory Leak Detection

Development mode continuously scans runtime resources.

## Leak Detector Tracks

* Active VideoFrames.
* Active ImageBitmaps.
* GPU textures.
* Workers.
* Audio contexts.
* OffscreenCanvas instances.

---

## Leak Thresholds

Example warnings:

```text id="hy59h0"
Warning:

VideoFrames Alive: 18

Expected: <= 8

Potential Leak Detected
```

---

## Leak Recovery

Coordinator requests cleanup.

If worker ignores cleanup:

Worker restarted.

---

# 4.25 Runtime Memory Metrics

Collected every heartbeat.

```typescript id="ivys4k"
interface RuntimeMemoryMetrics {

    heapUsedMB:number;

    gpuTextures:number;

    gpuMemoryMB:number;

    videoFramesAlive:number;

    imageBitmapsAlive:number;

    chunkBufferMB:number;

}
```

Visible inside developer diagnostics.

---

# 4.26 Browser Compatibility Strategy

Memory capabilities differ.

## Chrome / Edge

* SharedArrayBuffer.
* WebCodecs.
* OffscreenCanvas.
* GPU acceleration.

Best experience.

---

## Firefox

* Partial WebCodecs.
* Software decode fallback.
* Reduced texture pool.

---

## Safari

* Limited WebCodecs.
* Aggressive memory cleanup.
* Smaller chunk buffers.

Scheduler adapts automatically.

---

# 4.27 Acceptance Tests

## Ownership Tests

* VideoFrame transferred once.
* ImageBitmap released after Gemini.
* No duplicate ownership.

## Pool Tests

* Texture reuse.
* Idle eviction.
* Bucket reuse.

## Long Recording Tests

* 2-hour recording.
* Stable heap.
* Stable GPU memory.
* Continuous chunk flush.

## Leak Tests

* No leaked VideoFrames.
* No leaked textures.
* Workers release resources on dispose.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 4.2)

1. Every transferable object has one owner.
2. VideoFrames must be closed immediately after transfer.
3. ImageBitmaps replace VideoFrames for analysis.
4. SharedArrayBuffer stores synchronization state only.
5. Ring buffers are mandatory for realtime queues.
6. GPU textures must come from reusable pools.
7. Recording chunks flush continuously to IndexedDB.
8. Memory pressure pauses AI before affecting recording.
9. Manual cleanup is mandatory; never depend on browser GC.
10. Leak detection is built into the Runtime Coordinator.

---

# 4.28 Scheduler Core Philosophy

The scheduler is responsible for coordinating every asynchronous subsystem without affecting recording quality.

The scheduler answers one question continuously:

> "What work should execute next?"

## Scheduler Objectives

* Never block recording.
* Keep preview smooth.
* Keep AI utilization high during idle CPU.
* Avoid browser long tasks.
* Keep memory bounded.
* Prioritize user interactions.

---

## Scheduler Layers

```text
Scheduler
│
├── Frame Scheduler
├── Task Scheduler
├── AI Scheduler
├── OCR Scheduler
├── Thumbnail Scheduler
├── Export Scheduler
└── Cleanup Scheduler
```

Each scheduler controls a different workload type.

---

# 4.29 Frame Scheduler

Frame Scheduler is the highest-priority scheduler in TryLipi.

Responsibilities:

* Receive VideoFrames.
* Timestamp ordering.
* Queue insertion.
* Backpressure handling.
* Frame routing.

---

## Frame Pipeline

```text
VideoFrame
    │
Frame Scheduler
    ├──────── Recorder
    ├──────── Preview
    ├──────── Vision
    └──────── Storage
```

One frame fan-outs into multiple consumers.

---

## Frame States

| State       | Meaning                       |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- |
| RECEIVED    | TrackProcessor produced frame |
| QUEUED      | Waiting for consumer          |
| TRANSFERRED | Ownership transferred         |
| CONSUMED    | Consumer completed            |
| RELEASED    | Frame closed                  |

---

## Frame Packet

```typescript
interface ScheduledFrame {

    frameId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    priority:number;

    consumers:string[];

}
```

Scheduler tracks which consumers still need the frame.

---

## Consumer Completion Rules

A frame is released only when:

* Recorder consumed.
* Preview consumed.
* Vision consumed (or skipped).

Then Capture Worker closes the frame.

---

# 4.30 Recorder Scheduling

Recorder always receives frames first.

Guarantees:

* Zero frame loss.
* Timestamp ordering.
* Chunk continuity.

Recorder bypasses AI queues.

---

## Recorder Priority

Priority value:

P0

Recorder cannot be preempted.

---

## Recorder Overflow Policy

If encoder slows:

* Increase chunk flush frequency.
* Expand temporary encoder queue.
* Never discard captured frames.

---

# 4.31 Preview Scheduling

Preview uses proxy media.

Preview latency target:

**16 ms maximum**

---

## Preview Render Tick

Runs on display refresh.

Target:

60 FPS.

Supports:

30 / 60 / 90 / 120 Hz displays.

---

## Preview Frame Skipping

Allowed only for preview.

Algorithm:

```text
Frame N
Frame N+1
Frame N+2
Frame N+3

Display N
Skip N+1
Display N+2
Display N+3
```

Timeline timestamps remain unchanged.

---

## Preview Budget

| Stage     | Budget |
| --------- | ------ |
| Decode    | 3 ms   |
| Camera    | 2 ms   |
| Blur      | 2 ms   |
| Captions  | 2 ms   |
| Cursor    | 1 ms   |
| Composite | 2 ms   |

---

# 4.32 Vision Scheduler

Vision scheduler decides which frames require analysis.

Vision does **not** analyze every frame.

---

## Sampling Strategy

| Recording FPS | Vision FPS |
| ------------- | ---------- |
| 30 FPS        | 15 FPS     |
| 60 FPS        | 20 FPS     |
| 120 FPS       | 24 FPS     |

Adaptive sampling reduces CPU load.

---

## Vision Sampling Rules

Always analyze when:

* Scene change.
* Cursor click.
* New modal.
* Navigation transition.
* Significant scroll stop.

Otherwise sample periodically.

---

## Vision Queue Packet

```typescript
interface VisionTask {

    frameId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    samplingReason:string;

}
```

---

# 4.33 OCR Scheduler

OCR is one of the most CPU-intensive engines.

Scheduler batches OCR work.

---

## OCR Batch Lifecycle

```text
Detected Regions
      │
Deduplicate
      │
Merge Regions
      │
OCR Batch
      │
Store Results
```

---

## OCR Deduplication

Skip OCR if region unchanged.

Criteria:

* Same bbox.
* Same hash.
* Same confidence history.

---

## OCR Batch Limits

| Limit       | Value |
| ----------- | ----- |
| Max Regions | 50    |
| Max Pixels  | 12 MP |
| Timeout     | 25 ms |

Remaining regions wait for next batch.

---

## OCR Priority

Priority increases when:

* User pauses recording.
* Preview idle.
* Scroll stopped.

Priority decreases during fast scrolling.

---

# 4.34 AI Scheduler

Gemini requests are extremely expensive compared to OCR.

AI Scheduler optimizes token usage.

---

## AI Scheduler Responsibilities

* Batch requests.
* Merge prompts.
* Context reuse.
* Retry management.
* Token budgeting.

---

## AI Queue Lifecycle

```text
Semantic Candidate
       │
Context Builder
       │
Prompt Builder
       │
Gemini Queue
       │
API Call
       │
Validation
       │
Timeline Update
```

---

## AI Queue States

| State      | Meaning           |
| ---------- | ----------------- |
| queued     | Waiting           |
| batching   | Collecting frames |
| processing | Gemini request    |
| validating | JSON validation   |
| completed  | Stored            |
| retry      | Retry scheduled   |

---

## Gemini Batch Rules

Batch together:

* Nearby timestamps.
* Same screen.
* Same application window.
* Same scene.

Never batch unrelated scenes.

---

## AI Budget Rules

Target concurrent Gemini requests:

| Device           | Concurrent Requests |
| ---------------- | ------------------- |
| Low-end Laptop   | 1                   |
| Mid-range        | 2                   |
| High-end Desktop | 3                   |
| Export Mode      | 4                   |

---

## AI Yielding

Gemini pauses immediately when:

* Recording overload.
* Preview latency high.
* Memory pressure high.

Jobs remain queued.

---

# 4.35 Dynamic Throttling Engine

Scheduler constantly adapts workload.

---

## Inputs

* CPU usage.
* Queue depth.
* Memory pressure.
* GPU latency.
* Recording FPS.
* Preview FPS.

---

## Throttling Levels

| Level    | Behavior                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------ |
| NONE     | Full quality                   |
| LIGHT    | Reduce OCR frequency           |
| MEDIUM   | Reduce Vision sampling         |
| HIGH     | Pause Gemini                   |
| CRITICAL | Suspend thumbnails & summaries |

Recording unaffected.

---

## Throttling State Machine

```text
Healthy
   │
Light
   │
Medium
   │
High
   │
Critical
   │
Recovering
```

Transitions require hysteresis to avoid oscillation.

---

## Recovery Delay

System remains in degraded mode until metrics stabilize for several seconds.

Prevents rapid enable/disable loops.

---

# 4.36 Adaptive FPS Scheduler

Preview FPS adapts to device capability.

---

## Supported Display Rates

* 24 Hz
* 30 Hz
* 60 Hz
* 90 Hz
* 120 Hz
* Variable Refresh Rate

---

## Adaptive Preview Policy

| Device Load | Preview FPS          |
| ----------- | -------------------- |
| Idle        | Display refresh rate |
| Medium      | 60 FPS               |
| High        | 45 FPS               |
| Critical    | 30 FPS               |

Recording FPS remains original.

---

## Animation Tick

Timeline animations interpolate independently from preview FPS.

Camera remains smooth even if preview renders at 30 FPS.

---

# 4.37 Worker Pool Architecture

Not every task needs a dedicated worker.

Pools execute homogeneous jobs.

---

## Pools

```text
OCR Pool
  ├── OCR Worker 1
  ├── OCR Worker 2

Vision Pool
  ├── Vision Worker 1

Thumbnail Pool
  ├── Thumbnail Worker 1
```

Pool size determined by hardware concurrency.

---

## Pool Size Rules

```typescript
ocrPoolSize = Math.min(2, navigator.hardwareConcurrency / 4)

thumbnailPoolSize = 1

visionPoolSize = 1
```

Prevent excessive worker creation.

---

## Pool Scheduler

Tasks distributed round-robin.

Busy workers skipped.

Idle workers preferred.

---

# 4.38 CPU Budget Manager

Every subsystem has a CPU budget.

---

## Budget Allocation

| Worker    | CPU Budget    |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Capture   | Highest       |
| Preview   | High          |
| Timeline  | Medium        |
| Vision    | Medium        |
| OCR       | Low           |
| Gemini    | Opportunistic |
| Thumbnail | Idle only     |

---

## CPU Time Slice

Scheduler tracks average execution time.

```typescript
interface CPUBudget {

    workerId:string;

    averageExecutionMs:number;

    maxBudgetMs:number;

}
```

Workers exceeding budgets become throttling candidates.

---

## Budget Violations

If Preview exceeds budget:

* reduce preview resolution.
* skip intermediate preview frames.

If OCR exceeds budget:

* shrink OCR batch size.

---

# 4.39 Long Task Detection

Browser "Long Tasks" freeze UI.

Scheduler detects them.

---

## Long Task Threshold

**50 ms**

Any synchronous execution beyond threshold is logged.

---

## Detection Sources

* PerformanceObserver.
* Worker heartbeat delay.
* Render latency spike.

---

## Long Task Recovery

Actions:

1. Pause Gemini.
2. Flush preview queue.
3. Yield event loop.
4. Resume workloads gradually.

---

## Long Task Packet

```typescript
interface LongTaskEvent {

    workerId:string;

    durationMs:number;

    timestamp:number;

}
```

Stored only in diagnostics mode.

---

# 4.40 Idle Scheduler

Idle Scheduler executes non-critical work.

---

## Idle Tasks

* Thumbnail generation.
* AI summaries.
* Scene clustering.
* Chapter generation.
* Cache cleanup.

---

## Idle Detection

Runs only when:

* Recording stopped.
* Preview paused.
* User inactive briefly.

Uses idle callbacks where available.

---

# 4.41 Scheduler Metrics

Collected continuously.

| Metric                 | Purpose      |
| ---------------------- | ------------ |
| Queue Depth            | Backpressure |
| Worker Latency         | Health       |
| Average Task Duration  | CPU budget   |
| Tasks/sec              | Throughput   |
| Dropped Preview Frames | Diagnostics  |

---

## Scheduler Dashboard Contract

```typescript
interface SchedulerMetrics {

    queueDepth:number;

    previewFPS:number;

    droppedPreviewFrames:number;

    aiQueueSize:number;

    ocrQueueSize:number;

    captureLatencyMs:number;

}
```

Developer diagnostics visualize these metrics.

---

# 4.42 Scheduler State Machine

Entire scheduler has one global state.

```text
BOOTING
   │
READY
   │
RECORDING
   │
ANALYZING
   │
EDITING
   │
EXPORTING
   │
IDLE
```

Each state enables different schedulers.

---

## Scheduler Permissions by State

| Scheduler         | Recording  | Editing    | Export     |
| ----------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| Frame Scheduler   | ✅          | ❌          | ❌          |
| Preview Scheduler | ✅          | ✅          | Optional   |
| OCR Scheduler     | Limited    | Full       | Full       |
| Gemini Scheduler  | Limited    | Full       | Full       |
| Export Scheduler  | ❌          | ❌          | ✅          |
| Cleanup Scheduler | Background | Background | Background |

---

# 4.43 Acceptance Tests

## Scheduler Tests

* Capture queue never starves.
* Preview skips frames without timestamp drift.
* OCR batches merge identical regions.
* Gemini batching groups nearby frames.

## Throttling Tests

* High CPU pauses Gemini.
* Memory pressure pauses OCR.
* Recovery resumes AI automatically.

## Pool Tests

* OCR workers distribute load evenly.
* Idle tasks execute only when scheduler idle.

## Long Recording Tests

* 3-hour recording.
* Stable queue depths.
* Stable preview FPS.
* Constant memory usage.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 4.3)

1. Frame Scheduler has absolute priority over every other scheduler.
2. Preview frames may be skipped; recording frames may never be skipped.
3. Vision sampling is adaptive and event-driven.
4. OCR is batch-oriented and deduplicates unchanged regions.
5. Gemini requests are batched by scene and timestamp proximity.
6. Dynamic throttling always sacrifices AI before recording quality.
7. Worker pools scale with hardware concurrency.
8. Long tasks over 50 ms trigger scheduler recovery actions.
9. Idle Scheduler performs only non-critical work.
10. Scheduler metrics are continuously collected for diagnostics.

---

# 4.44 Runtime Recovery Philosophy

A recording session must survive partial failures whenever possible.

TryLipi is designed around **recoverable failures**, not application crashes.

## Golden Recovery Rules

1. Worker crashes must not terminate recording.
2. Timeline state must survive worker restart.
3. Recording chunks must already be persisted.
4. Recovery uses immutable packets.
5. Recovery is automatic before user intervention.

---

## Recovery Levels

| Level | Recovery                          |
| ----- | --------------------------------- |
| L1    | Restart single worker             |
| L2    | Restore worker state from packets |
| L3    | Restore runtime checkpoint        |
| L4    | Restore project checkpoint        |
| L5    | Manual recovery UI                |

Most failures should stop at **L1**.

---

# 4.45 Worker Restart Protocol

Every worker participates in the restart protocol.

## Restart Lifecycle

```text id="9d8p3s"
Heartbeat Timeout
       │
Coordinator Detects Failure
       │
Worker Marked Dead
       │
Dispose Resources
       │
Spawn New Worker
       │
Replay State Packets
       │
Worker Healthy
```

No page refresh required.

---

## Worker Restart Packet

```typescript id="htbjof"
interface WorkerRestartEvent {

    workerId:string;

    reason:string;

    restartedAt:number;

    recoveredPackets:number;

}
```

Used for diagnostics only.

---

## Restart Eligibility

Workers that can restart safely:

* OCR
* Vision
* Cursor
* Gemini
* Preview
* Thumbnail

Workers requiring checkpoint recovery:

* Timeline
* Storage
* Export

Capture Worker has a dedicated recovery path.

---

# 4.46 Capture Recovery Pipeline

Capture is the highest-priority subsystem.

## Capture Failure Sources

* MediaStream ended.
* Browser revoked permission.
* Display disconnected.
* Window closed.
* Track processor exception.

---

## Capture Recovery

```text id="w7pwpd"
Capture Error
      │
Stop Recording Queue
      │
Flush Chunk Buffer
      │
Attempt Stream Reconnect
      │
Resume Recording
```

If reconnect fails, recording finalizes gracefully.

---

## Recording Integrity Rules

Before reconnect:

* Current chunk flushed.
* Metadata checkpoint updated.
* Timeline timestamp preserved.

No corrupted chunk chain.

---

# 4.47 Timeline Recovery

Timeline is authoritative editing state.

## Timeline Recovery Flow

```text id="f3kkb8"
Timeline Worker Crash
       │
Read Latest Timeline Snapshot
       │
Replay Event Log
       │
Restore Undo Stack
       │
Restore Selection State
```

Timeline snapshots are append-only.

---

## Timeline Replay Guarantees

* Event ordering preserved.
* Track IDs preserved.
* Version increments preserved.
* Selection restored.

---

# 4.48 Runtime Checkpoint Engine

Checkpoints provide crash recovery.

## Checkpoint Types

| Type                 | Frequency             |
| -------------------- | --------------------- |
| Recording Checkpoint | Every chunk flush     |
| Timeline Checkpoint  | Every 30 seconds      |
| Project Checkpoint   | Every minute          |
| Export Checkpoint    | Every encoded segment |

---

## Checkpoint Layout

```text id="4sszls"
checkpoints/

├── runtime-0001.json

├── runtime-0002.json

├── timeline-0003.json

└── recording-0004.json
```

---

## Runtime Checkpoint Contract

```typescript id="lmk0h4"
interface RuntimeCheckpoint {

    checkpointId:string;

    projectId:string;

    timelineVersion:number;

    recordingChunkCount:number;

    playbackTimestampUs:number;

    workerStates:string[];

}
```

---

# 4.49 Crash Recovery Pipeline

Entire browser crashes require project recovery.

## Recovery Boot

```text id="qxbtxa"
Browser Opens
     │
Recovery Scanner
     │
Latest Manifest
     │
Latest Runtime Checkpoint
     │
Verify Chunks
     │
Restore Project
```

---

## Recovery Verification

Verify:

* checksum
* chunk order
* timeline version
* schema compatibility

Only verified checkpoints restore automatically.

---

## Corruption Detection

If checksum mismatch detected:

* isolate damaged chunk.
* recover remaining recording.
* notify user after recovery.

Never overwrite corrupted data.

---

# 4.50 Runtime Diagnostics Architecture

Diagnostics exist only in Developer Mode.

## Diagnostics Modules

```text id="wxpnx1"
Developer Diagnostics
│
├── Worker Inspector
├── Memory Inspector
├── Queue Inspector
├── Timeline Inspector
├── GPU Inspector
├── AI Inspector
└── Export Inspector
```

Each inspector reads runtime metrics only.

---

## Diagnostics Overlay

Displays:

* FPS
* Memory
* Queue depth
* Worker latency
* Active workers
* GPU textures

Similar to Chrome DevTools performance HUD.

---

# 4.51 Worker Inspector

Shows real-time worker information.

## Information Displayed

| Metric        |
| ------------- |
| Worker Status |
| Queue Size    |
| CPU Time      |
| Memory        |
| Uptime        |
| Restart Count |
| Heartbeat Age |

---

## Worker Status Colors

| Status | Meaning        |
| ------ | -------------- |
| Green  | Healthy        |
| Yellow | Warning        |
| Orange | Throttled      |
| Red    | Restart Needed |
| Gray   | Disabled       |

---

## Inspector Packet

```typescript id="pm2cti"
interface WorkerInspectorData {

    workerId:string;

    state:string;

    queueDepth:number;

    memoryMB:number;

    uptime:number;

}
```

# 4.52 Queue Inspector

# 5.1 Purpose of Browser APIs & Capability Detection

Everything TryLipi does depends on browser capabilities.

Unlike Electron or native desktop applications, a browser can:

* support an API,
* partially support it,
* gate it behind permissions,
* disable it due to security,
* remove it on browser updates.

Therefore TryLipi contains a dedicated **Browser Compatibility Layer (BCL)**.

The BCL abstracts every browser capability into a stable runtime interface.

No other engine directly calls browser APIs.

---

## Responsibilities of the Browser Compatibility Layer

The BCL is responsible for:

* Detecting supported APIs.
* Detecting browser engine.
* Detecting browser version.
* Detecting operating system.
* Detecting hardware acceleration.
* Detecting codec support.
* Detecting GPU capabilities.
* Detecting permission availability.
* Detecting security restrictions.
* Producing one immutable `BrowserCapabilities` object.

Every engine consumes this object.

---

## Why This Layer Exists

Without BCL:

* Capture code becomes browser-specific.
* Rendering engine contains feature checks.
* Export engine becomes fragmented.
* Safari bugs leak into business logic.

The BCL isolates browser complexity.

---

# 5.2 Capability Detection Philosophy

Capability detection is **feature-first**, not browser-first.

## Golden Capability Rules

1. Never assume Chrome supports everything.
2. Never detect browser before detecting feature.
3. Feature detection always wins over user-agent parsing.
4. Browser version is only a compatibility hint.
5. Every capability has a fallback strategy.

---

## Detection Priority

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=240>**Priority**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Method**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>1</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Runtime feature detection (`"VideoEncoder" in window`).</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>2</table-cell>
    <table-cell>API behavior validation.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>3</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Security validation.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>4</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Browser version compatibility.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>5</table-cell>
    <table-cell>User-agent fingerprint (last resort).</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

---

## Runtime Detection Example

```typescript id="hbgyft"
const supportsWebCodecs =

    typeof VideoEncoder !== "undefined" &&

    typeof VideoDecoder !== "undefined";
```

This is preferred over checking browser version.

---

# 5.3 Browser Capability Manager

Browser Capability Manager is created before any worker starts.

Responsibilities:

* Detect capabilities.
* Validate secure context.
* Cache results.
* Expose immutable capability object.

```text id="rybqxy"
Application Starts
       │
Capability Manager
       │
Feature Detection
       │
Security Validation
       │
Permission Snapshot
       │
Capability Object Frozen
```

After initialization the object is immutable.

---

```text id="ck9zyl"
Capability Manager
│
├── Browser Detector
├── Feature Detector
├── Codec Detector
├── GPU Detector
├── Permission Detector
├── Security Detector
├── Audio Detector
└── Display Detector
```

Each detector runs independently.

# 5.7 Secure Context Requirements

Most browser APIs require secure contexts.

## Allowed Secure Contexts

* HTTPS
* localhost
* 127.0.0.1

Everything else is unsupported.

---

## Secure Context Validation

```typescript id="gfkpcu"
const isSecure = window.isSecureContext;
```

If false:

* recording disabled
* SharedArrayBuffer disabled
* WebCodecs may fail
* clipboard APIs restricted

---

## Why HTTPS Is Mandatory

Required for:

* Screen Capture API.
* Clipboard API.
* SharedArrayBuffer.
* Service Workers.
* WebCodecs in some browsers.

Production deployment must always use HTTPS.

---

# 5.8 Cross-Origin Isolation Requirements

SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation.

## Required Headers

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=260>**Header**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Value**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy</table-cell>
    <table-cell>`same-origin`</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy</table-cell>
    <table-cell>`require-corp`</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

These headers are mandatory in production.

---

## Isolation Detection

```typescript id="8drmrj"
const isolated = crossOriginIsolated === true;
```

Capability Manager exposes this flag.

---

## Isolation Levels

| Level          | Features                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------- |
| Full Isolation | SharedArrayBuffer enabled |
| Partial        | OffscreenCanvas only      |
| None           | No shared memory          |

TryLipi supports all three levels.

---

# 5.9 Permission State Machine

Permissions change dynamically.

Never cache permission forever.

## Permission Lifecycle

```text id="0td6m5"
Unknown
   │
Prompt
   │
Granted
   │
Denied
   │
Revoked
```

Workers observe permission updates.

---

## Permission Snapshot

```typescript id="4k55pm"
interface PermissionStateSnapshot {

    screen:"granted"|"prompt"|"denied";

    microphone:"granted"|"prompt"|"denied";

}
```

Snapshot updates on permission changes.

---

## Permission Rules

* Never assume granted.
* Re-check after browser focus.
* Detect revoked permissions immediately.

# 5.12 Multi-Monitor Discovery

Users may have multiple monitors.

The browser picker exposes available displays.

## Supported Workflows

* Single monitor recording.
* External monitor recording.
* Laptop + monitor recording.
* Browser tab recording.
* Window recording.

TryLipi never enumerates monitors directly for privacy.

Available after user selection.


# 5.13 Capture Resolution Discovery

Capture resolution comes from the selected track.

Rules:

* Never trust CSS viewport.
* Always trust MediaStreamTrack settings.

---

## Resolution Contract

```typescript id="h0vysu"
interface CaptureResolution {

    width:number;

    height:number;

    frameRate:number;

    aspectRatio:number;

}
```

Resolution is immutable for the recording session.

---

## Retina / HiDPI Notes

On HiDPI displays:

* Logical viewport ≠ captured pixels.
* Camera engine uses pixel resolution.
* UI engine uses CSS resolution.

Conversion occurs inside Vision Engine.

---

# 5.14 Canonical Rules (Part 5.1)

1. Browser Capability Layer is the only subsystem that talks directly to browser APIs.
2. Feature detection always takes precedence over browser detection.
3. Browser version is only a compatibility hint.
4. BrowserCapabilities is immutable after initialization.
5. HTTPS is mandatory for production.
6. Cross-origin isolation enables SharedArrayBuffer but is optional for degraded mode.
7. Permission state is dynamic and must be monitored continuously.
8. Screen capture capabilities are detected after feature validation.
9. Capture resolution comes from MediaStreamTrack settings, never CSS viewport.
10. Multi-monitor support relies on browser privacy-preserving APIs only.

# 5.15 Screen Capture Engine Overview

The Screen Capture Engine is responsible for turning a browser permission into a deterministic recording session.

Unlike traditional media apps, the browser owns the picker UI and permission lifecycle.

TryLipi owns everything **after** the user selects a surface.

## Responsibilities

* Create capture session.
* Negotiate capture constraints.
* Create MediaStreams.
* Capture video + system audio + microphone.
* Monitor track health.
* Detect surface changes.
* Recover from permission loss.
* Emit immutable CaptureSession state.

---

## Capture Engine Modules

```text
Screen Capture Engine
│
├── Capture Session Manager
├── Constraint Builder
├── Audio Negotiator
├── Cursor Manager
├── Surface Switch Manager
├── Track Observer
├── Permission Observer
└── Capture Recovery Manager
```

Every module is independent.

---

# 5.16 Capture Session Lifecycle

A recording session follows a strict lifecycle.

```text
Idle
 │
Request Capture
 │
Browser Picker
 │
Permission Granted
 │
Negotiating Constraints
 │
Capture Active
 │
Paused
 │
Resumed
 │
Stopping
 │
Stopped
```

Every transition emits an event.

---

## Session State Contract

```typescript
type CaptureSessionState =
    | "idle"
    | "requesting"
    | "negotiating"
    | "active"
    | "paused"
    | "recovering"
    | "stopping"
    | "stopped"
    | "error";
```

The Capture Worker owns this state.

---

## Capture Session Object

```typescript
interface CaptureSession {

    sessionId:string;

    state:CaptureSessionState;

    stream:MediaStream;

    createdAt:number;

    startedAt:number;

}
```

Session IDs persist into project metadata.

---

# 5.17 `getDisplayMedia()` Implementation

This is the only browser entry point for screen recording.

## Invocation Rules

* Must originate from user gesture.
* Cannot auto-start recording.
* Cannot reopen picker silently.
* Cannot bypass browser UI.

---

## Capture Request Pipeline

```text
User Click
    │
Constraint Builder
    │
getDisplayMedia()
    │
Browser Picker
    │
MediaStream Returned
    │
Track Validation
    │
Capture Session Created
```

---

## Capture Wrapper

The BCL wraps browser APIs.

```typescript
interface DisplayCaptureRequest {

    captureVideo:boolean;

    captureAudio:boolean;

    captureMicrophone:boolean;

    preferredSurface?:"browser"|"window"|"monitor";

}
```

Other engines never call `getDisplayMedia()` directly.

---

## Validation Before Recording

Immediately validate:

* Video track exists.
* Track enabled.
* Width available.
* Height available.
* Frame rate readable.
* ReadyState is `"live"`.

---

# 5.18 Capture Constraints Architecture

Constraints determine capture behavior.

TryLipi builds constraints dynamically.

## Constraint Builder

Inputs:

* Browser capabilities.
* User preferences.
* Surface type.
* Audio preference.

Outputs browser-safe constraints.

---

## Canonical Video Constraints

```typescript
interface CaptureVideoConstraints {

    frameRate:number;

    width:number;

    height:number;

    cursor:"always"|"motion"|"never";

}
```

---

## Resolution Strategy

Priority order:

1. Native monitor resolution.
2. User override.
3. Browser negotiated value.
4. Safe fallback.

Never upscale capture.

---

## Frame Rate Negotiation

Preferred FPS:

| User Setting | Browser Request    |
| ------------ | ------------------ |
| Auto         | Native display FPS |
| 30 FPS       | 30                 |
| 60 FPS       | 60                 |
| 120 FPS      | 120 (if supported) |

Actual FPS validated after stream creation.

---

## Dynamic Constraint Downgrade

If browser rejects requested constraints:

Fallback order:

1. Reduce FPS.
2. Reduce resolution.
3. Remove optional cursor preference.
4. Retry capture.

Never silently disable video.

---

# 5.19 Cursor Capture Modes

Browsers expose cursor behavior differently.

TryLipi abstracts cursor capture into one model.

## Cursor Modes

| Mode   | Meaning                      |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| always | Cursor always visible.       |
| motion | Cursor appears while moving. |
| never  | Cursor hidden.               |

---

## Runtime Cursor Strategy

Even when browser captures cursor:

TryLipi still tracks cursor independently for effects.

Captured cursor becomes optional.

---

## Cursor Policy Matrix

| Browser Cursor | TryLipi Cursor            |
| -------------- | ------------------------- |
| Visible        | Optional replacement      |
| Hidden         | Synthetic cursor rendered |
| Motion-only    | Timeline reconstructed    |

This enables custom cursor animations.

---

## Cursor Metadata

```typescript
interface CursorCaptureSettings {

    browserCursorVisible:boolean;

    syntheticCursorEnabled:boolean;

    cursorMode:"always"|"motion"|"never";

}
```

---

# 5.20 System Audio Capture

System audio is negotiated independently.

## Audio Sources

* Tab audio.
* Window audio.
* Entire screen audio.
* Microphone audio.

These are separate streams.

---

## Audio Negotiation Pipeline

```text
Display Picker
      │
Video Track
      │
Audio Track?
      │
Validate Audio
      │
Merge Audio Graph
```

---

## Audio Capture Modes

| Mode             | Description          |
| ---------------- | -------------------- |
| System Only      | Screen/tab audio.    |
| Mic Only         | Voiceover.           |
| System + Mic     | Mixed during export. |
| Silent Recording | Video only.          |

---

## Audio Validation

Immediately verify:

* Audio track exists.
* Audio enabled.
* ReadyState `"live"`.
* Sample rate readable.

Fallback to microphone-only if unavailable.

---

# 5.21 Audio Track Negotiation

Audio tracks differ by surface.

| Surface       | Typical Audio Support |
| ------------- | --------------------- |
| Browser Tab   | Best support          |
| Window        | Browser dependent     |
| Entire Screen | OS/browser dependent  |

Capture Engine exposes capability flags instead of assuming support.

---

## Audio Metadata

```typescript
interface AudioCaptureMetadata {

    sampleRate:number;

    channelCount:number;

    systemAudio:boolean;

    microphone:boolean;

}
```

Used later by Audio Worker.

---

# 5.22 CaptureController API

Modern Chromium exposes CaptureController.

TryLipi uses it when available.

## Responsibilities

* Surface switching.
* Focus behavior.
* Session control.

Capability detection required.

---

## CaptureController Contract

```typescript
interface CaptureControllerCapability {

    supported:boolean;

    surfaceSwitching:boolean;

}
```

Feature-gated through BCL.

---

## Controller Lifecycle

```text
Session Starts
      │
Controller Attached
      │
Surface Switch Requested
      │
Browser UI
      │
Track Updated
```

Fallback exists if unsupported.

---

# 5.23 Surface Switching Engine

Users should switch tabs/windows without ending recording when supported.

## Surface Switching Flow

```text
Active Capture
      │
Switch Requested
      │
Browser Picker
      │
New Video Track
      │
Replace Track
      │
Timeline Event
```

Recording session remains continuous.

---

## Timeline Surface Event

```typescript
interface SurfaceSwitchEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    previousSurface:string;

    nextSurface:string;

}
```

Export reproduces surface changes.

---

## Unsupported Browsers

If switching unsupported:

* Stop capture.
* Persist chunk.
* Start new capture session.
* Stitch sessions in timeline.

User sees one continuous project.

---

# 5.24 Track Lifecycle Management

Every MediaStreamTrack is actively monitored.

## Track States

```text
Created
 │
Live
 │
Muted
 │
Ended
 │
Disposed
```

Track Observer watches transitions.

---

## Track Metadata

```typescript
interface TrackMetadata {

    trackId:string;

    kind:"video"|"audio";

    readyState:string;

    muted:boolean;

}
```

---

## Track Events

* started
* muted
* unmuted
* ended
* restarted

Events enter Timeline diagnostics.

---

# 5.25 Track Health Observer

Observer runs continuously.

Checks:

* readyState
* muted
* settings changes
* frame rate changes
* resolution changes

Heartbeat every few seconds.

---

## Health States

| State   | Meaning              |
| ------- | -------------------- |
| Healthy | Live frames arriving |
| Warning | FPS dropped          |
| Muted   | Track muted          |
| Ended   | Recording stopped    |

Coordinator reacts automatically.

---

# 5.26 Permission Revocation Handling

Permissions may disappear during recording.

Examples:

* User stops sharing.
* Browser UI stops sharing.
* Monitor disconnected.
* Tab closed.

---

## Revocation Flow

```text
Track Ended
     │
Permission Observer
     │
Recovery Manager
     │
Attempt Recovery
     │
Stop Gracefully
```

---

## User Notification Policy

User receives runtime notification only after recovery attempt.

Recording chunks already persisted.

---

## Revocation Packet

```typescript
interface CaptureRevokedEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    reason:string;

    recoverable:boolean;

}
```

Stored for diagnostics.

---

# 5.27 Capture Pause & Resume

Pause never destroys MediaStream.

## Pause Behavior

* Stop preview rendering.
* Stop AI scheduling.
* Continue session metadata.
* Preserve timestamps.

---

## Resume Behavior

* Restart preview.
* Resume scheduler.
* Continue timestamp timeline.

No timeline discontinuity.

---

## Pause Event

```typescript
interface CapturePauseEvent {

    pausedAt:number;

    resumedAt?:number;

}
```

Timeline stores pause markers.

---

# 5.28 Browser Quirk Layer

Every browser has quirks isolated here.

## Chrome

* Full WebCodecs.
* Best system audio.
* CaptureController support.

## Edge

* Chromium behavior.
* Minor picker differences.

## Firefox

* Different track behaviors.
* Partial WebCodecs.
* Different cursor behavior.

## Safari

* Limited worker rendering.
* Limited capture APIs.
* Aggressive permission resets.

---

## Quirk Registry

```typescript
interface BrowserQuirk {

    browser:string;

    feature:string;

    workaround:string;

}
```

Workarounds remain centralized.

---

# 5.29 Capture Capability Cache

Capability detection runs once per session.

Cache includes:

* browser engine
* secure context
* codecs
* GPU
* permissions
* CaptureController
* SharedArrayBuffer

Immutable snapshot shared with workers.

---

## Cache Rules

* Created at startup.
* Updated only for permissions.
* Read-only for workers.
* Persisted in memory only.

---

# 5.30 Acceptance Tests

## Capture Tests

* Browser picker launches.
* 4K capture starts.
* FPS detected correctly.
* Resolution detected correctly.

## Audio Tests

* System audio captured.
* Mic captured.
* Mixed capture supported.
* Missing audio fallback works.

## Surface Tests

* Monitor capture.
* Window capture.
* Browser tab capture.
* Surface switching timeline event created.

## Recovery Tests

* User stops sharing.
* Track ended event emitted.
* Capture recovery attempted.
* Recording finalized without corruption.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 5.2)

1. Only Browser Capability Layer invokes `getDisplayMedia()`.
2. Capture sessions have deterministic lifecycle states.
3. Constraints are generated dynamically from capabilities.
4. Cursor capture is abstracted into a browser-independent model.
5. System audio and microphone negotiation are independent.
6. Surface switching becomes timeline metadata.
7. Track Observer continuously validates MediaStream health.
8. Permission revocation triggers recovery before shutdown.
9. Browser-specific quirks remain isolated from runtime engines.
10. Capture metadata is immutable after session creation.

---

# 5.31 Capability Scoring Philosophy

Different machines support different browser APIs and different levels of hardware acceleration.

Instead of checking features repeatedly, TryLipi builds one **Capability Score** during startup.

Every runtime engine reads from this snapshot.

## Golden Rules

1. Capabilities are detected once.
2. Scores are immutable during recording.
3. Detection is feature-based.
4. Performance tiers derive from measured capabilities.
5. Scheduler decisions depend on capability tiers.

---

## Capability Snapshot Lifecycle

```text id="ds9pqk"
Browser Starts
      │
Capability Detection
      │
Validation
      │
Performance Scoring
      │
Immutable Snapshot
      │
Shared With Runtime
```

Workers never probe browser APIs themselves.

---

# 5.32 WebCodecs Capability Engine

WebCodecs is the preferred encoding/decoding pipeline.

## Required APIs

TryLipi validates:

* VideoEncoder
* VideoDecoder
* VideoFrame
* EncodedVideoChunk
* AudioEncoder
* AudioDecoder

Support must be individually verified.

---

## Detection Pipeline

```text id="nkyn57"
API Exists?
     │
Constructor Works?
     │
Configuration Supported?
     │
Capability Confirmed
```

Existence alone is insufficient.

---

## Capability Contract

```typescript id="gocw4r"
interface WebCodecsCapability {

    supported:boolean;

    videoEncoder:boolean;

    videoDecoder:boolean;

    audioEncoder:boolean;

    audioDecoder:boolean;

    videoFrame:boolean;

}
```

Frozen into BrowserCapabilities.

---

## Validation Strategy

Every codec configuration is validated using browser-native capability APIs before runtime.

---

# 5.33 Video Codec Detection

TryLipi supports multiple codecs depending on browser support.

## Preferred Codec Order

| Codec     | Use Case                    |
| --------- | --------------------------- |
| H.264 AVC | Universal export            |
| VP9       | High quality previews       |
| AV1       | Future export option        |
| HEVC      | Experimental Safari support |

---

## Codec Capability Matrix

| Codec | Recording | Preview  | Export       |
| ----- | --------- | -------- | ------------ |
| AVC   | Preferred | Yes      | Yes          |
| VP9   | Optional  | Yes      | Optional     |
| AV1   | Optional  | Optional | Experimental |
| HEVC  | No        | No       | Experimental |

---

## Codec Probe Pipeline

```text id="t7oqky"
Codec Candidate
      │
Browser Validation
      │
Supported
      │
Store Capability
```

---

## Codec Metadata

```typescript id="qvwqnp"
interface VideoCodecCapability {

    codec:string;

    encoder:boolean;

    decoder:boolean;

    hardwareAcceleration:boolean;

}
```

---

# 5.34 Hardware Encoder Detection

Hardware encoding dramatically reduces CPU usage during export.

## Detection Goals

Detect:

* availability
* supported codec
* supported resolutions
* supported bit depths

```text id="ytnr3v"
VideoEncoder Available
      │
Hardware Preference Requested
      │
Browser Accepts?
      │
Hardware Encoder Enabled
```

```typescript id="y8xq1v"
    available:boolean;

    codec:string;

    maxWidth:number;

    maxHeight:number;

    maxFPS:number;

}
```

---

## Supported Export Targets

TryLipi validates:

* 1080p60
* 1440p60
* 4K30
* 4K60

Fallback selected automatically.

# 5.35 Hardware Decoder Detection

Preview playback relies heavily on decoder performance.

## Detection

Validate:

* decoder exists
* configuration accepted
* hardware preferred
* decode latency acceptable

---

## Decoder Capability

```typescript id="dyc3b7"
interface HardwareDecoderCapability {

    available:boolean;

}
```

---

Hardware decode preferred.

Software decode fallback only for unsupported browsers.

# 5.36 GPU Capability Engine

GPU capability affects preview rendering and exports.

## GPU Detection Responsibilities

* Hardware acceleration.
* GPU renderer.
* Texture limits.
* Canvas acceleration.
* WebGL support.

```text id="vvlsdc"
     │
GPU Available?

WebGL Validation

Texture Limits
```

Validate:

* texture allocation
* framebuffer creation

Failure downgrades renderer.

# 5.37 GPU Texture Capability Detection

Renderer depends on maximum texture size.

## Target Texture Sizes

| Capability | Required |
| ---------- | -------- |
| 1080p      | 2048+    |
| 1440p      | 4096     |
| 4K         | 8192     |

## Texture Allocation Test

Allocate progressively larger textures until browser rejects.

Result cached.

* Small
* Medium
* Large
* XL

```text id="v8nbn1"
   │
```

If unsupported:

Renderer runs on UI thread with reduced performance budget.

* WebGL1 fallback.
* Floating-point textures.
* Shader compilation.

* Compile shader.
* Allocate texture.
* Draw test frame.

```typescript id="w6zwkv"
    floatingPointTextures:boolean;

}
```

```text id="jcw7rf"
      │
Request Adapter

Request Device
```

# 5.46 Performance Tier Engine

Capabilities become runtime performance tiers.

## Tier Inputs

* CPU cores.
* GPU acceleration.
* WebCodecs.
* Memory.
* Texture limits.

## Tier Definitions

| Tier   | Device Example   |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| Tier 1 | Older laptop     |
| Tier 2 | Mid-range laptop |
| Tier 3 | Gaming laptop    |
| Tier 4 | High-end desktop |

## Example Feature Matrix

| Feature             | T1      | T2       | T3   | T4   |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------- | ---- | ---- |
| 4K Recording        | Limited | Yes      | Yes  | Yes  |
| 4K60 Preview        | No      | Partial  | Yes  | Yes  |
| AI During Recording | Reduced | Moderate | Full | Full |
| WebGPU Blur         | No      | Optional | Yes  | Yes  |

## Tier Contract

```typescript id="8qnyta"

    | "tier3"
    | "tier4";
```

All detection results combine into one object.


Snapshot distributed during runtime startup.

* Immutable.
* Versioned.
* Available immediately after startup.

# Canonical Rules (Part 5.3)

1. Capability detection runs once during startup.
2. WebCodecs support is validated, not assumed.
3. Codec support is probed per codec.
4. Hardware encoder and decoder are detected independently.
5. GPU capability is validated through real rendering tests.
6. OffscreenCanvas worker rendering is feature-gated.
7. WebGPU is optional and feature flagged.
8. Internal rendering uses linear RGBA regardless of display color space.
9. Performance tiers drive scheduler behavior.
10. BrowserCapabilities is immutable and shared read-only.

# 5.50 Progressive Fallback Philosophy

Every feature in TryLipi must have one of three states:

* Native implementation.
* Optimized fallback.
* Unsupported with graceful degradation.

The application should never crash because one browser feature is unavailable.

## Golden Rules

1. Every capability has a fallback chain.
2. Recording is always prioritized over visual enhancements.
3. Fallbacks must preserve timeline determinism.
4. Unsupported features never corrupt project files.
5. Users should receive capability-aware UI messaging only when necessary.

---

## Fallback Hierarchy

```text
Native Capability
       │
Optimized Browser Fallback
       │
Software Fallback
       │
Feature Disabled
```

Every feature follows this hierarchy independently.

---

# 5.51 Capability Resolution Engine

Capability Resolution Engine converts detected capabilities into runtime decisions.

## Resolution Inputs

* BrowserCapabilities
* Feature Flags
* Performance Tier
* Project Requirements
* User Preferences

---

## Resolution Pipeline

```text
BrowserCapabilities
        │
Capability Resolver
        │
Feature Decision
        │
Runtime Configuration
```

Workers receive resolved configuration instead of raw capabilities.

---

## Runtime Feature Decision Contract

```typescript
interface RuntimeFeatureDecision {

    smartCamera:"native"|"fallback"|"disabled";

    semanticBlur:"native"|"fallback"|"disabled";

    exportEngine:"webcodecs"|"canvas"|"software";

    previewRenderer:"offscreen"|"main-thread";

}
```

This object drives initialization.

---

# 5.52 Browser Degradation Matrix

Every browser gets a predefined degradation strategy.

## Browser Capability Levels

| Browser             | Level   | Rendering Strategy |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------ |
| Chrome Stable       | Full    | Native Pipeline    |
| Edge Stable         | Full    | Native Pipeline    |
| Firefox Latest      | Partial | Hybrid Pipeline    |
| Safari Latest       | Partial | Hybrid + Software  |
| Unsupported Browser | Minimal | Software Pipeline  |

---

## Feature Matrix

| Feature                | Native   | Firefox      | Safari       | Legacy      |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ------------ | ------------ | ----------- |
| WebCodecs              | Yes      | Partial      | Partial      | No          |
| OffscreenCanvas Worker | Yes      | Yes          | Partial      | No          |
| System Audio           | Yes      | Limited      | Limited      | No          |
| WebGPU                 | Optional | Experimental | Experimental | No          |
| Smart Blur             | Native   | Fallback     | Fallback     | Disabled    |
| Auto Zoom              | Native   | Native       | Native       | Reduced FPS |

---

## Runtime Degradation Rules

Priority order for disabling features:

1. AI summaries.
2. Thumbnail generation.
3. OCR frequency.
4. Preview FPS.
5. Blur quality.
6. Camera interpolation quality.

Recording resolution is never reduced automatically after recording starts.

---

# 5.53 Feature Dependency Graph

Features depend on browser capabilities.

```text
WebCodecs
    │
Preview Decoder
    │
Timeline Preview

OffscreenCanvas
    │
Worker Renderer
    │
Blur Engine

AudioWorklet
    │
Mic Processing
```

Resolver disables dependent features automatically.

---

## Dependency Resolution Rules

If OffscreenCanvas unavailable:

* Worker rendering disabled.
* Preview renderer moves to UI thread.
* Scheduler lowers preview budget.

---

# 5.54 WebCodecs Fallback Pipeline

When WebCodecs is unavailable, TryLipi switches rendering architecture.

## Preferred Pipeline

```text
VideoFrame
    │
WebCodecs Decoder
    │
GPU Texture
    │
Renderer
```

---

## Fallback Pipeline

```text
MediaStream
     │
HTMLVideoElement
     │
Canvas DrawImage
     │
ImageBitmap
     │
Renderer
```

Higher CPU usage but identical timeline behavior.

---

## Decoder Resolution Strategy

| Priority | Decoder            |
| -------- | ------------------ |
| 1        | WebCodecs          |
| 2        | HTMLVideoElement   |
| 3        | Canvas Decode      |
| 4        | Software ImageData |

---

## Fallback Rules

Timeline timestamps remain identical regardless of decoder implementation.

---

# 5.55 Software Rendering Pipeline

Software rendering exists for browsers lacking worker rendering.

## Pipeline

```text
Video Element
      │
Canvas
      │
CPU Composition
      │
Canvas Presentation
```

---

## CPU Composition Order

1. Camera transform.
2. Blur.
3. Highlight.
4. Caption.
5. Cursor.
6. Background.

Matches GPU render graph exactly.

---

## Performance Expectations

| Output | Expected FPS |
| ------ | ------------ |
| 720p   | 60 FPS       |
| 1080p  | 45–60 FPS    |
| 1440p  | 30–45 FPS    |
| 4K     | 20–30 FPS    |

Software renderer lowers preview FPS before lowering resolution.

---

# 5.56 OffscreenCanvas Fallback Engine

If worker rendering unavailable:

## Rendering Migration

```text
Worker Renderer
        │
Capability Failure
        │
Main Thread Renderer
```

Timeline renderer remains identical.

---

## UI Thread Budget

Maximum preview work:

**8 ms**

Remaining frame time reserved for React UI.

---

## Render Queue Changes

Worker queue removed.

Preview queue becomes main-thread scheduler queue.

---

# 5.57 Firefox Compatibility Layer

Firefox differs from Chromium in multiple APIs.

## Known Differences

* Partial WebCodecs.
* Different MediaStreamTrack behavior.
* Different AudioContext timing.
* Different capture cursor implementation.

---

## Firefox Workarounds

| Issue                      | Workaround             |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Missing WebCodecs feature  | Canvas decoder         |
| Track settings unavailable | Cached metadata        |
| Cursor behavior            | Synthetic cursor       |
| Audio drift                | Audio clock correction |

All workarounds remain inside Browser Compatibility Layer.

---

## Firefox Rendering Policy

Prefer:

* OffscreenCanvas.
* WebGL2.
* Canvas decoder fallback.

Avoid unsupported WebCodecs features.

---

# 5.58 Safari Compatibility Layer

Safari receives dedicated compatibility logic.

## Safari Challenges

* Partial WebCodecs.
* Limited worker canvas rendering.
* Permission resets more aggressively.
* Audio capture limitations.

---

## Safari Strategy

| Feature | Safari Strategy          |
| ------- | ------------------------ |
| Preview | Main-thread fallback     |
| Blur    | CPU blur if needed       |
| Export  | Canvas renderer          |
| Audio   | Separate validation path |

---

## Permission Recovery

Safari may revoke permissions during navigation.

Permission Observer performs additional validation when tab regains focus.

---

## Rendering Budget

Preview FPS defaults lower on Safari when required to maintain responsiveness.

---

# 5.59 Legacy Browser Handling

Unsupported browsers receive graceful degradation.

## Unsupported Browser Criteria

* No Screen Capture API.
* No Canvas rendering.
* No MediaRecorder equivalent.
* Insecure context.

---

## Unsupported Feature Policy

| Capability                | Behavior                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Screen Capture Missing    | Disable recording UI            |
| WebGL Missing             | CPU renderer                    |
| SharedArrayBuffer Missing | Disable shared-memory scheduler |
| AudioWorklet Missing      | Legacy audio path               |

Project editing still works if project already exists.

---

## Browser Upgrade Recommendation

Capability Manager exposes recommended browser version without blocking application startup.

---

# 5.60 Runtime Capability Health Monitoring

Capabilities may change after startup.

Examples:

* GPU reset.
* Permission revoked.
* Monitor disconnected.
* Hardware acceleration disabled.

---

## Health Watchers

Monitor:

* Video track health.
* Audio track health.
* GPU context loss.
* Canvas context loss.
* Visibility changes.

---

## Capability Health State

```typescript
interface CapabilityHealth {

    gpuHealthy:boolean;

    captureHealthy:boolean;

    audioHealthy:boolean;

    rendererHealthy:boolean;

}
```

---

## GPU Context Loss Recovery

```text
Context Lost
     │
Pause Preview
     │
Recreate Context
     │
Rebuild Texture Pool
     │
Resume Preview
```

Timeline unaffected.

---

# 5.61 Browser Update Migration

Browsers change APIs over time.

Capability Manager stores capability schema version separately.

## Migration Strategy

```text
Old Browser
     │
Capability Snapshot v1
     │
Browser Updated
     │
Capability Snapshot v2
     │
Resolver Rebuild
```

Projects never depend on capability snapshots.

---

## Migration Rules

* Re-run capability detection.
* Preserve project files.
* Preserve timeline.
* Preserve recording metadata.

Only runtime configuration changes.

---

# 5.62 Capability Versioning

Capabilities are versioned independently from projects.

```typescript
interface CapabilitySnapshotMetadata {

    version:string;

    browserVersion:number;

    detectedAt:number;

}
```

Used for diagnostics.

---

# 5.63 Browser Compatibility Test Matrix

Every browser release passes compatibility tests.

## Chrome Tests

* Screen capture.
* System audio.
* 4K60 recording.
* WebCodecs encode.
* Worker rendering.

---

## Firefox Tests

* Canvas decoder.
* Worker rendering.
* Cursor fallback.
* Audio synchronization.

---

## Safari Tests

* Main-thread renderer.
* Audio fallback.
* Permission recovery.
* Export pipeline.

---

## Cross-Platform Tests

Platforms:

* Windows 10.
* Windows 11.
* macOS Intel.
* macOS Apple Silicon.
* Ubuntu (experimental).

---

# 5.64 Automated Capability Tests

Startup automatically validates runtime environment.

## Validation Categories

* Capture APIs.
* Codec APIs.
* Rendering APIs.
* Audio APIs.
* Security APIs.

---

## Validation Packet

```typescript
interface CapabilityValidationResult {

    feature:string;

    passed:boolean;

    fallbackApplied:boolean;

}
```

Stored only in diagnostics.

---

# 5.65 Browser Compatibility Dashboard

Developer Mode displays capability snapshot.

## Dashboard Panels

* Browser Info.
* Security.
* Capture.
* Rendering.
* Audio.
* GPU.
* Codec.
* Performance Tier.

---

## Example Dashboard

```text
Chrome 140

WebCodecs: ✅

OffscreenCanvas: ✅

WebGPU: ⚠️ Disabled

Performance Tier: Tier 3
```

Useful for debugging user reports.

---

The Browser Compatibility Layer is complete only if:

### Detection

* Feature detection implemented.
* Security validation implemented.
* Permission validation implemented.

### Capture

* Screen capture.
* Audio capture.
* Surface switching.

### Rendering

* GPU pipeline.
* CPU fallback pipeline.
* OffscreenCanvas fallback.

### Compatibility

* Chrome.
* Edge.
* Firefox.
* Safari.
* Legacy degradation.

### Recovery

* Permission recovery.
* GPU recovery.
* Context recovery.

---

# 5.67 Canonical Acceptance Checklist

## Capability Tests

* Immutable BrowserCapabilities.
* Capability Resolver output verified.
* Performance Tier assigned correctly.

## Rendering Tests

* GPU renderer selected when available.
* CPU renderer selected when required.
* Timeline identical between renderers.

## Browser Tests

* Firefox fallback path.
* Safari fallback path.
* Legacy unsupported browser behavior.

## Recovery Tests

* GPU context loss recovered.
* Permission revoked recovered.
* Browser update triggers capability refresh.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 5.4)

1. Every browser feature has a fallback chain.
2. Capability Resolver converts raw capabilities into runtime decisions.
3. Timeline behavior is identical across native and fallback pipelines.
4. Browser-specific workarounds remain isolated inside the Browser Compatibility Layer.
5. Software rendering preserves render graph ordering.
6. GPU context loss is recoverable without project corruption.
7. Browser updates never modify project schema.
8. Capability snapshots are versioned independently.
9. Unsupported browsers degrade gracefully instead of crashing.
10. Browser Compatibility Layer is the only source of truth for browser behavior.

# 6.1 Capture Engine Philosophy

The Capture Engine is the heart of TryLipi.

Every exported video begins here.

Everything downstream depends on one invariant:

> **Capture must be deterministic, lossless, timestamp-first, and independent from preview rendering.**

The Capture Engine is responsible for producing an immutable recording timeline that can be replayed identically weeks later on another machine.

---

## Golden Capture Rules

1. Capture is immutable.
2. Recording timestamps are canonical.
3. Preview never owns recording frames.
4. Audio and video clocks remain independent until synchronization.
5. Capture continues even if AI fails.
6. Capture continues even if preview drops frames.
7. Recording survives worker crashes through checkpoints.

---

## Capture Engine Responsibilities

* Create recording session.
* Manage MediaStreams.
* Manage MediaStreamTracks.
* Produce VideoFrames.
* Produce AudioData.
* Timestamp every packet.
* Forward packets to scheduler.
* Persist recording chunks.
* Recover interrupted sessions.

---

# 6.2 End-to-End Recording Pipeline

The complete recording pipeline spans multiple workers.

```text
Browser Picker
      │
MediaStream
      │
Capture Session Manager
      │
MediaStreamTrackProcessor
      │
ReadableStream<VideoFrame>
      │
Capture Worker
      │
Frame Scheduler
 ┌────┼─────────────┬─────────────┐
 │    │             │             │
 ▼    ▼             ▼             ▼
Recorder Preview   Vision      Storage
 │                  │
 ▼                  ▼
Chunk Encoder     AI Pipeline
```

The recording branch is completely isolated from preview and AI.

---

## Recording Pipeline Stages

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=220>**Stage**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Purpose**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Capture</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Receive MediaStreamTracks.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Decode</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Create VideoFrames.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Timestamp</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Assign canonical timestamps.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Schedule</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Route frames to consumers.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Persist</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Write immutable recording chunks.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

---

# 6.3 Capture Session Architecture

Capture Session represents one uninterrupted recording.

## Session Responsibilities

* Own MediaStream.
* Own track observers.
* Own timestamps.
* Own chunk sequence.
* Emit lifecycle events.

---

## Capture Session Object

```typescript
interface CaptureSession {

    sessionId:string;

    state:CaptureSessionState;

    createdAt:number;

    startedAt:number;

    stoppedAt?:number;

    mediaStream:MediaStream;

    videoTrackId:string;

    audioTrackIds:string[];

}
```

Session metadata becomes part of project manifest.

---

## Session Lifecycle

```text
Idle
 │
Preparing
 │
Recording
 │
Paused
 │
Recording
 │
Stopping
 │
Stopped
```

State transitions are append-only events.

---

# 6.4 Capture Coordinator

Capture Coordinator orchestrates the recording runtime.

Responsibilities:

* Track creation.
* Timestamp ownership.
* Worker communication.
* Recovery.
* Chunk lifecycle.

---

## Coordinator Modules

```text
Capture Coordinator
│
├── Video Track Manager
├── Audio Track Manager
├── Timestamp Engine
├── Chunk Manager
├── Recovery Manager
├── Cursor Capture Manager
└── Track Observer
```

No rendering logic exists here.

---

## Coordinator Guarantees

* One recording session.
* One timestamp authority.
* One chunk sequence.
* Multiple consumers.

---

# 6.5 MediaStream Internals

MediaStream contains independent tracks.

TryLipi treats MediaStream as transport only.

## Stream Topology

```text
MediaStream
│
├── Video Track
├── System Audio Track
└── Microphone Track
```

Tracks remain independent until Audio Engine.

---

## Stream Validation

Immediately validate:

* active stream
* track count
* live video track
* live audio tracks

Recording never starts with invalid topology.

---

## Stream Metadata

```typescript
interface StreamMetadata {

    streamId:string;

    active:boolean;

    trackCount:number;

    videoTracks:number;

    audioTracks:number;

}
```

---

# 6.6 MediaStreamTrack Topology

Tracks are managed individually.

## Track Categories

| Category     | Source            |
| ------------ | ----------------- |
| Video        | Screen/Window/Tab |
| System Audio | Browser/OS        |
| Microphone   | User device       |

Each track receives its own observer.

---

## Video Track Metadata

```typescript
interface VideoTrackMetadata {

    trackId:string;

    width:number;

    height:number;

    frameRate:number;

    displaySurface:string;

}
```

---

## Audio Track Metadata

```typescript
interface AudioTrackMetadata {

    trackId:string;

    sampleRate:number;

    channelCount:number;

    source:"system"|"microphone";

}
```

---

# 6.7 MediaStreamTrackProcessor Architecture

TrackProcessor converts MediaStreamTrack into VideoFrames.

This becomes the canonical frame source.

## Pipeline

```text
Video Track
     │
MediaStreamTrackProcessor
     │
ReadableStream<VideoFrame>
     │
Capture Worker
```

No HTMLVideoElement involved.

---

## Reader Lifecycle

```text
Track
 │
Processor
 │
Reader
 │
Read Loop
 │
VideoFrames
```

Reader exists only during active recording.

---

## Processor Contract

```typescript
interface TrackProcessorRuntime {

    processor:MediaStreamTrackProcessor;

    reader:ReadableStreamDefaultReader<VideoFrame>;

}
```

---

# 6.8 Video Capture Pipeline

Video capture pipeline is timestamp-first.

## Frame Flow

```text
VideoFrame Created
      │
Timestamp Assigned
      │
Frame Scheduler
      │
Chunk Encoder
      │
Preview
      │
Vision
```

Recording branch executes first.

---

## Timestamp Assignment Rules

Timestamp assigned immediately after reading frame.

Never later.

Microseconds become canonical storage unit.

---

## Frame Metadata Packet

```typescript
interface VideoFramePacket {

    frameId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    durationUs:number;

    sequence:number;

}
```

Sequence number prevents ordering ambiguity.

---

# 6.9 Audio Capture Pipeline

Audio pipeline is independent.

## Audio Flow

```text
Audio Track
     │
MediaStreamTrackProcessor
     │
AudioData
     │
Audio Scheduler
     │
Chunk Encoder
```

Audio does not pass through preview renderer.

---

## Audio Packet

```typescript
interface AudioPacket {

    packetId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    sampleCount:number;

    durationUs:number;

}
```

---

## Multiple Audio Tracks

Supported combinations:

* System only.
* Mic only.
* System + Mic.

Mixed later during export.

---

# 6.10 Timestamp Engine

Timestamp Engine is the canonical time authority.

## Responsibilities

* Assign timestamps.
* Detect drift.
* Normalize clocks.
* Maintain monotonic ordering.

---

## Timestamp Sources

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=220>**Source**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Usage**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>VideoFrame.timestamp</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Primary video timestamp.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>AudioData.timestamp</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Primary audio timestamp.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>performance.now()</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Diagnostics only.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

Never use wall clock for synchronization.

---

## Monotonic Timestamp Rules

* Never decrease.
* Never duplicate.
* Preserve microsecond precision.

Validation occurs before scheduling.

---

# 6.11 Track Synchronization

Video and audio clocks differ.

Synchronization occurs continuously.

## Sync Pipeline

```text
Video Clock
      │
Timestamp Engine
      │
Audio Clock
      │
Drift Detector
      │
Sync Metadata
```

No resampling during recording.

---

## Drift Metadata

```typescript
interface DriftMetadata {

    videoTimestampUs:number;

    audioTimestampUs:number;

    offsetUs:number;

}
```

Stored separately from media packets.

---

## Synchronization Window

Target maximum drift:

**±2 milliseconds**

Warnings generated after threshold exceeded.

---

# 6.12 Capture State Machine

Capture Engine exposes one authoritative state.

```text
Idle
 │
Preparing
 │
Negotiating
 │
Recording
 │
Paused
 │
Recovering
 │
Stopping
 │
Stopped
 │
Error
```

Workers observe state changes through Runtime Coordinator.

---

## State Transition Rules

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=240>**Transition**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Allowed**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Idle → Preparing</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Preparing → Recording</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Recording → Paused</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Paused → Recording</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Recording → Recovering</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Recovering → Recording</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Yes</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Stopping → Recording</table-cell>
    <table-cell>No</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

---

# 6.13 Capture Events

Capture emits immutable runtime events.

## Event Categories

* capture.started
* capture.paused
* capture.resumed
* capture.recovering
* capture.stopped
* capture.error
* capture.trackEnded
* capture.trackMuted

---

## Capture Event Contract

```typescript
interface CaptureEvent {

    category:"capture";

    event:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    sessionId:string;

}
```

Timeline stores selected events.

---

## Pipeline Tests

# Canonical Rules (Part 6.1)

1. Capture Engine is the canonical recording authority.
2. MediaStream is transport only.
3. MediaStreamTracks are managed independently.
4. TrackProcessor is the primary frame source.
5. VideoFrames receive timestamps immediately.
6. Audio packets are timestamped independently.
7. Timestamp Engine owns synchronization metadata.
8. Recording pipeline is isolated from preview.
9. Capture state transitions are append-only.
10. Session metadata is immutable after recording begins.
