# 8.1 Timeline Philosophy

The Timeline is **the single source of truth** for every edit in TryLipi.

Pixels are **never edited directly**.

Instead, every operation becomes a temporal instruction attached to timestamps.

Rendering happens later from timeline instructions.

## Golden Timeline Rules

1. Timeline is immutable.
2. Media is immutable.
3. Edits are timestamped events.
4. Rendering is deterministic.
5. Undo/Redo never mutates previous timeline state.
6. Timeline survives crashes through event replay.
7. Export reads only timeline state.

---

## Timeline Responsibilities

* Track recorded media.
* Track edits.
* Track effects.
* Track animations.
* Track captions.
* Track cursor effects.
* Track AI suggestions.
* Track audio automation.
* Serialize complete projects.

---

# 8.2 Temporal Data Model

Everything exists somewhere on a time axis.

TryLipi uses **microseconds internally**.

Milliseconds are UI only.

## Canonical Time Units

| Unit         | Usage                |
| ------------ | -------------------- |
| Microseconds | Runtime timeline     |
| Milliseconds | UI rendering         |
| Frames       | Preview calculations |
| Seconds      | User interface       |

---

## Timeline Coordinates

Every object has temporal coordinates.

```typescript
interface TemporalCoordinate {

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

    durationUs:number;

}
```

Used everywhere.

---

## Timeline Never Stores Frame Numbers

Frame numbers depend on FPS.

Timeline stores timestamps only.

Frame numbers are derived when needed.

---

# 8.3 Timeline Architecture Overview

Timeline is layered.

```text
Project
 │
Sequence
 │
Tracks
 │
Clips
 │
Effects
 │
Animations
```

Everything is attached to tracks.

---

## Timeline Runtime Topology

```text
Timeline Engine
│
├── Track Store
├── Clip Store
├── Event Store
├── Selection Store
├── Playback Store
├── History Store
└── Serialization Store
```

Independent stores reduce update cost.

---

# 8.4 Timeline Coordinate System

Timeline uses absolute recording time.

## Coordinate Origins

```text
Recording Starts
Time = 0 µs
```

Every timestamp is relative to recording start.

---

## Coordinate Example

```text
0s
│
Clip A

5s
│
Clip B

10s
│
Zoom Event

13s
│
Caption
```

Everything references one global timeline.

---

## Absolute vs Relative Time

<table>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell width=220>**Coordinate**</table-cell>
    <table-cell>**Purpose**</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Absolute Time</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Entire sequence timeline.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
  <table-row>
    <table-cell>Relative Time</table-cell>
    <table-cell>Inside clip.</table-cell>
  </table-row>
</table>

Both stored explicitly.

---

# 8.5 Timeline Object Hierarchy

Timeline contains immutable hierarchical objects.

## Object Tree

```text
Project
 └── Sequence
      ├── Video Tracks
      ├── Audio Tracks
      ├── Cursor Track
      ├── Caption Track
      └── Effect Tracks
```

Special tracks simplify rendering.

---

## Hierarchy Rules

* Project owns sequences.
* Sequence owns tracks.
* Tracks own clips.
* Clips own effects.
* Effects own keyframes.

Ownership is immutable.

---

# 8.6 Project Model

A project contains everything needed to reproduce a video.

## Project Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineProject {

    projectId:string;

    createdAt:number;

    updatedAt:number;

    sequences:string[];

    settings:ProjectSettings;

}
```

Media lives separately.

---

## Project Responsibilities

* Metadata.
* Timeline.
* Assets.
* Export presets.
* Theme.
* Creator branding.

---

## Project Versioning

Projects are versioned independently from runtime capabilities.

---

# 8.7 Sequence Model

A project may contain multiple sequences.

Future-proof for advanced editing.

## Sequence Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineSequence {

    sequenceId:string;

    durationUs:number;

    videoTracks:string[];

    audioTracks:string[];

}
```

Current MVP uses one sequence.

---

## Why Multiple Sequences

Future features:

* Shorts from long recording.
* Multiple exports.
* Alternate edits.
* Templates.

---

# 8.8 Track Model

Tracks organize temporal objects.

## Track Categories

| Track   | Purpose             |
| ------- | ------------------- |
| Video   | Recording clips     |
| Audio   | Audio clips         |
| Cursor  | Cursor events       |
| Caption | Captions            |
| Camera  | Zoom/Pan            |
| Blur    | Blur regions        |
| Overlay | Shapes & highlights |
| AI      | Suggestions         |

---

## Track Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineTrack {

    trackId:string;

    type:string;

    clipIds:string[];

    locked:boolean;

    hidden:boolean;

}
```

---

## Track Rules

Tracks never overlap clips of the same type unless allowed.

---

# 8.9 Clip Model

Clips reference immutable media.

## Clip Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineClip {

    clipId:string;

    assetId:string;

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

    offsetUs:number;

}
```

---

## Clip Coordinates

* Timeline Start.
* Timeline End.
* Source Offset.
* Source Duration.

Source media remains untouched.

---

## Clip Rules

* References asset only.
* Never duplicates media.
* Trim changes coordinates only.

---

# 8.10 Timeline Clock Engine

Timeline playback depends on one canonical clock.

## Clock Responsibilities

* Playback position.
* Scrubbing.
* Zoom calculations.
* Animation interpolation.

---

## Clock Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineClock {

    currentUs:number;

    playbackRate:number;

    playing:boolean;

}
```

---

## Clock Rules

Playback clock never modifies timeline data.

---

# 8.11 Playback Cursor

Timeline cursor represents playback head.

## Cursor Responsibilities

* Current position.
* Snap.
* Seek.
* Frame stepping.

---

## Cursor Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineCursor {

    positionUs:number;

    snapped:boolean;

}
```

---

## Cursor Rules

Cursor is UI state only.

Not persisted in exported projects.

---

# 8.12 Timeline Metadata Store

Metadata is separate from media.

## Metadata Categories

* selections
* markers
* labels
* colors
* comments
* AI annotations

---

## Metadata Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineMetadata {

    labels:string[];

    markers:string[];

    annotations:string[];

}
```

---

## Persistence Rules

Metadata stored separately from clips.

Allows collaborative editing later.

---

# 8.13 Immutable Event Sourcing

Timeline history is append-only.

## Event Sourcing Pipeline

```text
User Action
     │
Timeline Event
     │
Event Store
     │
Reducer
     │
New Timeline Snapshot
```

Previous snapshot untouched.

---

## Event Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineEvent {

    eventId:string;

    timestamp:number;

    type:string;

    payload:unknown;

}
```

---

## Why Event Sourcing

Enables:

* Undo.
* Redo.
* Recovery.
* Collaboration.
* Time travel debugging.

---

# 8.14 Timeline Snapshot Model

Snapshots accelerate loading.

## Snapshot Contents

* tracks
* clips
* keyframes
* metadata
* history pointer

---

## Snapshot Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineSnapshot {

    version:number;

    eventOffset:number;

    createdAt:number;

}
```

Snapshots generated periodically.

---

# 8.15 Acceptance Tests

## Timeline Tests

* Project loads.
* Sequence loads.
* Tracks created.
* Clips positioned.

## Coordinate Tests

* Microsecond precision.
* Absolute timestamps.
* Relative offsets.

## Event Tests

* Events append.
* Snapshot replay.
* Immutable history.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 8.1)

1. Timeline is the canonical editing source of truth.
2. Media assets are immutable.
3. Timeline stores timestamps, not pixels.
4. Projects own sequences.
5. Sequences own tracks.
6. Tracks own clips.
7. Clips reference immutable assets.
8. Event sourcing is append-only.
9. Snapshots accelerate replay.
10. Timeline clock is runtime state only.

# 8.16 Track Engine Philosophy

Tracks organize independent streams of temporal events.

Unlike traditional editors, TryLipi treats **everything as a track**, including cursor movement, smart camera zooms, blur masks, captions, AI suggestions, overlays, and audio automation.

## Golden Track Rules

1. Tracks are independent.
2. Tracks are ordered.
3. Track IDs never change.
4. Clips belong to exactly one primary track.
5. Tracks never own media directly.

---

## Track Categories

| Track Type | Description                 |
| ---------- | --------------------------- |
| Video      | Recorded screen clips       |
| Audio      | System & microphone clips   |
| Cursor     | Cursor events               |
| Camera     | Smart Camera keyframes      |
| Blur       | Blur regions                |
| Caption    | Subtitle clips              |
| Overlay    | Shapes & annotations        |
| Automation | Volume & opacity automation |
| AI         | AI-generated edits          |

---

# 8.17 Track Registry

Timeline keeps a registry for every track.

## Registry Responsibilities

* Track lookup.
* Ordering.
* Visibility.
* Lock state.
* Color labels.
* Metadata.

---

## Registry Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineTrackRegistry {

    trackIds:string[];

    order:string[];

    metadata:Map<string, TrackMetadata>;

}
```

---

## Metadata Contract

```typescript
interface TrackMetadata {

    trackId:string;

    type:string;

    name:string;

    color:string;

    locked:boolean;

    hidden:boolean;

    muted:boolean;

}
```

---

# 8.18 Track Ordering Model

Track order determines rendering order.

## Rendering Order (Top → Bottom)

```text
Overlay Track
Caption Track
Cursor Track
Camera Track
Blur Track
Video Track
Background Track
```

Audio tracks render separately.

---

## Ordering Rules

* Overlay always above video.
* Blur evaluated before overlays.
* Cursor rendered after blur.
* Captions rendered after cursor.

---

# 8.19 Track Indexing Engine

Large timelines require indexing.

## Primary Indexes

| Index         | Purpose         |
| ------------- | --------------- |
| Track ID      | Lookup          |
| Clip ID       | Lookup          |
| Timestamp     | Playback        |
| Interval Tree | Range queries   |
| Layer Index   | Rendering order |

---

## Timestamp Index

```text
0µs
│
Clip A

2,000,000µs
│
Clip B

5,000,000µs
│
Clip C
```

---

## Track Index Contract

```typescript
interface TrackIndex {

    clipIndex:Map<string,string>;

    timestampIndex:IntervalTree;

}
```

---

# 8.20 Interval Tree Engine

Timeline queries must be logarithmic.

Interval trees answer:

* active clips
* overlapping clips
* visible clips
* selection range

---

## Interval Tree Structure

```text
Timeline Interval Tree

[0-5]

├── [0-2]

└── [2-5]
```

---

## Query Complexity

| Query          | Complexity   |
| -------------- | ------------ |
| Active clip    | O(log n)     |
| Range lookup   | O(log n + k) |
| Overlap lookup | O(log n + k) |

Supports thousands of clips.

---

# 8.21 Clip Engine Philosophy

Clips reference immutable assets.

A clip is only a **view** into source media.

## Golden Clip Rules

1. Source media immutable.
2. Clip references source asset.
3. Trim changes view.
4. Split creates references.
5. Delete removes reference, not media.

---

## Clip Responsibilities

* Source offset.
* Timeline position.
* Speed.
* Transform references.
* Metadata.

---

# 8.22 Clip Lifecycle

## Lifecycle

```text
Asset Imported
      │
Clip Created
      │
Trimmed
      │
Split
      │
Moved
      │
Deleted
```

Asset remains unchanged.

---

## Lifecycle States

| State   | Meaning           |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| Active  | Visible clip      |
| Hidden  | Disabled clip     |
| Muted   | Audio disabled    |
| Deleted | Reference removed |

---

# 8.23 Clip Reference Model

Every clip references media.

## Reference Contract

```typescript
interface ClipReference {

    clipId:string;

    assetId:string;

    sourceStartUs:number;

    sourceEndUs:number;

    timelineStartUs:number;

}
```

---

## Reference Rules

* Multiple clips may reference same asset.
* References never duplicate media.
* Asset survives clip deletion.

---

# 8.24 Clip Metadata Store

Metadata separated from source.

## Metadata

* title
* color
* labels
* AI confidence
* thumbnail cache
* markers

---

## Metadata Contract

```typescript
interface ClipMetadata {

    clipId:string;

    label:string[];

    color:string;

    markers:string[];

}
```

---

# 8.25 Trim Engine

Trim changes clip boundaries.

## Trim Types

| Type       | Description                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------ |
| Left Trim  | Change clip start              |
| Right Trim | Change clip end                |
| Slip Trim  | Move source window             |
| Slide Trim | Move clip preserving neighbors |

---

## Left Trim Example

```text
Before

|----------Clip----------|

After

    |------Clip------|
```

---

## Trim Contract

```typescript
interface TrimOperation {

    clipId:string;

    edge:"left"|"right";

    deltaUs:number;

}
```

---

## Trim Rules

* Never modify source asset.
* Update timeline coordinates.
* Preserve source boundaries.
* Emit timeline event.

---

# 8.26 Source Boundary Validation

Clip cannot trim beyond source media.

## Validation Rules

Reject trim if:

* source start less than zero.
* source end greater than asset duration.
* duration becomes negative.

---

## Boundary Metadata

```typescript
interface ClipBoundary {

    assetDurationUs:number;

    clipStartUs:number;

    clipEndUs:number;

}
```

---

# 8.27 Split Engine

Split creates two clip references.

## Split Pipeline

```text
Clip
 │
Split Position
 │
Left Clip

Right Clip
```

---

## Split Contract

```typescript
interface SplitOperation {

    clipId:string;

    splitTimestampUs:number;

}
```

---

## Split Rules

* Preserve source asset.
* Generate new clip ID.
* Preserve metadata.
* Copy automation references.

---

# 8.28 Ripple Engine

Ripple editing shifts downstream clips.

## Ripple Delete Example

```text
A B C D

Delete B

A C D
```

Gap removed automatically.

---

## Ripple Insert

```text
A B

Insert Clip

A New B
```

Everything shifts.

---

## Ripple Contract

```typescript
interface RippleOperation {

    timestampUs:number;

    deltaUs:number;

}
```

---

# 8.29 Ripple Propagation Rules

Ripple affects:

* video clips
* audio clips
* captions
* cursor events
* camera events
* blur events

All synchronized tracks shift equally.

---

## Propagation Pipeline

```text
Ripple Event
     │
Affected Tracks
     │
Shift Events
     │
Reindex Timeline
```

---

# 8.30 Gap Management Engine

Timeline gaps are first-class objects.

## Gap Types

| Type            | Meaning           |
| --------------- | ----------------- |
| Empty Gap       | Nothing present   |
| Locked Gap      | Cannot ripple     |
| Placeholder Gap | Reserved duration |

---

## Gap Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineGap {

    gapId:string;

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

}
```

---

## Gap Detection

Gaps computed automatically between adjacent clips.

---

# 8.31 Gap Index

Timeline stores gaps separately.

Benefits:

* ripple previews.
* insert previews.
* snap targets.
* AI insertion.

---

## Gap Rules

Gaps never overlap clips.

---

# 8.32 Multi-Track Synchronization

Tracks stay synchronized through timestamps.

## Synchronization Targets

* captions
* cursor
* blur
* camera
* overlays
* audio automation

---

## Sync Contract

```typescript
interface SynchronizationGroup {

    groupId:string;

    trackIds:string[];

}
```

---

## Sync Rules

Ripple affects synchronization groups together.

---

# 8.33 Clip Linking Engine

Linked clips move together.

## Example

Screen recording clip linked with microphone clip.

Move video.

Audio follows automatically.

---

## Link Contract

```typescript
interface ClipLink {

    linkId:string;

    clipIds:string[];

}
```

---

## Link Operations

* move
* ripple
* delete
* mute
* split

Maintain synchronization.

---

# 8.34 Temporal Query Engine

Timeline exposes fast queries.

## Query Types

* active clip
* clips in range
* clips after timestamp
* clips before timestamp
* nearest gap
* nearest marker

---

## Query Contract

```typescript
interface TemporalQuery {

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

}
```

---

## Query APIs

```typescript
getActiveClips(timeUs)

getClipsInRange(start,end)

getNearestGap(timeUs)

getLinkedClips(clipId)
```

---

# 8.35 Spatial + Temporal Queries

Future Smart Camera requires both.

## Combined Queries

Example:

Find cursor events between:

2s–4s

inside clip A

within viewport.

---

## Query Pipeline

```text
Timeline Range
      │
Track Filter
      │
Spatial Filter
      │
Result Set
```

---

# 8.36 Acceptance Tests

## Track Tests

* Track registry loads.
* Track ordering correct.
* Hidden/locked state preserved.

## Clip Tests

* Clip references immutable asset.
* Split creates two clips.
* Trim respects source boundaries.

## Ripple Tests

* Ripple delete shifts tracks.
* Ripple insert preserves sync groups.

## Query Tests

* Interval tree lookup.
* Gap detection.
* Active clip lookup.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 8.2)

1. Every editable entity lives on a track.
2. Tracks are independently indexed.
3. Clips reference immutable media.
4. Trimming changes coordinates only.
5. Splitting duplicates references, not media.
6. Ripple propagates through synchronization groups.
7. Gaps are explicit timeline objects.
8. Interval trees power temporal queries.
9. Linked clips preserve synchronization.
10. Timeline queries must scale logarithmically.

# 8.37 Timeline Editing Philosophy

Every timeline edit is an immutable operation applied to timeline state.

The editor **never mutates clips directly**.

Instead:

* generate operation,
* validate,
* append event,
* reducer produces new state.

## Golden Editing Rules

1. Editing never mutates source media.
2. Every edit is reversible.
3. Every edit is timestamp-aware.
4. Editing preserves synchronization groups.
5. Ripple edits propagate consistently.

---

## Timeline Editing Pipeline

```text
Pointer Event
      │
Editing Engine
      │
Validation Engine
      │
Timeline Operation
      │
Event Store
      │
Reducer
      │
Updated Timeline Snapshot
```

---

# 8.38 Selection Engine

Selection is independent from timeline state.

## Selection Responsibilities

* clip selection
* track selection
* marker selection
* keyframe selection
* region selection

Selection is UI-only runtime state.

---

## Selection Store Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineSelectionStore {

    selectedClipIds:string[];

    selectedTrackIds:string[];

    selectedKeyframes:string[];

}
```

---

## Selection Modes

| Mode     | Description          |
| -------- | -------------------- |
| Single   | One clip             |
| Additive | Ctrl/Cmd click       |
| Toggle   | Toggle selected item |
| Range    | Shift selection      |
| Lasso    | Drag region          |

---

# 8.39 Region Selection Engine

Users can drag across timeline.

## Region Selection Pipeline

```text
Mouse Down
    │
Selection Rectangle
    │
Temporal Query
    │
Clip Set
    │
Selection Store
```

---

## Region Rules

Select clips whose visible timeline interval intersects region.

---

## Selection Metadata

```typescript
interface RegionSelection {

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

    trackIds:string[];

}
```

---

# 8.40 Drag Engine

Dragging clips updates timeline coordinates.

## Drag Lifecycle

```text
Pointer Down
      │
Capture Selection
      │
Preview Position
      │
Snap Resolution
      │
Drop
      │
Timeline Event
```

---

## Drag State Contract

```typescript
interface DragState {

    clipIds:string[];

    deltaUs:number;

    targetTrackId:string;

}
```

---

## Drag Rules

* Preview only until drop.
* Timeline unchanged while dragging.
* Drop emits operation.

---

# 8.41 Magnetic Timeline Engine

Magnetic timeline snaps clips to nearby objects.

## Snap Targets

* clip boundaries
* markers
* playhead
* gaps
* keyframes
* sequence boundaries

---

## Snap Radius

Measured in pixels in UI.

Converted into microseconds.

---

## Snap Priority

| Priority | Target        |
| -------- | ------------- |
| 1        | Clip boundary |
| 2        | Marker        |
| 3        | Playhead      |
| 4        | Gap           |
| 5        | Sequence edge |

---

# 8.42 Snap Engine

Snap engine resolves nearest target.

## Pipeline

```text
Candidate Position
      │
Nearby Targets
      │
Distance Sort
      │
Best Match
      │
Snap Preview
```

---

## Snap Metadata

```typescript
interface SnapResult {

    snapped:boolean;

    snappedTimestampUs:number;

    targetType:string;

}
```

---

## Snap Rules

Never snap across locked tracks.

---

# 8.43 Move Engine

Move changes timeline start/end.

## Move Types

* horizontal
* vertical
* cross-track
* ripple move
* linked move

---

## Move Operation

```typescript
interface MoveOperation {

    clipIds:string[];

    destinationTrackId:string;

    deltaUs:number;

}
```

---

## Validation Rules

Reject move if:

* destination locked,
* overlap illegal,
* outside sequence.

---

# 8.44 Slip Edit Engine

Slip changes source window.

Timeline position unchanged.

## Example

```text
Timeline Position

|---------Clip---------|

Source Offset Changes
```

---

## Slip Contract

```typescript
interface SlipOperation {

    clipId:string;

    sourceDeltaUs:number;

}
```

---

## Slip Rules

Neighbors unchanged.

---

# 8.45 Slide Edit Engine

Slide moves clip while preserving neighbors.

## Example

```text
A B C

Slide B

A  B  C
```

Neighbors trimmed automatically.

---

## Slide Contract

```typescript
interface SlideOperation {

    clipId:string;

    deltaUs:number;

}
```

---

## Slide Rules

Sequence duration unchanged.

---

# 8.46 Replace Edit Engine

Replace swaps media while preserving timeline position.

## Replace Pipeline

```text
Existing Clip
      │
New Asset
      │
Preserve Timing
      │
Replace Reference
```

---

## Replace Contract

```typescript
interface ReplaceOperation {

    clipId:string;

    assetId:string;

}
```

---

## Replace Rules

Preserve:

* transforms
* captions
* linked effects
* automation

---

# 8.47 Insert Edit Engine

Insert pushes downstream clips.

## Insert Pipeline

```text
Drop Clip
    │
Gap Exists?

Yes → Insert

No → Ripple
```

---

## Insert Rules

Gaps preferred over ripple.

---

## Insert Contract

```typescript
interface InsertOperation {

    clipId:string;

    insertTimestampUs:number;

}
```

---

# 8.48 Group Editing Engine

Groups allow editing multiple clips together.

## Group Lifecycle

```text
Select Clips
     │
Create Group
     │
Move
Trim
Ripple
Ungroup
```

---

## Group Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineGroup {

    groupId:string;

    clipIds:string[];

}
```

---

## Group Rules

Nested groups not allowed in MVP.

---

# 8.49 Linked Editing Engine

Linked clips preserve relationships.

Example:

Video + microphone.

## Link Operations

* move
* split
* ripple
* trim
* mute

---

## Link Validation

All linked clips remain synchronized unless explicitly unlinked.

---

## Link Metadata

```typescript
interface ClipLinkMetadata {

    linkId:string;

    synchronizationGroup:string;

}
```

---

# 8.50 Multi-Track Editing Engine

Operations span multiple synchronized tracks.

## Example

Ripple delete affects:

* video
* captions
* cursor
* camera
* blur
* overlays

---

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
Timeline Operation
      │
Sync Group Resolver
      │
Affected Tracks
      │
Apply Delta
```

---

## Multi-Track Rules

Locked tracks excluded.

Hidden tracks still synchronized.

---

# 8.51 Conflict Resolution Engine

Timeline detects illegal edits.

## Conflict Types

| Conflict          | Resolution       |
| ----------------- | ---------------- |
| Clip overlap      | Reject or ripple |
| Locked track      | Reject           |
| Sequence overflow | Reject           |
| Gap conflict      | Insert gap       |

---

## Conflict Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineConflict {

    type:string;

    clipIds:string[];

    timestampUs:number;

}
```

---

## Conflict Policies

Editing engine never silently discards edits.

---

# 8.52 Ripple Preview Engine

Ripple preview occurs before commit.

## Preview Pipeline

```text
Drag Clip
     │
Ripple Simulation
     │
Preview Ghost Clips
```

---

## Preview Rules

Ghost clips are UI-only.

No timeline mutation until drop.

---

# 8.53 Hover Preview Engine

Hovering clips reveals temporal preview.

Preview includes:

* source thumbnail
* duration
* markers
* AI suggestions

---

## Preview Metadata

```typescript
interface HoverPreview {

    clipId:string;

    previewTimestampUs:number;

}
```

---

# 8.54 Keyboard Editing Engine

Timeline operations support keyboard shortcuts.

## Examples

| Shortcut         | Operation     |
| ---------------- | ------------- |
| S                | Split         |
| Delete           | Delete        |
| Shift+Delete     | Ripple Delete |
| Ctrl/Cmd+G       | Group         |
| Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G | Ungroup       |
| Arrow Keys       | Frame step    |

Keyboard operations emit same timeline events.

---

## Selection Tests

* Region selection.
* Multi-select.
* Track selection.

## Editing Tests

* Move.
* Trim.
* Split.
* Slip.
* Slide.
* Replace.

## Snap Tests

* Clip boundary snap.
* Marker snap.
* Gap snap.

## Ripple Tests

* Ripple preview.
* Ripple delete.
* Multi-track ripple.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 8.3)

1. Editing generates immutable timeline operations.
2. Selection is runtime-only UI state.
3. Drag previews never mutate timeline.
4. Magnetic snapping resolves nearest legal target.
5. Slip edits modify source offsets only.
6. Slide edits preserve sequence duration.
7. Replace edits preserve timeline metadata.
8. Ripple previews are simulations until commit.
9. Groups synchronize edits across clips.
10. Conflict resolution happens before event creation.

---

1. Event Sourcing Philosophy
2. Timeline Event Store
3. Reducer Engine

# 8.56 Event Sourcing Philosophy

TryLipi does **not** store timeline state as mutable JSON after every edit.

Instead it stores an append-only stream of immutable events.

Timeline state is a projection generated by replaying those events.

## Golden Event Rules

1. Events are immutable.
2. Events are append-only.
3. Reducers create new state.
4. History is never rewritten.
5. Undo creates inverse events instead of deleting history.

---

## Event Sourcing Pipeline

```text
User Action
     │
Timeline Operation
     │
Event Validation
     │
Event Store
     │
Reducer
     │
Timeline Snapshot
```

This architecture enables deterministic replay.

---

# 8.57 Timeline Event Store

The Event Store is the canonical history of the project.

## Responsibilities

* Append events.
* Maintain ordering.
* Generate event IDs.
* Persist to IndexedDB.
* Support replay.

---

## Event Store Structure

```text
timeline-events/

000001.json

000002.json

000003.json

...
```

Events are ordered by sequence number, not timestamp.

---

## Event Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineEvent {

    eventId:string;

    sequence:number;

    createdAt:number;

    type:string;

    payload:unknown;

}
```

---

## Event Categories

| Category | Examples           |
| -------- | ------------------ |
| Clip     | Split, trim, move  |
| Track    | Lock, mute         |
| Timeline | Ripple, insert     |
| Camera   | Zoom keyframe      |
| Caption  | Add/edit/delete    |
| Blur     | Create/update mask |
| Cursor   | Highlight/click    |
| Audio    | Volume automation  |

---

# 8.58 Event Ordering Engine

Ordering must be deterministic.

## Ordering Rules

Events sorted by:

1. Sequence number.
2. Creation order.
3. Conflict resolution order.

---

## Sequence Generator

```typescript
interface EventSequence {

    current:number;

    next():number;

}
```

Sequence numbers never decrease.

---

## Ordering Guarantees

* No duplicate sequence numbers.
* Stable replay across devices.
* Stable undo history.

---

# 8.59 Reducer Engine

Reducers transform timeline state.

Reducers are pure functions.

## Reducer Responsibilities

* Apply event.
* Validate payload.
* Return new state.
* Preserve previous snapshot.

---

## Reducer Pipeline

```text
Current State
      │
Timeline Event
      │
Reducer
      │
New Timeline State
```

---

## Reducer Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineReducer {

    reduce(

        state:TimelineState,

        event:TimelineEvent

    ):TimelineState;

}
```

No side effects allowed.

---

# 8.60 Immutable State Tree

Reducers return structural copies.

## Tree Layout

```text
Timeline State
│
├── Tracks
├── Clips
├── Metadata
├── Selection
├── History Pointer
└── Playback State
```

Selection excluded from persistence.

---

## Structural Sharing

Only modified branches copied.

Everything else reused.

Supports large timelines efficiently.

---

# 8.61 Undo / Redo Philosophy

Undo is event-based.

No mutable history stacks.

## Golden Undo Rules

1. Undo creates inverse event.
2. Redo reapplies original event.
3. Timeline history preserved.
4. Undo never mutates event log.

---

## Undo Pipeline

```text
Timeline Event
      │
Inverse Generator
      │
Undo Event
      │
Reducer
```

---

# 8.62 Undo Event Generator

Every event knows how to invert itself.

## Example

| Event         | Undo Event    |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Trim Left     | Reverse Trim  |
| Move          | Reverse Move  |
| Split         | Merge         |
| Ripple Delete | Ripple Insert |

---

## Undo Contract

```typescript
interface UndoOperation {

    targetEventId:string;

    inverseEvent:TimelineEvent;

}
```

---

## Unsupported Undo

Operations without inverse rejected during validation.

---

# 8.63 Redo Engine

Redo simply reapplies stored event.

## Redo Flow

```text
Undo Event
    │
History Pointer
    │
Original Event
    │
Reducer
```

---

## History Pointer

```typescript
interface HistoryPointer {

    eventSequence:number;

    snapshotVersion:number;

}
```

Pointer moves forward/backward.

---

## History Rules

Future history discarded only after new edit branch.

---

# 8.64 Snapshot Engine

Replaying thousands of events every load is slow.

Snapshots accelerate startup.

## Snapshot Responsibilities

* Serialize current timeline.
* Store event offset.
* Compress state.
* Enable replay from checkpoint.

---

## Snapshot Structure

```text
snapshot.json

tracks

clips

keyframes

metadata

historyPointer
```

---

## Snapshot Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineSnapshot {

    snapshotId:string;

    eventSequence:number;

    createdAt:number;

}
```

---

# 8.65 Snapshot Generation Policy

Generate snapshots:

* every 100 events.
* every autosave.
* before export.
* before browser unload.

---

## Snapshot Pipeline

```text
Reducer State
      │
Serializer
      │
Snapshot Blob
      │
IndexedDB
```

---

## Snapshot Rules

Snapshots immutable.

Older snapshots retained until compaction.

---

# 8.66 Autosave Engine

Autosave persists timeline incrementally.

## Autosave Triggers

* every few seconds while editing.
* timeline idle.
* clip dropped.
* caption edited.
* before unload.

---

## Autosave Pipeline

```text
Timeline Dirty
      │
Debounce
      │
Snapshot
      │
Persist
```

---

## Dirty State Tracker

```typescript
interface DirtyTimelineState {

    dirty:boolean;

    changedEventCount:number;

}
```

---

## Autosave Rules

Never autosave selection state.

Only persistent timeline state.

---

# 8.67 Timeline Serialization

Serialization converts runtime state into project format.

## Serialized Components

* manifest
* timeline
* tracks
* clips
* events
* assets
* metadata

---

## Project Layout

```text
project/

manifest.json

timeline.json

events/

tracks/

assets.json

metadata.json
```

---

## Serialization Contract

```typescript
interface SerializedTimeline {

    version:number;

    timeline:TimelineState;

    events:TimelineEvent[];

}
```

---

# 8.68 Incremental Serialization

Avoid writing entire timeline repeatedly.

## Incremental Save Strategy

Persist only:

* new events.
* updated snapshot.
* changed metadata.

Everything else reused.

---

## Incremental Save Pipeline

```text
Dirty Events
     │
Append Events
     │
Update Snapshot
     │
Commit
```

---

## Benefits

* faster saves
* lower disk writes
* crash resilience

---

# 8.69 Crash Recovery Replay

Recovery rebuilds timeline from latest snapshot.

## Replay Pipeline

```text
Load Snapshot
      │
Read Event Offset
      │
Replay Remaining Events
      │
Restore Timeline
```

---

## Replay Rules

Events applied in sequence order.

Validation occurs before reducer.

---

## Replay Contract

```typescript
interface ReplayResult {

    restoredEvents:number;

    snapshotId:string;

}
```

---

# 8.70 Event Validation Engine

Corrupted events rejected before replay.

## Validation Checks

* schema version
* payload validity
* sequence continuity
* timestamp validity
* referenced clip exists

---

## Validation Result

```typescript
interface EventValidationResult {

    valid:boolean;

    reason?:string;

}
```

---

## Failure Policy

Skip invalid event.

Log diagnostics.

Continue replay if possible.

---

# 8.71 Event Compaction Engine

Long editing sessions generate thousands of events.

Compaction reduces replay cost.

## Compaction Rules

Safe events merged into snapshot.

Raw event history preserved until cleanup threshold.

---

## Compaction Candidates

* repeated drag updates.
* repeated caption edits.
* temporary selection events.
* hover previews.

---

## Compaction Pipeline

```text
Old Events
    │
Compactor
    │
Snapshot Updated
    │
Archive Events
```

---

# 8.72 Timeline Version Migration

Projects survive future releases.

## Version Responsibilities

* detect version.
* migrate schema.
* preserve compatibility.

---

## Migration Contract

```typescript
interface TimelineMigration {

    from:number;

    to:number;

    migrate(state:unknown):unknown;

}
```

---

## Migration Rules

Never mutate original project.

Always create upgraded copy.

---

# 8.73 Replay Performance Strategy

Replay optimized through batching.

## Batch Replay

Replay events in chunks.

```text
Events

1–100

101–200

201–300
```

Apply sequentially.

---

## Replay Optimizations

* structural sharing
* batched reducers
* indexed clip lookup
* deferred UI updates

---

# 8.74 Acceptance Tests

## Event Tests

* Append event.
* Sequence preserved.
* Replay deterministic.

## Undo Tests

* Undo trim.
* Undo split.
* Undo ripple delete.

## Snapshot Tests

* Snapshot generated.
* Replay from snapshot.
* Incremental replay.

## Recovery Tests

* Browser restart restores timeline.
* Autosave restored.
* Corrupted event skipped safely.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 8.4)

1. Timeline history is append-only.
2. Reducers are pure functions.
3. Undo generates inverse events.
4. Redo reapplies stored events.
5. Snapshots accelerate replay.
6. Autosave is incremental.
7. Replay starts from latest snapshot.
8. Events validated before replay.
9. Event compaction never changes timeline meaning.
10. Timeline version migration is forward-only.

---

# 8.75 Timeline Performance Philosophy

The timeline must remain smooth regardless of project length.

A 10-minute project and a 6-hour project should feel equally responsive.

## Golden Performance Rules

1. Render only visible items.
2. Virtualize thumbnails.
3. Virtualize waveforms.
4. Keep scrolling at 60 FPS.
5. Timeline queries must be logarithmic.
6. Playback must never depend on React rendering.

---

## Performance Goals

| Interaction    | Target     |
| -------------- | ---------- |
| Scroll FPS     | 60 FPS     |
| Zoom FPS       | 60 FPS     |
| Drag FPS       | 60 FPS     |
| Playhead FPS   | 60 FPS     |
| Marker updates | Under 1 ms |

---

# 8.76 Virtual Timeline Engine

Timeline is rendered through virtualization.

The DOM never contains every clip in the project.

## Virtualization Pipeline

```text id="b5u0xw"
Timeline State
      │
Viewport Window
      │
Visible Clip Query
      │
Virtual Timeline Renderer
      │
React Components
```

---

## Responsibilities

* Query visible clips.
* Query visible markers.
* Query visible thumbnails.
* Recycle DOM elements.
* Cache viewport calculations.

---

## Virtual Timeline Contract

```typescript id="d8imzx"
interface VirtualTimelineWindow {

    viewportStartUs:number;

    viewportEndUs:number;

    zoom:number;

}
```

---

# 8.77 Visible Window Renderer

Only clips inside viewport are rendered.

## Visible Window Example

```text id="k4q93k"
Entire Timeline (60 min)

|-------------------------------------------------------------|

Visible Window (18s)

          |-----------|
```

Everything outside the window is skipped.

---

## Visible Clip Query

```typescript id="wzqtdk"
getVisibleClips(

    viewportStartUs,

    viewportEndUs

)
```

Uses interval tree from Part 8.2.

---

## Overscan Window

Render additional clips before and after viewport.

Purpose:

* smooth scrolling.
* prevent pop-in.

---

## Overscan Rules

Default overscan:

* 2 seconds left.
* 2 seconds right.

Configurable by zoom level.

---

# 8.78 Clip Virtualization Engine

Clip DOM nodes are recycled.

## Lifecycle

```text id="vkx0wd"
Clip Leaves Viewport
      │
Detach React Node
      │
Return Component To Pool
      │
Reuse For New Clip
```

---

## Virtual Clip Contract

```typescript id="kqpk0b"
interface VirtualClip {

    clipId:string;

    virtualIndex:number;

}
```

---

## Virtualization Rules

* Clip metadata stays in store.
* DOM node recycled.
* Selection preserved.

---

# 8.79 Thumbnail Virtualization Engine

Generating thousands of thumbnails is expensive.

## Thumbnail Levels

| Level  | Resolution |
| ------ | ---------- |
| Tiny   | 80px       |
| Small  | 160px      |
| Medium | 320px      |
| Large  | 640px      |

Resolution depends on zoom.

---

## Thumbnail Pipeline

```text id="26fmxr"
Timeline Window
      │
Thumbnail Cache
      │
Decode Missing
      │
Display Visible
```

---

## Thumbnail Cache Rules

Never decode invisible thumbnails.

---

## Thumbnail Contract

```typescript id="2rxkrf"
interface TimelineThumbnail {

    assetId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    resolution:number;

}
```

---

# 8.80 Thumbnail Decode Scheduler

Decode thumbnails in background.

Priority:

1. Visible thumbnails.
2. Overscan thumbnails.
3. Future thumbnails.

---

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text id="hbfpyo"
Need Thumbnail
      │
Priority Queue
      │
Decoder Worker
      │
Cache
```

---

## Decode Rules

Cancel decode if thumbnail leaves viewport.

---

# 8.81 Audio Waveform Virtualization

Waveforms are sampled at multiple resolutions.

## Multi-Level Waveforms

```text id="1prnyy"
Audio

Full Samples

↓

1024 Buckets

↓

256 Buckets

↓

64 Buckets
```

---

## Waveform Levels

| Zoom   | Waveform     |
| ------ | ------------ |
| Far    | 64 buckets   |
| Medium | 256 buckets  |
| Near   | 1024 buckets |

---

## Waveform Contract

```typescript id="pdt22j"
interface WaveformLevel {

    resolution:number;

    buckets:Float32Array;

}
```

---

# 8.82 Infinite Zoom Engine

Timeline zoom changes temporal scale.

## Zoom Scale

```text id="9wb2cz"
Seconds Per Pixel

100

50

10

1

0.25

0.05
```

---

## Zoom Responsibilities

* scale viewport.
* preserve cursor anchor.
* update thumbnails.
* update waveform detail.

---

## Zoom Contract

```typescript id="jw88s4"
interface TimelineZoomState {

    pixelsPerSecond:number;

    zoomLevel:number;

}
```

---

# 8.83 Cursor-Centered Zoom

Zoom should anchor around cursor position.

## Pipeline

```text id="lmtywn"
Cursor Position
      │
Current Timestamp
      │
Scale Timeline
      │
Cursor Timestamp Preserved
```

Professional editing behavior.

---

## Anchor Rules

Timestamp under cursor remains constant while zooming.

---

# 8.84 Marker Engine

Markers annotate timeline positions.

## Marker Types

| Marker         | Purpose          |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| User Marker    | Manual bookmark  |
| AI Marker      | AI suggestion    |
| Chapter Marker | Video chapters   |
| Error Marker   | Diagnostics      |
| Export Marker  | Segment boundary |

---

## Marker Contract

```typescript id="gd7z2d"
interface TimelineMarker {

    markerId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    type:string;

    color:string;

}
```

---

## Marker Rules

Markers never modify playback.

---

# 8.85 Guide Engine

Guides appear while editing.

## Guide Types

* snap guide
* playhead guide
* alignment guide
* ripple preview guide
* selection guide

---

## Guide Pipeline

```text id="nvuxgm"
Drag Clip
    │
Nearby Target
    │
Guide Renderer
```

---

## Guide Contract

```typescript id="pqwxzi"
interface TimelineGuide {

    timestampUs:number;

    type:string;

}
```

---

# 8.86 Timeline Grid Engine

Grid depends on zoom level.

## Grid Levels

| Zoom       | Grid   |
| ---------- | ------ |
| Far        | 10 s   |
| Medium     | 5 s    |
| Close      | 1 s    |
| Very Close | Frames |

---

## Grid Generation Pipeline

```text id="mk3c6i"
Zoom
 │
Grid Density
 │
Visible Grid Lines
```

---

## Grid Rules

Grid generated procedurally.

---

# 8.87 Scroll Synchronization Engine

Horizontal scroll synchronizes timeline layers.

## Synchronized Layers

* clips
* waveforms
* thumbnails
* markers
* guides
* playhead

---

## Scroll Pipeline

```text id="l5hqim"
Scroll Event
     │
Viewport Offset
     │
Update Layers
```

---

## Scroll Rules

One shared scroll state.

---

# 8.88 Playback Synchronization

Playback updates independently from React rendering.

## Playback Pipeline

```text id="98tkp0"
Timeline Clock
      │
Playhead Position
      │
Visible Window Update
```

---

## Playback Rules

* React receives position updates.
* Renderer interpolates between updates.
* Playback never blocks on timeline render.

---

# 8.89 Timeline Cache Engine

Cache expensive calculations.

## Cached Items

* clip layout
* waveform buckets
* marker layout
* thumbnail layout
* snap targets

---

## Cache Invalidation

Invalidate only affected regions after edits.

---

## Cache Contract

```typescript id="bk1s9j"
interface TimelineCache {

    clipLayoutVersion:number;

    waveformVersion:number;

    markerVersion:number;

}
```

---

# 8.90 Performance Budget Engine

Timeline has strict runtime budgets.

## Budgets

| Component          | Budget     |
| ------------------ | ---------- |
| Visible clip query | Under 1 ms |
| Thumbnail lookup   | Under 2 ms |
| Waveform lookup    | Under 2 ms |
| Playhead render    | Under 1 ms |
| Scroll update      | Under 4 ms |

Target total under **8 ms/frame**.

---

## Large Timeline Targets

| Timeline Size   | Target      |
| --------------- | ----------- |
| 1,000 clips     | 60 FPS      |
| 5,000 clips     | 60 FPS      |
| 10,000 events   | 60 FPS      |
| 100,000 markers | Virtualized |

---

# 8.91 Timeline Stress Strategy

Stress scenarios include:

* 6-hour recording.
* 5,000 captions.
* 10,000 cursor events.
* 20,000 blur keyframes.
* Continuous playback.

Timeline virtualization must remain bounded.

---

## Stress Metrics

Track:

* visible DOM nodes.
* thumbnail cache size.
* waveform cache size.
* scroll latency.

---

# 8.92 Definition of Done

Timeline Engine complete only if:

### Rendering

* Visible clip virtualization.
* Thumbnail virtualization.
* Waveform virtualization.

### Interaction

* Infinite zoom.
* Cursor-centered zoom.
* Snap guides.
* Marker engine.

### Performance

* 60 FPS scroll.
* 60 FPS drag.
* Constant DOM size.
* Cached layout calculations.

---

## Virtualization Tests

* Only visible clips rendered.
* DOM nodes recycled.
* Overscan prevents pop-in.

## Zoom Tests

* Cursor anchor preserved.
* Waveforms update resolution.
* Grid density changes.

## Marker Tests

* AI markers visible.
* User markers editable.
* Marker queries logarithmic.

## Performance Tests

* 6-hour timeline scroll remains smooth.
* Thumbnail decoding prioritized.
* Playback independent from React rendering.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 8.5)

1. Timeline renders only the visible viewport.
2. Clip DOM nodes are recycled.
3. Thumbnails are generated lazily.
4. Waveforms use multi-resolution buckets.
5. Zoom is cursor-centered.
6. Guides are runtime-only visual aids.
7. Scroll state is shared across layers.
8. Playback is independent from UI rendering.
9. Timeline caches expensive layout calculations.
10. Timeline performance is bounded regardless of project length.

# 9.1 Smart Camera Philosophy

Smart Camera is not screen recording.

Smart Camera creates the illusion that a human camera operator is filming the screen.

Instead of moving pixels, it moves a **virtual camera** over a static recording.

Every camera movement is deterministic and timeline-based.

## Golden Camera Rules

1. Recording never changes.
2. Camera moves over recording.
3. Camera state is timeline data.
4. Zooms are keyframe driven.
5. Pans are interpolated.
6. Camera can be AI-generated or user-authored.
7. Export reproduces identical camera movement.

---

## Responsibilities

The Smart Camera Engine controls:

* Auto zoom.
* Auto pan.
* Cursor follow.
* Spotlight.
* Face follow.
* UI element focus.
* Manual camera keyframes.
* Safe cropping.
* Motion smoothing.

---

# 9.2 Camera Engine Overview

The engine is independent from rendering.

```text id="vxt9ef"
Timeline
   │
Camera Track
   │
Camera Engine
   │
Viewport Solver
   │
Preview Renderer
   │
Export Renderer
```

Camera calculations happen before rendering.

---

## Camera Engine Modules

```text id="m9kll9"
Smart Camera Engine
│
├── Camera Track Store
├── Subject Tracker
├── Viewport Solver
├── Motion Planner
├── Interpolator
├── Constraint Solver
├── Smoothing Engine
└── Camera Preview Engine
```

Each module owns one responsibility.

---

# 9.3 Camera Coordinate System

The camera operates inside recording coordinates.

## Coordinate Spaces

| Space            | Description               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| Screen Space     | Original recording pixels |
| Viewport Space   | Visible output frame      |
| Normalized Space | 0–1 coordinates           |
| Timeline Space   | Timestamped camera state  |

---

## Recording Coordinates

```text id="zw9ccw"
3840 × 2160 Recording

(0,0) ---------------- (3840,0)

  │

  │

(0,2160) ----------- (3840,2160)
```

Camera never changes recording coordinates.

---

## Normalized Coordinates

Everything inside camera engine converts to normalized coordinates.

```typescript id="ocx7ps"
interface NormalizedPoint {

    x:number;

    y:number;

}
```

Resolution independent.

---

# 9.4 Virtual Camera Model

The camera is a rectangle moving across the recording.

## Camera Rectangle

```text id="yxj7wc"
Full Recording

+---------------------------+

|        Recording          |

|    +--------------+       |

|    | Camera View  |       |

|    +--------------+       |

+---------------------------+
```

Viewport is a crop window.

---

## Camera Contract

```typescript id="vmub5s"
interface VirtualCamera {

    x:number;

    y:number;

    zoom:number;

    rotation:number;

    viewportWidth:number;

    viewportHeight:number;

}
```

---

## Camera Properties

* Position.
* Zoom.
* Rotation (future).
* Aspect ratio.
* Padding.
* Anchor point.

---

Camera state changes over time.

## States

```text id="pbxpl1"
Idle

Tracking Cursor

Tracking Subject

Transition

Manual

Paused
```

Only one active state at a time.

---

## State Contract

```typescript id="hxy8tn"
interface CameraState {

    state:string;

    timestampUs:number;

}
```

Timeline stores transitions.

---

# 9.6 Camera Timeline Track

Camera movements live on their own track.

## Track Responsibilities

* Zoom keyframes.
* Position keyframes.
* AI suggestions.
* Manual overrides.

---

```typescript id="y4lkta"
    keyframeIds:string[];

}
```

---

## Why Separate Track

Enables:

* undo independently,
* disable Smart Camera,
* replace AI movement,
* manual editing.

Every camera movement is defined by keyframes.

1. Smart Camera is a virtual camera, not pixel manipulation.
2. Camera movement is timeline data.

# 9.16 Cursor Tracking Philosophy

The cursor is the primary storytelling signal during screen recordings.

A professional editor does **not** keep the cursor centered at all times. Instead, the camera reacts to cursor intent.

The Smart Camera Engine classifies cursor behavior before generating camera movement.

## Golden Cursor Rules

1. Cursor movement is captured independently from video.
2. Cursor events live on their own timeline track.
3. Camera follows intent, not raw coordinates.
4. Small cursor jitter never moves the camera.
5. Camera anticipates clicks instead of reacting late.
6. Scrolls generate different behavior than clicks.

---

## Cursor Responsibilities

* Position tracking.
* Velocity calculation.
* Click detection.
* Drag detection.
* Scroll detection.
* Idle detection.
* Hover detection.
* Intent classification.

---

# 9.17 Cursor Capture Pipeline

Cursor capture runs continuously during recording.

## Pipeline

```text id="7um5mb"
Browser Pointer Events
       │
Cursor Capture Worker
       │
Normalization Engine
       │
Cursor Timeline Track
       │
Smart Camera Engine
```

Video recording never depends on cursor capture.

---

## Cursor Event Sources

| Event         | Purpose          |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| Pointer Move  | Position updates |
| Pointer Down  | Click begins     |
| Pointer Up    | Click ends       |
| Wheel         | Scroll detection |
| Pointer Leave | Visibility state |
| Pointer Enter | Cursor restored  |

---

## Cursor Event Contract

```typescript id="zvb4za"
interface CursorEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    x:number;

    y:number;

    type:string;

}
```

---

# 9.18 Cursor Coordinate Normalization

Cursor coordinates must remain independent from resolution.

## Coordinate Spaces

| Space           | Example           |
| --------------- | ----------------- |
| Raw Screen      | (1780,920)        |
| Recording Space | (1920,1080)       |
| Normalized      | (0.927,0.851)     |
| Viewport Space  | Depends on camera |

---

## Normalization Pipeline

```text id="5kxdck"
Pointer Coordinates
       │
Recording Resolution
       │
Normalized Coordinates
       │
Timeline Cursor Event
```

---

## Cursor Position Contract

```typescript id="bvmw1n"
interface NormalizedCursorPosition {

    timestampUs:number;

    normalizedX:number;

    normalizedY:number;

}
```

---

# 9.19 Cursor Sampling Strategy

Pointer events arrive at inconsistent frequencies.

TryLipi resamples cursor positions.

## Sampling Targets

| Scenario        | Sampling Rate |
| --------------- | ------------- |
| Idle            | 15 Hz         |
| Normal Movement | 60 Hz         |
| Dragging        | 90 Hz         |
| Stylus/Future   | Up to 120 Hz  |

---

## Sampling Pipeline

```text id="q2xsz5"
Raw Pointer Events
      │
Timestamp Interpolator
      │
Fixed Cursor Samples
```

Consistent sampling simplifies interpolation.

---

# 9.20 Cursor Velocity Engine

Velocity predicts user intent.

## Velocity Formula

Velocity is calculated between consecutive normalized samples.

Metrics stored:

* pixels/second
* normalized distance
* acceleration
* movement angle

---

## Velocity Contract

```typescript id="t5ldue"
interface CursorVelocity {

    speed:number;

    direction:number;

    acceleration:number;

}
```

---

## Velocity Categories

| Speed     | Interpretation       |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| Very Low  | Hover                |
| Low       | Reading              |
| Medium    | Navigation           |
| High      | Intentional movement |
| Very High | Rapid relocation     |

---

# 9.21 Cursor Acceleration Engine

Acceleration is more useful than speed.

## Why Acceleration Matters

Example:

* Cursor slows before clicking.
* Cursor accelerates toward button.
* Cursor stops immediately before interaction.

This predicts zoom targets earlier.

---

## Acceleration Pipeline

```text id="mhly2k"
Velocity Samples
      │
Acceleration Calculator
      │
Intent Predictor
```

---

## Acceleration Rules

Ignore single-frame spikes.

Use moving average.

---

# 9.22 Cursor Smoothing Engine

Raw cursor movement is noisy.

## Smoothing Pipeline

```text id="q8w6pn"
Raw Cursor
     │
Low-Pass Filter
     │
Smoothed Cursor
     │
Camera Planner
```

---

## Smoothing Goals

* remove jitter.
* preserve responsiveness.
* preserve click accuracy.

---

## Filter Parameters

Future configurable presets:

* Subtle
* Default
* Aggressive

---

# 9.23 Click Burst Detection

Clicks create emphasis.

The camera prepares before clicks.

## Detection Pipeline

```text id="cfrukq"
Pointer Down
      │
Movement Stops
      │
Click Confirmed
      │
Burst Window
```

---

## Burst Window

Capture frames around click.

Example:

-100 ms

Click

+250 ms

Provides cinematic emphasis.

---

## Click Event Contract

```typescript id="ezyl5y"
interface ClickBurstEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    durationUs:number;

    clickType:string;

}
```

---

# 9.24 Double Click Detection

Double-click behavior differs.

## Detection Rules

Two clicks within configurable interval become DoubleClick event.

---

## Event Categories

| Type         | Camera Behavior           |
| ------------ | ------------------------- |
| Single Click | Zoom emphasis             |
| Double Click | Hold zoom slightly longer |
| Triple Click | No special behavior MVP   |

---

## Double Click Metadata

```typescript id="gzfg0v"
interface DoubleClickEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    clickCount:number;

}
```

---

# 9.25 Drag Detection Engine

Dragging should not trigger repeated zooms.

## Drag Pipeline

```text id="fzdjlwm"
Pointer Down
     │
Movement Threshold
     │
Drag Start
     │
Drag Move
     │
Drag End
```

---

## Drag Metadata

```typescript id="jlwm3q"
interface DragEvent {

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

    distance:number;

}
```

---

## Drag Rules

Camera widens slightly during long drags.

---

# 9.26 Hover Detection Engine

Hover indicates reading or explaining.

## Hover Detection Rules

Cursor speed below threshold.

Minimal movement for configurable duration.

---

## Hover Metadata

```typescript id="tahw0g"
interface HoverEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    durationUs:number;

}
```

---

## Hover Camera Behavior

Camera stays stable.

Avoid unnecessary movement.

---

# 9.27 Idle Detection Engine

Idle cursor often means narration.

## Idle Pipeline

```text id="hynwdk"
Cursor Stops
     │
Idle Timer
     │
Idle Event
```

---

## Idle Thresholds

| Duration | Behavior            |
| -------- | ------------------- |
| 300 ms   | Possible idle       |
| 700 ms   | Stable idle         |
| 2 s      | Long narration idle |

---

## Idle Metadata

```typescript id="u87qqy"
interface CursorIdleEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    idleDurationUs:number;

}
```

---

# 9.28 Scroll Intent Detection

Scrolling is different from cursor movement.

## Scroll Detection Pipeline

```text id="rbebza"
Wheel Event
    │
Direction Detection
    │
Velocity
    │
Scroll Intent
```

---

## Scroll Categories

| Scroll   | Meaning          |
| -------- | ---------------- |
| Slow     | Reading          |
| Medium   | Browsing         |
| Fast     | Searching        |
| Momentum | Touchpad inertia |

---

## Scroll Event Contract

```typescript id="5gqjj0"
interface ScrollEvent {

    timestampUs:number;

    delta:number;

    velocity:number;

}
```

---

# 9.29 Scroll Camera Strategy

Camera behavior depends on scroll intent.

## Behavior

| Intent      | Camera        |
| ----------- | ------------- |
| Reading     | Stay zoomed   |
| Browsing    | Follow slowly |
| Fast Search | Zoom out      |
| Momentum    | Ignore jitter |

---

## Scroll Hold

Prevent camera movement during momentum scrolling.

---

# 9.30 Cursor Intent Classifier

Cursor events become semantic actions.

## Intent Categories

| Intent     | Example           |
| ---------- | ----------------- |
| Reading    | Hover             |
| Clicking   | Button press      |
| Typing     | Text field        |
| Selecting  | Drag selection    |
| Navigating | Rapid cursor move |
| Waiting    | Idle              |

---

## Intent Pipeline

```text id="dl0iee"
Cursor Events
      │
Velocity
      │
Acceleration
      │
Classifier
      │
Camera Planner
```

---

## Intent Contract

```typescript id="1ckqzv"
interface CursorIntent {

    intent:string;

    confidence:number;

}
```

---

# 9.31 Auto Zoom Trigger Engine

Zoom triggers originate from intent.

## Trigger Sources

* click
* hover
* pause
* UI detection
* AI suggestion

---

## Trigger Pipeline

```text id="g3v05r"
Cursor Intent
      │
Zoom Trigger
      │
Motion Planner
```

---

## Trigger Contract

```typescript id="lphwkq"
interface CameraZoomTrigger {

    timestampUs:number;

    targetZoom:number;

    reason:string;

}
```

---

# 9.32 Zoom Trigger Rules

Default triggers:

| Event          | Zoom  |
| -------------- | ----- |
| Button Click   | 1.35× |
| Menu Click     | 1.5×  |
| Code Selection | 1.6×  |
| Typing         | 1.25× |
| Idle Narration | Hold  |

AI later overrides these defaults.

---

# 9.33 Camera Target Generator

Camera target is generated before motion.

## Pipeline

```text id="s3fdmy"
Subject
   │
Padding
   │
Aspect Solver
   │
Camera Target
```

## Target Contract

---

## Target Rules

Targets always legal after constraint solver.

---

# 9.34 Cursor Anticipation Engine

Camera should arrive before click.

## Anticipation Window

Observe cursor slowing before click.

Move camera slightly ahead of click timestamp.

---

## Pipeline

```text id="pwkh3x"
Acceleration Drop
      │
Likely Click
      │
Begin Camera Transition
```

---

## Anticipation Rules

Never anticipate rapid random cursor movement.

---

# 9.35 Multi-Monitor Cursor Normalization

Browser capture may include multiple displays.

## Multi-Monitor Pipeline

```text id="sj9rq5"
Global Cursor
     │
Captured Surface Bounds

Normalize To Recording Surface
```

Cursor outside recording surface ignored.

```typescript id="pkodlm"
    surfaceBounds:BoundingBox;

}
```

# 9.36 Cursor Visibility Engine

Cursor visibility changes.

* visible
* hidden
* outside surface
* locked pointer

---

## Visibility Metadata

```typescript id="okbsj4"

}
```

---

1. Cursor has its own timeline track.

3. Velocity and acceleration drive intent classification.
4. Click bursts create zoom opportunities.

6. Scroll behavior differs from cursor movement.

# 9.38 Motion Planning Philosophy

The cursor tells the camera **where to go**.

Motion Planning decides **how to get there**.

A professional camera never teleports. It accelerates, eases, settles, pauses, and anticipates motion.

## Golden Motion Rules

1. Camera never jumps unless explicitly requested.
2. Motion is continuous.
3. Zoom and pan may have different curves.
4. Camera has maximum velocity.
5. Camera has maximum acceleration.
6. Motion interruption is deterministic.
7. Preview and export produce identical paths.

---

## Motion Planning Pipeline

```text
Cursor / Subject Target
        │
 Motion Planner
        │
 Transition Graph
        │
 Path Optimizer
        │
 Interpolation Engine
        │
 Camera Keyframes
```

---

# 9.39 Camera Motion Planner

The planner receives camera targets and creates a motion timeline.

## Responsibilities

* Generate transitions.
* Merge nearby targets.
* Predict future movement.
* Avoid unnecessary motion.
* Produce camera keyframes.

---

## Planner Inputs

| Input           | Source           |
| --------------- | ---------------- |
| Cursor Target   | Cursor Engine    |
| Face Target     | Vision Engine    |
| UI Target       | Object Detection |
| Manual Keyframe | Timeline         |
| AI Suggestion   | Gemini Engine    |

---

## Planner Output

```typescript
interface PlannedCameraTransition {

    from:CameraViewport;

    to:CameraViewport;

    startUs:number;

    endUs:number;

    easing:string;

}
```

---

# 9.40 Transition Graph Engine

Camera movements form a directed graph.

Instead of isolated animations, the engine optimizes connected transitions.

## Transition Graph

```text
Zoom A

 │

Pan B

 │

Zoom C

 │

Hold D
```

Every transition knows previous and next neighbors.

---

## Graph Benefits

* Merge transitions.
* Remove redundant zooms.
* Smooth consecutive pans.
* Avoid oscillation.

---

## Transition Node Contract

```typescript
interface CameraTransitionNode {

    nodeId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    viewport:CameraViewport;

}
```

---

# 9.41 Camera Path Solver

The path solver computes the camera trajectory.

## Solver Inputs

* Current viewport.
* Target viewport.
* Constraints.
* Safe padding.
* Velocity limits.

---

## Solver Pipeline

```text
Start Viewport
      │
Constraint Solver
      │
Path Generator
      │
Interpolated Path
```

---

## Path Output

A continuous curve sampled during playback.

---

## Path Contract

```typescript
interface CameraPath {

    samples:CameraViewport[];

    durationUs:number;

}
```

---

# 9.42 Motion Types

Every transition belongs to one motion type.

| Motion       | Example                 |
| ------------ | ----------------------- |
| Zoom In      | Focus button            |
| Zoom Out     | Reveal UI               |
| Pan Left     | Sidebar navigation      |
| Pan Right    | Inspector panel         |
| Diagonal Pan | Cursor travel           |
| Dolly Zoom   | Future cinematic preset |
| Hold         | Narration               |

---

## Motion Classification Rules

Motion planner chooses type before interpolation.

---

# 9.43 Cinematic Interpolation Library

Interpolation defines camera personality.

## Supported Curves

| Curve             | Usage             |
| ----------------- | ----------------- |
| Linear            | Debug only        |
| Ease In           | Enter zoom        |
| Ease Out          | Exit zoom         |
| Ease In Out       | Default           |
| Cubic Bézier      | Cinematic         |
| Spring            | Cursor follow     |
| Critically Damped | Default smoothing |

---

## Default Curve

All Smart Camera transitions use **EaseInOutCubic** unless overridden.

---

## Curve Contract

```typescript
interface CameraCurve {

    curveId:string;

    duration:number;

}
```

---

# 9.44 Cubic Bézier Engine

Cinematic transitions use Bézier curves.

## Pipeline

```text
Start

Control Point A

Control Point B

End
```

---

## Why Bézier?

* Natural acceleration.
* Smooth deceleration.
* No robotic motion.

---

## Parameters

Future presets expose custom control points.

---

# 9.45 Spring Smoothing Engine

Cursor motion should feel attached by a spring.

## Spring Components

* stiffness
* damping
* mass
* velocity

---

## Spring Pipeline

```text
Target Position
      │
Spring Solver
      │
Smoothed Position
```

---

## Spring Contract

```typescript
interface SpringParameters {

    stiffness:number;

    damping:number;

    mass:number;

}
```

---

## Default Preset

Critically damped spring.

No oscillation after settling.

---

# 9.46 Velocity Constraint Engine

Camera speed must remain comfortable.

## Limits

| Movement      | Max Velocity |
| ------------- | ------------ |
| Cursor Follow | Low          |
| Manual Pan    | Medium       |
| AI Jump       | High         |
| Reveal Zoom   | Medium       |

---

## Velocity Pipeline

```text
Path

Velocity Solver

Clamped Path
```

---

## Velocity Rules

Prevent rapid edge-to-edge camera movement.

---

# 9.47 Acceleration Constraint Engine

Acceleration changes feel more noticeable than speed.

## Constraint Goals

* Prevent sudden starts.
* Prevent abrupt stops.
* Maintain cinematic feel.

---

## Acceleration Contract

```typescript
interface CameraAccelerationConstraint {

    maxAcceleration:number;

}
```

---

## Clamp Strategy

Acceleration smoothed before interpolation.

---

# 9.48 Motion Prediction Engine

Predict likely future cursor destination.

## Inputs

* Cursor velocity.
* Cursor acceleration.
* Cursor direction.
* Click probability.

---

## Prediction Window

Typically a short future window.

---

## Prediction Pipeline

```text
Cursor Samples

Trajectory Predictor

Future Target
```

---

## Benefits

Camera begins moving before click lands.

---

# 9.49 Zoom Hold Engine

Zoom should remain stable after interaction.

## Hold States

* Click Hold.
* Hover Hold.
* Typing Hold.
* AI Hold.

---

## Hold Pipeline

```text
Zoom Trigger

Hold Timer

Release Planner
```

---

## Hold Durations

| Action       | Default Hold           |
| ------------ | ---------------------- |
| Click        | Short hold             |
| Double Click | Longer hold            |
| Typing       | Sustained hold         |
| Hover        | Until movement resumes |

---

# 9.50 Zoom Release Logic

Returning to wide view is gradual.

## Release Pipeline

```text
Hold Ends

Release Curve

Wide Camera
```

---

## Release Rules

Release canceled if new interaction begins.

---

# 9.51 Motion Merge Engine

Nearby transitions should merge.

## Example

Three nearby clicks become one continuous move.

---

## Merge Conditions

* Distance below threshold.
* Time difference below threshold.
* Same subject.

---

## Merge Pipeline

```text
Transition A

Transition B

Merged Transition
```

---

# 9.52 Motion Interruption Engine

Camera may receive a new target before finishing.

## Interruption Modes

| Mode    | Behavior                       |
| ------- | ------------------------------ |
| Replace | New path immediately           |
| Blend   | Continue current then redirect |
| Queue   | Finish current transition      |

---

## Default Strategy

Blend for cursor movement.

Replace for manual edits.

---

## Interruption Contract

```typescript
interface CameraInterruption {

    currentTransition:string;

    nextTransition:string;

    strategy:string;

}
```

---

# 9.53 Camera Jitter Suppression

Small cursor movement shouldn't shake camera.

## Suppression Rules

Ignore movements inside dead zone.

---

## Dead Zone

Camera remains still while cursor moves within configurable radius.

---

## Pipeline

```text
Cursor Motion

Dead Zone Check

Camera Move?
```

---

# 9.54 Edge Resistance Engine

Camera slows near recording edges.

## Purpose

Avoid abrupt stops when cursor reaches screen edge.

---

## Edge Resistance Curve

Velocity gradually approaches zero near boundaries.

---

## Edge Rules

Viewport never clips outside recording.

---

# 9.55 Preview vs Export Interpolation

Preview prioritizes responsiveness.

Export prioritizes perfect accuracy.

## Preview

* Cached interpolation samples.
* Proxy resolution.
* Adaptive sampling.

## Export

* Full precision sampling.
* Master recording.
* Deterministic interpolation.

---

## Shared Timeline Guarantee

Both preview and export read identical camera keyframes.

---

# 9.56 Acceptance Tests

## Motion Tests

* Continuous pan.
* Continuous zoom.
* Bézier interpolation.

## Prediction Tests

* Cursor prediction.
* Click anticipation.
* Dead zone suppression.

## Constraint Tests

* Velocity clamped.
* Acceleration clamped.
* Edge resistance applied.

## Export Tests

* Preview path equals export path.
* Keyframes identical.
* Motion deterministic.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 9.3)

1. Motion planning converts targets into cinematic transitions.
2. Camera paths are continuous curves.
3. Cubic Bézier is the default cinematic interpolation.
4. Spring smoothing follows cursor naturally.
5. Velocity and acceleration are independently constrained.
6. Zoom hold prevents distracting zoom oscillation.
7. Nearby transitions merge when appropriate.
8. Motion interruption follows deterministic strategies.
9. Dead zones suppress cursor jitter.
10. Preview and export interpolate the same timeline data.

# 9.57 AI Subject Tracking Philosophy

Smart Camera should follow **what the viewer should look at**, not simply where the cursor is.

The tracking engine combines deterministic computer vision with AI scene understanding.

## Golden Tracking Rules

1. Subjects persist across frames.
2. Tracking survives cursor disappearance.
3. Multiple detectors may describe the same subject.
4. AI suggests subjects.
5. Deterministic trackers maintain temporal continuity.
6. Manual overrides always win.

---

## Supported Subject Types

| Subject Type  | Source             |
| ------------- | ------------------ |
| Cursor        | Cursor Engine      |
| Face          | MediaPipe / Vision |
| Button        | Gemini + Vision    |
| Text Field    | Vision             |
| Dialog        | Vision             |
| Card / Panel  | Vision             |
| Window        | Browser metadata   |
| Custom Region | User               |

---

# 9.58 Subject Detection Pipeline

Detection is separated into multiple stages.

## Pipeline Overview

```text
VideoFrame
    │
Frame Sampler
    │
Vision Detectors
    │
Candidate Subjects
    │
Subject Fusion Engine
    │
Subject Tracker
    │
Smart Camera
```

No single detector owns the final result.

---

## Detection Frequency

| Detector      | Frequency    |
| ------------- | ------------ |
| Cursor        | Every frame  |
| Face          | 10–20 FPS    |
| UI Detection  | 3–5 FPS      |
| Gemini Vision | Event-driven |
| OCR           | On demand    |

Detectors have different sampling budgets.

---

# 9.59 Subject Candidate Model

Every detector produces candidates.

## Candidate Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectCandidate {

    candidateId:string;

    type:string;

    boundingBox:BoundingBox;

    confidence:number;

    detector:string;

}
```

Candidates are temporary.

---

## Candidate Lifecycle

```text
Detector Output
      │
Candidate Pool
      │
Fusion Engine
      │
Tracked Subject
```

---

# 9.60 Face Tracking Engine

Face tracking is primarily for webcam overlays and talking-head videos.

## Responsibilities

* Detect faces.
* Track identity.
* Smooth bounding boxes.
* Handle temporary disappearance.

---

## Face Detection Pipeline

```text
VideoFrame
     │
MediaPipe Face Detector
     │
Bounding Boxes
     │
Face Tracker
```

---

## Face Contract

```typescript
interface FaceSubject {

    faceId:string;

    boundingBox:BoundingBox;

    landmarks:number[];

    confidence:number;

}
```

---

## Face Rules

* Face IDs persist while visible.
* Confidence decays gradually.
* Camera centers on face, not forehead.

---

# 9.61 Face Landmark Engine

Landmarks stabilize framing.

## Landmark Regions

* eyes
* nose
* mouth
* chin
* ears

---

## Landmark Uses

* face center
* head rotation
* zoom framing
* future portrait effects

---

## Landmark Contract

```typescript
interface FaceLandmark {

    x:number;

    y:number;

    visibility:number;

}
```

---

# 9.62 Face Tracking Persistence

Temporary disappearance shouldn't lose identity.

## Persistence Window

Face remains "tracked" for a short configurable timeout.

---

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Face Missing
     │
Prediction
     │
Search Nearby
     │
Restore Identity
```

---

## Recovery Rules

Do not immediately create a new face ID.

---

# 9.63 UI Element Tracking Engine

UI tracking identifies interface components.

## Supported Components

| Component | Examples         |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| Button    | Save, Publish    |
| Input     | Search box       |
| Sidebar   | VS Code Explorer |
| Dialog    | Settings modal   |
| Toolbar   | Browser toolbar  |
| Card      | Dashboard widget |

---

## Detection Pipeline

```text
VideoFrame
     │
Edge + Layout Detection
     │
UI Candidates
     │
Tracker
```

---

## UI Subject Contract

```typescript
interface UISubject {

    uiId:string;

    role:string;

    boundingBox:BoundingBox;

    confidence:number;

}
```

---

# 9.64 DOM + Vision Fusion

When recording the TryLipi tab, DOM is available.

When recording external tabs, only pixels are available.

## Fusion Strategy

| Recording Target | Detection    |
| ---------------- | ------------ |
| Same Origin      | DOM + Vision |
| External Tab     | Vision only  |
| Entire Screen    | Vision only  |
| Window Capture   | Vision only  |

DOM improves accuracy but is optional.

---

## DOM Metadata

```typescript
interface DOMSubject {

    elementId:string;

    tagName:string;

    boundingBox:BoundingBox;

}
```

---

# 9.65 Multi-Object Tracking Engine

Multiple objects may exist simultaneously.

Example:

* Cursor.
* Button.
* Dialog.
* Avatar.

All tracked independently.

---

## Tracker Topology

```text
Subject Registry
│
├── Cursor
├── Face
├── Button
├── Dialog
└── Custom Region
```

---

## Registry Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectRegistry {

    subjectIds:string[];

    activeSubjects:Map<string,TrackedSubject>;

}
```

---

# 9.66 Identity Assignment Engine

Objects retain identity across frames.

## Identity Inputs

* bounding box overlap
* feature similarity
* detector confidence
* temporal continuity

---

## Matching Pipeline

```text
Frame N Subjects
       │
Frame N+1 Candidates
       │
Identity Matcher
       │
Tracked IDs
```

---

## Identity Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectIdentity {

    subjectId:string;

    persistent:boolean;

}
```

---

# 9.67 Bounding Box Smoothing Engine

Raw detections jitter.

## Smoothing Pipeline

```text
Raw Bounding Boxes
        │
Temporal Filter
        │
Smoothed Bounding Boxes
```

---

## Smoothing Goals

* stable zoom
* stable pan
* stable spotlight

---

## Bounding Box Contract

```typescript
interface SmoothedBoundingBox {

    x:number;

    y:number;

    width:number;

    height:number;

}
```

---

# 9.68 Confidence Engine

Every tracked subject has confidence.

## Confidence Sources

* detector score
* tracking stability
* temporal persistence
* AI agreement

---

## Confidence Categories

| Confidence | Interpretation       |
| ---------- | -------------------- |
| High       | Reliable subject     |
| Medium     | Use cautiously       |
| Low        | Candidate only       |
| Lost       | Remove after timeout |

---

## Confidence Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectConfidence {

    detector:number;

    temporal:number;

    combined:number;

}
```

---

# 9.69 Confidence Smoothing

Confidence should not fluctuate every frame.

## Pipeline

```text
Detector Scores
      │
Moving Average
      │
Confidence Curve
```

---

## Rules

Increase confidence quickly.

Decrease confidence gradually.

---

# 9.70 Occlusion Recovery Engine

Subjects may disappear behind menus.

## Occlusion Types

| Type                 | Example                 |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Temporary UI overlay | Dropdown                |
| Scroll               | Element leaves viewport |
| Window overlap       | Modal                   |
| Cursor hidden        | Pointer hidden          |

---

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Subject Lost
     │
Motion Prediction
     │
Search Window
     │
Recovered
```

---

## Recovery Rules

Reuse identity when possible.

---

# 9.71 Subject Priority Engine

Multiple valid subjects compete for camera attention.

## Priority Levels

| Subject             | Priority |
| ------------------- | -------- |
| Manual Selection    | Highest  |
| Cursor Click Target | High     |
| Active Dialog       | High     |
| Face Speaking       | High     |
| Hovered Button      | Medium   |
| Background UI       | Low      |

---

## Priority Resolver

```text
Subjects
   │
Priority Rules
   │
Winning Subject
```

---

## Priority Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectPriority {

    subjectId:string;

    priority:number;

}
```

---

# 9.72 AI + Vision Fusion Engine

Gemini Vision adds semantic understanding.

Vision provides geometry.

Gemini provides meaning.

## Fusion Pipeline

```text
Vision Subjects
      │
Gemini Suggestions
      │
Fusion Engine
      │
Final Subject
```

---

## Example

Vision detects three cards.

Gemini says:

"Pricing card is being discussed."

Pricing card receives higher priority.

---

## Fusion Contract

```typescript
interface AISubjectSuggestion {

    subjectId:string;

    semanticLabel:string;

    confidence:number;

}
```

---

# 9.73 Subject Persistence Engine

A subject should remain active briefly after disappearing.

## Persistence States

* Active.
* Cooling Down.
* Lost.
* Removed.

---

## State Machine

```text
Active

Cooling

Lost

Removed
```

---

## Persistence Rules

Avoid camera flicker between nearby subjects.

---

# 9.74 Manual Override Engine

Users can manually pin camera targets.

## Override Actions

* Pin subject.
* Ignore AI.
* Replace subject.
* Delete subject.

---

## Override Contract

```typescript
interface ManualCameraOverride {

    subjectId:string;

    enabled:boolean;

}
```

---

## Override Priority

Manual override always beats AI suggestions.

---

# 9.75 Subject Timeline Track

Tracked subjects become timeline events.

## Timeline Metadata

* subject enters.
* subject leaves.
* confidence changes.
* priority changes.

---

## Event Contract

```typescript
interface SubjectTimelineEvent {

    subjectId:string;

    timestampUs:number;

    event:string;

}
```

---

# 9.76 Acceptance Tests

## Face Tests

* Face detected.
* Face identity persists.
* Face recovered after occlusion.

## UI Tests

* Button detected.
* Dialog detected.
* Bounding boxes stabilized.

## Fusion Tests

* Gemini suggestion merged.
* Priority resolved.
* Manual override wins.

## Tracking Tests

* Subject persistence.
* Confidence smoothing.
* Identity continuity.

---

# Canonical Rules (Part 9.4)

1. AI tracking combines deterministic vision with semantic AI.
2. Subjects have persistent identities.
3. Bounding boxes are temporally smoothed.
4. Confidence is combined across detectors.
5. Occlusion recovery preserves identity whenever possible.
6. Subject priority determines camera focus.
7. DOM metadata enhances tracking but is optional.
8. Manual overrides always have highest priority.
9. Subject events live on a timeline track.
10. Smart Camera never follows unstable low-confidence detections.
