# 12.61 Lip Sync Philosophy

The **Lip Sync Engine** aligns spoken audio with visual timeline events at **phoneme-level precision**. Unlike subtitle timing systems that only synchronize text with timestamps, TryLipi synchronizes multiple independent timeline layers simultaneously.

The engine creates a deterministic relationship between:

- Audio waveform.
- Spoken transcript.
- Individual phonemes.
- Visual mouth shapes (visemes).
- Video timeline frames.

This metadata becomes reusable across preview, export, AI dubbing, avatar generation, multilingual voice replacement, and future AI presenter features.

## Golden Lip Sync Principles

1. Audio is always the source of truth.
2. Every word owns one phoneme sequence.
3. Every phoneme maps to one viseme.
4. Alignment uses microsecond timestamps.
5. Alignment survives transcript edits.
6. Preview and export use identical metadata.
7. Drift correction never modifies original audio.

---

# 12.62 Alignment System Architecture

Every recorded voice track generates an independent **Voice Timeline**.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Audio Timeline Track
        │
        ▼
Transcript (Word Timestamps)
        │
        ▼
Phoneme Extraction Engine
        │
        ▼
Viseme Mapping Engine
        │
        ▼
Voice Timeline Builder
        │
        ▼
Playback Renderer / Export Renderer
```

### Major Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Transcript Reader | Reads canonical transcript. |
| Phoneme Extractor | Converts words into phonemes. |
| Viseme Mapper | Converts phonemes into mouth shapes. |
| Alignment Builder | Creates Voice Timeline. |
| Drift Corrector | Detects synchronization drift. |
| Playback Synchronizer | Syncs captions, transcript and waveform. |

---

# 12.63 Voice Timeline Engine

The Voice Timeline stores alignment metadata independently from transcript text.

## Voice Timeline Hierarchy

```text
Voice Timeline
├── Speaker Segments
│   ├── Sentences
│   │   ├── Words
│   │   │   ├── Phonemes
│   │   │   └── Visemes
│   │   └── Confidence
│   └── Metadata
└── Language Information
```

### Voice Timeline Interface

```ts
interface VoiceTimeline {
  timelineId: string;
  version: number;
  language: string;
  segments: VoiceSegment[];
}
```

### Voice Segment Interface

```ts
interface VoiceSegment {
  segmentId: string;
  speakerId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  words: VoiceWord[];
}
```

### Voice Word Interface

```ts
interface VoiceWord {
  word: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  phonemes: VoicePhoneme[];
}
```

### Voice Timeline Rules

- Timeline contains no waveform samples.
- Timeline references transcript words.
- Timeline revisions are immutable.
- Timeline timestamps originate from the Capture Clock.

---

# 12.64 Phoneme Extraction Engine

A phoneme is the smallest distinguishable speech sound.

## Example Word → Phoneme Conversion

| Word | Phoneme Sequence |
|------|------------------|
| Hello | HH AH L OW |
| Camera | K AE M ER AH |
| Creator | K R IY EY T ER |
| TryLipi | T R AY L IH P IY |
| Fitness | F IH T N AH S |

### Extraction Pipeline

```text
Transcript Word
      │
Language Detection
      │
Pronunciation Dictionary
      │
Language Rules
      │
Phoneme Sequence
      │
Timeline Alignment
```

### Phoneme Interface

```ts
interface VoicePhoneme {
  phoneme: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

### Supported Languages

| Language | Status |
|----------|--------|
| English | IPA Dictionary |
| Hindi | Native Phoneme Rules |
| Telugu | Native Phoneme Rules |
| Tamil | Planned |
| Kannada | Planned |
| Malayalam | Planned |

### Processing Rules

- English uses IPA dictionaries.
- Indian languages use language-specific phoneme rules.
- Mixed-language words preserve pronunciation source language.
- Proper nouns retain original pronunciation.

---

# 12.65 Viseme Mapping Engine

A viseme represents a visible mouth shape.

Different phonemes often produce identical mouth movements.

### Mapping Pipeline

```text
Phoneme Timeline
      │
Viseme Lookup Table
      │
Viseme Timeline
      │
Animation Renderer
```

### Canonical Viseme Set

| Viseme | Mouth Shape |
|--------|-------------|
| V0 | Silence |
| V1 | Closed Lips |
| V2 | Slightly Open |
| V3 | Wide Open |
| V4 | Rounded Lips |
| V5 | Teeth Touch Lower Lip |
| V6 | Tongue Behind Teeth |
| V7 | Smile Shape |

### Example Phoneme → Viseme Mapping

| Phoneme | Viseme |
|----------|--------|
| P | V1 |
| B | V1 |
| M | V1 |
| F | V5 |
| V | V5 |
| AH | V3 |
| EE | V7 |
| O | V4 |
| W | V4 |

### Viseme Interface

```ts
interface VisemeFrame {
  viseme: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

### Viseme Rules

- One phoneme maps to exactly one viseme.
- Silence maps to V0.
- Consecutive identical visemes merge during rendering.
- Viseme duration equals phoneme duration.

---

# 12.66 Word-to-Phoneme Alignment

Each word duration is distributed across phonemes to produce frame-accurate mouth animation.

### Alignment Pipeline

```text
Word Timestamp
      │
Duration Estimator
      │
Phoneme Duration Calculator
      │
Phoneme Timeline
```

### Example Alignment

| Word | Total Duration | Phoneme Durations |
|------|----------------|-------------------|
| Hello | 480 ms | HH 90 / AH 120 / L 90 / OW 180 |
| Camera | 600 ms | K 80 / AE 140 / M 120 / ER 120 / AH 140 |

### Alignment Interface

```ts
interface PhonemeAlignment {
  phoneme: string;
  durationUs: number;
}
```

### Alignment Rules

- Total phoneme duration equals word duration.
- First phoneme starts at word start timestamp.
- Final phoneme ends at word end timestamp.
- No gaps exist between phonemes inside a word.

---

# 12.67 Caption-to-Audio Synchronization

Captions are synchronized directly from transcript timestamps.

### Synchronization Pipeline

```text
Transcript Words
      │
Sentence Builder
      │
Caption Segment Builder
      │
Caption Timeline
```

### Caption Timeline Interface

```ts
interface CaptionTimelineSegment {
  captionId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  words: string[];
}
```

### Caption Generation Rules

- Caption starts at first spoken word.
- Caption ends at last spoken word.
- Reading speed is configurable.
- Maximum characters per line is configurable.
- Sentence boundaries prefer natural pauses.

### Default Reading Rules

| Parameter | Default |
|-----------|---------|
| Words Per Minute | 160 |
| Max Characters / Line | 36 |
| Max Lines | 2 |
| Minimum Caption Duration | 700 ms |

---

**End of Part 12.4A**

Next continuation: **12.4B — Waveform Alignment, Drift Correction, Playback Synchronization & AI Dubbing Timeline Preparation**.

# 12.68 Waveform Alignment Engine

The **Waveform Alignment Engine** synchronizes spoken words with waveform peaks so that every caption, transcript word, and timeline cursor aligns perfectly with visible audio peaks.

This is the engine that powers precise subtitle editing, waveform snapping, AI silence removal, and word-level trimming.

## Responsibilities

- Associate waveform peaks with spoken words.
- Snap playhead to spoken words.
- Highlight waveform during playback.
- Enable word-level trimming.
- Support caption waveform preview.

---

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
PCM Samples
     │
Waveform Peak Generator
     │
Peak Timeline
     │
Word Timestamp Association
     │
Waveform Alignment Map
```

---

## Waveform Layers

| Layer | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| PCM Samples | Source audio samples. |
| Peak Cache | Visual waveform. |
| Word Timeline | Transcript timestamps. |
| Alignment Map | Peak-to-word relationship. |

---

## Alignment Interface

```ts
interface WaveformAlignment {
  wordId: string;
  peakIndex: number;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

---

## Alignment Rules

- Every word references waveform peaks.
- Waveform cache remains immutable.
- Alignment metadata can be regenerated.

---

# 12.69 Timeline Drift Correction Engine

Long recordings may accumulate synchronization drift because browser playback clocks and capture clocks are independent.

The Drift Correction Engine continuously validates synchronization without modifying recorded audio.

## Drift Sources

| Source | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Playback Clock | Browser playback latency. |
| Sample Clock | Audio sample accumulation. |
| Rendering Clock | Video rendering delay. |
| Caption Timeline | Caption cursor delay. |

---

## Drift Detection Pipeline

```text
Render Clock
     │
Transcript Timestamp
     │
Audio Timestamp
     │
Drift Calculator
     │
Correction Map
```

---

## Drift Formula

```text
driftUs = transcriptTimestampUs - audioTimestampUs
```

---

## Drift Thresholds

| Drift | Action |
|-------|--------|
| 0–500 µs | Ignore |
| 500–2,000 µs | Smooth correction |
| Above 2,000 µs | Segment re-alignment |

---

## Drift Interface

```ts
interface DriftCorrection {
  segmentId: string;
  offsetUs: number;
  reason: string;
}
```

---

## Correction Strategy

1. Detect drift every playback frame.
2. Build correction map.
3. Smoothly interpolate timestamps.
4. Preserve audio timing.
5. Preserve caption timing.

---

## Rules

- Drift correction never edits audio samples.
- Drift correction edits only playback metadata.
- Export uses corrected timeline metadata.

---

# 12.70 Playback Synchronization Engine

Playback synchronization keeps every editor component perfectly aligned.

## Playback Components

| Component | Synchronization Source |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Video Frame | Render Clock |
| Audio Sample | Audio Clock |
| Transcript Cursor | Voice Timeline |
| Caption Cursor | Caption Timeline |
| Waveform Cursor | Waveform Alignment |

---

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
Render Clock
     │
 ┌───┼──────────────┬─────────────┐
 ▼   ▼              ▼             ▼
Video Audio      Transcript     Caption
Frame Cursor      Cursor         Cursor
                  │
                  ▼
             Waveform Cursor
```

---

## Playback State Interface

```ts
interface PlaybackSyncState {
  timestampUs: number;
  activeWordId: string;
  activeCaptionId: string;
  activeSpeakerId: string;
}
```

---

## Playback Responsibilities

- Highlight active word.
- Highlight active sentence.
- Animate waveform cursor.
- Scroll transcript automatically.
- Animate karaoke captions.

---

## Synchronization Rules

- All UI components follow Render Clock.
- No component owns independent playback time.
- Seeking updates every synchronization layer.

---

# 12.71 Karaoke Word Highlight Engine

TryLipi supports karaoke-style captions where words highlight while being spoken.

## Pipeline

```text
Word Timeline
     │
Playback Timestamp
     │
Word Highlight Engine
     │
Caption Renderer
```

---

## Highlight Modes

| Mode | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Word | Current word highlighted. |
| Progressive | Text fills progressively. |
| Bounce | Active word scales slightly. |
| Glow | Active word glows. |
| Underline | Animated underline. |

---

## Highlight Interface

```ts
interface KaraokeWordState {
  wordId: string;
  progress: number;
  active: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

- Highlight progress derives from word timestamps.
- Animation is deterministic.

---

# 12.72 AI Dubbing Timeline Preparation

Dubbing requires preserving semantic timing across different languages.

## Dubbing Preparation Pipeline

```text
Source Transcript
      │
Sentence Groups
      │
Translation
      │
Target Transcript
      │
Alignment Preparation
```

---

## Metadata Preserved

| Metadata | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Speaker ID | Voice ownership. |
| Start Timestamp | Alignment. |
| End Timestamp | Alignment. |
| Emotion Placeholder | Future voice synthesis. |
| Language | Translation context. |

---

## Dubbing Segment Interface

```ts
interface DubbingSegment {
  sourceSegmentId: string;
  sourceLanguage: string;
  targetLanguage: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

---

## Dubbing Rules

- Original timeline preserved.
- Translation creates new timeline.
- Original transcript never changes.

---

# 12.73 Voice Stretch & Compression Preparation

Translated speech may be longer or shorter than original speech.

This engine prepares timing metadata for future AI voice synthesis.

## Timing Cases

| Translation | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| Shorter | Stretch voice naturally. |
| Longer | Compress pauses first. |
| Much Longer | Split sentence intelligently. |

---

## Timing Strategy

```text
Translated Sentence
      │
Duration Comparison
      │
Timing Optimizer
      │
Target Voice Timeline
```

---

## Timing Interface

```ts
interface DubbingTimingAdjustment {
  originalDurationUs: number;
  targetDurationUs: number;
  stretchRatio: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

- Never change semantic sentence order.
- Prefer silence compression over speech compression.

---

# 12.74 Timeline Alignment Editing Model

Users can manually adjust alignment when required.

## Editable Objects

- Word timing.
- Caption timing.
- Speaker boundaries.
- Sentence boundaries.
- Viseme offsets.

---

## Editing Pipeline

```text
Timeline Selection
      │
Drag / Keyboard Offset
      │
Alignment Edit Layer
      │
Alignment Revision
```

---

## Editing Interface

```ts
interface TimelineAlignmentEdit {
  targetId: string;
  offsetUs: number;
  operation: "move" | "trim" | "split" | "merge";
}
```

---

## Editing Rules

- Offset edits metadata only.
- Audio waveform remains unchanged.
- Transcript text remains unchanged.

---

# 12.75 Alignment Revision Engine

Every alignment edit creates an immutable revision.

## Revision Pipeline

```text
Voice Timeline
      │
Alignment Edit
      │
Revision Builder
      │
Immutable Revision
```

---

## Revision Interface

```ts
interface AlignmentRevision {
  revisionId: string;
  timelineId: string;
  createdAt: number;
  author: "user" | "ai";
}
```

---

## Revision Rules

- Unlimited revisions.
- Undo/Redo supported.
- Export uses selected revision.

---

# 12.76 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes lip-sync diagnostics.

## Metrics

- Active phoneme.
- Active viseme.
- Word latency.
- Drift amount.
- Playback latency.
- Alignment revisions.
- Caption synchronization state.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface LipSyncDiagnostics {
  driftUs: number;
  activePhoneme: string;
  activeViseme: string;
  playbackLatencyMs: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Drift High | Timeline exceeds threshold. |
| Missing Phoneme | Unknown pronunciation. |
| Missing Viseme | Unsupported mapping. |
| Caption Drift | Caption differs from transcript timing. |

---

# 12.77 Acceptance Tests

## Waveform Tests

- Waveform peaks align with spoken words.
- Seeking updates waveform cursor instantly.
- Zoom maintains alignment.

## Lip Sync Tests

- Every word owns phonemes.
- Every phoneme maps to visemes.
- Viseme timing equals phoneme timing.

## Playback Tests

- Transcript cursor matches playback.
- Caption cursor matches playback.
- Karaoke highlighting matches spoken words.

## Drift Tests

- Long recordings remain synchronized.
- Drift correction preserves audio timing.

## Editing Tests

- Alignment edits update playback.
- Undo/Redo restores revisions.
- Audio remains unchanged.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 12.4B)

1. Waveform alignment derives from PCM peaks.
2. Playback synchronization follows the Render Clock.
3. Drift correction never edits audio samples.
4. Karaoke highlighting derives from word timestamps.
5. AI dubbing creates a new voice timeline.
6. Translation timing preserves semantic sentence order.
7. Alignment edits modify metadata only.
8. Every alignment edit creates an immutable revision.
9. Preview and export use identical alignment metadata.
10. Voice Timeline remains independent from Transcript Timeline.

---

# 14.01 AI Editing Philosophy

The **AI Editing Engine** is the decision-making brain of TryLipi.

Unlike traditional editors that wait for manual user actions, TryLipi continuously understands the video and produces suggested edits, automation actions, highlights, zooms, captions, B-roll opportunities, and viral clips.

The AI engine **never edits the source timeline directly**. Instead, it creates an editable graph of AI-generated actions.

---

## Golden AI Editing Principles

1. AI suggestions are always reversible.
2. Original media is immutable.
3. AI operates on metadata layers.
4. AI edits produce timeline actions, not rendered pixels.
5. Every AI action has confidence metadata.
6. AI actions can be accepted, rejected, or modified.
7. AI processing is deterministic whenever possible.

---

## Responsibilities

The AI Editing Engine owns:

- Video understanding.
- Audio understanding.
- Transcript understanding.
- Scene understanding.
- Cursor understanding.
- Face understanding.
- Automation workflows.
- AI edit suggestions.

---

# 14.02 AI Editing Engine Overview

Every imported project automatically builds an AI understanding graph.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Video + Audio + Transcript
            │
            ▼
Feature Extraction Pipeline
            │
            ▼
AI Context Store
            │
            ▼
AI Orchestration Engine
            │
 ┌──────────┼──────────┐
 ▼          ▼          ▼
Scene AI   Audio AI   Visual AI
 └──────────┼──────────┘
            ▼
AI Edit Graph
            │
            ▼
Automation Engine
            │
            ▼
Timeline Suggestions
```

---

## Core AI Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Feature Extractor | Generate AI-ready metadata. |
| Context Store | Store extracted AI context. |
| Orchestrator | Coordinate AI jobs. |
| Scene Engine | Detect scenes. |
| Visual Engine | Detect faces, cursor, objects. |
| Audio Engine | Detect silence, emotion, speech. |
| Automation Engine | Produce AI edits. |

---

# 14.03 AI Orchestration Layer

The orchestration layer coordinates dozens of AI jobs without blocking editing.

## Responsibilities

- Job scheduling.
- Dependency resolution.
- Retry management.
- Cache management.
- Parallel execution.
- Priority scheduling.

---

## Orchestration Pipeline

```text
Project Imported
       │
       ▼
Job Planner
       │
       ▼
Priority Queue
       │
 ┌─────┼──────────┐
 ▼     ▼          ▼
Audio Visual Transcript
AI     AI      AI
 └─────┼──────────┘
       ▼
Context Store
```

---

## Job Priorities

| Priority | Jobs |
|----------|------|
| Critical | Transcript generation |
| High | Silence detection |
| High | Scene detection |
| Medium | Cursor analysis |
| Medium | Face tracking |
| Low | Thumbnail suggestions |
| Background | Viral clip analysis |

---

## Orchestrator Interface

```ts
interface AIJob {
  jobId: string;
  type: AIJobType;
  priority: number;
  status: AIJobStatus;
}
```

---

## Rules

- Critical jobs execute first.
- Independent jobs execute in parallel.
- Failed jobs retry independently.

---

# 14.04 AI Processing Graph

Instead of a linear pipeline, AI processing is represented as a graph.

## Why a Graph?

Different AI systems reuse outputs from previous systems.

Example:

- Transcript powers captions.
- Transcript powers silence removal.
- Transcript powers hook detection.
- Scene detection powers B-roll insertion.

---

## Processing Graph

```text
Transcript
   │
   ├──────────────┐
   ▼              ▼
Captions      Silence Detection
                   │
                   ▼
             Jump Cut Suggestions

Video Frames
   │
   ├───────────┐
   ▼           ▼
Faces       Objects
   │           │
   └────┬──────┘
        ▼
    Smart Zoom
```

---

## Graph Interface

```ts
interface AIProcessingNode {
  nodeId: string;
  dependencies: string[];
  outputs: string[];
}
```

---

## Rules

Nodes execute only after dependencies complete.

---

# 14.05 AI Job Scheduler

The scheduler manages AI execution across CPU, GPU, WASM workers, and cloud APIs.

## Scheduling Strategy

| Worker Type | Jobs |
|-------------|------|
| Web Worker | Scene detection |
| Audio Worker | Silence detection |
| WASM Worker | RNNoise, FFT |
| GPU Worker | Vision preprocessing |
| Cloud Queue | Gemini analysis |

---

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text
AI Jobs
   │
Priority Queue
   │
Worker Dispatcher
   │
Available Workers
```

---

## Scheduler Interface

```ts
interface AIWorkerTask {
  taskId: string;
  worker: "cpu" | "gpu" | "wasm" | "cloud";
}
```

---

## Rules

- CPU-intensive jobs never block UI.
- GPU jobs share rendering resources safely.
- Cloud jobs execute asynchronously.

---

# 14.06 AI Feature Extraction Pipeline

Every imported project generates reusable AI features.

## Feature Categories

| Feature | Source |
|---------|--------|
| Transcript | Audio |
| Speaker Timeline | Audio |
| Waveform Peaks | Audio |
| Scene Cuts | Video |
| Face Timeline | Video |
| Cursor Timeline | Screen Recording |
| Object Timeline | Vision AI |

```text
      │
Frame Decoder
      │
Audio Decoder
      │
Feature Extractors
      │
Feature Cache
```


---

---

```text
├── Scene

│   ├── Faces
```

Scene Graph becomes the foundation for:

- Smart Zoom.
- AI B-roll.
- Shorts generation.
- Thumbnail suggestions.
- Topic chapters.

---

---

# 14.08 Edit Graph Architecture

AI never edits the timeline directly.

Instead, AI produces **Edit Nodes**.

---

---

| Podcast | Speaker captions |
| Fitness Reel | CTA zooms + captions |
| Product Review | B-roll + highlights |

---

---

# 14.10 AI Context Store

The Context Store is the central memory layer for AI.

- Transcript.
- Faces.
- Cursor.
- Objects.
- Motion.
- Emotion.
- Scenes.

- Accepted AI edits.


```ts
  visionContext: object;

}
```

---

---

# 14.11 AI Event Bus

Every AI subsystem communicates through an event bus.

```text
      │
      ▼

      │
      ├── Zoom Engine
```

---

# 14.12 AI Pipeline Lifecycle

Every AI job follows one lifecycle.

## Lifecycle

```text
Queued
   │
Running
   │
Completed
   │
Cached
```

---

## Lifecycle Interface

```ts
interface AIJobLifecycle {
  status: "queued" | "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cached";
}
```

---

## Retry Rules

- Retry failed cloud jobs.
- Retry failed worker jobs independently.
- Never restart completed jobs.

---

# 14.13 Performance Strategy

The AI engine must remain responsive while editing.

## Performance Budget

| Component | Target |
|----------|--------|
| Transcript Extraction | Background |
| Scene Detection | Background |
| Cursor Detection | Background |
| Face Detection | Background |
| Silence Detection | Under 2× realtime |
| UI Latency | Under 16 ms |

---

## Scheduling Rules

- Editing always has priority.
- AI pauses during heavy exports.
- Cached features prevent recomputation.

---

# 14.14 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes AI internals.

- Running AI jobs.
- Cached jobs.
- Worker utilization.
- GPU utilization.
- Context cache size.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface AIEngineDiagnostics {
  runningJobs: number;
  cachedJobs: number;
  workerUtilization: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Worker Timeout | Worker exceeded timeout. |
| Cloud Retry | Cloud job retried. |
| Cache Miss | Feature missing from cache. |
| Dependency Failed | Required AI node failed. |

---

# 14.15 Acceptance Tests

## Orchestration Tests

- Independent jobs execute in parallel.
- Dependencies respected.
- Failed jobs retry individually.

## Graph Tests

- Scene Graph builds correctly.
- Edit Graph produces reversible edits.
- Automation Graph executes sequentially.

## Context Tests

- Transcript cached.
- Faces cached.
- Objects cached.
- Context updates after edits.

## Event Tests

- Scene events trigger zoom engine.
- Transcript events trigger caption engine.
- Audio events trigger silence detection.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 14.1)

1. AI never edits the timeline directly.
2. Every AI edit is represented as an Edit Node.
3. AI jobs execute through the orchestration layer.
4. Feature extraction happens once and is cached.
5. Scene Graph is the semantic representation of the video.
6. Automation Graph is user-editable.
7. AI Context Store is the shared memory layer.
8. AI Event Bus connects all AI subsystems.
9. Critical AI jobs execute before background jobs.
10. Every AI action includes confidence metadata.

---

# 14.21 Silence Removal Philosophy

Silence removal is one of the highest-impact AI editing features in TryLipi.

Instead of removing every silent region, TryLipi understands **speech rhythm**, **sentence boundaries**, and **breathing pauses** to produce natural edits.

## Editing Goals

- Remove unnecessary silence.
- Preserve conversational pauses.
- Preserve dramatic pauses.
- Preserve breathing where appropriate.
- Never cut words.

---

## Golden Smart Trimming Principles

1. Speech is never cut mid-word.
2. Sentence boundaries have higher priority than silence.
3. Natural breathing pauses are preserved when needed.
4. Every trim suggestion is reversible.
5. Jump cuts are metadata edits, not destructive edits.
6. Silence thresholds are configurable.
7. AI confidence accompanies every trim suggestion.

---

# 14.22 Smart Trimming Architecture

The Smart Trimming Engine combines waveform analysis and transcript understanding.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Audio Track
      │
      ▼
Waveform Analysis
      │
      ▼
Speech Activity Detection
      │
      ▼
Pause Classification
      │
      ▼
Trim Suggestion Engine
      │
      ▼
Jump Cut Graph
      │
      ▼
Timeline Suggestions
```

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Waveform Analyzer | Detect low-energy regions. |
| Speech Activity Detector | Detect speaking windows. |
| Pause Classifier | Classify silence type. |
| Filler Detector | Detect filler words. |
| Jump Cut Builder | Create trim actions. |
| Ripple Editor | Maintain timeline continuity. |

---

# 14.23 Audio Silence Detection Engine

Silence detection operates directly on PCM samples.

## Detection Pipeline

```text
PCM Samples
      │
Frame Energy
      │
RMS Calculation
      │
Silence Threshold
      │
Silence Timeline
```

---

## Energy Calculation

Each audio frame computes:

- RMS energy.
- Peak amplitude.
- Zero-crossing rate.

---

## Silence Threshold Defaults

| Parameter | Default |
|-----------|---------|
| Frame Size | 20 ms |
| RMS Threshold | -42 dB |
| Minimum Silence | 200 ms |
| Merge Gap | 120 ms |

---

## Silence Segment Interface

```ts
interface SilenceSegment {
  segmentId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  averageDb: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

- Silence detection runs before transcript analysis.
- Silence metadata is cached.

---

# 14.24 Speech Activity Timeline

Speech Activity Detection (VAD) converts audio into speaking intervals.

## Timeline Example

```text
Time →
██████░░░░████████░░███████░░░░░
Speech Silence Speech Silence Speech Silence
```

---

## Timeline Interface

```ts
interface SpeechActivitySegment {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Detection Sources

| Signal | Usage |
|--------|------|
| Energy | Voice detection |
| Spectral Features | Speech probability |
| Transcript Alignment | Validation |
| VAD Confidence | Final score |

---

## Rules

Speech activity timeline becomes the foundation for jump cuts.

---

# 14.25 Pause Classification Engine

Not all silence is removable.

The Pause Classification Engine labels pauses by intent.

## Pause Categories

| Pause Type | Remove? |
|------------|----------|
| Natural Breath | Usually No |
| Thinking Pause | Optional |
| Sentence Pause | Usually Preserve |
| Dead Air | Yes |
| Intro Delay | Yes |
| Outro Delay | Yes |

---

## Classification Pipeline

```text
Silence Timeline
      │
Transcript Context
      │
Duration Analysis
      │
Pause Classifier
```

---

## Pause Interface

```ts
interface PauseClassification {
  pauseId: string;
  type: "breath" | "thinking" | "sentence" | "deadAir";
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Duration Heuristics

| Duration | Classification |
|----------|----------------|
| Under 120 ms | Ignore |
| 120–350 ms | Breath Candidate |
| 350–700 ms | Thinking Pause |
| 700–1500 ms | Sentence Pause |
| Above 1500 ms | Dead Air Candidate |

---

## Rules

Classification uses transcript punctuation to refine decisions.

---

# 14.26 Breathing Detection Engine

Breathing pauses should not always be removed.

## Detection Pipeline

```text
PCM Audio
      │
Spectral Shape
      │
Breath Detector
      │
Breath Timeline
```

---

## Breath Characteristics

- Broadband noise.
- Short inhale/exhale.
- Low speech probability.

---

## Breath Interface

```ts
interface BreathSegment {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  intensity: number;
}
```

---

## Breath Policies

| Mode | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| Preserve | Leave breaths untouched. |
| Reduce | Shorten breaths. |
| Remove | Remove completely. |

---

## Rules

Breaths near sentence endings are preserved by default.

---

# 14.27 Filler Word Detection Engine

The filler detector combines transcript analysis with speech confidence.

## Supported Fillers

### English

- um
- uh
- like
- actually
- basically
- literally
- you know

### Hindi / Hinglish

- matlab
- toh
- haan...
- achha...
- woh...
- dekho...

### Telugu

- ante
- mari
- adhi...
- em...

---

## Detection Pipeline

```text
Transcript
      │
Tokenization
      │
Filler Dictionary
      │
Context Filter
      │
Filler Timeline
```

---

## Filler Interface

```ts
interface FillerWord {
  word: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Context Rules

- "Like" is not removed when used as a verb.
- "Actually" is preserved inside meaningful sentences if configured.

---

# 14.28 Sentence-Aware Jump Cut Engine

Jump cuts remove silence **between semantic units**.

## Jump Cut Pipeline

```text
Speech Timeline
      │
Pause Classification
      │
Sentence Boundary Detection
      │
Jump Cut Suggestions
```

---

## Example

**Original**

```text
Hello everyone...
          (1.6 sec pause)

Welcome back.
```

**Suggestion**

```text
Hello everyone.
Welcome back.
```

---

## Jump Cut Interface

```ts
interface JumpCutSuggestion {
  cutId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  reason: string;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Jump Cut Reasons

| Reason | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Dead Air | Remove silence. |
| Breath | Optional trim. |
| Thinking Pause | Optional trim. |
| Intro Delay | Remove beginning silence. |
| Outro Delay | Remove ending silence. |

---

## Rules

Jump cuts never overlap transcript words.

---

# 14.29 Dead Air Detection Engine

Dead air refers to silence with no conversational value.

## Detection Signals

- Long silence.
- No speech probability.
- No transcript words.
- No significant waveform peaks.

---

## Detection Pipeline

```text
Silence Timeline
      │
Speech Probability
      │
Transcript Check
      │
Dead Air Detector
```

---

## Dead Air Interface

```ts
interface DeadAirRegion {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  durationUs: number;
}
```

---

## Default Rules

| Region | Default Action |
|--------|----------------|
| Intro Silence | Remove |
| Outro Silence | Remove |
| Mid Dead Air | Suggest Removal |
| Music Only | Preserve |

---

# 14.30 Jump Cut Graph

All trim suggestions become graph nodes.

## Jump Cut Graph

```text
Timeline
   │
AI Jump Cut Graph
├── Cut #1
├── Cut #2
├── Cut #3
└── Cut #4
```

---

## Graph Interface

```ts
interface JumpCutNode {
  cutId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  accepted: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

Rejected cuts remain in graph history.

---

# 14.31 AI Trim Suggestions

The editor presents non-destructive trim recommendations.

## Suggestion Types

| Suggestion | Default |
|-----------|---------|
| Remove Intro Silence | Enabled |
| Remove Outro Silence | Enabled |
| Remove Dead Air | Enabled |
| Remove Filler Word | Optional |
| Reduce Breath | Optional |

---

## Suggestion Interface

```ts
interface AITrimSuggestion {
  suggestionId: string;
  confidence: number;
  previewDurationSavedUs: number;
}
```

---

## UI Behaviour

Each suggestion shows:

- Duration saved.
- Confidence.
- Preview button.
- Accept / Reject.

---

# 14.32 Batch Trimming Workflow

Users can apply multiple trim suggestions simultaneously.

## Workflow

```text
AI Suggestions
      │
Selection
      │
Batch Apply
      │
Jump Cut Graph
      │
Ripple Timeline
```

---

## Batch Interface

```ts
interface BatchTrimOperation {
  suggestionIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Rules

Batch operations create one undo checkpoint.

---

# 14.33 Smart Ripple Editing

Ripple editing automatically closes gaps created by trims.

## Ripple Pipeline

```text
Jump Cut Applied
      │
Gap Removed
      │
Timeline Shift
      │
Audio + Video + Captions Shift
```

---

## Ripple Interface

```ts
interface RippleOperation {
  offsetUs: number;
}
```

---

## Ripple Rules

- Preserve synchronization.
- Preserve caption timing.
- Preserve markers.
- Preserve transitions.

---

# 14.34 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes trimming internals.

## Metrics

- Silence segments detected.
- Dead air duration.
- Breaths detected.
- Filler words detected.
- Suggested cuts.
- Accepted cuts.
- Time saved.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface SmartTrimDiagnostics {
  silenceCount: number;
  deadAirDurationUs: number;
  fillerWords: number;
  acceptedCuts: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Word Boundary Conflict | Suggested cut intersects speech. |
| Caption Drift | Caption timing mismatch after ripple. |
| Excessive Trim | More than configured percentage removed. |

---

# 14.35 Acceptance Tests

## Silence Detection Tests

- Detect intro silence.
- Detect outro silence.
- Detect mid-video silence.
- Ignore low-volume speech.

## Breath Tests

- Preserve natural breaths.
- Remove optional breaths.
- Detect inhale/exhale correctly.

## Filler Detection Tests

- Detect "um", "uh", "matlab", "ante".
- Preserve meaningful "like".

## Jump Cut Tests

- Never cut inside a word.
- Preserve sentence timing.
- Ripple maintains synchronization.

## Batch Editing Tests

- Batch trims create one undo checkpoint.
- Accept/reject updates Jump Cut Graph.
- Timeline remains synchronized.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 14.2)

1. Silence detection operates on PCM samples.
2. Speech Activity Detection is the foundation of trimming.
3. Pause classification distinguishes removable silence from natural pauses.
4. Breathing detection is configurable per workflow.
5. Filler detection combines transcript and audio confidence.
6. Jump cuts are represented as graph nodes, not destructive edits.
7. Dead air removal preserves music-only sections unless configured otherwise.
8. Ripple editing shifts every dependent timeline layer together.
9. Every trim suggestion is reversible.
10. Timeline synchronization is preserved after every accepted cut.

---

- Shot boundary detection.
- Face detection timeline.
- Cursor detection and interaction understanding.
- Gesture detection.
- Object detection.

- UI element understanding.
- Topic segmentation and semantic scene graph.

# 14.41 Semantic Video Understanding Philosophy

The **Semantic Video Understanding Engine** transforms raw video frames into structured knowledge that AI editing workflows can use.

Instead of seeing pixels, TryLipi understands:

- Scenes.
- Camera cuts.
- Faces.
- Cursor movement.
- Buttons.
- Windows.
- Code editors.
- Charts.
- Products.
- Gestures.
- Spoken topics.

This understanding powers intelligent editing instead of rule-based editing.

---

## Golden Semantic Principles

1. Pixels are never edited directly.
2. AI extracts reusable semantic metadata.
3. Every semantic object belongs to a timeline.
4. Semantic metadata is cached.
5. Multiple AI systems reuse the same metadata.
6. Video understanding is deterministic whenever possible.
7. Timeline timestamps remain frame accurate.

---

## Responsibilities

Semantic Video AI owns:

- Shot detection.
- Scene detection.
- Cursor understanding.
- Face detection.
- Object detection.
- OCR.
- Gesture detection.
- Topic segmentation.

---

# 14.42 Scene Understanding Architecture

Scene understanding combines visual AI, transcript AI, and motion AI.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Video Frames
      │
Frame Decoder
      │
Vision Feature Extraction
      │
Semantic Feature Store
      │
Scene Understanding Engine
      │
Scene Graph Builder
      │
AI Automation Engine
```

---

## AI Feature Sources

| Source | Semantic Output |
|--------|-----------------|
| Video Frames | Objects, faces, gestures |
| Audio | Speech timeline |
| Transcript | Topics |
| Cursor | UI interaction timeline |
| Motion | Camera movement |

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Vision Extractor | Extract frame embeddings. |
| Scene Detector | Detect visual scenes. |
| Cursor Engine | Understand mouse interaction. |
| OCR Engine | Read screen text. |
| Topic Engine | Understand spoken topics. |
| Scene Graph Builder | Build semantic graph. |

---

# 14.43 Shot Boundary Detection Engine

A **shot** is a continuous camera segment.

The Shot Boundary Engine identifies where visual continuity changes.

```text

      │

      │

      │
Cut Detector
      │
Shot Timeline
```

## Supported Shot Types

| Shot Type | Detection |
|-----------|-----------|
| Hard Cut | Yes |
| Fade In | Yes |
| Fade Out | Yes |
| Cross Fade | Yes |
| Flash Transition | Yes |
| Slide Transition | Yes |
| Zoom Transition | Yes |

## Shot Interface

```ts
interface ShotSegment {
  shotId: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  transitionType: string;
}
```

---

## Detection Signals

- Histogram difference.
- Structural similarity.
- Optical flow discontinuity.
- Brightness jump.
- Motion discontinuity.

---

## Rules

- Shots never overlap.
- Timeline stores transition metadata separately.

---

The Scene Graph is immutable after feature extraction.

# 14.55 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes semantic understanding metrics.

---

## Metrics

- Scenes detected.
- Shots detected.
- Faces tracked.
- Cursor interactions.
- OCR regions.
- Objects detected.
- Topics generated.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface SemanticDiagnostics {
  scenes: number;
  shots: number;
  faces: number;
  cursorEvents: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| OCR Failure | Text unreadable. |
| Cursor Lost | Cursor tracking interrupted. |
| Face Lost | Face tracker confidence dropped. |
| Topic Ambiguous | Low topic confidence. |

---

# 14.56 Acceptance Tests

## Scene Detection Tests

- Detect hard cuts.
- Detect fades.
- Detect slide changes.
- Detect browser tab switches.

## Face Tests

- Stable face IDs.
- Re-identify after occlusion.
- Timeline remains continuous.

## Cursor Tests

- Detect click positions.
- Detect scrolling.
- Detect drag operations.
- Detect text selection.

## OCR Tests

- Extract visible headings.
- Detect code blocks.
- Preserve timestamps.

## Topic Tests

- Generate semantic chapters.
- Preserve chapter ordering.
- Handle multilingual transcripts.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 14.3)

1. Scene detection combines transcript, vision, and motion signals.
2. Shots and scenes are different timeline entities.
3. Face IDs remain stable throughout the project.
4. Cursor tracking is independent from frame rate.
5. UI elements become semantic anchors for automation.
6. OCR text becomes searchable timeline metadata.
7. Object tracking produces reusable timeline entities.
8. Gestures act as automation triggers.
9. Motion analysis feeds Smart Zoom and Highlight engines.
10. Semantic Scene Graph is the shared metadata layer reused by all downstream AI systems.

---

# 14.61 Viral Clip Philosophy

The Viral Clip Engine identifies the **most valuable moments** inside long-form videos.

Instead of clipping based only on transcript keywords, TryLipi combines audio, visual, transcript, emotion, motion, and interaction signals into one highlight score.

This enables automatic generation of:

- Shorts
- Instagram Reels
- TikTok clips
- YouTube Chapters
- Hook previews
- Social teasers

---

## Golden Viral Detection Principles

1. Highlights are semantic, not purely visual.
2. Every highlight has a confidence score.
3. Highlights remain editable.
4. AI suggests multiple clips instead of one.
5. Clips preserve sentence boundaries whenever possible.
6. Original timeline is never modified.
7. Every clip references original timeline timestamps.

---

## Responsibilities

The Highlight Engine owns:

- Hook detection.
- Viral scoring.
- CTA detection.
- Emotional peaks.
- Laughter detection.
- Applause detection.
- Topic highlights.
- Chapter suggestions.

---

# 14.62 Highlight Detection Architecture

Multiple AI systems contribute to one highlight score.

```text
Video + Audio + Transcript
          │
          ▼
Semantic Scene Graph
          │
          ▼
Highlight Signal Extractors
          │
 ┌────────┼────────┐
 ▼        ▼        ▼
Emotion  CTA     Motion
AI       AI       AI
 └────────┼────────┘
          ▼
Highlight Scoring Engine
          │
          ▼
Clip Suggestions
```

---

## Highlight Signals

| Signal | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| Emotion | Excitement detection |
| Motion | Visual attention |
| Transcript | Important statements |
| Face | Expressions |
| Cursor | Screen interaction |
| Gesture | Emphasis |
| Audio Energy | Excitement level |

---

7. Viral clips preserve sentence boundaries whenever possible.

# 14.81 Automation Engine Philosophy

The **Automation Workflow Engine** transforms semantic AI understanding into actual editing actions.

Unlike template-based editors, TryLipi creates an editable graph of AI actions that users can customize, reorder, disable, or replace.

The automation engine is inspired by workflow systems rather than one-click black boxes.

---

## Golden Automation Principles

1. Every automation produces editable actions.
2. AI never modifies source media.
3. Automation is deterministic whenever possible.
4. Actions execute on timeline metadata.
5. Every action has confidence metadata.
6. Workflows are reusable.
7. Users can override any AI decision.

---

## Responsibilities

The Automation Engine owns:

- Auto Zoom.
- Auto Pan.
- Auto B-Roll.
- Auto Emojis.
- Auto Captions.
- Auto CTA Effects.
- Auto Music Ducking.
- Auto Transitions.
- Workflow orchestration.

---

# 14.82 AI Edit Action Architecture

Every AI edit becomes a reusable **Edit Action**.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Semantic Scene Graph
        │
        ▼
AI Decision Engine
        │
        ▼
Edit Action Builder
        │
        ▼
Edit Action Graph
        │
        ▼
Timeline Renderer
```

---

## Edit Action Categories

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Camera | Zoom, Pan, Focus |
| Audio | Duck Music, Volume Boost |
| Visual | B-Roll, Emoji, Sticker |
| Caption | Style, Highlight, Karaoke |
| Transition | Fade, Slide, Flash |
| Timeline | Jump Cut, Trim |

---

## Edit Action Interface

```ts
interface AIEditAction {
  actionId: string;
  actionType: string;
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  confidence: number;
  editable: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

- Actions never modify source media.
- Timeline references action IDs.

---

All AI actions are stored inside one graph.

```text
AI Edit Graph
├── Zoom Actions
├── B-Roll Actions
├── Caption Actions
├── Transition Actions
├── Audio Actions
└── Emoji Actions
```

---

## Graph Interface

```ts
interface AIEditActionGraph {
  actions: AIEditAction[];
}
```

---

## Graph Properties

| Property | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Immutable Nodes | Safe undo history. |
| Dependency Edges | Action ordering. |
| Confidence Metadata | AI confidence. |

---

## Rules

Rejected actions remain in graph history.

---

```text
Timeline Suggestions
```

## Workflow Tests

- Built-in presets execute correctly.
- Custom workflows serialize correctly.
- Undo restores automation actions.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 14.5)

1. AI edits are represented as Edit Actions.
2. Automation workflows generate graphs, not direct timeline edits.
3. Auto Zoom targets semantic regions, not raw pixels.
4. Camera actions merge when compatible.
5. B-Roll actions never modify source video.
6. Music ducking follows speech activity timeline.
7. Workflow Builder stores workflows as JSON graphs.
8. Action conflicts are resolved before rendering.
9. Automation layer is independently toggleable.
10. Every automation action remains editable and reversible.

# 16.01 Virtual Camera Philosophy

TryLipi does **not** record physical camera movement.

Instead, every zoom, pan, crop, and focus is produced by a **Virtual Camera** operating on the rendered video timeline.

This makes Smart Zoom completely editable.

---

## Why a Virtual Camera?

Instead of changing pixels:

- Original video remains untouched.
- Camera movement becomes metadata.
- Multiple camera paths can coexist.
- Export renders camera motion non-destructively.

This architecture enables Screen Studio–style cinematic movement inside a browser.

---

## Golden Camera Principles

1. Original media is immutable.
2. Camera movement is metadata.
3. Camera always renders inside safe boundaries.
4. Every camera move is reversible.
5. Camera paths are frame-accurate.
6. Preview and export use identical camera metadata.
7. Camera actions never crop outside source bounds.

---

## Responsibilities

The Camera Engine owns:

- Zoom.
- Pan.
- Focus.
- Tracking.
- Camera interpolation.
- Camera viewport.
- Safe cropping.
- Motion smoothing.

---

# 16.02 Camera Engine Overview

The Camera Engine consumes semantic AI events and produces viewport animations.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Semantic Scene Graph
        │
        ▼
Camera Decision Engine
        │
        ▼
Camera Timeline Builder
        │
        ▼
Viewport Renderer
        │
        ▼
Preview / Export Renderer
```

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Camera Timeline | Stores camera keyframes. |
| Viewport Engine | Calculates visible crop. |
| Focus Engine | Selects target region. |
| Motion Engine | Generates camera paths. |
| Constraint Engine | Prevents invalid crops. |

---

# 16.03 Camera Coordinate System

The camera operates in **normalized project coordinates** instead of pixels.

## Coordinate Space

```text
(0,0)
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│                               │
│                               │
│            Frame              │
│                               │
│                               │
└───────────────────────────────┘
                     (1,1)
```

---

## Coordinate Rules

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| 0 | Left / Top edge |
| 0.5 | Center |
| 1 | Right / Bottom edge |

---

## Camera Point Interface

```ts
interface CameraPoint {
  x: number;
  y: number;
}
```

---

## Why Normalized Coordinates?

- Resolution independent.
- Works for 720p–8K.
- Same timeline for portrait and landscape exports.

---

# 16.04 Camera Timeline Architecture

Every camera movement exists on its own timeline layer.

## Timeline Layout

```text
Timeline
├── Video Layer
├── Audio Layer
├── Caption Layer
├── Camera Layer
│    ├── Zoom
│    ├── Pan
│    ├── Focus
│    └── Rotation
└── Overlay Layer
```

---

## Camera Timeline Interface

```ts
interface CameraTimeline {
  keyframes: CameraKeyframe[];
}
```

---

## Camera Layers

| Layer | Editable |
|-------|----------|
| Zoom | Yes |
| Pan | Yes |
| Focus | Yes |
| Rotation | Future |
| Tilt | Future |

---

## Rules

Camera timeline never edits video timeline timestamps.

---

# 16.05 Camera Target System

Camera targets represent regions of interest.

## Target Sources

| Target | Source |
|--------|--------|
| Face | Face Timeline |
| Cursor | Cursor Timeline |
| Object | Object Timeline |
| OCR Region | OCR Timeline |
| Manual Selection | User |

---

## Target Pipeline

```text
Semantic Event
      │
Target Selector
      │
Target Bounding Box
      │
Camera Planner
```

---

## Target Interface

```ts
interface CameraTarget {
  targetId: string;
  type: "face" | "cursor" | "object" | "manual";
  bounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

## Priority Rules

1. Manual target.
2. Active speaker face.
3. Cursor click.
4. Gesture target.
5. OCR heading.
6. Object target.

---

# 16.06 Camera Keyframe Engine

Every camera movement begins and ends with keyframes.

## Keyframe Timeline

```text
Time →
●────────────●────────────●
Zoom In      Pan          Zoom Out
```

---

## Keyframe Interface

```ts
interface CameraKeyframe {
  timestampUs: number;
  viewport: CameraViewport;
}
```

---

## Keyframe Properties

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Timestamp | Frame position |
| Zoom | Scale value |
| Center | Focus point |
| Rotation | Future support |
| Easing | Motion curve |

---

## Rules

Camera keyframes are immutable timeline nodes.

---

# 16.07 Camera Interpolation Engine

Smooth camera movement is generated between keyframes.

## Motion Pipeline

```text
Keyframe A
     │
Interpolation
     │
Motion Curve
     │
Keyframe B
```

---

## Supported Curves

| Curve | Usage |
|-------|-------|
| Linear | Constant movement |
| Ease In | Smooth zoom start |
| Ease Out | Smooth zoom finish |
| Ease In-Out | Default |
| Cubic | Cinematic movement |
| Spring | Future support |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CameraInterpolation {
  easing: "linear" | "easeInOut" | "cubic";
}
```

---

## Rules

Ease In-Out is the default interpolation.

---

# 16.08 Camera Viewport Engine

Viewport defines which portion of the original frame is visible.

## Viewport Diagram

```text
Source Frame
┌────────────────────────────┐
│                            │
│      ┌──────────────┐      │
│      │ Viewport      │      │
│      └──────────────┘      │
│                            │
└────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Viewport Interface

```ts
interface CameraViewport {
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
  zoom: number;
}
```

---

## Viewport Responsibilities

- Calculate crop rectangle.
- Maintain aspect ratio.
- Prevent overflow.
- Support portrait exports.

---

## Rules

Viewport is resolution-independent.

---

# 16.09 Safe Area Engine

Safe areas prevent important content from being cropped.

## Supported Outputs

| Output | Safe Area |
|--------|-----------|
| YouTube Landscape | 16:9 |
| Shorts | 9:16 |
| Reels | 9:16 |
| TikTok | 9:16 |
| Square | 1:1 |

---

## Safe Area Pipeline

```text
Viewport
    │
Aspect Ratio
    │
Safe Area Calculator
    │
Adjusted Viewport
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface SafeArea {
  aspectRatio: string;
  padding: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Camera targets must remain inside safe area margins.

---

# 16.10 Camera Constraints Engine

Prevents invalid camera movement.

## Constraints

| Constraint | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| Min Zoom | Prevent over-zooming out. |
| Max Zoom | Preserve quality. |
| Edge Clamp | Prevent empty borders. |
| Face Margin | Preserve face visibility. |
| Cursor Margin | Preserve cursor visibility. |

---

## Constraint Pipeline

```text
Camera Viewport
      │
Constraint Validator
      │
Adjusted Viewport
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CameraConstraint {
  minZoom: number;
  maxZoom: number;
}
```

---

## Default Values

| Parameter | Default |
|----------|---------|
| Min Zoom | 1.0x |
| Max Zoom | 2.5x |
| Edge Margin | 24 px equivalent |

---

# 16.11 Camera State Machine

The camera behaves like a deterministic state machine.

## States

```text
Idle
 │
Focus
 │
Zoom
 │
Pan
 │
Track
 │
Return
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CameraState {
  state: "idle" | "focus" | "zoom" | "pan" | "track";
}
```

---

## Transition Rules

| From | To |
|------|----|
| Idle | Focus |
| Focus | Zoom |
| Zoom | Track |
| Track | Return |
| Return | Idle |

---

## Rules

Only one primary camera state is active at a time.

---

# 16.12 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes virtual camera metrics.

## Metrics

- Camera keyframes.
- Active viewport.
- Zoom level.
- Focus target.
- Safe area violations.
- Interpolation latency.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CameraDiagnostics {
  zoomLevel: number;
  keyframes: number;
  activeTarget: string;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Unsafe Crop | Viewport exceeds frame bounds. |
| Missing Target | Focus target disappeared. |
| Zoom Overflow | Max zoom exceeded. |

---

# 16.13 Acceptance Tests

## Viewport Tests

- Viewport stays inside source frame.
- Safe areas respected.

## Keyframe Tests

- Keyframes interpolate correctly.
- Undo restores camera timeline.

## Target Tests

- Face target selected correctly.
- Cursor target selected correctly.
- Manual target overrides AI.

## Constraint Tests

- Camera never leaves frame.
- Max zoom enforced.
- Portrait exports remain safe.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 16.1)

1. Camera movement is metadata, not pixel manipulation.
2. Camera timeline is independent from video timeline.
3. Viewports use normalized coordinates.
4. Camera targets come from semantic AI metadata.
5. Every movement begins and ends with keyframes.
6. Interpolation is deterministic and editable.
7. Safe areas are enforced before rendering.
8. Constraints prevent invalid crops.
9. Camera state machine guarantees predictable motion.
10. Preview and export share identical camera metadata.

---

- Cursor-follow camera.
- Click-aware zooms.
- Scroll-aware zooms.

# 16.21 Smart Zoom Philosophy

Smart Zoom is the signature feature of TryLipi's screen recording editor.

Instead of users manually animating camera crops, the AI continuously understands **where the viewer should look** and creates cinematic camera movements automatically.

The Smart Zoom Engine is **attention-driven**, not cursor-driven.

---

## Viewer Attention Hierarchy

Priority determines where the camera moves.

| Priority | Target |
|----------|--------|
| Manual Focus | User-selected region |
| Cursor Click | Click destination |
| Active Speaker Face | Webcam overlay |
| Gesture Target | Pointing hand |
| Important UI Element | Button / Dropdown |
| OCR Heading | Text heading |
| Cursor Hover | Interactive region |
| Motion Region | Moving object |

---

## Golden Smart Zoom Principles

1. Camera follows attention, not cursor noise.
2. Cursor movement alone is insufficient for zooming.
3. Zooms should feel cinematic.
4. Every zoom is reversible.
5. Smart Zoom never crops outside safe areas.
6. Zooms align with semantic interactions.
7. Camera motion minimizes viewer fatigue.

---

# 16.22 Smart Zoom Architecture

Smart Zoom consumes semantic events and produces camera keyframes.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Semantic Scene Graph
        │
Cursor Timeline
        │
UI Timeline
        │
OCR Timeline
        │
Face Timeline
        ▼
Attention Engine
        ▼
Zoom Planner
        ▼
Camera Timeline
        ▼
Viewport Renderer
```

---

## Smart Zoom Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Attention Engine | Decide viewer focus. |
| Cursor Engine | Track interactions. |
| Zoom Planner | Create zoom keyframes. |
| Focus Planner | Select target bounds. |
| Recovery Planner | Return to default framing. |

---

# 16.23 Cursor Timeline Engine

Cursor movement becomes a high-frequency semantic timeline.

Unlike video FPS, cursor events are sampled independently.

## Cursor Timeline Pipeline

```text
Screen Recording
       │
Cursor Detector
       │
Cursor Position Timeline
       │
Cursor Event Timeline
```

---

## Cursor Sampling Strategy

| Recording FPS | Cursor Sampling |
|--------------|-----------------|
| 30 FPS | 60 Hz |
| 60 FPS | 120 Hz |
| 120 FPS | 240 Hz |

Cursor interpolation ensures smooth movement even when recording FPS is lower.

---

## Cursor Event Types

| Event | Stored? |
|------|----------|
| Move | Yes |
| Hover | Yes |
| Click | Yes |
| Double Click | Yes |
| Drag Start | Yes |
| Drag End | Yes |
| Scroll | Yes |
| Selection | Yes |

---

## Cursor Timeline Interface

```ts
interface CursorTimelineFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  position: CameraPoint;
  velocity: number;
  acceleration: number;
  interaction: CursorInteraction;
}
```

---

## Cursor History Window

Smart Zoom keeps a rolling history.

| Window | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| Previous 150 ms | Velocity smoothing |
| Previous 400 ms | Hover prediction |
| Previous 800 ms | Attention prediction |

---

## Rules

- Cursor timeline is immutable.
- Cursor timestamps are microsecond accurate.
- Timeline survives replay and export.

---

# 16.24 Cursor Movement Prediction Engine

Human cursor movement contains intent.

The prediction engine estimates **where the cursor is going** before it arrives.

---

## Prediction Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
      │
Velocity Estimator
      │
Acceleration Estimator
      │
Destination Predictor
      │
Focus Candidate
```

---

## Prediction Signals

| Signal | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| Velocity | Cursor speed. |
| Direction | Future path. |
| Deceleration | Preparing for click. |
| Hover Duration | Intent confidence. |
| UI Element Proximity | Snap prediction. |

---

## Prediction Interface

```ts
interface CursorPrediction {
  predictedPosition: CameraPoint;
  confidence: number;
  etaMs: number;
}
```

---

## Cursor Behaviors

| Behavior | Prediction |
|----------|------------|
| Straight movement | Linear prediction |
| Curve movement | Bézier prediction |
| Fast flick | Ignore until stable |
| Hover slowdown | Prepare zoom |

---

## Rules

Prediction never creates keyframes by itself.

---

# 16.25 Click Detection & Click Zoom Engine

Clicks indicate the highest-confidence attention signal.

---

## Click Zoom Pipeline

```text
Cursor Event
     │
Click Detector
     │
Target Bounds Lookup
     │
Zoom Planner
```

---

## Click Zoom Lifecycle

```text
Cursor Moving
      │
Click Detected
      │
Camera Zoom In
      │
Focus Lock
      │
Zoom Recovery
```

---

## Click Zoom Interface

```ts
interface ClickZoomAction extends ZoomAction {
  clickPosition: CameraPoint;
  targetElementId?: string;
}
```

---

## Click Zoom Timing

| Phase | Duration |
|-------|----------|
| Ease In | 180–250 ms |
| Focus Hold | 300–1200 ms |
| Ease Out | 250–400 ms |

---

## Smart Click Types

| Click | Zoom Behaviour |
|------|----------------|
| Button | Tight zoom |
| Dropdown | Medium zoom |
| Code Editor | Cursor-centered zoom |
| Browser Tab | Wide zoom |
| Checkbox | Light zoom |

---

## Rules

Multiple clicks merge into one zoom if sufficiently close.

---

# 16.26 Scroll Detection & Scroll Zoom Engine

Scrolling changes viewer attention vertically.

---

## Scroll Pipeline

```text
Scroll Event
     │
Direction Detection
     │
Scroll Momentum
     │
Camera Planner
```

---

## Scroll Behaviours

| Scroll | Camera Behaviour |
|--------|------------------|
| Slow Scroll | Follow viewport |
| Fast Scroll | Delay camera |
| Section Jump | Re-center viewport |
| Infinite Scroll | Dynamic follow |

---

## Scroll Interface

```ts
interface ScrollEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  direction: "up" | "down";
  velocity: number;
}
```

---

## Scroll Recovery Rules

- Ignore overscroll bounce.
- Ignore inertial scroll after stop.
- Follow content instead of pointer.

---

# 16.27 Cursor Velocity & Smoothing Engine

Raw cursor movement is noisy.

The smoothing engine creates cinematic movement.

---

## Smoothing Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
      │
Noise Filter
      │
Velocity Smoothing
      │
Motion Curve
```

---

## Filters

| Filter | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| EMA | Smooth velocity |
| Kalman | Predict motion |
| Bézier | Smooth path |
| Cubic | Camera interpolation |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CursorSmoothing {
  rawPosition: CameraPoint;
  smoothedPosition: CameraPoint;
}
```

---

## Smoothing Rules

Fast cursor flicks should not shake the camera.

---

# 16.28 Dynamic Focus Planner

The Focus Planner decides what deserves camera attention.

---

## Candidate Sources

| Candidate | Priority |
|-----------|----------|
| Manual Focus | Highest |
| Click Target | High |
| Active Cursor Hover | High |
| Face | Medium |
| OCR Heading | Medium |
| Object | Medium |
| Motion Region | Low |

---

## Planner Pipeline

```text
Semantic Candidates
       │
Ranking Engine
       │
Focus Candidate
       │
Viewport Planner
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface FocusCandidate {
  targetId: string;
  priority: number;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Focus Duration Rules

| Event | Hold Time |
|------|-----------|
| Button Click | 700 ms |
| Heading | 1200 ms |
| Cursor Hover | 500 ms |
| Face | Until speaker changes |

---

# 16.29 Zoom Intensity Model

Zoom intensity adapts automatically.

---

## Zoom Levels

| Mode | Scale |
|------|-------|
| Tiny | 1.10x |
| Light | 1.20x |
| Medium | 1.35x |
| Strong | 1.60x |
| Hero | 2.00x |

---

## Intensity Inputs

- UI element size.
- Screen resolution.
- Cursor precision.
- Viewer attention confidence.
- Output aspect ratio.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ZoomIntensity {
  scale: number;
  reason: string;
}
```

---

## Dynamic Rules

- Small buttons receive stronger zooms.
- Large windows receive lighter zooms.
- Full-screen code editors rarely exceed 1.3x.

---

# 16.30 Smart Framing Engine

Framing ensures important context remains visible.

---

## Framing Pipeline

```text
Focus Target
      │
Safe Area Calculator
      │
Margin Calculator
      │
Viewport Optimizer
```

---

## Margin Rules

| Element | Margin |
|---------|--------|
| Cursor | 10% viewport |
| Face | 15% viewport |
| Heading | 12% viewport |
| Button | 18% viewport |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface SmartFrame {
  viewport: CameraViewport;
  marginRatio: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Framing preserves nearby context rather than cropping tightly.

---

# 16.31 Multi-Target Camera Selection

Sometimes multiple targets compete for attention.

---

## Example

```text
Face Speaking
      +
Cursor Clicking
      +
Important Button
```

Camera chooses one or blends multiple targets.

---

## Selection Pipeline

```text
Attention Candidates
       │
Priority Ranking
       │
Winner Selection
       │
Camera Target
```

---

## Selection Strategies

| Situation | Behaviour |
|----------|-----------|
| Face + Cursor | Split focus |
| Cursor + OCR | OCR wins after click |
| Multiple Faces | Active speaker wins |
| Gesture + Cursor | Gesture wins temporarily |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CameraTargetSelection {
  selectedTargetId: string;
  competingTargets: string[];
}
```

---

## Rules

Selection changes require transition smoothing.

---

# 16.32 Focus Lock Engine

After a zoom begins, camera should not immediately chase another target.

---

## Focus Lock Lifecycle

```text
Zoom Begins
     │
Focus Lock
     │
Hold Timer
     │
Release
```

---

## Lock Durations

| Target | Lock |
|--------|------|
| Button Click | 700 ms |
| Face | Continuous while speaking |
| Heading | 1200 ms |
| Cursor Hover | 450 ms |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface FocusLock {
  targetId: string;
  lockUntilUs: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Focus lock prevents camera jitter.

---

# 16.33 Zoom Recovery Engine

Camera should gracefully return to its default framing.

---

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Focus Complete
      │
Recovery Planner
      │
Ease Out
      │
Default Viewport
```

---

## Recovery Modes

| Mode | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| Immediate | Quick return |
| Delayed | Hold after interaction |
| Progressive | Smooth zoom out |
| Scene Change | Jump to new framing |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ZoomRecovery {
  recoveryStartUs: number;
  recoveryDurationUs: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Recovery should never interrupt a new higher-priority target.

---

# 16.34 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes Smart Zoom internals.

---

## Metrics

- Cursor events.
- Hover predictions.
- Click zooms.
- Scroll zooms.
- Focus locks.
- Recovery events.
- Average zoom duration.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface SmartZoomDiagnostics {
  clickZooms: number;
  hoverZooms: number;
  averageZoomScale: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Cursor Lost | Tracking interrupted. |
| Unsafe Zoom | Viewport exceeds safe bounds. |
| Prediction Failure | Confidence below threshold. |
| Focus Thrashing | Rapid target switching. |

---

# 16.35 Acceptance Tests

## Cursor Tests

- Cursor timeline sampled independently.
- Prediction follows smooth movement.
- Hover confidence increases correctly.

## Click Zoom Tests

- Button click zooms correctly.
- Code editor click centers viewport.
- Multiple nearby clicks merge.

## Scroll Tests

- Camera follows slow scroll.
- Ignores inertial bounce.
- Maintains framing during long pages.

## Focus Tests

- Focus lock prevents jitter.
- Recovery restores default framing.
- Manual focus overrides AI.

## Performance Tests

- Cursor smoothing under 16 ms latency.
- Zoom planner generates deterministic keyframes.
- Preview equals export.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 16.2)

1. Smart Zoom follows viewer attention, not raw cursor movement.
2. Cursor timeline is sampled independently from video FPS.
3. Clicks are the strongest automatic zoom trigger.
4. Scroll behaviour follows content, not pointer position.
5. Cursor prediction prepares camera motion but never creates edits directly.
6. Zoom intensity adapts to UI element size and output format.
7. Smart Framing always preserves surrounding context.
8. Focus Lock prevents camera jitter during interactions.
9. Zoom Recovery returns smoothly unless interrupted by a higher-priority target.
10. Smart Zoom metadata is identical in preview and export.

---

# 16.41 Face Tracking Philosophy

The Face Tracking Engine converts every visible person into a persistent semantic entity that exists across the entire project timeline.

Unlike ordinary face detection, TryLipi tracks **identity continuity**, **speaker activity**, **visibility**, and **camera importance**.

This enables cinematic camera behavior for:

- Talking-head YouTube videos.
- Podcasts.
- Interviews.
- Fitness coaching videos.
- Webinar recordings.
- Webcam overlays.
- Future AI avatar editing.

---

## Golden Face Tracking Principles

1. Face detection is separate from face identity.
2. Face IDs remain stable across the project timeline.
3. Speaking activity is independent of visibility.
4. Camera framing follows active speakers, not simply visible faces.
5. Face metadata is reusable across AI systems.
6. Face tracking survives temporary occlusion.
7. Manual speaker overrides AI selection.

---

## Responsibilities

The Face Engine owns:

- Face detection.
- Face identity tracking.
- Active speaker timeline.
- Pose estimation.
- Gesture detection.
- Webcam overlay framing.
- Face priority scoring.

---

# 16.42 Face Tracking Architecture

The face pipeline combines vision AI and audio AI.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Video Frames
      │
      ▼
Face Detector
      │
      ▼
Face Embedding Generator
      │
      ▼
Identity Tracker
      │
      ▼
Speaker Synchronization
      │
      ▼
Face Timeline Graph
```

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Face Detector | Detect face bounding boxes. |
| Embedding Generator | Generate identity vectors. |
| Identity Tracker | Maintain stable face IDs. |
| Speaker Sync | Match voice to faces. |
| Pose Engine | Head/body orientation. |
| Gesture Engine | Hand/body gestures. |

---

# 16.43 Face Detection Engine

```ts
interface DetectedFace {

}
```

| Landmarks | Pose estimation. |

---

## Detection Rules

- Ignore faces below confidence threshold.
- Ignore faces below minimum size.
- Preserve detection timestamps.

# 16.44 Persistent Face Identity Engine

Every detected face becomes a persistent identity.

## Identity Pipeline

```text
Detected Face
     │
Embedding Generator
     │
Embedding Matching
     │
Persistent Face ID
```

---

## Identity Interface

```ts
interface FaceIdentity {
  faceId: string;
  embeddingId: string;
  firstSeenUs: number;
  lastSeenUs: number;
}
```

---

## Identity Matching Signals

| Signal | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| Face Embedding | Primary identity. |
| Hair / Clothing | Recovery signal. |
| Motion Path | Continuity. |
| Position History | Tracking stability. |

---

## Occlusion Recovery

| Situation | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Person turns away | Preserve ID. |
| Temporary obstruction | Predict location. |
| Leaves frame briefly | Recover ID on return. |
| Completely new person | New face ID. |

---

## Rules

Face IDs never change because of temporary occlusion.

# 16.55 Acceptance Tests

## Face Tests

- Stable identities across frames.
- Recover identity after occlusion.
- Ignore low-confidence faces.

## Speaker Tests

- Correct active speaker timeline.
- Smooth speaker transitions.
- Speaker switch updates camera.

## Gesture Tests

- Pointing triggers camera.
- Raised hand triggers CTA focus.
- Thumbs up triggers highlight.

## Talking Head Tests

- Maintain eye-line framing.
- Dynamic framing follows movement.
- Webcam overlay remains stable.

## Performance Tests

- Face tracking remains deterministic.
- Pose updates synchronize with timeline.
- Preview equals export.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 16.3)

1. Face detection and face identity are separate systems.
2. Face IDs persist across occlusions whenever confidence remains sufficient.
3. Active speaker timeline combines transcript, lip motion, and audio signals.
4. Camera transitions smoothly between speakers.
5. Pose estimation produces reusable timeline metadata.
6. Gestures act as camera triggers, not edits.
7. Talking-head framing follows cinematic composition rules.
8. Webcam overlays are independent semantic camera targets.
9. Face priority determines automatic camera selection.
10. All face, pose, and gesture metadata remain editable and reusable across AI workflows.

# 16.61 Motion Tracking Philosophy

Motion Tracking allows TryLipi's virtual camera to follow **semantic regions** instead of following arbitrary pixels.

A semantic region can be:

- Browser tab.
- Code editor.
- Terminal window.
- Button.
- Image.
- Product.
- Phone screen.
- Slide heading.
- Chart.
- Cursor-selected element.

Unlike traditional video trackers, the Region Camera Engine understands **what** is moving, not just **where** pixels move.

---

## Golden Motion Tracking Principles

1. Track semantic regions, not pixels.
2. Every tracked region has a persistent identity.
3. Tracking survives scrolling and zooming.
4. Camera follows semantic intent.
5. Region tracking is resolution-independent.
6. Multiple trackers may coexist.
7. Tracking metadata is reusable across AI workflows.

---

## Responsibilities

The Motion Tracking Engine owns:

- Object tracking.
- Screen region tracking.
- Window tracking.
- UI component tracking.
- Product tracking.
- Motion prediction.
- Dynamic crop stabilization.

---

# 16.62 Region Camera Engine Architecture

The Region Camera Engine transforms tracked regions into camera targets.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Video Frames
      │
Semantic Region Detector
      │
Region Tracker
      │
Region Timeline
      │
Camera Planner
      │
Viewport Timeline
```

---

## Region Sources

| Source | Example |
|--------|---------|
| Cursor Selection | Button |
| OCR Region | Heading |
| UI Detection | Sidebar |
| Object Detection | Phone |
| Face Tracking | Webcam |
| Manual Selection | Custom box |

---

## Region Types

| Region Type | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| Static Region | Does not move. |
| Dynamic Region | Moves within frame. |
| Scroll Region | Moves with page scroll. |
| Floating Region | Overlay/webcam. |
| Window Region | Browser/app window. |

---

# 16.70 Region Persistence Engine

Tracked regions survive temporary disappearance.

## Persistence Pipeline

```text
Tracked Region
      │
Visibility Loss
      │
Persistence Cache
      │
Region Recovery
```

---

## Recovery Examples

| Event | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Scroll Away | Recover after scroll back |
| Temporary Overlay | Preserve region |
| Cursor Covers Region | Ignore |
| Popup Opens | Resume after popup closes |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface RegionPersistence {
  regionId: string;
  suspended: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

Recovered regions retain original IDs.

---

# 16.71 Dynamic Crop Stabilization Engine

Camera movement should remain stable even while following moving regions.

## Stabilization Pipeline

```text
Camera Target
      │
Motion Smoothing
      │
Crop Stabilizer
      │
Viewport Timeline
```

---

## Stabilization Goals

| Goal | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Reduce Jitter | Smooth tracking. |
| Preserve Target | Keep target centered. |
| Smooth Velocity | Cinematic motion. |
| Avoid Bounce | Ignore tiny movements. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CropStabilization {
  stabilizedViewport: CameraViewport;
}
```

---

## Stabilization Filters

| Filter | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| EMA | Minor smoothing |
| Kalman | Target prediction |
| Bézier | Camera motion curve |
| Cubic | Export interpolation |

---

## Rules

Small cursor jitter never shakes viewport.

---

# 16.74 Acceptance Tests

## Region Tests

- Browser regions remain stable during scroll.
- VS Code sidebar tracked independently.
- Terminal window tracked after resize.

## Object Tests

- Phone remains centered during movement.
- Laptop tracking survives partial occlusion.
- Product zoom remains smooth.

## Window Tests

- Window switch triggers transition.
- Resize updates viewport.

## Stabilization Tests

- Jitter removed.
- Camera follows moving target smoothly.
- Export matches preview.

## Performance Tests

- Region tracking under target latency.
- Multiple objects tracked simultaneously.
- Motion graph cached for reuse.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 16.4)

1. Region tracking is semantic rather than pixel-based.
2. Screen regions maintain persistent IDs across scrolling.
3. Window tracking survives resizing and focus changes.
4. UI components become reusable camera anchors.
5. Product tracking integrates with Smart Zoom and B-Roll engines.
6. Motion prediction assists planning but never edits timelines directly.
7. Region persistence recovers temporarily hidden targets.
8. Dynamic crop stabilization removes camera jitter.
9. Motion Timeline Graph is shared across AI systems.
10. Preview and export use identical region tracking metadata.

# 16.81 Cinematic Camera Philosophy

The **Cinematic Camera Engine** transforms AI camera decisions into visually pleasing motion.

Rather than snapping between crops, TryLipi creates movement that feels like a professional camera operator following attention.

Every camera movement is rendered using animation curves, stabilization, motion blending, and safe framing.

---

## Golden Cinematic Principles

1. Camera movement should feel intentional.
2. Motion should preserve viewer context.
3. Camera acceleration should be smooth.
4. No abrupt jumps unless explicitly requested.
5. Camera animation is deterministic.
6. Preview equals export.
7. Every preset is editable.

---

## Responsibilities

The Cinematic Camera Engine owns:

- Camera animation presets.
- Dolly movement.
- Push/Pull zooms.
- Orbit simulation.
- Parallax simulation.
- Camera blending.
- Export animation rendering.
- Motion interpolation.

---

# 16.82 Cinematic Camera Architecture

The camera animation engine sits between AI planning and rendering.

## High-Level Pipeline

```text
Camera Timeline
      │
Camera Animation Planner
      │
Animation Curves
      │
Motion Blender
      │
Viewport Timeline
      │
Renderer
```

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Animation Planner | Convert keyframes into motion. |
| Curve Engine | Generate easing curves. |
| Motion Blender | Merge overlapping movements. |
| Camera Renderer | Produce viewport transforms. |
| Export Motion Engine | Render animation consistently. |

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 16.5)

1. Cinematic camera movement is generated from metadata, not pixel edits.
2. Camera presets are reusable timeline assets.
3. Dolly, Push, Pull, Orbit, and Parallax are viewport transforms.
4. Multi-camera shots reuse one source recording.
5. Camera blending resolves overlapping actions before rendering.
6. Export uses the exact same camera timeline as preview.
7. GPU renders transforms while CPU prepares metadata.
8. Camera presets are workspace-level reusable assets.
9. The architecture remains compatible with future 3D depth-aware cameras.
10. Every cinematic camera action remains editable until export.
