# 17.01 Rendering Engine Philosophy

The Export Engine converts an editable TryLipi project into a deterministic video file.

Unlike traditional editors that render directly from timeline objects, TryLipi renders through a **Render Graph** that guarantees identical preview and export output.

The rendering engine is browser-native and optimized for:

- Chrome
- Edge
- Arc
- Brave
- Future Chromium browsers

without requiring native desktop APIs.

---

## Golden Rendering Principles

1. Preview and export must produce identical frames.
2. Rendering is deterministic.
3. Rendering is resolution independent.
4. Timeline objects never render themselves directly.
5. Every renderable object becomes a render node.
6. Rendering is incremental whenever possible.
7. Export never modifies project state.

---

## Responsibilities

The Rendering Engine owns:

- Timeline rendering.
- Layer compositing.
- Camera transforms.
- Caption rendering.
- Audio synchronization.
- Export encoding.
- Render caching.
- Progressive previews.

---

# 17.02 Export Engine Overview

Rendering is divided into independent stages.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Project Snapshot
        │
        ▼
Render Graph Builder
        │
        ▼
Frame Scheduler
        │
 ┌──────┼─────────────┐
 ▼      ▼             ▼
Video   Captions    Overlays
Layers  Layers      Layers
 └──────┼─────────────┘
        ▼
GPU Compositor
        ▼
Frame Buffer
        ▼
Video Encoder
```

---

## Rendering Stages

| Stage | Responsibility |
|-------|----------------|
| Snapshot | Immutable export state. |
| Graph Builder | Build render DAG. |
| Scheduler | Determine render order. |
| Compositor | Merge layers. |
| Encoder | Produce final video stream. |

---

## Export Modes

| Mode | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Preview | Interactive playback. |
| Draft Export | Fast export. |
| Full Export | Final quality. |
| Background Export | Worker rendering. |

---

# 17.03 Browser Rendering Architecture

Rendering is split across multiple execution environments.

## Architecture

```text
UI Thread
   │
Render Scheduler
   │
 ├──────────────┐
 ▼              ▼
GPU Worker   Audio Worker
 ▼              ▼
Frame Output   PCM Output
      └──────┬───────┘
             ▼
        Encoder Worker
```

---

## Thread Responsibilities

| Thread | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| UI Thread | Timeline editing. |
| Render Worker | Frame generation. |
| GPU Worker | Composition. |
| Audio Worker | Audio mixing. |
| Encoder Worker | Video encoding. |

---

## Rules

- UI thread never performs export rendering.
- Export rendering continues independently.

---

# 17.04 Timeline Render Graph

Everything visible becomes a node inside a directed acyclic graph.

## Render Graph

```text
Render Graph
├── Video Track
├── Camera Layer
├── Caption Layer
├── Emoji Layer
├── Overlay Layer
├── Transition Layer
├── B-Roll Layer
└── Color Layer
```

---

## Node Interface

```ts
interface RenderNode {
  nodeId: string;
  dependencies: string[];
  zIndex: number;
}
```

---

## Dependency Examples

```text
Video Frame
    │
Camera Transform
    │
Caption Layer
    │
Emoji Layer
```

---

## Rules

Nodes render only after dependencies resolve.

---

# 17.05 Render Scheduler

The scheduler determines exactly which frames must be rendered.

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text
Timeline Snapshot
      │
Dirty Region Detector
      │
Frame Queue
      │
Render Workers
```

---

## Scheduler Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Frame Ordering | Sequential timeline frames. |
| Dirty Detection | Render only changed regions during preview. |
| Worker Distribution | Parallel rendering. |
| Progress Tracking | Export progress updates. |

---

## Scheduler Interface

```ts
interface RenderTask {
  frameNumber: number;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Preview renders dirty frames only.

Export renders every frame.

---

# 17.06 Frame Composition Engine

## Composition Order

```text
Background
   │
Video
   │
Camera Crop
   │
B-Roll
   │
Captions
   │
Emoji
   │
Cursor Highlight
   │
UI Overlay
```

---

```text
Render Nodes
      │
Transform Stack
      │
Blend Engine
      │
RGBA Frame Buffer
```

---

## Blend Modes (MVP)

| Blend Mode | Supported |
|-----------|-----------|
| Normal | ✅ |
| Multiply | ✅ |
| Screen | ✅ |
| Overlay | ✅ |
| Additive | Future |
| Difference | Future |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CompositeLayer {
  layerId: string;
  blendMode: string;
}
```

---

## Rules

Composition order is deterministic.

---

# 17.07 Layer Rendering Pipeline

Every timeline layer owns a renderer.

```text
Timeline Layer
      │
Renderer Adapter
      │

      │
```

## Supported Layers

|-------|----------|
| Video | Video Renderer |

| Captions | Typography Renderer |
| Emoji | Overlay Renderer |
| Camera | Transform Renderer |


---

---

# 17.08 Audio / Video Synchronization Engine

Frame rendering follows the master timeline clock.

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
Timeline Clock
      │
Video Timestamp
      │
Audio Timestamp
      │
Sync Validator
```

---

## Timeline Clock

Everything derives from microsecond timestamps.

| Timeline | Precision |
|----------|-----------|
| Video | Microseconds |
| Audio | Samples |
| Captions | Microseconds |
| Camera | Microseconds |

---

## Sync Interface

```ts
interface AVSyncState {
  frameTimestampUs: number;
  audioTimestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Drift Policies

| Drift | Action |
|------|--------|
| <1 ms | Ignore |
| 1–5 ms | Correct metadata |
| >5 ms | Recalculate frame alignment |

---

## Rules

Export uses synchronized timestamps only.

---

```text
      │

      │

      │
```

```text
      │
```

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 17.1)

1. Rendering operates on immutable project snapshots.
2. Timeline rendering uses a directed acyclic render graph.
3. Preview renders dirty regions only.
4. Export renders the complete timeline.
5. Camera transforms occur before overlays.
6. Audio/video synchronization is timestamp-driven.
7. Frame buffers are pooled and reused.
8. Render cache is incrementally invalidated.
9. Export sessions are isolated from project edits.
10. Preview and export share identical rendering logic.

# 17.21 Browser Encoding Philosophy

TryLipi performs professional-quality exports **inside the browser** without uploading project media to a server.

The export engine chooses the fastest available encoder while preserving identical output quality.

## Golden Encoding Principles

1. Encoding happens after rendering.
2. Encoding never modifies render output.
3. WebCodecs is the primary encoder.
4. FFmpeg WASM is the universal fallback.
5. Hardware acceleration is preferred when available.
6. Browser capability determines encoder selection.
7. Export quality presets remain deterministic.

---

## Responsibilities

The Encoding Engine owns:

- Video encoding.
- Audio encoding.
- Container muxing.
- Codec selection.
- Hardware acceleration detection.
- Fallback strategy.
- Export presets.

---

# 17.22 Encoding Engine Architecture

The encoding system is isolated from rendering.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Rendered Frames
       │
       ▼
Encoding Planner
       │
 ┌─────┼────────────┐
 ▼     ▼            ▼
WebCodecs FFmpeg WASM Audio Encoder
  │         │            │
  └─────────┼────────────┘
            ▼
      Container Muxer
            ▼
        Export File
```

---

## Core Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Encoding Planner | Choose encoder. |
| Video Encoder | Encode rendered frames. |
| Audio Encoder | Encode PCM. |
| Container Muxer | Merge audio/video streams. |
| Export Writer | Produce downloadable file. |

---

## Encoder Selection Priority

| Priority | Encoder |
|----------|---------|
| 1 | WebCodecs Hardware Encoder |
| 2 | WebCodecs Software Encoder |
| 3 | FFmpeg WASM |
| 4 | Future Cloud Encoder |

---

# 17.23 WebCodecs Video Pipeline

WebCodecs is the primary export path for Chromium browsers.

## Pipeline

```text
RGBA Frame Buffer
        │
VideoFrame
        │
VideoEncoder
        │
Encoded Chunks
        │
Muxer
```

---

## Encoding Lifecycle

```text
Render Frame
     │
Create VideoFrame
     │
Encode()
     │
Chunk Callback
     │
Mux Buffer
```

---

## WebCodecs Interface

```ts
interface WebCodecVideoEncoderConfig {
  codec: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  bitrate: number;
  framerate: number;
}
```

---

## Supported Codecs (MVP)

| Codec | Browser Support |
|-------|-----------------|
| H.264 AVC | ✅ Primary |
| VP9 | ✅ Chrome/Edge |
| AV1 | ✅ Modern Chromium |
| HEVC | Future (browser dependent) |

---

## Frame Types

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Key Frame | Scene starts |
| Delta Frame | Standard frames |
| Forced Key Frame | Scene transitions |

---

## Rules

- VideoFrames are released immediately after encoding.
- Frame timestamps use microseconds.

---

# 17.24 Audio Encoding Pipeline

Audio encoding runs independently from video encoding.

## Pipeline

```text
PCM Timeline
     │
Audio Mixer
     │
Audio Encoder
     │
Encoded Audio Chunks
     │
Muxer
```

---

## Audio Formats

| Codec | Status |
|-------|--------|
| AAC | MVP Default |
| Opus | WebM Export |
| PCM | WAV Export |
| FLAC | Future |

---

## Audio Interface

```ts
interface AudioEncoderConfig {
  codec: "aac" | "opus";
  sampleRate: number;
  channels: number;
  bitrate: number;
}
```

---

## Default Audio Settings

| Parameter | Default |
|----------|---------|
| Sample Rate | 48,000 Hz |
| Channels | Stereo |
| Bitrate | 192 kbps |

---

## Rules

Audio timestamps derive from the master timeline clock.

---

# 17.25 FFmpeg WASM Fallback Pipeline

FFmpeg WASM guarantees exports when WebCodecs is unavailable.

## Fallback Pipeline

```text
Rendered Frames
      │
PNG / YUV Buffers
      │
FFmpeg WASM
      │
Video Stream
      │
Mux Output
```

---

## FFmpeg Responsibilities

- Encode unsupported codecs.
- GIF export.
- MOV export.
- Image sequence export.
- Legacy browser support.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface FFmpegExportConfig {
  codec: string;
  crf: number;
  preset: string;
}
```

---

## FFmpeg Use Cases

| Situation | Use FFmpeg? |
|----------|-------------|
| Safari without WebCodecs | Yes |
| GIF Export | Yes |
| Image Sequence | Yes |
| MP4 without Hardware Encoder | Yes |

---

## Rules

FFmpeg runs inside a dedicated Worker.

---

# 17.26 Codec Capability Detection Engine

Before export, TryLipi detects browser encoding capabilities.

## Capability Pipeline

```text
Browser
   │
Capability Probe
   │
Codec Matrix
   │
Encoder Planner
```

---

## Capability Checks

| Capability | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| WebCodecs Available | Primary encoder |
| AV1 Support | Enable AV1 preset |
| VP9 Support | WebM export |
| Hardware Encoder | Fast export |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CodecCapabilities {
  webCodecs: boolean;
  av1: boolean;
  vp9: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

Capability detection runs once per session.

---

# 17.27 Hardware Acceleration Engine

TryLipi automatically detects GPU encoding support.

## Pipeline

```text
GPU Capability Probe
       │
VideoEncoder Test
       │
Acceleration Result
```

---

## Hardware Detection States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Hardware | GPU encoding enabled |
| Software | CPU encoder |
| Unsupported | FFmpeg fallback |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface HardwareEncoderState {
  accelerated: boolean;
  encoderName?: string;
}
```

---

## Export Strategy

| State | Strategy |
|------|----------|
| GPU Available | WebCodecs Hardware |
| GPU Busy | Software WebCodecs |
| Unsupported | FFmpeg |

---

## Rules

Hardware acceleration is optional, never required.

---

# 17.28 Encoding Preset Engine

Presets expose quality without exposing codec complexity.

## Built-in Presets

| Preset | Resolution | Bitrate |
|--------|------------|---------|
| Draft | 720p | 4 Mbps |

| Creator | 1080p | 12 Mbps |

| Platform | Default |

| YouTube | H.264 |
| Shorts | H.264 |
| Instagram | H.264 |
| TikTok | H.264 |
| Web | VP9 Optional |

---

## Rules

Presets remain editable.

---

# 17.29 Multi-Pass Encoding Strategy

Different export modes use different encoding strategies.

## Modes

| Mode | Strategy |
|------|----------|
| Draft | Single Pass |
| Standard | Single Pass |
| Creator | High Quality Single Pass |
| Master | Multi-Pass |

---

## Pipeline

```text
Render Frames
      │
Pass Planner
      │
Encoder
```

---

```ts
}
```

---

## Rules

Multi-pass exports prioritize quality over speed.

---

# 17.30 Encoder Worker Architecture

Encoding never blocks the UI.

```text
UI Thread
   │
Export Manager
   │
Encoder Worker
   │
Mux Worker
   │
File Writer
```

## Worker Responsibilities

| Worker | Task |
|--------|------|
| Encoder Worker | Encode video frames |
| Audio Worker | Encode audio |
| Mux Worker | Merge streams |

```ts
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

Workers communicate via transferable buffers.

---

# 17.31 Browser Compatibility Matrix

TryLipi chooses the optimal encoder per browser.

## Chromium Matrix

| Browser | WebCodecs | Hardware |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Chrome | ✅ | ✅ |
| Edge | ✅ | ✅ |
| Brave | ✅ | ✅ |
| Arc | ✅ | ✅ |
| Opera | ✅ | Usually |

## Non-Chromium Matrix

| Browser | Strategy |
|---------|----------|
| Firefox | FFmpeg WASM |
| Safari | WebCodecs if available, else FFmpeg |

## Rules

Browser detection never changes export quality presets.

| WebM | VP9 + Opus |
| MOV | H.264 + AAC |
| GIF | Indexed Frames |

```text
Video Chunks
      │
Audio Chunks
      │
Muxer
      │
Container Writer
```

```ts
interface ExportContainer {
  container: "mp4" | "webm" | "mov";
}
```

# 17.33 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes encoding metrics.

- Hardware acceleration state.
- Frames encoded.

- Bitrate.
- Dropped frames.
- Container size.

```ts
interface EncodingDiagnostics {

}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| WebCodecs Unsupported | Fallback activated. |

# 17.34 Acceptance Tests

## Codec Tests

- H.264 exports correctly.
- VP9 exports correctly.
- AV1 exports when supported.

## Audio Tests

- AAC synchronized.
- Opus synchronized.
- Stereo preserved.

## Worker Tests

- Transferable buffers reused.

## Container Tests

- MP4 plays correctly.
- WebM plays correctly.
- GIF exports loop correctly.

## Compatibility Tests

- Chrome uses WebCodecs.
- Firefox falls back to FFmpeg.
- Safari exports successfully.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 17.2)

1. WebCodecs is the primary browser encoder.
2. FFmpeg WASM is the universal fallback.
3. Encoding is isolated from rendering.
4. Hardware acceleration is preferred but optional.
5. Capability detection runs once per session.
6. Encoding presets abstract codec complexity.
7. Workers own encoding and muxing workloads.
8. Export containers preserve master timeline timestamps.
9. Preview rendering never uses export encoders.
10. Browser compatibility affects implementation, not exported timeline behavior.

# 17.41 GPU Rendering Philosophy

The GPU compositor is responsible for producing every preview frame and preparing frames for export.

Instead of rendering HTML elements directly, every timeline layer becomes a GPU texture that is composed inside a deterministic rendering pipeline.

---

## Golden GPU Principles

1. GPU renders every visible frame.
2. UI components never render directly into export frames.
3. Layers become GPU textures.
4. GPU rendering is deterministic.
5. Color management is centralized.
6. GPU and CPU share immutable frame metadata.
7. Preview renderer and export renderer share shaders whenever possible.

---

## Responsibilities

The GPU Engine owns:

- Layer compositing.
- Camera transforms.
- Blur shaders.
- Caption rendering.
- Mask rendering.
- Color conversion.
- Export frame composition.

---

# 17.42 GPU Compositor Architecture

The compositor combines render layers into one GPU frame.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Render Graph
     │
Texture Upload
     │
GPU Texture Atlas
     │
Shader Pipeline
     │
Framebuffer
     │
Preview / Export Frame
```

---

## GPU Layer Stack

| Layer | GPU Texture |
|--------|-------------|
| Background | Texture |
| Video | Texture |
| B-Roll | Texture |
| Camera Crop | Matrix Transform |
| Captions | Glyph Texture |
| Emoji | Sprite Texture |
| Cursor Highlight | Vector Texture |
| Overlay | Texture |

---

## Compositor Interface

```ts
interface GPUCompositor {
  compose(frameNumber: number): GPUFrame;
}
```

---

## Rules

Layer ordering is controlled exclusively by the Render Graph.

---

# 17.43 WebGL Rendering Backend

WebGL2 is the MVP rendering backend.

## Rendering Pipeline

```text
Frame Data
    │
Texture Upload
    │
Vertex Shader
    │
Fragment Shader
    │
Framebuffer
```

---

## WebGL Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Texture Rendering | Video frames. |
| Camera Scaling | Viewport transforms. |
| Blend Modes | Layer composition. |
| Blur | Caption shadows. |
| Masks | Shape clipping. |

---

## GPU Context Interface

```ts
interface WebGLRenderer {
  gl: WebGL2RenderingContext;
}
```

---

## Required Extensions

| Extension | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| EXT_color_buffer_float | Float framebuffers |
| OES_texture_float | Float textures |
| EXT_disjoint_timer_query | GPU profiling |

---

## Rules

WebGL context loss must be recoverable.

---

# 17.44 Future WebGPU Backend

WebGPU becomes the future rendering backend.

---

## WebGPU Goals

- Better compute shaders.
- Faster texture uploads.
- GPU timeline processing.
- AI preprocessing.
- HDR rendering.

---

## Architecture

```text
Render Graph
      │
GPU Buffers
      │
Render Pipeline
      │
Texture Output
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface WebGPURenderer {
  device: GPUDevice;
}
```

---

## Migration Strategy

| Feature | WebGL | WebGPU |
|--------|--------|---------|
| Preview | MVP | Future |
| Export | MVP | Future |
| Blur | Shader | Compute Shader |
| Color Conversion | Shader | Compute Shader |

---

## Rules

Renderer abstraction hides backend differences.

---

# 17.45 Texture Atlas Engine

Thousands of textures cannot be uploaded every frame.

Atlas groups reusable textures.

## Atlas Architecture

```text
Texture Atlas
├── Caption Glyphs
├── Emoji Sprites
├── Icons
├── Shapes
├── Cursor Assets
└── Sticker Assets
```

---

## Pipeline

```text
Asset
  │
Atlas Builder
  │
Texture Coordinates
  │
Shader Sampling
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface TextureAtlasEntry {
  atlasId: string;
  uv: Float32Array;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Reduced GPU uploads.
- Faster draw calls.
- Better batching.

---

## Rules

Atlas is immutable during export.

---

# 17.46 Layer Composition Shader Pipeline

Shaders combine layers.

## Shader Pipeline

```text
Vertex Shader
      │
Transform Matrix
      │
Fragment Shader
      │
Blend Output
```

---

## Vertex Responsibilities

- Translation.
- Scale.
- Rotation.
- UV mapping.

---

## Fragment Responsibilities

- Blend colors.
- Alpha composition.
- Blur.
- Gradient rendering.
- Mask clipping.

---

## Shader Interface

```ts
interface LayerShader {
  uniforms: ShaderUniforms;
}
```

---

## Supported Blend Modes

| Blend | Shader |
|-------|--------|
| Normal | MVP |
| Multiply | MVP |
| Overlay | MVP |
| Screen | MVP |
| Soft Light | Future |
| Color Dodge | Future |

---

## Rules

Every blend mode is implemented as a fragment shader.

---

# 17.47 RGBA → YUV Conversion Engine

Video encoders expect YUV frames instead of RGBA.

## Conversion Pipeline

```text
RGBA Framebuffer
      │
GPU Conversion Shader
      │
YUV420 Buffer
      │
Encoder
```

---

## Supported Formats

| Format | Use |
|--------|-----|
| RGBA8 | Preview |
| YUV420P | MP4 Export |
| NV12 | Hardware Encoding |
| RGBA16F | Future HDR |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ColorConversion {
  inputFormat: string;
  outputFormat: string;
}
```

---

## Conversion Rules

- GPU performs conversion whenever possible.
- CPU fallback available.

---

# 17.48 Color Management Pipeline

Consistent colors across preview and export.

## Color Pipeline

```text
Source Asset
     │
Decode
     │
Working Color Space
     │
GPU Composition
     │
Export Color Space
```

---

## Working Spaces

| Color Space | Status |
|-------------|--------|
| sRGB | MVP Default |
| Display-P3 | Future |
| Rec.709 | Export |
| HDR10 | Future |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ColorProfile {
  workingSpace: "srgb" | "rec709";
}
```

---

## Gamma Rules

- Linearize before blending.
- Apply output gamma after composition.

---

# 17.49 HDR & Wide Color Roadmap

Future exports support HDR workflows.

## HDR Goals

| Feature | Status |
|--------|--------|
| Display-P3 Preview | Future |
| HDR10 Export | Future |
| HLG Export | Future |
| 10-bit Pipeline | Future |

---

## HDR Pipeline

```text
16-bit Texture
      │
Wide Gamut Shader
      │
HDR Export
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface HDRSettings {
  enabled: boolean;
}
```

---

## Rules

HDR remains compatible with SDR exports.

---

# 17.50 GPU Memory Management

GPU memory is limited.

The compositor aggressively manages texture lifetimes.

## Memory Pipeline

```text
Decoded Asset
      │
Texture Cache
      │
GPU Texture Pool
      │
LRU Eviction
```

---

## Texture States

| State | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Resident | In GPU memory |
| Cached | CPU memory |
| Evicted | Reload when needed |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface GPUTexturePool {
  residentTextures: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Textures unused beyond threshold become eviction candidates.

---

# 17.51 Render Pass Pipeline

Rendering occurs through multiple GPU passes.

## Pass Sequence

```text
Pass 1 Background
Pass 2 Video
Pass 3 Camera Transform
Pass 4 B-Roll
Pass 5 Captions
Pass 6 Emoji
Pass 7 Overlays
Pass 8 Cursor Effects
```

---

## Pass Interface

```ts
interface RenderPass {
  passId: string;
  shader: string;
}
```

---

## Pass Rules

Each pass writes to an intermediate framebuffer.

---

# 17.52 GPU Synchronization Engine

GPU and CPU timelines must stay synchronized.

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
CPU Render Queue
      │
GPU Command Queue
      │
Fence
      │
Frame Ready
```

---

## Synchronization Interface

```ts
interface GPUFence {
  frameNumber: number;
}
```

---

## Synchronization Goals

| Goal | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Prevent tearing | Frame ordering |
| Prevent stale textures | Upload synchronization |
| Export consistency | Deterministic ordering |

---

## Rules

GPU fences complete before encoding begins.

---

# 17.53 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes GPU metrics.

## Metrics

- GPU render time.
- Draw calls.
- Shader switches.
- Texture uploads.
- Texture cache hit rate.
- GPU memory usage.
- Framebuffer allocations.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface GPUDiagnostics {
  drawCalls: number;
  textureUploads: number;
  gpuMemoryMB: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Texture Overflow | GPU pool exhausted. |
| Shader Compile Failure | Fallback shader. |
| Context Lost | WebGL context reset. |
| GPU Stall | Fence timeout. |

---

# 17.54 Acceptance Tests

## Shader Tests

- Blend modes render correctly.
- Camera transforms deterministic.
- Caption shadows identical.

## Texture Tests

- Atlas coordinates stable.
- Emoji batching works.
- Texture eviction reloads correctly.

## Color Tests

- Preview matches export.
- Gamma preserved.
- Rec.709 output validated.

## GPU Tests

- Draw calls minimized.
- Context recovery works.
- GPU fences synchronize encoding.

## Performance Tests

- 60 FPS preview sustained.
- GPU memory pool reused.
- No texture leaks across long projects.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 17.3)

1. GPU compositor owns all visual composition.
2. WebGL2 is the MVP rendering backend.
3. WebGPU remains an abstraction-compatible future backend.
4. Texture atlases minimize draw calls.
5. Every layer is rendered through shaders.
6. RGBA is converted to YUV before encoding.
7. Color management is centralized through a working color space.
8. GPU memory uses pooled textures with LRU eviction.
9. Render passes write into intermediate framebuffers.
10. GPU synchronization guarantees identical preview and export output.

---

# 17.61 Background Export Philosophy

Exports must **never block editing**.

A creator should be able to continue editing another project while an export runs in the background.

This requires complete separation between:

- Timeline Editing
- Rendering
- Encoding
- File Writing

---

## Golden Background Export Principles

1. Exports run independently of UI editing.
2. Every export uses an immutable project snapshot.
3. Multiple exports may run simultaneously.
4. Exports survive temporary UI inactivity.
5. Export progress is deterministic.
6. Background workers own rendering workloads.
7. Failed exports are resumable whenever possible.

---

## Responsibilities

Background Export Engine owns:

- Export queue.
- Worker orchestration.
- Parallel rendering.
- Pause/resume.
- Progress estimation.
- Export recovery.
- Notifications.

---

# 17.62 Export Queue Architecture

All exports enter a centralized queue.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
User Clicks Export
        │
Export Queue
        │
Export Scheduler
        │
Worker Pool
        │
Renderer
        │
Encoder
        │
Completed Export
```

---

## Queue States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Waiting | Pending export |
| Preparing | Snapshot creation |
| Rendering | Frames rendering |
| Encoding | Video encoding |
| Finalizing | Muxing / file writing |
| Completed | Finished |
| Failed | Recoverable error |
| Cancelled | User cancelled |

---

## Queue Interface

```ts
interface ExportQueueItem {
  exportId: string;
  projectId: string;
  status: ExportStatus;
  priority: number;
}
```

---

## Queue Rules

- FIFO by default.
- Priority exports may bypass waiting jobs.
- Queue survives UI navigation inside the app.

---

# 17.63 Export Session Manager

Every export becomes an isolated immutable session.

## Session Lifecycle

```text
Create Snapshot
      │
Allocate Workers
      │
Render Timeline
      │
Encode Streams
      │
Finalize Container
      │
Complete Session
```

---

## Session Interface

```ts
interface ExportSession {
  sessionId: string;
  snapshotId: string;
  startedAtUs: number;
  status: ExportStatus;
}
```

---

## Session Snapshot

Contains:

- Timeline graph.
- Assets.
- Fonts.
- Camera timeline.
- Captions.
- Export settings.

---

## Rules

Edits made after snapshot creation never affect an active export.

---

# 17.64 Worker Pool Orchestration Engine

Rendering is distributed across dedicated workers.

## Worker Architecture

```text
Export Manager
      │
 ┌────┼───────────────┐
 ▼    ▼               ▼
Render Worker 1   Render Worker 2
 ▼                 ▼
Chunk Output    Chunk Output
      └────┬───────┘
           ▼
      Encoder Worker
```

---

## Worker Types

| Worker | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Render Worker | Render frames |
| Audio Worker | Audio mixing |
| GPU Worker | Texture composition |
| Encoder Worker | Encode video |
| File Writer Worker | Save output |

---

## Worker Pool Interface

```ts
interface WorkerPool {
  renderWorkers: number;
  encoderWorkers: number;
}
```

---

## Worker Scaling

| Device | Workers |
|--------|---------|
| Low-end Laptop | 2 |
| Mid-range Laptop | 4 |
| High-end Desktop | 6–8 |

---

## Rules

Worker count adapts to CPU capabilities.

---

# 17.65 Parallel Frame Rendering Engine

Frames are rendered in parallel chunks.

## Chunk Rendering Pipeline

```text
Frame Queue
     │
Chunk Generator
     │
Worker Pool
     │
Rendered Chunk Buffers
```

---

## Chunk Size Strategy

| Resolution | Frames Per Chunk |
|------------|------------------|
| 720p | 180 |
| 1080p | 120 |
| 1440p | 90 |
| 4K | 60 |

---

## Chunk Interface

```ts
interface FrameChunk {
  chunkId: string;
  startFrame: number;
  endFrame: number;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Parallel rendering.
- Better memory control.
- Resume from chunk boundaries.
- Progress estimation.

---

## Rules

Chunks maintain original timeline order.

---

# 17.66 Chunk Rendering Architecture

Chunks flow independently through rendering and encoding.

## Architecture

```text
Chunk
 │
Render
 │
GPU Compose
 │
Encode
 │
Release Buffers
```

---

## Chunk States

| State | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Queued | Awaiting worker |
| Rendering | GPU rendering |
| Encoded | Encoded video chunk |
| Flushed | Written to container |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ChunkProgress {
  renderedFrames: number;
  encodedFrames: number;
}
```

---

## Rules

Completed chunks release GPU memory immediately.

---

# 17.67 Progress Estimation Engine

Progress must feel accurate.

## Progress Pipeline

```text
Frame Count
     │
Rendered Frames
     │
Encoded Frames
     │
ETA Calculator
```

---

## Progress Formula

```text
Progress =
Rendered Frames
--------------------
Total Frames
```

---

## ETA Signals

| Signal | Used? |
|--------|-------|
| Remaining Frames | Yes |
| Average Frame Time | Yes |
| Encoding Latency | Yes |
| Disk Writing | Yes |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ExportProgress {
  percentage: number;
  etaSeconds: number;
}
```

---

## UI Milestones

| Progress | UI |
|----------|----|
| 0–5% | Preparing |
| 5–70% | Rendering |
| 70–95% | Encoding |
| 95–100% | Finalizing |

---

## Rules

ETA updates every few seconds, not every frame.

---

# 17.68 Pause / Resume Export Engine

Users may pause exports without losing work.

## Lifecycle

```text
Rendering
   │
Pause
   │
Persist Worker State
   │
Resume
   │
Continue Rendering
```

---

## Pause Interface

```ts
interface ExportPauseState {
  pausedChunkId: string;
  frameOffset: number;
}
```

---

## Resume Behavior

| Situation | Resume Point |
|----------|--------------|
| Pause Rendering | Current chunk |
| Pause Encoding | Current encoder buffer |
| Pause Finalizing | Container writing stage |

---

## Rules

Resume always starts from chunk boundary.

---

# 17.69 Memory-Aware Render Scheduler

Rendering adapts to available RAM and GPU memory.

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text
Memory Monitor
      │
Chunk Planner
      │
Worker Allocation
```

---

## Memory Thresholds

| Available Memory | Behavior |
|-----------------|----------|
| High | Larger chunks |
| Medium | Default chunks |
| Low | Smaller chunks |
| Critical | Reduce concurrency |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface MemorySchedule {
  chunkSize: number;
  maxWorkers: number;
}
```

---

## Dynamic Adjustments

- Reduce worker count.
- Flush texture cache.
- Reduce preview priority.
- Delay next chunk.

---

## Rules

Scheduler never exceeds safe memory thresholds.

---

# 17.70 Export Recovery Engine

Exports recover from recoverable failures.

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Export Failure
      │
Checkpoint Lookup
      │
Restore Chunk
      │
Resume Export
```

---

## Checkpoint Contents

- Chunk ID.
- Frame index.
- Encoder state.
- Export metadata.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ExportCheckpoint {
  chunkId: string;
  frameNumber: number;
}
```

---

## Recoverable Failures

| Failure | Recovery |
|--------|----------|
| Worker Crash | Restart chunk |
| GPU Context Loss | Recreate textures |
| Encoder Restart | Resume chunk |
| Memory Pressure | Retry smaller chunk |

---

## Rules

Project snapshot never changes during recovery.

---

# 17.71 Background Notification Pipeline

Users receive export updates without watching progress.

## Notification Pipeline

```text
Export State
      │
Notification Manager
      │
Toast / Browser Notification
```

---

## Notification Events

| Event | Notification |
|------|--------------|
| Started | Export started |
| Half Complete | Optional |
| Completed | Download ready |
| Failed | Retry available |
| Cancelled | Export cancelled |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ExportNotification {
  exportId: string;
  type: string;
}
```

---

## Rules

Notifications are optional and user-controlled.

---

# 17.72 Multi-Export Queue Strategy

Supports exporting multiple projects simultaneously.

## Queue Example

```text
Queue
├── Project A (Rendering)
├── Project B (Waiting)
├── Project C (Encoding)
└── Project D (Paused)
```

---

## Scheduling Policies

| Policy | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| FIFO | Default |
| Priority | Premium future |
| Sequential | Low-memory mode |
| Parallel | High-memory mode |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ExportQueueStrategy {
  policy: "fifo" | "parallel";
}
```

---

## Rules

Parallel exports share worker pools fairly.

---

# 17.73 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes export infrastructure metrics.

## Metrics

- Queue size.
- Active workers.
- Render FPS.
- Encoded chunks.
- ETA accuracy.
- Memory usage.
- Recovery attempts.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ExportQueueDiagnostics {
  activeExports: number;
  activeWorkers: number;
  queueLength: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Queue Stalled | No worker progress. |
| Worker Restarted | Recovery initiated. |
| Memory Pressure | Concurrency reduced. |
| Checkpoint Recovery | Export resumed. |

---

# 17.74 Acceptance Tests

## Queue Tests

- Multiple exports queue correctly.
- Priority exports schedule correctly.

## Worker Tests

- Render workers distribute chunks.
- Encoder worker receives ordered chunks.
- Worker restart resumes export.

## Pause/Resume Tests

- Pause preserves chunk state.
- Resume continues correctly.
- Progress remains accurate.

## Recovery Tests

- GPU context loss recovered.
- Worker crash resumes chunk.
- Memory pressure reduces chunk size.

## Performance Tests

- UI remains responsive during export.
- Multiple exports share resources safely.
- ETA remains within acceptable tolerance.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 17.4)

1. Exports always run from immutable project snapshots.
2. Export queue owns scheduling independently from the UI.
3. Rendering is distributed across worker pools.
4. Frames are rendered and encoded in ordered chunks.
5. Progress is based on rendered and encoded frame counts.
6. Pause/resume operates at chunk boundaries.
7. Memory-aware scheduling dynamically adjusts concurrency.
8. Export checkpoints enable recovery from worker failures.
9. Multiple exports may coexist through fair worker scheduling.
10. Background exports never block timeline editing.

# 17.81 Export Quality Philosophy

The export engine must produce platform-optimized videos while preserving creator intent.

Creators shouldn't need to understand codecs or bitrate theory. Instead, TryLipi exposes simple presets while internally selecting the optimal rendering pipeline.

---

## Golden Export Quality Principles

1. Export quality is deterministic.
2. Resolution scaling never modifies timeline metadata.
3. Frame rate conversion preserves animation timing.
4. Bitrate presets optimize for destination platform.
5. Export metadata remains platform compatible.
6. Thumbnail generation shares the render graph.
7. Every export format uses the same project snapshot.

---

## Responsibilities

The Quality Engine owns:

- Resolution presets.
- Frame rate presets.
- Bitrate calculation.
- Codec tuning.
- Thumbnail generation.
- Export metadata.
- Delivery pipeline.

---

# 19.01 Project System Philosophy

The **Project System** is the operating system of TryLipi.

Every creator action—editing videos, adding captions, generating B-roll, applying Smart Zoom, AI edits, voiceovers, thumbnails, scripts, camera movements, and exports—is represented inside a deterministic project architecture.

A TryLipi project is **not** a rendered video.

It is a complete description of **how** a video should be rendered.

Unlike Premiere (`.prproj`) or Final Cut libraries, TryLipi projects are designed to be:

- Browser-native.
- Cloud-native.
- Offline-capable.
- AI-native.
- Versionable.
- Portable between devices.
- Deterministic across preview and export.

---

## Golden Project Principles

1. Projects are immutable snapshots of editable state.
2. Assets are referenced, never embedded into timeline objects.
3. Every entity has a globally unique identifier.
4. Timeline edits never modify original assets.
5. Projects remain portable between browsers and operating systems.
6. Undo/Redo operates through snapshot graphs.
7. Project schema remains forward-compatible across TryLipi releases.

---

## Responsibilities

The Project System owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Workspace | Root container for projects and shared assets. |
| Project | Complete editable video document. |
| Timeline | References media and edits. |
| Assets | Imported media library. |
| Snapshots | Immutable editing history. |
| Metadata | Project identity and configuration. |
| Manifest | Version and dependency information. |
| Migration Engine | Upgrade older projects safely. |

---

# 19.02 Workspace Architecture

A workspace is the highest-level container inside TryLipi.

Every creator works inside one or more workspaces.

## Workspace Hierarchy

```text
Workspace
│
├── Projects
│   ├── Launch Reel.trylipi
│   ├── YouTube Tutorial.trylipi
│   └── Shorts Batch.trylipi
│
├── Shared Assets
│   ├── Brand Logos
│   ├── Intro Music
│   ├── LUTs
│   └── Fonts
│
├── Templates
│
├── AI Presets
│
├── Camera Presets
│
└── Export History
```

---

## Workspace Responsibilities

| Resource | Scope |
|----------|-------|
| Projects | Workspace |
| Fonts | Workspace |
| Brand Assets | Workspace |
| AI Presets | Workspace |
| Templates | Workspace |
| Export History | Workspace |
| Team Library | Future |

---

## Workspace Interface

```ts
interface Workspace {
  workspaceId: string;
  ownerId: string;
  name: string;
  createdAtUs: number;
  updatedAtUs: number;
  projectIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Workspace Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Personal | Single creator workspace. |
| Team | Shared workspace for collaborators. |
| Brand | Workspace with shared brand kit. |
| Enterprise | Organization-wide workspace. |

---

## Engineering Rules

- Projects cannot exist outside a workspace.
- Shared assets are workspace-scoped.
- Team permissions never modify project ownership.

---

# 19.03 Canonical `.trylipi` Project Format

Every TryLipi project is stored as a canonical `.trylipi` package.

This format is designed to be:

- Human inspectable.
- Compressible.
- Streamable.
- Versionable.
- Migration-safe.

---

## Project Package Layout

```text
launch-reel.trylipi
│
├── manifest.json
├── timeline.json
├── assets.json
├── captions.json
├── camera.json
├── audio.json
├── ai.json
├── export.json
│
├── thumbnails/
│
├── cache/
│
└── history/
```

---

## Package Components

| File | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| manifest.json | Project metadata. |
| timeline.json | Timeline graph. |
| assets.json | Asset registry. |
| captions.json | Caption metadata. |
| camera.json | Camera timeline. |
| audio.json | Audio metadata. |
| ai.json | AI-generated edits. |
| export.json | Export presets/history. |

---

## Design Goals

| Goal | Why |
|------|-----|
| Portable | Works across browsers/devices. |
| Diffable | Future version history. |
| Partial Loading | Large projects load incrementally. |
| Compression Friendly | Fast cloud sync. |

---

## Engineering Rules

- Assets are referenced by IDs.
- Timeline never stores binary media.
- Project package is immutable during export.

---

# 19.04 Project Manifest Specification

The manifest is the project's root metadata document.

Everything begins here.

## Manifest Structure

```json
{
  "projectId": "proj_01JTRYP123",
  "schemaVersion": "3.1.0",
  "workspaceId": "ws_01HXYZ",
  "name": "Launch Reel",
  "createdAtUs": 1756300200000000,
  "updatedAtUs": 1756302800000000,
  "thumbnailAssetId": "asset_thumb_01",
  "timelineId": "timeline_main",
  "durationUs": 48300000,
  "frameRate": 60,
  "canvas": {
    "width": 1080,
    "height": 1920,
    "aspectRatio": "9:16"
  }
}
```

---

## Required Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| projectId | Globally unique project ID. |
| schemaVersion | Project schema version. |
| workspaceId | Parent workspace. |
| timelineId | Root timeline. |
| createdAtUs | Creation timestamp. |
| updatedAtUs | Last modification timestamp. |

---

## Optional Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| thumbnailAssetId | Project poster frame. |
| brandPresetId | Brand kit reference. |
| language | Default transcript language. |
| aiProfileId | Creator AI profile. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Manifest is loaded before every other file.

---

# 19.05 Project Dependency Graph

Every editable object belongs to a dependency graph.

Nothing exists independently.

## Dependency Graph

```text
Project
│
├── Timeline
│   ├── Video Tracks
│   ├── Audio Tracks
│   ├── Caption Tracks
│   └── Camera Timeline
│
├── Asset Registry
│
├── AI Metadata
│
└── Export Settings
```

---

## Dependency Relationships

| Parent | Child |
|--------|-------|
| Project | Timeline |
| Timeline | Clips |
| Clip | Asset |
| Caption Track | Transcript |
| Camera Timeline | Smart Zoom |
| Export Settings | Presets |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ProjectDependency {
  sourceId: string;
  targetId: string;
  relation: string;
}
```

---

## Why Dependency Graph Exists

- Safe deletion.
- Asset cleanup.
- AI recomputation.
- Export planning.
- Migration validation.

---

## Engineering Rules

No circular dependencies are allowed.

---

# 19.06 Asset Ownership Model

Assets live independently from timelines.

## Ownership Hierarchy

```text
Workspace
│
Project
│
Asset Registry
│
```

```ts
}
```

|------|---------|

| Referenced | Used on timeline. |

## Snapshot Guarantees

| Portable | Sync across devices. |
| Hashable | Version comparison. |

---

# 19.09 Snapshot Graph & History Architecture

Undo/Redo is powered by a directed snapshot graph.

```text
S1
│
S2
│
S3
├──── S4
│
└──── S5
      │
      S6
```

```ts
}
```

---

## History Operations

| Operation | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Undo | Parent snapshot. |
| Redo | Child snapshot. |
| Restore | Jump to snapshot. |
| Branch | Future collaboration. |

---

|------|-------------|

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 19.1)

1. `.trylipi` is the canonical project package format.
2. Every project belongs to exactly one workspace.
3. Manifest loads before every other project file.
4. Timeline owns edits; Asset Registry owns media.
5. Assets are referenced by immutable IDs.
6. Project snapshots are append-only and immutable.
7. Undo/Redo is implemented through a snapshot graph.
8. Dependency graphs must remain acyclic.
9. Export operates on immutable snapshots only.
10. Project identity and schema version never change after creation.

# 19.21 Media Library Philosophy

The **Media Library** is the canonical source of truth for every reusable asset inside a TryLipi project.

Nothing on the timeline owns binary media.

Every clip, overlay, sticker, caption background, emoji, audio file, LUT, font, and AI-generated image references an asset inside the Media Library.

This architecture enables:

- Non-destructive editing.
- Asset reuse across timelines.
- Offline editing.
- AI-generated asset management.
- Incremental downloads.
- Fast rendering through asset caching.

---

## Golden Media Library Principles

1. Assets are immutable after import.
2. Timeline stores references, never binary data.
3. Every imported asset receives a globally unique Asset ID.
4. Duplicate assets are automatically detected.
5. Assets can exist without being used on a timeline.
6. Local and cloud assets share one abstraction.
7. Import pipeline is asynchronous and resumable.

---

## Responsibilities

The Media Library owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Asset Registry | Canonical asset database. |
| Import Engine | All asset ingestion. |
| Storage Layer | Local/cloud storage abstraction. |
| Upload Queue | Cloud synchronization. |
| Preview Cache | Posters & thumbnails. |
| Integrity Engine | Hash verification. |
| Streaming Loader | Incremental asset loading. |

---

# 19.22 Asset Registry Architecture

The **Asset Registry** is the project's internal media database.

Every imported resource becomes exactly one asset record.

## Asset Registry Hierarchy

```text
Workspace
│
Project
│
Asset Registry
│
├── Videos
├── Images
├── Audio
├── GIFs
├── Stickers
├── Emojis
├── Fonts
├── LUTs
├── AI Generated Assets
└── Screen Recordings
```

---

## Registry Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Identity | Generate Asset IDs. |
| Metadata | Duration, dimensions, MIME type. |
| References | Timeline ownership. |
| Storage Location | Local/cloud path. |
| Integrity | SHA-256 fingerprint. |

---

## Asset Registry Interface

```ts
interface AssetRegistry {
  assetId: string;
  assetType: AssetType;
  storageId: string;
  metadata: AssetMetadata;
}
```

---

## Asset Types (MVP)

| Asset Type | Examples |
|------------|----------|
| Video | MP4, MOV, WebM |
| Image | PNG, JPEG, WebP |
| Audio | MP3, WAV, AAC |
| Screen Recording | Browser recordings |
| GIF | Imported GIF |
| Emoji | Unicode & custom emoji |
| Sticker | PNG/WebP overlays |
| Font | TTF, OTF |
| LUT | `.cube` |
| AI Image | Generated thumbnails/B-roll |

---

## Engineering Rules

- Asset IDs are immutable.
- Registry survives autosave and recovery.
- Registry never stores decoded media.

1. Asset Registry is the canonical media database.

# 19.41 Asset Lifecycle Philosophy

Every asset inside TryLipi follows a deterministic lifecycle from import until permanent deletion.

The lifecycle guarantees that assets are:

- Never modified destructively.
- Always recoverable while referenced.
- Efficiently cached.
- Automatically optimized for editing.
- Safely garbage collected when unused.

Assets transition through states instead of being immediately deleted or duplicated.

---

## Golden Asset Lifecycle Principles

1. Assets are immutable after import.
2. Derived assets (proxies, thumbnails, previews) are separate resources.
3. Timeline references keep assets alive.
4. Deletion is reference-aware.
5. Storage optimization never changes source assets.
6. Cache is disposable; assets are not.
7. Garbage collection is deterministic.

---

## Responsibilities

The Asset Lifecycle Engine owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Asset State Machine | Asset lifecycle transitions. |
| Proxy Generator | Editing proxies. |
| Thumbnail Generator | Posters & previews. |
| Deduplication | Duplicate detection. |
| Cache Manager | Preview cache lifecycle. |
| Garbage Collector | Remove orphaned resources. |

---

# 19.42 Asset Lifecycle State Machine

Every asset transitions through predefined states.

## Lifecycle Diagram

```text
Imported
   │
Analyzing
   │
Registered
   │
Ready
   │
Referenced
   │
Unused
   │
Archived
   │
Deleted
```

---

## Asset States

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Imported | Binary received. |
| Analyzing | Metadata extraction running. |
| Registered | Added to registry. |
| Ready | Available for editing. |
| Referenced | Used by timeline/project. |
| Unused | Exists but unused. |
| Archived | Hidden but recoverable. |
| Deleted | Removed permanently. |

---

## Lifecycle Interface

```ts
interface AssetLifecycleState {
  assetId: string;
  state:
    | "imported"
    | "analyzing"
    | "ready"
    | "referenced"
    | "unused"
    | "archived"
    | "deleted";
}
```

---

## Transition Rules

| From | To |
|------|----|
| Imported | Analyzing |
| Analyzing | Ready |
| Ready | Referenced |
| Referenced | Unused |
| Unused | Archived |
| Archived | Deleted |

---

## Engineering Rules

Assets cannot transition directly from **Referenced** to **Deleted**.

---

# 19.43 Proxy Generation Engine

High-resolution videos are expensive to decode during editing.

TryLipi automatically creates lightweight editing proxies.

## Proxy Pipeline

```text
Original Video
      │
Media Analyzer
      │
Proxy Planner
      │
WebCodecs / FFmpeg
      │
Proxy Storage
      │
Timeline Preview
```

---

## Proxy Levels

| Proxy | Resolution | Usage |
|-------|------------|------|
| Tiny | 240p | Slow devices |
| Low | 480p | Basic editing |
| Medium | 720p | Default preview |
| High | 1080p | High-quality preview |

---

## Proxy Interface

```ts
interface VideoProxy {
  proxyId: string;
  assetId: string;
  resolution: string;
  bitrateMbps: number;
}
```

---

## Proxy Metadata

| Metadata | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Resolution | Preview scaling |
| Bitrate | Faster decoding |
| FPS | Match source |
| Duration | Timeline sync |

---

## Engineering Rules

- Proxy duration must exactly equal source duration.
- Proxy timestamps must match original timestamps.

---

# 19.44 Adaptive Proxy Selection Engine

The editor automatically selects the best proxy for current conditions.

## Selection Pipeline

```text
Device Capability
       │
Canvas Zoom
       │
Playback Mode
       │
Proxy Selector
```

---

## Inputs

| Input | Effect |
|------|--------|
| Device RAM | Proxy quality |
| GPU Capability | Resolution selection |
| Timeline Zoom | Detail level |
| Playback FPS | Proxy switching |

---

## Selection Matrix

| Device | Default Proxy |
|--------|---------------|
| Low-end Laptop | 480p |
| Mid-range Laptop | 720p |
| High-end Desktop | 1080p |
| Export | Original Asset |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ProxySelection {
  assetId: string;
  selectedProxyId: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Exports always use the original asset—not proxies.

---

# 19.45 Thumbnail & Poster Generation Pipeline

Every visual asset receives a thumbnail and poster frame.

## Pipeline

```text
Asset
 │
Frame Extractor
 │
Poster Generator
 │
Thumbnail Generator
 │
Cache
```

## Thumbnail Types

| Type | Usage |
|------|-------|
| Poster | Asset card |
| Timeline Thumbnail | Timeline strip |
| Grid Thumbnail | Media library |
| AI Thumbnail | Future recommendations |

---

## Generation Strategy

| Asset | Thumbnail Source |
|------|------------------|
| Video | First meaningful frame |
| Image | Image resize |
| GIF | Representative frame |
| Recording | First non-black frame |

---

## Thumbnail Interface

```ts
interface AssetThumbnail {
  assetId: string;
  posterAssetId: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Thumbnails are generated asynchronously after import.

---

# 19.46 Timeline Hover Preview Engine

Hover previews provide instant visual feedback.

## Preview Pipeline

```text
Video Asset
     │
Preview Sampler
     │
Keyframe Strip
     │
Hover Preview Cache
```

---

## Preview Strip Generation

```text
00:00
00:02
00:04
00:06
00:08
...
```

---

## Preview Density

| Duration | Preview Interval |
|----------|------------------|
| Less than 30s | Every 1s |
| 30s–5m | Every 2s |
| 5m–30m | Every 5s |
| Greater than 30m | Adaptive |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface HoverPreviewStrip {
  assetId: string;
  previewFrames: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Preview strips reuse decoded keyframes whenever possible.

---

# 19.47 Deduplication Engine

Duplicate imports waste storage and upload bandwidth.

Every imported asset is fingerprinted.

## Deduplication Pipeline

```text
Imported Asset
      │
SHA-256
      │
Registry Lookup
      │
Duplicate Decision
```

---

## Duplicate Outcomes

| Outcome | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| Exact Match | Reuse asset |
| Different File Same Metadata | Keep both |
| Same Hash Different Name | Alias existing asset |
| Partial Match | Independent asset |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface DeduplicationResult {
  duplicate: boolean;
  existingAssetId?: string;
}
```

---

## Deduplication Scope

| Scope | Supported |
|------|-----------|
| Same Project | Yes |
| Same Workspace | Yes |
| Different Workspace | Future |
| Cloud Library | Future |

---

## Engineering Rules

Asset IDs remain stable even when aliases exist.

---

# 19.48 Asset Garbage Collection Engine

Unused derived resources are cleaned automatically.

## Garbage Collection Pipeline

```text
Registry Scan
      │
Reference Counter
      │
Unused Asset Finder
      │
Cleanup Planner
```

---

## Garbage Collection Targets

| Resource | Collect? |
|----------|----------|
| Proxy Files | Yes |
| Thumbnail Cache | Yes |
| Preview Cache | Yes |
| Temporary Upload Blob | Yes |
| Source Asset | Only when deleted |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface GarbageCollectionJob {
  assetId: string;
  reclaimableBytes: number;
}
```

---

## Collection Rules

Assets referenced by:

- Timeline
- Undo history
- Snapshot history
- Export queue

cannot be collected.

---

# 19.49 Storage Optimization Engine

Storage optimization reduces disk usage automatically.

## Optimization Pipeline

```text
Storage Scan
      │
Optimization Planner
      │
Cache Cleanup
      │
Proxy Compression
```

---

## Optimization Targets

| Target | Strategy |
|--------|----------|
| Preview Cache | Remove oldest previews |
| Proxy Cache | Remove unused proxies |
| Upload Cache | Remove completed uploads |
| Temporary Decode Cache | Immediate cleanup |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface StorageOptimization {
  bytesRecovered: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Optimization never deletes original assets.

---

# 19.50 Asset Cache Eviction Strategy

Preview assets live in disposable caches.

## Cache Hierarchy

```text
Memory Cache
     │
Disk Cache
     │
OPFS Cache
```

---

## Eviction Strategy

| Cache | Policy |
|------|--------|
| Memory | LRU |
| GPU Texture | LRU |
| Preview Strip | LFU + LRU |
| Thumbnails | Persistent until storage pressure |

---

## Cache Interface

```ts
interface AssetCacheEntry {
  assetId: string;
  lastAccessedUs: number;
}
```

---

## Eviction Priority

1. Temporary decode cache.
2. Preview strip cache.
3. Proxy cache.
4. Thumbnail cache.
5. Original assets never evicted.

---

## Engineering Rules

Cache eviction is transparent to creators.

---

# 19.51 Preview Artifact Generation Pipeline

TryLipi generates reusable preview artifacts after import.

## Generated Artifacts

| Artifact | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Poster | Asset card |
| Thumbnail Strip | Timeline preview |
| Waveform | Audio preview |
| Duration Preview | Metadata |
| Dominant Color | UI placeholder |

---

## Artifact Pipeline

```text
Imported Asset
      │
Artifact Generator
      │
Artifact Registry
      │
Preview UI
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface PreviewArtifact {
  artifactId: string;
  assetId: string;
  artifactType: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Artifacts regenerate only when source asset changes.

---

# 19.52 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes asset lifecycle metrics.

## Metrics

- Imported assets.
- Proxy generation time.
- Thumbnail generation latency.
- Cache hit rate.
- Storage reclaimed.
- Duplicate assets.
- Garbage collection runs.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface AssetLifecycleDiagnostics {
  proxyCount: number;
  cacheHitRate: number;
  reclaimedStorageMB: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Proxy Generation Failed | Fallback to original asset. |
| Thumbnail Missing | Regeneration scheduled. |
| Duplicate Collision | Fingerprint mismatch. |
| Cache Eviction Storm | Excessive storage pressure. |

---

# 19.53 Acceptance Tests

## Lifecycle Tests

- Asset transitions correctly through lifecycle states.
- Referenced assets cannot be deleted.
- Archived assets recover successfully.

## Proxy Tests

- Proxy duration matches original.
- Timeline playback uses proxies.
- Export uses originals.

## Thumbnail Tests

- Poster generated correctly.
- Timeline hover previews appear.
- Thumbnail cache reused.

## Deduplication Tests

- Duplicate imports reuse existing asset.
- Alias references preserved.
- Fingerprints validated.

## Garbage Collection Tests

- Unused proxies removed.
- Temporary caches reclaimed.
- Timeline references protected.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 19.3)

1. Assets follow a deterministic lifecycle state machine.
2. Editing proxies are derived assets separate from originals.
3. Proxy selection adapts to device capability and playback mode.
4. Exports always render from original assets.
5. Every visual asset generates reusable preview artifacts.
6. SHA-256 fingerprinting powers deduplication across projects and workspaces.
7. Garbage collection is reference-aware and snapshot-aware.
8. Storage optimization never modifies or deletes original media.
9. Cache eviction follows LRU/LFU policies for disposable artifacts only.
10. Preview artifacts are regenerated only when the underlying asset changes.

# 19.61 Asset Organization Philosophy

A creator's workspace can eventually contain **thousands of assets**.

TryLipi must make assets discoverable within milliseconds using a combination of:

- Folder hierarchy.
- Collections.
- Tags.
- Favorites.
- Smart AI collections.
- Semantic search.
- Metadata indexing.

Unlike Premiere or Final Cut, folders are **organizational only**. Asset identity never depends on folder location.

---

## Golden Asset Organization Principles

1. Asset identity is independent of folders.
2. Assets can belong to multiple collections simultaneously.
3. Search works across the entire workspace.
4. Smart collections update automatically.
5. Folder moves never change Asset IDs.
6. Tags are metadata, not hierarchy.
7. Search indexes are incremental.

---

## Responsibilities

The Organization Engine owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Folder Tree | Manual hierarchy. |
| Collections | Multi-folder organization. |
| Tags | Metadata labels. |
| Search Index | Fast asset discovery. |
| Smart Collections | AI-powered dynamic folders. |
| Brand Library | Shared reusable assets. |

---

- Folder depth is unlimited.
- Folder IDs remain immutable.

1. Folders organize assets but never define asset identity.
2. Collections allow many-to-many asset organization.
3. Global search indexes the entire workspace.

5. Tags are normalized metadata labels.
6. Smart collections are rule-driven and automatically updated.
7. Favorites, Recent, and Pinned assets are workspace-level quick-access metadata.
8. Brand Kits provide reusable assets across projects.
9. Semantic AI search uses embeddings alongside keyword search.
10. Filtering operates on indexed metadata without mutating asset state.

# 19.81 Autosave Philosophy

Autosave is one of the most critical systems inside TryLipi.

A creator should **never lose edits**, even if:

- Browser crashes.
- Laptop battery dies.
- Tab refreshes unexpectedly.
- Internet disconnects.
- Export is running.
- AI job fails midway.

Instead of periodically saving the whole project, TryLipi records **editing operations** and builds immutable snapshots in the background.

---

## Golden Autosave Principles

1. Every meaningful edit becomes an operation.
2. Autosave is incremental, not full-project serialization.
3. UI editing is never blocked by saving.
4. Autosave is deterministic and idempotent.
5. Snapshots are append-only.
6. Recovery never corrupts project history.
7. Local recovery works offline.

---

## Responsibilities

The Autosave Engine owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Operation Log | Record every edit. |
| Snapshot Builder | Create checkpoints. |
| Recovery Engine | Restore unfinished sessions. |
| Backup Engine | Local/cloud backups. |
| Migration Engine | Upgrade project schema. |

---

# 19.82 Operation Log Architecture

The Operation Log is the foundation of autosave.

Instead of saving `timeline.json` after every edit, TryLipi stores editing operations.

## Operation Pipeline

```text
User Edit
    │
Operation Generator
    │
Operation Queue
    │
Operation Log
    │
Snapshot Builder
```

---

## Examples of Operations

| User Action | Operation |
|-------------|-----------|
| Move clip | `MOVE_CLIP` |
| Split clip | `SPLIT_CLIP` |
| Delete clip | `DELETE_CLIP` |
| Add caption | `ADD_CAPTION` |
| Smart Zoom generated | `ADD_CAMERA_ACTION` |
| Volume changed | `UPDATE_AUDIO_GAIN` |

---

## Operation Interface

```ts
interface ProjectOperation {
  operationId: string;
  projectId: string;
  timestampUs: number;
  operationType: OperationType;
  payload: unknown;
}
```

---

## Operation Categories

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Timeline | Move, trim, split |
| Asset | Import, rename |
| Caption | Add, update |
| Camera | Zoom, pan |
| Audio | Fade, gain |
| AI | AI-generated edits |

---

## Engineering Rules

Operations are immutable once written.

---

# 19.83 Real-Time Autosave Engine

Autosave runs continuously in the background.

## Autosave Pipeline

```text
Operation Queue
      │
Debounce Window
      │
Snapshot Builder
      │
Local Persistence
      │
Cloud Sync Queue
```

---

## Autosave Triggers

| Trigger | Autosave |
|---------|----------|
| Clip move | Yes |
| Caption edit | Yes |
| Asset import | Yes |
| AI edit completed | Yes |
| Camera keyframe | Yes |
| Timeline zoom | No |

---

## Autosave Timing

| Event | Delay |
|------|-------|
| Single edit | 2 seconds |
| Continuous dragging | After drag ends |
| AI batch edits | Immediate snapshot |
| Project idle | Background checkpoint |

---

## Autosave Interface

```ts
interface AutosaveState {
  pendingOperations: number;
  lastSavedSnapshotId: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Autosave never interrupts playback or dragging interactions.

---

# 19.84 Snapshot Checkpoint Engine

Snapshots group operations into recoverable checkpoints.

## Snapshot Timeline

```text
Operations
O1 O2 O3 O4 O5
 │
Checkpoint A

O6 O7 O8
 │
Checkpoint B

O9 O10
 │
Checkpoint C
```

---

## Checkpoint Interface

```ts
interface SnapshotCheckpoint {
  checkpointId: string;
  snapshotId: string;
  operationRange: string[];
}
```

---

## Checkpoint Triggers

| Trigger | Create Checkpoint |
|---------|-------------------|
| 25 operations | Yes |
| AI workflow completed | Yes |
| Asset import completed | Yes |
| Export started | Yes |
| Idle 30 seconds | Yes |

---

## Benefits

- Fast recovery.
- Smaller writes.
- Incremental cloud sync.
- Version history.

---

## Engineering Rules

Checkpoint frequency adapts for large projects.

---

# 19.85 Crash Recovery System

Crash Recovery restores unfinished editing sessions.

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Unexpected Shutdown
        │
Recovery Detector
        │
Checkpoint Loader
        │
Operation Replay
        │
Recovered Project
```

---

## Crash Detection Sources

| Source | Supported |
|--------|-----------|
| Browser crash | Yes |
| Tab reload | Yes |
| Power loss | Yes |
| Renderer crash | Yes |
| GPU context loss | Partial |

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface CrashRecovery {
  recoverySnapshotId: string;
  operationsReplayed: number;
}
```

---

## Recovery Strategy

| Situation | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Unsaved operations | Replay operations |
| Snapshot exists | Restore checkpoint |
| Corrupted checkpoint | Restore previous checkpoint |
| Export interrupted | Restore export state |

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery always validates snapshot integrity before replay.

---

# 19.86 Backup & Recovery Architecture

Projects maintain multiple backup layers.

## Backup Hierarchy

```text
Project
│
├── Autosave Checkpoints
├── Local Backups
├── Cloud Backups
├── Export Snapshots
└── Recovery Snapshots
```

---

## Backup Types

| Backup | Frequency |
|--------|-----------|
| Autosave | Every few operations |
| Local Recovery | Continuous |
| Cloud Sync | Background |
| Manual Version | User initiated |
| Export Snapshot | Before export |

---

## Backup Interface

```ts
interface ProjectBackup {
  backupId: string;
  backupType: string;
  createdAtUs: number;
}
```

---

## Retention Policy

| Backup | Retention |
|--------|-----------|
| Autosave | Last 100 checkpoints |
| Recovery | Last 10 sessions |
| Manual Versions | Unlimited |
| Cloud | Workspace policy |

---

## Engineering Rules

Backups never overwrite immutable snapshots.

---

# 19.87 Version Migration Engine

Projects remain compatible across TryLipi releases.

## Migration Pipeline

```text
Project Manifest
      │
Schema Validator
      │
Migration Planner
      │
Migration Operations
      │
Updated Snapshot
```

---

## Migration Interface

```ts
interface SchemaMigration {
  fromVersion: string;
  toVersion: string;
  migrationSteps: string[];
}
```

---

## Migration Examples

| Version | Migration |
|---------|-----------|
| 3.0 → 3.1 | Camera metadata update |
| 3.1 → 3.2 | Audio schema extension |
| 3.2 → 4.0 | AI workflow graph update |

---

## Migration Rules

- Never mutate original snapshot.
- Always create migrated snapshot.
- Migration is reversible whenever possible.

---

## Engineering Rules

Projects always open using the latest supported schema after migration.

---

# 19.88 Schema Compatibility Engine

Schema compatibility prevents old projects from breaking.

## Compatibility Layers

```text
Project Schema
      │
Compatibility Adapter
      │
Current Runtime Schema
```

---

## Compatibility Types

| Compatibility | Supported |
|--------------|-----------|
| Backward | Yes |
| Forward | Partial |
| Patch Version | Automatic |
| Major Version | Migration required |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CompatibilityResult {
  compatible: boolean;
  requiresMigration: boolean;
}
```

---

## Compatibility Guarantees

- Old projects remain editable.
- Unknown fields preserved.
- Deprecated fields mapped.

---

## Engineering Rules

Schema adapters never discard recognized metadata.

---

# 19.89 Conflict Resolution Engine

Conflicts may occur during sync or recovery.

## Conflict Sources

| Source | Example |
|--------|---------|
| Local vs Cloud | Different snapshots |
| Two Devices | Concurrent edits |
| Migration | Different schema versions |
| Recovery | Duplicate autosave sessions |

---

## Resolution Pipeline

```text
Conflict Detector
      │
Snapshot Comparator
      │
Merge Planner
      │
Resolved Snapshot
```

---

## Resolution Strategies

| Conflict | Strategy |
|----------|----------|
| Different snapshots | Latest common ancestor merge |
| Metadata only | Merge automatically |
| Timeline conflict | Preserve both branches |
| Asset conflict | Reference existing asset |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface SnapshotConflict {
  baseSnapshotId: string;
  localSnapshotId: string;
  remoteSnapshotId: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline conflicts never silently overwrite edits.

---

# 19.90 Project Recovery UI Architecture

Recovery is surfaced through a dedicated UI.

## Recovery Flow

```text
App Launch
    │
Recovery Detector
    │
Recovery Dialog
    │
Restore Snapshot
```

---

## Recovery UI Sections

| Section | Purpose |
|---------|----------|
| Last Autosave | Restore latest checkpoint |
| Manual Versions | Restore previous version |
| Recovery Sessions | Crash recovery |
| Cloud Versions | Restore synced project |

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface RecoveryCandidate {
  snapshotId: string;
  createdAtUs: number;
  recoveryReason: string;
}
```

---

## Recovery UX Rules

- Preview snapshot before restoring.
- Duplicate project before risky restore.
- Allow comparison with current project.

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery UI never deletes current project automatically.

---

# 19.91 Recovery & Migration Diagnostics

Developer Mode exposes recovery infrastructure metrics.

## Metrics

- Autosave interval.
- Pending operations.
- Snapshot count.
- Recovery checkpoints.
- Backup size.
- Migration duration.
- Conflict count.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface RecoveryDiagnostics {
  pendingOperations: number;
  checkpointCount: number;
  migrationTimeMs: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Autosave Delayed | Operation queue backlog. |
| Snapshot Corrupted | Integrity validation failed. |
| Migration Failed | Rollback initiated. |
| Conflict Unresolved | Manual resolution required. |

---

# 19.92 Acceptance Tests

## Autosave Tests

- Every edit produces operation log.
- Debounced autosave creates checkpoint.
- UI remains responsive during autosave.

## Recovery Tests

- Browser crash restores latest checkpoint.
- Operation replay restores edits.
- Corrupted checkpoint falls back safely.

## Backup Tests

- Manual versions persist.
- Cloud backups restore correctly.
- Export snapshot preserved.

## Migration Tests

- Older schema migrates successfully.
- Unknown metadata preserved.
- Rollback available after migration failure.

## Conflict Tests

- Concurrent edits create branches.
- Metadata merges automatically.
- Timeline conflicts preserve both histories.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 19.5)

1. Autosave is operation-based, not file-based.
2. Every meaningful edit becomes an immutable operation.
3. Checkpoints group operations into recoverable snapshots.
4. Crash recovery restores snapshots before replaying operations.
5. Backups exist independently of autosave snapshots.
6. Schema migrations always create new snapshots.
7. Compatibility adapters preserve deprecated metadata whenever possible.
8. Conflict resolution never silently overwrites timeline edits.
9. Recovery UI always preserves the current project before restoration.
10. Project recovery and migration are deterministic across devices.

# 20.01 AI Runtime Philosophy

The **AI Workflow Engine** is the operating system that powers every AI feature inside TryLipi.

Instead of each AI feature directly calling Gemini, OpenAI, Whisper, or an internal model, every feature becomes a **workflow** executed by a centralized runtime.

This architecture makes AI:

- Deterministic.
- Interruptible.
- Resumable.
- Parallelizable.
- Cost-aware.
- Observable.
- Replaceable across providers.

Every AI action is treated like a background job operating on immutable project snapshots.

---

## Golden AI Runtime Principles

1. AI features never execute directly from the UI.
2. Every AI action becomes a workflow.
3. Workflows operate on immutable project snapshots.
4. AI jobs are resumable after interruption.
5. Workflow outputs are deterministic for identical inputs.
6. AI providers are abstracted behind one runtime.
7. Every AI execution is observable and replayable.

---

## Responsibilities

The AI Runtime owns:

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Workflow Engine | Execute AI workflows. |
| Scheduler | Queue AI tasks. |
| Context Engine | Build prompts and inputs. |
| Capability Registry | Route tasks to providers. |
| Event Bus | Broadcast workflow progress. |
| Persistence Layer | Save workflow state. |

---

# 20.02 AI Runtime Architecture

All AI features flow through one orchestration runtime.

## High-Level Architecture

```text
UI Action
    │
Workflow Builder
    │
AI Runtime
    │
Scheduler
    │
Provider Adapter
    │
Model Execution
    │
Timeline Updates
```

---

## Runtime Layers

| Layer | Responsibility |
|-------|----------------|
| Workflow Layer | Build execution graph. |
| Scheduler Layer | Queue & prioritize jobs. |
| Context Layer | Assemble prompts/assets. |
| Provider Layer | Gemini/OpenAI/etc. adapters. |
| Result Layer | Apply edits to timeline. |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface AIRuntime {
  workflowId: string;
  projectSnapshotId: string;
  state: AIRuntimeState;
}
```

---

## Runtime States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Created | Workflow initialized. |
| Waiting | Awaiting scheduler. |
| Running | AI execution active. |
| Paused | User/system paused. |
| Completed | Workflow finished. |
| Failed | Recoverable failure. |
| Cancelled | User cancelled workflow. |

---

## Engineering Rules

The runtime is the only component allowed to communicate with AI providers.

---

# 20.03 AI Workflow Graph Engine

Every AI feature is represented as a directed workflow graph.

## Workflow Graph Example

```text
Auto B-Roll Workflow

Transcript
    │
Scene Detection
    │
Keyword Extraction
    │
B-Roll Search
    │
Ranking
    │
Timeline Placement
```

## Workflow Graph Components

| Component | Purpose |

| Output | Structured workflow result. |

## Workflow Interface

```ts
interface AIWorkflowGraph {
  workflowId: string;
  nodes: WorkflowNode[];
  edges: WorkflowEdge[];
}
```

---

## Supported Graph Types

| Workflow | Graph |
|----------|-------|
| Auto Captions | Sequential |
| Smart Zoom | Sequential |
| AI Thumbnail | Branching |
| Auto B-Roll | DAG |
| Viral Clip Generator | Multi-stage DAG |
| Translation Workflow | Fan-out/Fan-in |

---

## Engineering Rules

Workflow graphs must be acyclic.

---

# 20.04 AI Workflow Execution Lifecycle

Every workflow follows the same lifecycle regardless of feature.

## Lifecycle

```text
Create Workflow
      │
Validate Context
      │
Build Graph
      │
Queue Tasks
      │
Execute Nodes
      │
Collect Outputs
      │

```

## Lifecycle Stages

| Stage | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Initialize | Build workflow metadata. |
| Validate | Assets & permissions. |
| Schedule | Queue runnable nodes. |
| Execute | AI provider execution. |
| Merge | Combine outputs. |
| Commit | Timeline snapshot update. |

---

## Workflow Interface

```ts
interface WorkflowExecution {
  workflowId: string;
  currentNodeId: string;
  completedNodeIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Commit Strategy

Outputs are applied only after validation.

---

## Engineering Rules

Workflow commits create immutable project snapshots.

| Speech | Transcription, translation. |

| Editing | Smart Zoom, silence removal. |

---

## Engineering Rules

- Snapshot-specific.
- Provider-independent.

## Engineering Rules

# 20.07 AI Runtime Scheduler

The Scheduler controls execution order.

```text
Workflow Queue
      │
Priority Planner
      │
Worker Assignment
      │
Execution Queue
```

## Priority Levels

| Priority | Examples |
|----------|----------|

| High | User-triggered AI edit. |


## Engineering Rules

Scheduler never runs dependent nodes early.

## Persistence Tests

- Completed nodes aren't rerun.

## Event Bus Tests

- Completion triggers snapshot commit.

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.1)

1. Every AI feature executes through the centralized AI Runtime.
2. Workflows operate exclusively on immutable project snapshots.
3. Workflow graphs must be directed acyclic graphs (DAGs).
4. Tasks declare dependencies before execution begins.
5. Scheduler controls execution order and priority.
6. Context generation is deterministic and provider-independent.
7. Capabilities abstract AI providers behind a registry.
8. Workflow state is checkpointed after every completed node.
9. Event Bus broadcasts ordered workflow lifecycle events.
10. Workflow completion always creates a new immutable project snapshot.

# 20.21 Background Job Philosophy

TryLipi performs dozens of AI operations simultaneously:

- Caption generation.
- Smart Zoom detection.
- B-Roll generation.
- Thumbnail scoring.
- Voice enhancement.
- Translation.
- Silence detection.
- Viral hook detection.

These operations **must never block editing**.

Every AI feature executes as a background job managed independently from the UI thread.

---

## Golden Background Job Principles

1. AI jobs never execute on the main UI thread.
2. Jobs are asynchronous and resumable.
3. Jobs are checkpointed after every stage.
4. Multiple workflows can execute simultaneously.
5. UI remains interactive during AI processing.
6. Failed jobs never corrupt project snapshots.
7. Background jobs are observable in real time.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Job Queue | Queue pending AI work. |
| Worker Pool | Execute jobs concurrently. |
| Scheduler | Assign workers. |
| Retry Engine | Recover failed jobs. |
| Cancellation Engine | Interrupt safely. |
| Resource Manager | CPU/GPU budgeting. |

---

# 20.22 AI Job Queue Architecture

Every workflow becomes one or more queued jobs.

## Queue Architecture

```text
AI Runtime
     │
Job Builder
     │
Priority Queue
     │
Worker Pool
     │
Completed Jobs
```

---

## Queue Types

| Queue | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| User Queue | Immediate user actions. |
| AI Queue | AI workflow execution. |
| Background Queue | Metadata indexing. |
| Export Queue | AI export preparation. |
| Recovery Queue | Resume interrupted jobs. |

---

## Queue Interface

```ts
interface AIJobQueue {
  queueId: string;
  pendingJobs: AIJob[];
  runningJobs: AIJob[];
}
```

---

## Job Lifecycle

```text
Queued
  │
Assigned
  │
Running
  │
Completed
  │
Archived
```

Failure path:

```text
Running
  │
Failed
  │
Retry Queue
```

---

## Priority Levels

| Priority | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Critical | Export captions. |
| High | User-triggered Smart Zoom. |
| Medium | AI Thumbnail generation. |
| Low | Semantic indexing. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Jobs remain immutable after entering the queue.

---

# 20.23 Worker Pool Architecture

Workers execute AI jobs independently.

## Worker Pool Diagram

```text
AI Job Queue
     │
Scheduler
     │
├── Worker 1
├── Worker 2
├── Worker 3
├── Worker 4
└── Worker N
```

---

## Worker Categories

| Worker | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Vision Worker | Gemini Vision tasks. |
| Language Worker | Prompt-based tasks. |
| Audio Worker | Whisper/Gemini audio. |
| Thumbnail Worker | Ranking & generation. |
| Metadata Worker | OCR, tags, indexing. |

---

## Worker Interface

```ts
interface AIWorker {
  workerId: string;
  workerType: AIWorkerType;
  currentJobId?: string;
}
```

---

## Worker States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Idle | Available. |
| Busy | Executing job. |
| Paused | Suspended. |
| Recovering | Restarting. |
| Offline | Removed from scheduler. |

---

## Worker Scaling

| Device | Workers |
|--------|---------|
| Low-End Laptop | 2 |
| Mid-Range Laptop | 4 |
| High-End Desktop | 6–8 |
| Cloud Worker | Dynamic |

---

## Engineering Rules

Workers never share mutable workflow context.

---

# 20.24 Distributed Task Scheduler

The scheduler distributes work across workers.

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text
Pending Queue
      │
Priority Planner
      │
Dependency Resolver
      │
Worker Assignment
```

---

## Scheduling Inputs

| Input | Effect |
|------|--------|
| Priority | Execution order. |
| Dependencies | Parent completion. |
| CPU Budget | Worker availability. |
| GPU Budget | Vision jobs. |
| Memory Budget | Batch sizing. |

---

## Scheduling Algorithm

1. Resolve dependencies.
2. Filter runnable jobs.
3. Sort by priority.
4. Assign available workers.
5. Monitor execution.

---

## Scheduler Interface

```ts
interface DistributedScheduler {
  activeWorkerIds: string[];
  runnableJobs: AIJob[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Scheduler decisions are deterministic given identical queue state.

---

# 20.25 Parallel Workflow Execution Engine

Independent workflow nodes execute simultaneously.

## Example DAG

```text
Transcript
    │
 ┌──┴─────┐
 │        │
Translate  Keywords
 │        │
Captions  B-Roll Search
 └──┬─────┘
 Timeline Merge
```
