## Parallel Execution Benefits

| Benefit | Result |
|---------|--------|
| Lower latency | Faster AI workflows. |
| Independent failures | Partial retries. |
| Better CPU utilization | Multiple workers active. |

---

## Parallel Execution Interface

```ts
interface ParallelWorkflowExecution {
  workflowId: string;
  activeNodeIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Synchronization Barrier

Child nodes wait until required parent nodes complete.

---

## Engineering Rules

Parallel execution never violates dependency ordering.

---

# 20.26 Batch Processing Engine

Many AI tasks are dramatically cheaper when processed in batches.

## Batch Candidates

| Task | Batch Size |
|------|------------|
| Scene Detection | 10–20 clips |
| Thumbnail Ranking | 20 frames |
| OCR | 20 frames |
| Caption Translation | 25 segments |
| Smart Tags | 50 assets |

---

## Batch Pipeline

```text
Tasks
 │
Batch Planner
 │
Provider Request
 │
Batch Result Splitter
```

---

## Batch Interface

```ts

  batchId: string;
  taskIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Batch Strategies

| Strategy | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Fixed Size | Caption translation. |
| Token Budget | Gemini requests. |
| Time Window | Live workflows. |
| Memory Budget | Vision inference. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Batch outputs map back to original task IDs.

---

# 20.27 Retry & Exponential Backoff Engine

Failures should recover automatically whenever safe.

## Retry Pipeline

```text
Job Failed
    │
Retry Policy
    │
Backoff Timer
    │
Retry Queue
```

---

## Retry Reasons

| Failure | Retry |
|---------|-------|
| Network Timeout | Yes |
| Rate Limit | Yes |
| Temporary API Error | Yes |
| Invalid Context | No |
| User Cancellation | No |

---

## Retry Schedule

| Attempt | Delay |
|---------|-------|
| First | Immediate |
| Second | 2 seconds |
| Third | 5 seconds |
| Fourth | 15 seconds |
| Fifth | 60 seconds |

---

## Retry Interface

```ts
interface RetryPolicy {
  maxAttempts: number;
  currentAttempt: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Retries reuse identical workflow context.

---

# 20.28 Pause, Resume & Cancellation Engine

Creators can interrupt AI workflows safely.

## State Machine

```text
Running
 │
Pause
 │
Paused
 │
Resume
 │
Running
```

Cancellation path:

```text
Running
 │
Cancel
 │
Cancelled
```

---

## Cancellation Policy

| Workflow Stage | Behavior |
|---------------|----------|
| Waiting | Remove from queue. |
| Running | Finish current request, discard output if needed. |
| Completed | Cannot cancel. |
| Failed | Retry optional. |

---

## Pause Interface

```ts
interface WorkflowControl {
  workflowId: string;
  paused: boolean;
}
```

---

## Resume Guarantees

- Resume from checkpoint.
- Skip completed nodes.
- Restore context exactly.

---

## Engineering Rules

Cancellation never modifies committed project snapshots.

---

# 20.29 Resource-Aware Scheduling Engine

AI jobs compete for CPU, GPU, RAM, network, and tokens.

## Resource Budget Pipeline

```text
System Metrics
     │
Budget Planner
     │
Scheduler Limits
```

---

## Resource Budgets

| Resource | Budget Owner |
|----------|--------------|
| CPU | Scheduler |
| GPU | Vision Worker |
| RAM | Batch Planner |
| Network | Upload Manager |
| Tokens | AI Runtime |

---

## Adaptive Limits

| Condition | Scheduler Action |
|-----------|------------------|
| Export Running | Lower AI concurrency. |
| Playback Active | Pause heavy AI jobs. |
| Idle Device | Increase worker count. |
| Battery Saver | Reduce AI workers. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ResourceBudget {
  cpuPercent: number;
  memoryMB: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Playback receives higher priority than background AI work.

---

```text
 │
```

## Cloud Workers

| Translation | Yes |
| Script Writing | Yes |
| B-Roll Ranking | Yes |
| Voice Enhancement | Yes |

```text
Video
 │

 │
Gemini Vision Ranking
 │
Local Timeline Merge
```

- Active workers.
- Idle workers.

- Average batch size.
- CPU utilization.

# 20.32 Acceptance Tests

## Queue Tests

- Jobs enqueue correctly.
- Priorities respected.
- Queue survives refresh.

## Worker Tests

- Workers execute independently.
- Idle workers receive new jobs.
- Worker restart preserves checkpoints.

## Scheduler Tests

- Dependency ordering enforced.
- Parallel nodes execute concurrently.
- Resource limits respected.

## Retry Tests

- Network failures retry successfully.
- Invalid jobs do not retry.
- Backoff timing matches policy.

## Cancellation Tests

- Waiting jobs cancel immediately.
- Running jobs checkpoint safely.
- Completed jobs remain immutable.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.2)

1. Every AI workflow is decomposed into background jobs.
2. Worker pools execute jobs independently from the UI thread.
3. Scheduler assigns runnable jobs using priority and dependency rules.
4. Parallel execution is allowed only for dependency-free workflow nodes.
5. Batch processing groups compatible AI tasks for efficiency.
6. Retry engine uses deterministic exponential backoff.
7. Pause and resume always restore from checkpoints.
8. Cancellation never mutates committed project snapshots.
9. Resource-aware scheduling prioritizes playback and exports over background AI work.
10. Execution targets (local vs cloud) are selected by the AI Runtime through the Capability Registry.

# 20.41 Workflow Dependency Philosophy

Large AI features inside TryLipi are **not single API calls**.

For example:

**Auto B-Roll**

- Transcript generation.
- Scene segmentation.
- Object detection.
- Semantic search.
- Asset ranking.
- Timeline placement.
- Transition generation.

If step 4 fails, steps 1–3 should not rerun.

This is why workflows execute as **dependency graphs with checkpoints**.

---

## Golden Dependency Principles

1. Every workflow is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph).
2. Nodes execute only when dependencies are satisfied.
3. Completed nodes are never recomputed unnecessarily.
4. Checkpoints persist successful node outputs.
5. Rollback affects only failed branches.
6. Timeline updates are incremental.
7. AI execution remains resumable indefinitely.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Dependency Graph | Node relationships. |
| Resolver | Runnable node discovery. |
| Checkpoint Engine | Persist completed stages. |
| Streaming Engine | Incremental outputs. |
| Validation Engine | Verify outputs. |
| Rollback Engine | Recover failed workflows. |

---

# 20.42 AI Dependency Graph Architecture

Every workflow is represented internally as a dependency graph.

## Example: Smart Zoom Workflow

```text
Transcript
    │
Speaker Timeline
    │
Face Tracking
    │
Emotion Detection
    │
Zoom Candidate Generation
    │
Camera Timeline Builder
    │
Timeline Snapshot
```

---

## Example: Thumbnail AI Workflow

```text
Video Frames
   │
Scene Detection
   │
Visual Quality Ranking
   │
Face Detection
   │
Text Safe Area Detection
   │
Thumbnail Ranking
```

---

## Graph Interface

```ts
interface WorkflowGraph {
  workflowId: string;
  nodes: WorkflowNode[];
  edges: WorkflowEdge[];
}
```

---

## Node Interface

```ts
interface WorkflowNode {
  nodeId: string;
  capabilityId: string;
  dependencyNodeIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Edge Types

| Edge | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Hard Dependency | Child waits for parent. |
| Soft Dependency | Child may continue with fallback. |
| Merge Dependency | Wait for multiple parents. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Dependency graphs must remain acyclic at validation time.

---

# 20.43 Dependency Resolution Engine

The Resolver decides which nodes are runnable.

## Resolution Pipeline

```text
Workflow Graph
      │
Completed Node Registry
      │
Dependency Resolver
      │
Runnable Node Queue
```

---

## Resolver Algorithm

1. Find unfinished nodes.
2. Verify parent completion.
3. Validate context availability.
4. Mark runnable.
5. Submit to Scheduler.

---

## Resolver Interface

```ts
interface DependencyResolver {
  runnableNodeIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Resolution States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Waiting | Dependencies incomplete. |
| Runnable | Ready for worker assignment. |
| Running | Worker executing. |
| Blocked | Missing context. |
| Completed | Output committed. |

---

## Merge Nodes

Example:

```text
Translation ─┐
             │
Transcript ──┼── Merge
             │
Speaker IDs ─┘
```

Merge executes only after all required parents complete.

---

## Engineering Rules

Dependency resolution must be deterministic for identical workflow state.

---

# 20.44 Workflow Checkpoint Engine

Checkpoints persist workflow progress after successful nodes.

## Checkpoint Architecture

```text
Workflow
 │
Node Completed
 │
Checkpoint Builder
 │
Checkpoint Storage
```

---

## Checkpoint Contents

| Stored Item | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| Node Outputs | Resume execution. |
| Context Hash | Integrity validation. |
| Snapshot ID | Project consistency. |
| Retry Metadata | Failure recovery. |
| Execution Metadata | Diagnostics. |

---

## Checkpoint Interface

```ts
interface WorkflowCheckpoint {
  checkpointId: string;
  workflowId: string;
  completedNodeIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Checkpoint Triggers

| Trigger | Save |
|---------|------|
| Node Completed | Yes |
| Merge Completed | Yes |
| Workflow Paused | Yes |
| Workflow Cancelled | Yes |
| Workflow Failed | Yes |

---

## Recovery Flow

```text
Reload Project
     │
Load Checkpoint
     │
Restore Graph State
     │
Resume Runnable Nodes
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Checkpoint restoration skips completed nodes.

---

# 20.48 Rollback & Compensation Engine

Rollback restores workflow consistency after failures.

## Rollback Pipeline

```text
Workflow Failure
      │
Failure Analyzer
      │
Rollback Planner
      │
Checkpoint Restore
```

## Rollback Types

| Type | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Node Rollback | Remove failed node output. |
| Branch Rollback | Remove dependent outputs. |
| Full Workflow Rollback | Restore checkpoint. |

```text
Translation ✅
```

```ts
}
```

## Engineering Rules

# 20.52 Acceptance Tests

## Dependency Tests

- DAG validation rejects cycles.
- Runnable nodes identified correctly.
- Merge nodes wait for parents.

## Checkpoint Tests

- Resume skips completed work.
- Checkpoint integrity verified.

## Streaming Tests

- Timeline preview updates progressively.
- Stream interruption resumes safely.

## Validation Tests

- Invalid timestamps rejected.
- Missing assets rejected.
- Camera bounds enforced.

## Rollback Tests

- Independent branches preserved.
- Snapshot history unchanged.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.3)

1. AI workflows execute as deterministic DAGs.
2. Dependency resolution determines runnable nodes.
3. Completed node outputs are checkpointed immediately.
4. Streaming outputs update temporary UI layers only.
5. Timeline changes are committed only after validation.
6. Rollback restores workflow state from checkpoints.
7. AI operation history is permanently linked to snapshots.
8. Progressive UI subscribes exclusively to workflow events.
9. Validation occurs before every snapshot commit.
10. Dependency graphs remain deterministic and replayable across devices.

# 20.61 AI Provider Philosophy

TryLipi is **AI-provider agnostic**.

The application never knows whether a workflow is executed using:

- Gemini 2.5 Flash
- Gemini 2.5 Pro
- GPT-5 Vision
- Whisper
- Claude
- Future local models
- Future open-source models

Every workflow requests a **capability**, and the runtime chooses the provider.

This architecture prevents vendor lock-in and allows automatic routing based on:

- Cost.
- Latency.
- Availability.
- Context size.
- Feature support.
- User subscription tier.

---

## Golden Provider Principles

1. UI never references model names.
2. Workflows request capabilities.
3. Providers implement a shared interface.
4. Prompts are provider-independent.
5. Responses normalize into canonical schemas.
6. Providers are interchangeable.
7. Runtime can dynamically reroute providers.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Capability Registry | Feature → provider mapping. |
| Provider Adapter | API-specific implementation. |
| Prompt Builder | Provider-neutral prompts. |
| Context Builder | Multimodal payload creation. |
| Streaming Engine | Incremental responses. |
| Response Normalizer | Unified output format. |

---

# 20.62 Provider Abstraction Layer

Every provider implements one standardized interface.

## Provider Architecture

```text
Workflow
    │
Capability Registry
    │
Provider Adapter
    │
Gemini Adapter
GPT Adapter
Claude Adapter
Whisper Adapter
Future Adapter
```

---

## Provider Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Authentication | API credentials. |

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.4)

1. AI workflows request capabilities, never providers.
2. Provider adapters isolate vendor-specific APIs.
3. Prompt templates are provider-independent and versioned.
4. Context Builder constructs deterministic multimodal inputs.
5. Token Budget Engine compresses context without changing semantics.
6. Streaming orchestration delivers ordered incremental outputs.
7. Provider failover preserves workflow capability behavior.
8. Concurrency limits are enforced centrally by the runtime.
9. Response normalization converts provider outputs into canonical schemas.
10. Context caching is snapshot-aware, capability-aware, and version-aware.

# 20.81 AI Cost Engine Philosophy

AI is TryLipi's largest operational expense.

Every caption, Smart Zoom, B-Roll search, translation, thumbnail ranking, OCR request, and script generation consumes provider resources.

The **AI Cost Engine** exists to make AI execution:

- Predictable.
- Budget-aware.
- Cache-efficient.
- Observable.
- User-tier aware.
- Profitable for TryLipi.

Instead of blindly sending requests, the runtime estimates cost **before execution** and records actual usage **after execution**.

---

## Golden Cost Principles

1. Every AI workflow has an estimated cost before execution.
2. Actual usage is recorded after completion.
3. Cached results cost zero additional tokens.
4. User budgets are enforced centrally.
5. Workflow cost is independent of provider billing APIs.
6. Token accounting is deterministic.
7. Cost analytics are available per project and per workspace.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Cost Estimator | Predict workflow cost. |
| Token Accountant | Record actual usage. |
| Budget Manager | Enforce limits. |
| Cache Engine | Avoid duplicate AI calls. |
| Analytics Engine | Aggregate AI usage. |

---

```ts
  inputTokens: number;

  cached: boolean;
}
```

|----------|-------|--------|--------|
| Caption Translation | 1,250 | 980 | No |
| Thumbnail Ranking | 3,800 | 120 | No |
| Script Rewrite | 2,100 | 1,900 | Yes |

---

## Engineering Rules

Token ledger entries are immutable once recorded.

- Remove storage paths.
- Remove authentication tokens.
- Replace sensitive references with aliases.

# 20.92 Acceptance Tests

## Token Tests

- Ledger records input/output tokens.
- Cached requests consume zero new tokens.
- Budget reservation finalized correctly.

## Budget Tests

- Workflow denied when credits exhausted.
- Cached workflows bypass billing.
- Reserved credits released after cancellation.

## Cache Tests

- Prompt cache reused for identical context.
- Asset cache reused across workflows.
- Model version invalidates cache correctly.

## Observability Tests

- Every workflow has trace ID.
- Telemetry events ordered correctly.
- Queue wait time recorded.

## Security Tests

- Prompt sanitization removes secrets.
- Internal IDs never leave runtime.
- Provider payload contains only canonical context.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.5)

1. Every AI workflow receives a pre-execution cost estimate.
2. Token ledger records immutable usage for every workflow.
3. Budgets are enforced before provider execution begins.
4. Prompt cache prevents duplicate AI requests for identical contexts.
5. AI-generated assets are cached separately from provider responses.
6. Every workflow generates telemetry and trace data.
7. Reliability is achieved through retries, checkpoints, and failover.
8. Prompt sanitization removes all internal infrastructure identifiers.
9. Context cache keys include snapshot hash, capability, and template version.
10. AI analytics are workspace-native and provider-independent.

- Workspace Invitations.
- Project Access Control (RBAC).
- Organization & Team hierarchy.
- Foundation for Figma-style real-time collaboration.

# 22.01 Performance Engine Philosophy

Performance is a **first-class feature** in TryLipi.

A creator should be able to edit:

- 4K screen recordings.
- Long podcasts.
- Hundreds of captions.
- AI-generated B-roll.
- Multiple video/audio tracks.

...inside a browser **without the editor becoming sluggish**.

Rather than optimizing later, every subsystem is designed around measurable performance budgets.

---

## Golden Performance Principles

1. Editing always has higher priority than background work.
2. Playback should remain smooth even while AI workflows execute.
3. Memory usage must stay bounded.
4. Rendering should be incremental.
5. Expensive work should be deferred whenever possible.
6. Everything should be measurable.
7. Performance decisions must be deterministic.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Runtime Optimizer | Browser performance tuning. |
| Memory Manager | Memory lifecycle. |
| Scheduler | Frame budget allocation. |
| Virtualization Engine | Visible-only rendering. |
| GPU Manager | Texture lifecycle. |
| Performance Monitor | Runtime metrics collection. |

---

# 22.02 Browser Runtime Architecture

TryLipi runs as a browser-native editor while behaving like a desktop application.

## Runtime Architecture

```text
Browser Runtime
│
├── UI Thread
├── Timeline Workers
├── Render Workers
├── AI Workers
├── Audio Workers
├── Storage Workers
└── Export Workers
```

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime Component | Responsibility |
|-------------------|----------------|
| Main Thread | UI, interactions. |
| Render Worker | Frame rendering. |
| Timeline Worker | Timeline calculations. |
| AI Worker | Background inference. |
| Audio Worker | Audio processing. |
| Storage Worker | OPFS & IndexedDB. |

---

## Runtime Goals

| Goal | Target |
|------|--------|
| Timeline Scroll | 60 FPS |
| Playback | 60 FPS |
| Dragging Clips | 60 FPS |
| Caption Editing | Instant |
| Zoom/Pan Preview | Smooth |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface BrowserRuntime {
  runtimeId: string;
  activeWorkers: number;
  memoryBudgetMB: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

The main thread should never perform heavy decoding, AI inference, or export rendering.

---

# 22.03 Performance Budget Engine

Every subsystem receives a performance budget.

## Performance Budget Hierarchy

```text
Frame Budget
│
├── UI Rendering
├── Timeline Layout
├── Video Rendering
├── Audio Scheduling
├── AI Updates
└── Background Tasks
```

---

## Budget Allocation (60 FPS Target)

| Task | Budget |
|------|--------|
| UI Layout | 2 ms |
| Timeline Rendering | 3 ms |
| Video Composition | 5 ms |
| Audio Sync | 1 ms |
| Interaction Handling | 2 ms |
| Spare Budget | ~3 ms |

**Target frame time:** **16.67 ms**

---

## Budget Interface

```ts
interface FrameBudget {
  uiMs: number;
  renderMs: number;
  backgroundMs: number;
}
```

---

## Budget Priorities

| Priority | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Critical | Playback. |
| High | User dragging timeline. |
| Medium | Thumbnail generation. |
| Low | AI metadata indexing. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Background jobs must yield when frame budget is exceeded.

---

# 22.04 Memory Management Architecture

Memory is centrally managed instead of relying entirely on browser garbage collection.

## Memory Architecture

```text
Memory Manager
│
├── Asset Cache
├── Texture Cache
├── Audio Buffers
├── Timeline Cache
├── AI Cache
└── Temporary Buffers
```

---

## Memory Categories

| Category | Managed |
|----------|---------|
| JavaScript Heap | Yes |
| GPU Memory | Yes |
| Audio Buffers | Yes |
| OPFS Buffers | Yes |
| Blob Cache | Yes |

---

## Memory Lifecycle

```text
Allocate
   │
Active
   │
Idle
   │
Eviction Candidate
   │
Released
```

---

## Memory Interface

```ts
interface MemoryAllocation {
  allocationId: string;
  category: MemoryCategory;
  bytes: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Every allocation must have an owner subsystem.

---

# 22.05 Object Pooling & Resource Reuse Engine

Creating thousands of temporary objects causes GC pauses.

TryLipi uses reusable pools.

## Pool Architecture

```text
Pool Manager
│
├── Timeline Objects
├── Frame Buffers
├── Audio Buffers
├── AI Context Objects
└── Event Objects
```

---

## Pool Lifecycle

```text
Acquire
   │
Use
   │
Reset
   │
Return to Pool
```

---

## Pool Types

| Pool | Resource |
|------|----------|
| Frame Pool | Video frames. |
| Caption Pool | Caption segments. |
| Timeline Pool | Clip objects. |
| Audio Pool | Sample buffers. |
| Event Pool | Workflow events. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ObjectPool<T> {
  acquire(): T;
  release(item: T): void;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Objects returned to pools must be reset before reuse.

---

# 22.06 Frame Budget Scheduler

Rendering work is distributed across animation frames.

## Scheduler Pipeline

```text
Animation Frame
      │
Frame Budget Calculator
      │
Task Scheduler
      │
Visible Updates
```

---

## Frame Scheduling Categories

| Category | Timing |
|----------|--------|
| Immediate | Pointer interactions. |
| Frame Task | Rendering. |
| Deferred | Thumbnail generation. |
| Idle Task | Metadata indexing. |

---

## Scheduler Interface

```ts
interface FrameScheduler {
  remainingFrameBudgetMs: number;
}
```

---

## Example Frame

```text
Frame Start
   │
UI Update
   │
Timeline Render
   │
Video Render
   │
Audio Sync
   │
Idle Tasks
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Idle tasks execute only when frame budget remains.

---

# 22.07 Timeline Virtualization Engine

Only visible timeline regions should render.

## Virtualization Pipeline

```text
Timeline
   │
Viewport Calculator
   │
Visible Window
   │
Renderer
```

---

## Example

A timeline containing **3,000 clips** may render only **120 visible clips**.

---

## Virtualized Elements

| Element | Virtualized |
|---------|-------------|
| Clips | Yes |
| Waveforms | Yes |
| Caption Blocks | Yes |
| Camera Keyframes | Yes |
| Markers | Yes |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface TimelineViewport {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Lower DOM count.
- Faster scrolling.
- Smaller React tree.
- Reduced memory usage.

---

## Engineering Rules

Virtualization must preserve timeline coordinates.

---

# 22.08 Asset Lazy Loading Engine

Large projects should load progressively.

## Lazy Loading Pipeline

```text
Project Open
     │
Manifest Loaded
     │
Visible Asset Resolver
     │
Lazy Asset Loader
```

---

## Lazy Loading Order

| Priority | Asset |
|----------|-------|
| High | Visible timeline clips. |
| High | Active audio tracks. |
| Medium | Nearby clips. |
| Low | Unused assets. |
| Lowest | Archived assets. |

---

## Asset States

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Metadata Loaded | Registry only. |
| Thumbnail Loaded | Preview ready. |
| Proxy Loaded | Playback ready. |
| Original Loaded | Export ready. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface LazyAssetState {
  assetId: string;
  loadState: AssetLoadState;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Original assets load only when required.

---

# 22.09 GPU Texture Memory Manager

GPU textures are limited resources.

## GPU Memory Architecture

```text
Video Frame
    │
Texture Upload
    │
Texture Cache
    │
Renderer
```

---

## Texture Lifecycle

```text
Decoded Frame
     │
GPU Upload
     │
Visible
     │
Evicted
```

---

## Texture Categories

| Texture | Source |
|---------|--------|
| Video Frame | Decoder |
| Image Asset | Image import |
| Sticker | PNG/WebP |
| Caption Background | Renderer |
| Gradient | Generated |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface GPUTextureAllocation {
  textureId: string;
  assetId: string;
}
```

---

## Eviction Strategy

- LRU.
- Invisible textures first.
- Proxy textures before originals.

---

## Engineering Rules

GPU memory usage must remain below device budget.

---

# 22.10 Background Performance Monitor

Performance metrics are collected continuously.

## Monitoring Pipeline

```text
Runtime Metrics
      │
Performance Collector
      │
Performance Store
      │
Developer Dashboard
```

---

## Collected Metrics

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| FPS | Playback/UI FPS. |
| Frame Time | Average render time. |
| Memory Usage | Heap + GPU. |
| Worker Utilization | Active workers. |
| Timeline Render Time | Timeline cost. |
| Cache Hit Rate | Asset cache performance. |

---

## Performance Thresholds

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| FPS | ≥ 60 |
| Frame Time | ≤ 16.67 ms |
| Timeline Scroll | ≥ 60 FPS |
| Memory Spike | Controlled |
| GC Pause | Minimal |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface RuntimePerformanceMetrics {
  averageFPS: number;
  averageFrameTimeMs: number;
  heapUsageMB: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance monitoring never blocks rendering.

---

# 22.11 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes production performance diagnostics.

## Metrics

- Current FPS.
- Frame budget usage.
- Heap memory.
- GPU memory.
- Active textures.
- Timeline virtualization count.
- Worker utilization.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface PerformanceDiagnostics {
  fps: number;
  gpuMemoryMB: number;
  heapMemoryMB: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Frame Budget Exceeded | Frame over 16.67 ms. |
| Memory Pressure | Heap exceeds threshold. |
| GPU Pressure | Texture cache overflow. |
| Virtualization Disabled | Excessive visible nodes. |

---

# 22.12 Acceptance Tests

## Runtime Tests

- Main thread remains responsive during AI execution.
- Playback remains smooth during exports.
- Timeline interactions remain responsive.

## Memory Tests

- Object pools reduce allocations.
- Texture eviction frees GPU memory.
- Asset lazy loading reduces initial memory footprint.

## Virtualization Tests

- Only visible clips render.
- Scroll performance remains stable with thousands of clips.
- Caption virtualization preserves positioning.

## Budget Tests

- Idle work pauses under frame pressure.
- Playback gets highest scheduler priority.
- Background tasks resume after idle.

## Monitoring Tests

- FPS reported accurately.
- Frame budget diagnostics update live.
- Memory usage metrics remain consistent.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 22.1)

1. Performance is budget-driven, not best-effort.
2. Main thread never performs heavy AI or rendering work.
3. Every subsystem receives a measurable frame budget.
4. Memory allocations have explicit ownership.
5. Object pooling minimizes garbage collection pauses.
6. Timeline rendering is fully virtualized.
7. Assets load progressively through lazy loading.
8. GPU textures follow an LRU eviction policy.
9. Playback always has higher priority than background work.
10. Runtime performance metrics are continuously observable.

---

# 22.21 Local-First Philosophy

TryLipi is designed as a **local-first video editor**.

Unlike traditional cloud editors, creators should be able to:

- Open projects without internet.
- Continue editing while offline.
- Import videos offline.
- Record screen offline.
- Generate waveforms and previews offline.
- Queue AI jobs for later execution.

The browser becomes the creator's desktop application.

Cloud synchronization is an enhancement—not a dependency.

---

## Golden Local-First Principles

1. Projects always open from local storage first.
2. Editing never depends on network connectivity.
3. Assets are stored locally before cloud upload.
4. Cloud synchronization happens asynchronously.
5. Offline edits are replayed when online.
6. Network failures never block editing.
7. Local project state is always authoritative until synchronization.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Offline Runtime | Run editor without internet. |
| OPFS Storage | Binary assets. |
| IndexedDB | Metadata database. |
| Service Worker | Offline application shell. |
| Sync Engine | Cloud synchronization. |
| Connectivity Manager | Online/offline detection. |

---

# 22.22 Offline Runtime Architecture

The offline runtime boots entirely from local resources.

## Runtime Boot Flow

```text
Browser Launch
      │
Service Worker
      │
Local Manifest
      │
IndexedDB Metadata
      │
OPFS Assets
      │
Editor Ready
```

---

## Offline Runtime Components

| Component | Offline |
|----------|----------|
| Timeline Editing | Yes |
| Playback | Yes |
| Screen Recording | Yes |
| Asset Import | Yes |
| Waveform Generation | Yes |
| AI Queue Creation | Yes |
| Cloud Sync | Deferred |

---

## Runtime Layers

```text
Offline Runtime
│
├── Local Project Loader
├── Storage Engine
├── Cache Manager
├── AI Queue Store
└── Connectivity Manager
```

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface OfflineRuntime {
  runtimeId: string;
  offlineReady: boolean;
  pendingSyncJobs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

The editor must become usable before network availability is checked.

---

# 22.23 OPFS Storage Engine

OPFS is the canonical binary storage layer.

## OPFS Directory Structure

```text
OPFS
│
├── projects/
│   └── project-id/
│
├── assets/
│   ├── videos/
│   ├── images/
│   ├── audio/
│   ├── stickers/
│   └── fonts/
│
├── proxies/
├── thumbnails/
├── waveforms/
├── cache/
└── temp/
```

---

## Storage Categories

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|
| assets | Original imported media. |
| proxies | Editing proxies. |
| thumbnails | Posters & previews. |
| waveforms | Audio previews. |
| cache | Disposable artifacts. |
| temp | Temporary rendering buffers. |

---

## OPFS Storage Interface

```ts
interface OPFSAssetLocation {
  assetId: string;
  relativePath: string;
}
```

---

## File Lifecycle

```text
Import
  │
Write to temp/
  │
Integrity Verification
  │
Move to assets/
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Files are atomically moved after integrity validation.

---

# 22.24 IndexedDB Metadata Engine

IndexedDB stores structured project metadata.

## IndexedDB Database Layout

```text
TryLipiDB
│
├── Projects
├── Assets
├── TimelineSnapshots
├── AIWorkflows
├── Captions
├── Waveforms
├── SearchIndex
├── Autosave
└── Settings
```

---

## Object Stores

| Store | Contents |
|-------|----------|
| Projects | Project manifest. |
| Assets | Asset registry. |
| TimelineSnapshots | Immutable snapshots. |
| AIWorkflows | Workflow checkpoints. |
| Captions | Caption metadata. |
| SearchIndex | Indexed metadata. |

---

## IndexedDB Interface

```ts
interface IndexedProjectRecord {
  projectId: string;
  snapshotId: string;
}
```

---

## Indexed Fields

- Asset IDs.
- Tags.
- Search keywords.
- Snapshot IDs.
- Workflow IDs.

---

## Engineering Rules

IndexedDB stores metadata only—not large binary media.

---

# 22.25 Service Worker Architecture

The Service Worker enables offline application startup.

## Service Worker Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| App Shell Cache | HTML/CSS/JS bundles. |
| Static Assets | Fonts/icons. |
| API Interception | Offline fallback. |
| Background Sync | Upload scheduling. |
| Update Detection | Runtime upgrades. |

---

## Service Worker Pipeline

```text
Browser Request
      │
Service Worker
      │
Cache / Network
      │
Editor Response
```

---

## Cache Categories

| Cache | Contents |
|------|----------|
| Shell Cache | App bundle. |
| Static Cache | Fonts/icons. |
| Runtime Cache | Small API responses. |
| Thumbnail Cache | Posters. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ServiceWorkerState {
  version: string;
  shellCached: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Service Worker never caches authenticated API responses containing sensitive data.

---

# 22.26 Offline Asset Cache Engine

Assets remain playable without internet.

## Cache Pipeline

```text
Asset Imported
     │
Asset Registry
     │
Local Cache Index
     │
Offline Playback
```

---

## Cached Asset Types

| Asset | Cached |
|------|--------|
| Videos | Yes |
| Images | Yes |
| Audio | Yes |
| Fonts | Yes |
| Stickers | Yes |
| Thumbnails | Yes |
| LUTs | Yes |

---

## Cache States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Cached | Fully offline. |
| Partial | Metadata only. |
| Streaming | Cloud-backed asset. |
| Missing | Requires download. |

---

## Cache Interface

```ts
interface OfflineAssetCache {
  assetId: string;
  cachedLocally: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Visible timeline assets receive highest cache priority.

---

# 22.27 Offline AI Queue Architecture

AI workflows created offline are queued instead of executed remotely.

## Offline AI Pipeline

```text
Offline Workflow
      │
Offline Queue
      │
Checkpoint Store
      │
Connectivity Restored
      │
Scheduler Execution
```

---

## Offline Queue Categories

| Queue | Example |
|------|----------|
| Translation | Pending translation. |
| Smart Zoom | Pending AI analysis. |
| Thumbnail Ranking | Pending Vision request. |
| Script Writer | Pending generation. |

---

## Queue Interface

```ts
interface OfflineAIJob {
  workflowId: string;
  queuedOffline: boolean;
}
```

---

## Offline Workflow UX

- Creator continues editing.
- Timeline marks pending AI nodes.
- AI executes automatically when online.

---

## Engineering Rules

Offline AI jobs preserve identical workflow context.

---

# 22.28 Background Sync Engine

Synchronization happens after connectivity returns.

## Sync Pipeline

```text
Connectivity Restored
       │
Sync Planner
       │
Upload Assets
       │
Upload Snapshots
       │
Upload AI Results
```

---

## Sync Priorities

| Priority | Sync Item |
|----------|-----------|
| Critical | Project snapshots. |
| High | Imported assets. |
| Medium | Thumbnails/proxies. |
| Low | Diagnostics. |

---

## Sync Interface

```ts
interface BackgroundSyncJob {
  syncJobId: string;
  syncState: SyncState;
}
```

---

## Sync States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Waiting | Pending internet. |
| Uploading | Active sync. |
| Verifying | Integrity validation. |
| Completed | Synced successfully. |
| Failed | Retry scheduled. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Sync is incremental and resumable.

---

# 22.29 Sync Conflict Resolution Engine

Offline edits may conflict with cloud edits.

## Conflict Pipeline

```text
Local Snapshot
      │
Cloud Snapshot
      │
Conflict Detector
      │
Merge Planner
```

---

## Conflict Sources

| Source | Example |
|--------|----------|
| Two Devices | Different edits offline. |
| Local AI | Cloud AI already completed. |
| Asset Rename | Different metadata. |
| Timeline Edit | Concurrent modifications. |

---

## Conflict Strategies

| Conflict | Resolution |
|----------|------------|
| Metadata | Merge automatically. |
| Timeline | Branch snapshots. |
| AI Output | Keep newest completed workflow. |
| Asset | Preserve both aliases. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface SyncConflict {
  conflictId: string;
  snapshotIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline conflicts never overwrite local edits silently.

---

# 22.30 Connectivity State Machine

Connectivity is centrally managed.

## Connectivity States

```text
Online
 │
Connection Lost
 │
Offline
 │
Reconnecting
 │
Online
```

---

## State Behaviors

| State | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| Online | Sync enabled. |
| Offline | Queue sync jobs. |
| Reconnecting | Verify network. |
| Online Restored | Resume sync queue. |

---

## Connectivity Interface

```ts
interface ConnectivityState {
  online: boolean;
  reconnectAttempts: number;
}
```

---

## Offline Banner Rules

- Editing continues.
- Export local video still works.
- AI jobs show "Queued until online."

---

## Engineering Rules

Connectivity changes never interrupt playback.

---

# 22.31 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes offline infrastructure metrics.

## Metrics

- OPFS storage usage.
- IndexedDB size.
- Cached assets.
- Pending sync jobs.
- Offline AI queue length.
- Connectivity transitions.
- Sync throughput.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface OfflineDiagnostics {
  opfsUsageMB: number;
  pendingSyncJobs: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| OPFS Nearly Full | Storage threshold exceeded. |
| IndexedDB Corrupted | Recovery required. |
| Sync Queue Growing | Connectivity unavailable. |
| Offline AI Queue Stale | Pending too long. |

---

# 22.32 Acceptance Tests

## Offline Runtime Tests

- Project opens without internet.
- Timeline edits persist offline.
- Playback works entirely offline.

## Storage Tests

- Assets stored in OPFS.
- Metadata stored in IndexedDB.
- Integrity survives refresh.

## Service Worker Tests

- App shell loads offline.
- Static assets served from cache.
- Update detection works correctly.

## Sync Tests

- Offline edits sync after reconnect.
- Upload resumes after interruption.
- Snapshot verification succeeds.

## Conflict Tests

- Timeline conflicts create branches.
- Metadata merges correctly.
- AI queue resumes after reconnect.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 22.2)

1. TryLipi is a local-first editor.
2. Projects always boot from local storage before cloud.
3. OPFS is the canonical binary asset store.
4. IndexedDB stores structured project metadata only.
5. Service Worker provides the offline application shell.
6. Offline AI workflows are queued with preserved checkpoints.
7. Background synchronization is incremental and resumable.
8. Connectivity changes never interrupt editing or playback.
9. Timeline conflicts create recoverable branches instead of overwriting edits.
10. Offline infrastructure remains fully observable through diagnostics.

13. Canonical Engineering Rules

---

# 22.41 Caching Philosophy

Caching is the biggest performance multiplier in TryLipi.

A creator repeatedly scrubs through the same timeline, previews the same clips, opens the same assets, regenerates thumbnails, and revisits AI outputs.

Instead of recomputing or reloading everything, TryLipi maintains a **multi-layer cache hierarchy** optimized for browser editing.

The cache system is designed around one idea:

> **Load once, reuse everywhere, invalidate deterministically.**

---

## Golden Cache Principles

1. Source assets are never caches.
2. Every cache layer has a clear ownership boundary.
3. Frequently accessed resources stay closest to the renderer.
4. Cache eviction never deletes original project data.
5. Cache invalidation is deterministic.
6. Predictive loading happens before creators need data.
7. Cache usage is measurable.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Cache Manager | Central cache orchestration. |
| Memory Cache | Hot runtime assets. |
| Disk Cache | Persistent previews/proxies. |
| AI Cache | Prompt/context reuse. |
| Prefetch Engine | Predictive loading. |
| Eviction Engine | Storage cleanup. |

---

# 22.42 Complete Cache Hierarchy

TryLipi maintains multiple cache layers.

## Cache Hierarchy

```text
Application Runtime
│
├── L1 Memory Cache
├── L2 GPU Texture Cache
├── L3 OPFS Cache
├── L4 IndexedDB Metadata Cache
├── L5 Service Worker Cache
└── L6 Cloud Cache
```

---

## Cache Layers

| Layer | Purpose | Lifetime |
|-------|---------|----------|
| L1 Memory | Active timeline assets. | Session |
| L2 GPU | Decoded textures. | Frame/session |
| L3 OPFS | Thumbnails, proxies, AI artifacts. | Persistent |
| L4 IndexedDB | Metadata/search indexes. | Persistent |
| L5 Service Worker | App shell/static assets. | Persistent |
| L6 Cloud Cache | Shared reusable AI results. | Workspace |

---

## Cache Lookup Order

```text
Memory
  ↓
GPU
  ↓
OPFS
  ↓
IndexedDB
  ↓
Service Worker
  ↓
Cloud
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Cache lookups stop at the first valid hit.

---

# 22.43 Cache Manager Architecture

The Cache Manager coordinates all cache layers.

## Cache Manager Pipeline

```text
Asset Request
     │
Cache Manager
     │
Lookup Strategy
     │
Hit / Miss
     │
Load Resource
```

---

## Cache Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Lookup | Multi-layer resolution. |
| Population | Store new cache entries. |
| Eviction | Remove disposable entries. |
| Metrics | Hit/miss statistics. |
| Validation | Version/hash verification. |

---

## Cache Manager Interface

```ts
interface CacheManager {
  cacheLayers: CacheLayer[];
  metrics: CacheMetrics;
}
```

---

## Cache States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Hot | Memory resident. |
| Warm | Disk cached. |
| Cold | Metadata only. |
| Missing | Fetch required. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Cache Manager is the only subsystem allowed to populate persistent caches.

---

# 22.44 Predictive Timeline Prefetch Engine

The timeline predicts what creators will view next.

## Prediction Pipeline

```text
Playback Head
      │
Viewport Predictor
      │
Prefetch Planner
      │
Asset Loader
```

---

## Prediction Window

```text
Current Frame
     │
+5 Seconds
+10 Seconds
+15 Seconds
```

Assets inside this window begin loading before playback reaches them.

---

## Prefetch Inputs

| Input | Used For |
|------|----------|
| Playback Direction | Forward/backward prefetch. |
| Scroll Velocity | Timeline navigation. |
| Zoom Level | Visible density. |
| Playback Speed | Buffer distance. |

---

## Prefetch Priorities

| Priority | Resource |
|----------|----------|
| Highest | Upcoming proxy frames. |
| High | Audio buffers. |
| Medium | Thumbnail strips. |
| Low | Nearby AI overlays. |

---

## Prefetch Interface

```ts
interface TimelinePrefetchWindow {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Prefetch must yield immediately when memory pressure increases.

---

# 22.45 Smart Asset Preloading Engine

Preloading reduces latency during editing.

## Preloading Pipeline

```text
Project Open
     │
Asset Importance Ranker
     │
Preload Queue
     │
Cache Population
```

---

## Importance Ranking

| Rank | Asset |
|-----|-------|
| Highest | Visible timeline clips. |
| High | Selected clips. |
| Medium | Adjacent clips. |
| Low | Library assets. |
| Lowest | Archived assets. |

---

## Preload Strategies

| Strategy | Trigger |
|----------|---------|
| Timeline Neighbor | Scrubbing nearby clips. |
| Hover Preview | Mouse hover. |
| Selection | Clip selected. |
| Playback | Upcoming playback window. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface AssetPreloadJob {
  assetId: string;
  preloadReason: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Preloading never downloads original assets unnecessarily.

---

# 22.46 Thumbnail & Poster Cache Engine

Thumbnail generation is expensive and reusable.

## Thumbnail Cache Pipeline

```text
Imported Asset
      │
Thumbnail Generator
      │
Poster Cache
      │
Timeline Preview
```

---

## Cached Preview Types

| Preview | Cached |
|---------|--------|
| Asset Poster | Yes |
| Timeline Strip | Yes |
| Hover Preview | Yes |
| Media Grid | Yes |
| AI Thumbnail Candidates | Yes |

---

## Cache Resolution

| Asset Change | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| Rename | Keep cache. |
| Move Folder | Keep cache. |
| Replace Media | Invalidate cache. |
| Delete Asset | Remove cache. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ThumbnailCacheEntry {
  assetId: string;
  posterVersion: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Poster cache survives browser restarts.

---

# 22.47 Proxy Cache Engine

Editing proxies are cached separately from original media.

## Proxy Cache Pipeline

```text
Video Import
     │
Proxy Generator
     │
Proxy Cache
     │
Playback Engine
```

---

## Proxy Cache Levels

| Proxy | Cached |
|------|--------|
| 240p | Yes |
| 480p | Yes |
| 720p | Yes |
| 1080p | Optional |
| Original | Never treated as cache |

---

## Cache Selection

| Playback Mode | Proxy |
|--------------|-------|
| Fast Scrubbing | 480p |
| Preview | 720p |
| High Quality Preview | 1080p |
| Export | Original |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface ProxyCacheEntry {
  assetId: string;
  proxyResolution: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Proxy cache invalidates only if original media changes.

---

# 22.48 AI Context & Prompt Cache Engine

AI context generation is expensive.

The same workflow should reuse existing context whenever possible.

## AI Cache Pipeline

```text
Workflow Context
      │
Context Hash
      │
Prompt Cache
      │
Cached Response
```

---

## Cached AI Resources

| Resource | Cached |
|----------|--------|
| Prompt Payload | Yes |
| Context Embeddings | Yes |
| OCR Results | Yes |
| Transcript Chunks | Yes |
| Speaker Labels | Yes |
| Vision Labels | Yes |

---

## Cache Key Components

```text
Snapshot Hash
Capability ID
Prompt Template Version
Model Version
Language
```

---

## Interface

```ts
interface AIContextCache {
  contextHash: string;
  cachedResponseId: string;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Lower token usage.
- Faster workflows.
- Deterministic replay.

---

## Engineering Rules

Prompt cache invalidates whenever prompt template version changes.

---

# 22.49 Cache Invalidation Engine

Caches remain correct through deterministic invalidation.

## Invalidation Pipeline

```text
Project Event
      │
Invalidation Planner
      │
Affected Cache Layers
      │
Cleanup Queue
```

---

## Invalidation Events

| Event | Invalidated |
|------|-------------|
| Timeline Edit | AI context cache. |
| Asset Replace | Thumbnail + proxy cache. |
| AI Template Update | Prompt cache. |
| Project Migration | Metadata cache. |
| Workspace Logout | Memory cache. |

---

## Selective Invalidation

```text
Asset Updated
     │
Poster Cache ❌
Proxy Cache ❌
Transcript Cache ✅
```

Only affected caches are rebuilt.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CacheInvalidationEvent {
  eventType: string;
  affectedCacheKeys: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Invalidation must be granular—not full-cache clears.

---

# 22.50 Storage Pressure & Cache Eviction Engine

Storage quotas differ across browsers and devices.

The cache system adapts automatically.

## Storage Pressure Pipeline

```text
Storage Monitor
      │
Pressure Detector
      │
Eviction Planner
      │
Cleanup Jobs
```

---

## Pressure Levels

| Level | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Normal | No eviction. |
| Medium | Remove temporary previews. |
| High | Remove unused proxies. |
| Critical | Aggressive cache cleanup. |

---

## Eviction Priority

| Order | Cache |
|------|-------|
| 1 | Temporary decode cache. |
| 2 | Hover previews. |
| 3 | Thumbnail strips. |
| 4 | Unused proxies. |
| 5 | AI context cache. |
| Never | Original project assets. |

---

## Eviction Strategy

| Strategy | Used |
|----------|------|
| LRU | Memory cache. |
| LFU | Preview cache. |
| TTL | Runtime cache. |
| Snapshot-Aware | AI cache. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface StoragePressureState {
  pressureLevel: StoragePressureLevel;
  reclaimableBytes: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Original assets and snapshots are never evicted automatically.

---

# 22.51 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes cache performance metrics.

## Metrics

- Cache hit rate.
- Cache miss rate.
- Prefetch success rate.
- Memory cache size.
- GPU cache usage.
- OPFS cache size.
- AI cache reuse percentage.
- Storage pressure level.

---

## Interface

```ts
interface CacheDiagnostics {
  hitRate: number;
  missRate: number;
  reclaimedStorageMB: number;
}
```

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Cache Thrashing | Frequent evictions. |
| Low Hit Rate | Prefetch ineffective. |
| Storage Pressure High | Cleanup scheduled. |
| AI Cache Stale | Version mismatch. |

---

# 22.52 Acceptance Tests

## Cache Tests

- Memory cache resolves before disk cache.
- Poster cache reused after restart.
- AI cache reused for identical workflow.

## Prefetch Tests

- Upcoming clips load before playback.
- Hover previews preload correctly.
- Scrubbing loads neighboring assets.

## Invalidation Tests

- Asset replacement rebuilds poster/proxy cache.
- Timeline edits invalidate AI context only.
- Prompt template updates invalidate prompt cache.

## Storage Tests

- High storage pressure evicts disposable caches.
- Original assets remain untouched.
- GPU texture cache respects LRU.

## Monitoring Tests

- Cache metrics update live.
- Hit/miss statistics accurate.
- Storage pressure transitions correctly.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 22.3)

1. TryLipi uses a six-layer cache hierarchy from memory to cloud.
2. Cache Manager owns all cache population and eviction.
3. Timeline prefetch predicts future playback windows.
4. Smart preloading prioritizes visible and nearby assets.
5. Thumbnail and proxy caches persist across sessions.
6. AI context cache eliminates duplicate provider requests.
7. Cache invalidation is granular and deterministic.
8. Storage pressure triggers progressive cache cleanup.
9. Original assets and immutable snapshots are never treated as caches.
10. Cache performance is continuously measurable through diagnostics.

---

# 22.61 Adaptive Rendering Philosophy

TryLipi should deliver the **best possible editing experience on every device** without asking creators to manually change dozens of settings.

A creator editing on:

- Windows laptop with Intel Iris GPU.
- RTX 4060 desktop.
- MacBook Air M2.
- Chromebook.
- Low-end office laptop.

...should receive different rendering strategies automatically.

Rendering quality is **adaptive**, while export quality always remains deterministic.

---

## Golden Adaptive Rendering Principles

1. Editing quality adapts to device capability.
2. Export quality never adapts automatically.
3. Playback quality may change dynamically.
4. User interaction always has priority over visual fidelity.
5. Adaptation decisions are reversible.
6. GPU memory is treated as a limited resource.
7. Browser capabilities determine rendering pipeline selection.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Adaptive Quality Engine | Dynamic playback quality. |
| GPU Scheduler | GPU workload balancing. |
| Capability Negotiator | Browser feature detection. |
| Performance Mode Manager | Quality profiles. |
| Compatibility Layer | Browser-specific behavior. |

---

# 22.62 Adaptive Playback Quality Engine

Playback quality changes dynamically based on runtime performance.

## Playback Pipeline

```text
Playback Starts
      │
Performance Monitor
      │
Adaptive Quality Engine
      │
Render Resolution Decision
      │
Renderer
```

---

## Playback Quality Levels

| Quality | Resolution Source | Target Usage |
|---------|-------------------|--------------|
| Ultra | Original asset | Preview mode |
| High | 1080p proxy | Powerful devices |
| Balanced | 720p proxy | Default editing |
| Performance | 480p proxy | Slow devices |
| Ultra Performance | 240p proxy | Memory pressure |

---

## Automatic Downgrade Conditions

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| FPS below target | Lower proxy quality. |
| Memory pressure | Reduce texture quality. |
| CPU saturation | Reduce frame sampling. |
| Battery saver | Balanced mode. |

---

## Adaptive Playback Interface

```ts
interface PlaybackQualityState {
  qualityLevel: PlaybackQuality;
  proxyResolution: string;
}
```

---

## Recovery Strategy

Quality automatically increases again when:

- FPS stabilizes.
- Memory pressure decreases.
- Playback becomes idle.

---

## Engineering Rules

Playback quality changes are invisible to exported videos.

---

# 22.63 Dynamic Resolution Scaling Engine

Rendering resolution adapts independently from canvas resolution.

## Resolution Scaling Pipeline

```text
Canvas Size
     │
Resolution Scaler
     │
Internal Render Resolution
     │
Display Output
```

---

## Scaling Levels

| Display Resolution | Internal Resolution |
|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1920×1080 | 1920×1080 |
| 1920×1080 | 1600×900 |
| 1920×1080 | 1280×720 |
| 2560×1440 | 1920×1080 |
| 3840×2160 | 2560×1440 |

---

## Scaling Inputs

| Input | Effect |
|------|--------|
| GPU Performance | Resolution scale. |
| FPS | Increase/decrease scale. |
| Canvas Zoom | Dynamic sampling. |
| Playback Speed | Lower quality during fast scrub. |

---

## Scaling Interface

```ts
interface DynamicResolutionScale {
  renderScale: number;
}
```

---

## Scale Example

```text
Canvas: 4K
Render: 75%
Display: Upscaled
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Scaling affects preview only—not timeline coordinates or exports.

---

# 22.64 GPU Scheduling Architecture

GPU work is centrally scheduled.

## GPU Scheduling Pipeline

```text
Render Requests
      │
GPU Scheduler
      │
Priority Queue
      │
GPU Commands
```

---

## GPU Work Categories

| Category | Priority |
|----------|----------|
| Playback Frames | Highest |
| User Interaction | Highest |
| Texture Uploads | High |
| Thumbnail Generation | Medium |
| AI Preview Rendering | Low |
| Background Cleanup | Lowest |

---

## GPU Queue

```text
GPU Queue
│
├── Playback
├── Texture Upload
├── Effects
├── AI Overlay
└── Cleanup
```

---

## GPU Scheduler Interface

```ts
interface GPUScheduler {
  pendingCommands: number;
}
```

---

## Scheduling Rules

- Playback interrupts background uploads.
- Texture uploads are chunked.
- Cleanup waits until idle.

---

## Engineering Rules

GPU queue starvation is prevented through priority scheduling.

---

# 22.65 Browser Capability Negotiation Engine

Different browsers expose different APIs.

The Capability Engine detects features during startup.

## Negotiation Pipeline

```text
Browser Boot
     │
Capability Detector
     │
Runtime Feature Map
     │
Renderer Configuration
```

---

## Capabilities Detected

| Capability | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| WebCodecs | Video decoding. |
| WebGPU | GPU rendering. |
| WebGL2 | Rendering fallback. |
| OPFS | Storage. |
| SharedArrayBuffer | High-performance workers. |
| WebAssembly SIMD | FFmpeg optimization. |
| OffscreenCanvas | Worker rendering. |

---

## Capability Interface

```ts
interface BrowserCapabilities {
  webCodecs: boolean;
  webGPU: boolean;
  offscreenCanvas: boolean;
}
```

---

## Renderer Selection

| Capabilities | Renderer |
|-------------|----------|
| WebGPU + WebCodecs | Highest-performance renderer. |
| WebGL2 + WebCodecs | Standard renderer. |
| WebGL2 only | Compatibility renderer. |
| Canvas2D fallback | Emergency renderer. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Capabilities are detected once and cached for the session.

---

| Balanced | 720p | Standard | Stable |
| Quality | 1080p | Full | Best preview |
| Battery Saver | 480p | Reduced | Conservative |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface PerformanceMode {
  mode: "auto" | "performance" | "balanced" | "quality" | "battery";
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

---

# 22.67 Thermal & Battery Awareness Engine

Long editing sessions can increase power consumption.

## Resource Awareness Pipeline

```text
System Signals
      │
Power Manager
      │
Adaptive Quality Engine
```

---

## Signals Used

| Signal | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Battery Saver Enabled | Lower concurrency. |
| Low Battery | Reduce preview quality. |
| Charging | Allow higher quality. |
| Idle Device | Resume background work. |

---

## Adaptive Behaviors

| Condition | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| Battery Saver | Pause background AI indexing. |
| Low Battery | Reduce GPU workload. |
| Charging | Resume queued background jobs. |
| Idle | Run cache cleanup. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface PowerAwareRuntime {
  batterySaverEnabled: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Thermal adaptation must never interrupt exports already in progress.

---

---

## Engineering Rules

# 22.71 Acceptance Tests

## Adaptive Quality Tests

- FPS recovery restores quality.

- Experimental features remain isolated.

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 22.4)

1. Playback quality adapts independently from export quality.
2. Dynamic resolution scaling affects preview rendering only.
3. GPU workloads are centrally prioritized by the GPU Scheduler.
4. Browser capabilities determine renderer selection at startup.
5. Performance modes modify runtime behavior without affecting project data.
6. Battery-aware adaptation reduces background work before playback quality.
7. Cross-browser compatibility is implemented through renderer profiles and fallbacks.
8. Feature flags isolate rendering experiments from production workflows.
9. GPU queue starvation is prevented through priority scheduling.
10. Renderer behavior is continuously observable through diagnostics.

# 22.81 Production Infrastructure Philosophy

Building the editor is only **half** of TryLipi.

Operating it reliably for millions of creators is equally important.

Production infrastructure must guarantee:

- Zero-loss editing.
- Safe releases.
- Instant rollback.
- Runtime monitoring.
- Crash diagnostics.
- Progressive feature rollout.
- Environment isolation.

TryLipi treats production as an extension of the editor architecture.

---

## Golden Production Principles

1. Production builds are deterministic.
2. Runtime configuration is environment-driven.
3. Every release is reversible.
4. Every crash generates diagnostics.
5. Monitoring is built into every subsystem.
6. Feature rollout happens gradually.
7. Production secrets never ship to the client.

---

## Responsibilities

| System | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Build System | Production bundles. |
| Monitoring Platform | Runtime telemetry. |
| Error Pipeline | Crash reporting. |
| Release Manager | Deployments & rollback. |
| Feature Flag Engine | Progressive rollout. |
| Config Manager | Environment configuration. |

---

# 22.82 Production Build Pipeline Architecture

TryLipi produces optimized browser builds for production.

## Build Pipeline

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 22.5)

1. Production builds are deterministic and versioned.
2. Startup bundles contain only core editor functionality.
3. Runtime configuration is environment-driven.
4. Telemetry is built into every subsystem.
5. Crash reports never contain creator media or secrets.
6. Feature rollout is progressive and reversible.
7. Stable, Beta, Canary, and Internal releases are isolated.
8. Rollbacks restore previous runtime manifests without destructive project changes.
9. Browser clients never receive provider credentials.
10. Production diagnostics expose runtime health without affecting editor performance.

# 12.01 Screen Recording Backend Philosophy

TryLipi's screen recorder is **not a single uploaded video**.

A recording consists of:

- Screen stream.
- Webcam stream.
- Microphone audio.
- System audio.
- Cursor events.
- Click animations.
- Keyboard events.
- Zoom metadata.
- Window metadata.
- Timeline markers.

The backend receives all of these independently and reconstructs a recording project.

---

## Golden Recording Principles

1. Recordings upload progressively while recording.
2. Uploads survive browser refreshes.
3. Uploads survive internet interruptions.
4. Screen, webcam and audio remain independently synchronized.
5. Cursor metadata is stored separately from video.
6. Every recording becomes a normal TryLipi project after ingestion.
7. Original recordings are immutable after upload completion.

---

## Responsibilities

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Recording Session Service | Create/manage recording sessions. |
| Chunk Upload Service | Receive media chunks. |
| Metadata Service | Cursor/keyboard/window events. |
| FFmpeg Worker | Merge streams after upload. |
| Storage Service | Persist recording assets. |
| Sync Engine | Resume interrupted uploads. |

---

# 12.02 Recording Session Lifecycle

Every recording begins with a backend session.

## Lifecycle Diagram

```text
Creator Starts Recording
          │
Create Recording Session
          │
Receive Session Token
          │
Stream Chunks
          │
Receive Metadata Events
          │
Upload Finished
          │
Finalize Recording
          │
FFmpeg Processing
          │
Recording Project Created
```

---

## Session Timeline

| Stage | Backend Action |
|--------|----------------|
| Session Created | Generate session ID. |
| Recording Started | Reserve storage paths. |
| Upload Active | Receive chunks continuously. |
| Upload Finished | Validate manifests. |
| Processing | Merge streams. |
| Completed | Project imported. |

---

## Recording Lifecycle States

```text
CREATED
   │
READY
   │
RECORDING
   │
UPLOADING
   │
PROCESSING
   │
COMPLETED
```

---

## Engineering Rules

A recording session exists independently of upload completion.

---

# 12.03 Recording Session Service Architecture

This service owns every active recording.

## Architecture

```text
Recorder Client
       │
API Gateway
       │
Recording Session Service
       │
Redis Session Cache
       │
Mongo Recording Collection
       │
GCS Reservation Service
```

---

## Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Session Creation | Generate recording ID. |
| Authentication | Workspace ownership. |
| Upload Reservation | Allocate upload targets. |
| Metadata Registration | Register expected streams. |
| Session Recovery | Restore interrupted recording. |

---

## Mongo Collection

```text
recording_sessions
│
├── sessionId
├── workspaceId
├── projectId
├── status
├── streams[]
├── uploadManifest
├── createdAt
└── expiresAt
```

---

## Session Interface

```ts
interface RecordingSession {
  sessionId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  projectId: string;
  status: RecordingSessionStatus;
}
```

---

## Redis Cache

Stores:

- Active upload offsets.
- Heartbeats.
- Chunk acknowledgements.
- Temporary metadata.

---

## Engineering Rules

Redis is authoritative only while recording is active.

---

# 12.04 Recording Session State Machine

The backend maintains deterministic recording states.

## State Machine

```text
CREATED
  │
READY
  │
RECORDING
  │
PAUSED
  │
RECORDING
  │
UPLOADING
  │
VERIFYING
  │
PROCESSING
  │
COMPLETED
```

---

## State Definitions

| State | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| CREATED | Session initialized. |
| READY | Client prepared to upload. |
| RECORDING | Receiving chunks. |
| PAUSED | Upload temporarily halted. |
| UPLOADING | Upload continuing after stop. |
| VERIFYING | Integrity verification. |
| PROCESSING | Merge worker active. |
| COMPLETED | Recording imported. |

---

## Failure States

| Failure | Recovery |
|---------|----------|
| Upload Lost | Resume offset. |
| Manifest Missing | Reject finalize request. |
| Corrupted Chunk | Request retransmission. |
| Timeout | Session expires. |

---

## Engineering Rules

State transitions are append-only events.

---

# 12.05 Chunk Upload Protocol

Videos upload in deterministic chunks.

## Upload Pipeline

```text
MediaRecorder
      │
Chunk Generator
      │
Upload Queue
      │
Chunk Upload API
      │
Chunk Storage
```

---

## Upload Streams

| Stream | Separate Upload |
|--------|-----------------|
| Screen Video | Yes |
| Webcam Video | Yes |
| Microphone Audio | Yes |
| System Audio | Yes |

---

## Chunk Format

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| sessionId | Recording session. |
| streamId | Screen/webcam/audio. |
| chunkIndex | Sequential index. |
| byteOffset | Upload offset. |
| durationMs | Chunk duration. |
| checksum | SHA256 checksum. |

---

## Chunk Upload Interface

```ts
interface RecordingChunk {
  sessionId: string;
  streamId: string;
  chunkIndex: number;
  checksum: string;
}
```

---

## Chunk Size Policy

| Network | Chunk Duration |
|---------|----------------|
| Fast WiFi | 4–6 seconds |
| Mobile | 2–3 seconds |
| Slow Connection | 1 second adaptive |

---

## Engineering Rules

Chunk indexes are immutable and strictly increasing.

---

# 12.06 Upload Manifest Architecture

The manifest describes the complete recording.

## Manifest Structure

```text
Recording Manifest
│
├── sessionId
├── streams
├── chunkCount
├── duration
├── codec
├── resolution
└── metadataVersion
```

---

## Stream Manifest

```text
streams
│
├── screen
├── webcam
├── microphone
└── systemAudio
```

---

## Manifest Interface

```ts
interface RecordingManifest {
  sessionId: string;
  streams: RecordingStreamManifest[];
}
```

---

## Manifest Verification

Checks:

- Missing chunks.
- Duplicate chunks.
- Duration consistency.
- Codec compatibility.

---

## Engineering Rules

Recording cannot finalize without a verified manifest.

---

# 12.07 Recording Session APIs

## REST Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /recordings/session` | Create session. |
| `GET /recordings/session/:id` | Session state. |
| `PATCH /recordings/session/:id` | Pause/resume. |
| `POST /recordings/chunks` | Upload chunk. |
| `POST /recordings/finalize` | Finalize recording. |
| `GET /recordings/upload-status/:id` | Resume upload. |

---

## Session Creation Response

```ts
interface CreateRecordingSessionResponse {
  sessionId: string;
  uploadToken: string;
  uploadEndpoints: UploadEndpoint[];
}
```

---

## Authentication

Requires:

- Workspace JWT.
- CSRF validation.
- Recording upload token.

---

## Engineering Rules

Chunk upload tokens expire independently from user sessions.

---

# 12.08 Chunk Validation Engine

Every uploaded chunk is validated before persistence.

## Validation Pipeline

```text
Chunk Upload
     │
Checksum Validation
     │
Codec Validation
     │
Chunk Order Validation
     │
Persist Chunk
```

---

## Validation Checks

| Check | Purpose |
|-------|----------|
| SHA256 | Integrity. |
| Stream Ownership | Prevent injection. |
| Chunk Order | Prevent duplicates. |
| Duration | Consistency. |
| Codec | Supported recording format. |

---

## Validation Interface

```ts
interface ChunkValidationResult {
  accepted: boolean;
  checksumValid: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Rejected chunks never enter persistent storage.

---

# 12.09 Upload Recovery & Resume Engine

Uploads survive interruptions.

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Browser Reconnect
      │
Resume API
      │
Chunk Offset Lookup
      │
Resume Upload Queue
```

---

## Recovery Data Stored

| Field | Purpose |
|------|----------|
| Last Chunk Index | Resume upload. |
| Uploaded Bytes | Offset recovery. |
| Stream Completion | Missing stream detection. |
| Manifest Progress | Upload completion. |

---

## Resume Interface

```ts
interface ResumeUploadState {
  uploadedChunkIndexes: number[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Resume requests never overwrite existing chunks.

---

# 12.10 Recording Metadata Service

Metadata is uploaded independently from media.

## Metadata Categories

| Metadata | Stored |
|----------|--------|
| Cursor Position | Yes |
| Mouse Click | Yes |
| Keyboard Events | Yes |
| Window Resize | Yes |
| Zoom Events | Yes |
| Active Window | Yes |

---

## Metadata Pipeline

```text
Recorder Client
      │
Metadata Event Queue
      │
Metadata Service
      │
Mongo + OPFS
```

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface RecordingMetadataEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  eventType: string;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Cursor replay.
- Click animations.
- Keyboard overlays.
- AI Smart Zoom alignment.

---

## Engineering Rules

Metadata timestamps use the recording timeline clock.

---

# 12.11 Diagnostics Engine

Developer Mode exposes recording backend diagnostics.

## Metrics

- Active recording sessions.
- Upload throughput.
- Chunk retry count.
- Resume success rate.
- Manifest validation failures.
- Metadata events received.
- Average upload latency.

---

## Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Missing Chunk | Upload gap detected. |
| Manifest Mismatch | Finalization blocked. |
| Upload Timeout | Session inactive. |
| Checksum Failure | Chunk rejected. |

---

# 12.12 Acceptance Tests

## Session Tests

- Session creation succeeds.
- Session resumes after refresh.
- Session expires correctly.

## Chunk Tests

- Chunk order preserved.
- Duplicate chunk rejected.
- Checksum validation enforced.

## Resume Tests

- Upload resumes from last chunk.
- Missing chunks requested again.
- Completed chunks skipped.

## Manifest Tests

- Missing streams rejected.
- Manifest checksum validated.
- Recording finalizes only after verification.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 12.1)

1. Every recording starts with a backend recording session.
2. Screen, webcam, microphone and system audio upload independently.
3. Chunk uploads are immutable and sequential.
4. Redis tracks temporary upload progress during active recording.
5. MongoDB stores authoritative recording session metadata.
6. Recording manifests define the complete upload structure.
7. Upload recovery resumes from the last acknowledged chunk.
8. Metadata events are synchronized using the recording timeline clock.
9. Recording finalization requires manifest integrity verification.
10. Completed recordings become immutable TryLipi projects.

# 12.21 Recording Reconstruction Philosophy

Uploading chunks is only **half of the backend**.

After recording stops, TryLipi reconstructs a complete editing project by combining multiple independent streams into a synchronized timeline.

A recording may contain:

- Screen video.
- Webcam video.
- Microphone audio.
- System audio.
- Cursor events.
- Keyboard events.
- Window movement.
- Zoom metadata.

The backend converts these raw streams into an editable TryLipi project without losing synchronization.

---

## Golden Reconstruction Principles

1. Every stream has its own timeline.
2. Synchronization uses timestamps—not arrival order.
3. Missing streams are handled gracefully.
4. Reconstruction is deterministic.
5. FFmpeg never modifies original uploaded chunks.
6. Generated timeline is editable immediately.
7. Reconstruction is resumable after worker failures.

---

## Responsibilities

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Reconstruction Worker | Build project timeline. |
| Sync Engine | Align timestamps. |
| FFmpeg Worker | Merge media streams. |
| Metadata Engine | Replay cursor/keyboard events. |
| Project Generator | Create editable project. |

---

# 12.22 Multi-Stream Synchronization Engine

Every recording stream is synchronized using a shared recording clock.

```text

Screen Webcam Microphone

System Audio Cursor Events
       │
Timestamp Alignment Engine
       │
Unified Recording Timeline
```

---

## Streams Supported

| Stream | Clock Source |
|--------|--------------|
| Screen Video | Recording clock |
| Webcam | Recording clock |
| Microphone | Recording clock |
| System Audio | Recording clock |
| Cursor | Event clock |
| Keyboard | Event clock |
| Window Events | Event clock |

---

## Timeline Units

| Unit | Precision |
|------|-----------|
| Timeline | Microseconds |
| Metadata | Microseconds |
| Frame Index | Derived from timestamps |

---

```ts
  streamId: string;
  startTimestampUs: number;
  endTimestampUs: number;
}
```

# 12.41 Live Upload Philosophy

Unlike traditional screen recorders, TryLipi **uploads while recording is still happening**.

Instead of waiting until recording finishes:

- Chunks upload continuously.
- Upload progress syncs in real time.
- Recording state survives refreshes.
- Backend knows recording progress every few seconds.

This enables:

- Instant cloud backup.
- Resume after crashes.
- Editing almost immediately after recording ends.
- Long recordings without huge upload waits.

---

## Golden Live Upload Principles

1. Upload begins during recording.
2. Recording never blocks waiting for uploads.
3. Upload queue is independent of MediaRecorder.
4. Backend acknowledges every uploaded chunk.
5. Progress survives browser refresh.
6. Network interruptions never discard recorded media.
7. Upload state is eventually consistent.

---

## Responsibilities

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Live Upload Runtime | Stream upload orchestration. |
| Upload Queue | Buffer outgoing chunks. |
| Heartbeat Service | Session liveness. |
| WebSocket Gateway | Progress synchronization. |
| Presence Service | Active recording status. |
| Telemetry Service | Upload metrics. |

---

# 12.42 Live Upload Runtime Architecture

Recording uploads continuously while new chunks are being generated.

## Runtime Pipeline

```text
MediaRecorder
      │
Chunk Generator
      │
Local Upload Queue
      │
Upload Worker
      │
API Gateway
      │
Chunk Storage
      │
WebSocket ACK
```

---

## Runtime Components

| Component | Responsibility |
|----------|----------------|
| MediaRecorder | Generates blobs. |
| Upload Queue | Stores pending chunks. |
| Upload Worker | Sends chunks. |
| ACK Listener | Tracks uploaded chunks. |
| Retry Queue | Failed uploads. |

---

## Upload Queue States

```text
CREATED
   │
QUEUED
   │
UPLOADING
   │
ACKNOWLEDGED
```

---

## Upload Runtime Interface

```ts
interface LiveUploadRuntime {
  sessionId: string;
  queuedChunks: number;
  uploadingChunks: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Media recording continues even if upload queue temporarily grows.

---

# 12.43 Recording Heartbeat Protocol

The backend continuously verifies that recording is alive.

## Heartbeat Pipeline

```text
Recorder Client
      │
Heartbeat Worker
      │
WebSocket / HTTP Ping
      │
Heartbeat Service
      │
Redis Session Cache
```

---

## Heartbeat Frequency

| State | Frequency |
|-------|-----------|
| Recording | Every 5 seconds |
| Uploading Only | Every 15 seconds |
| Paused | Every 20 seconds |
| Idle | Disabled |

---

## Heartbeat Payload

| Field | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| sessionId | Recording session. |
| recordingDuration | Elapsed recording time. |
| queuedChunks | Upload backlog. |
| uploadedChunks | Completed uploads. |
| batteryState | Client diagnostics. |
| networkType | Telemetry. |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface RecordingHeartbeat {
  sessionId: string;
  timestampUs: number;
  queuedChunks: number;
}
```

---

## Missed Heartbeat Strategy

| Missed Count | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| 1 | Mark delayed. |
| 3 | Attempt reconnect. |
| 6 | Mark disconnected. |
| 12 | Expire recording session. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Heartbeat timeout never deletes uploaded media.

---

# 12.45 Upload Buffer Management Engine

The recorder maintains an adaptive upload buffer.

## Buffer Pipeline

```text
Recorded Chunk
      │
Upload Buffer
      │
Upload Worker
      │
ACK Received
      │
Buffer Released
```

---

## Buffer States

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Pending | Waiting upload. |
| Uploading | In progress. |
| Uploaded | ACK received. |
| Retry | Waiting retry. |
| Failed | Manual recovery. |

---

## Adaptive Buffer Size

| Network | Max Buffered Chunks |
|---------|---------------------|
| WiFi | 30 |
| 5G | 20 |
| 4G | 12 |
| Slow Network | Dynamic |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface UploadBufferState {
  pendingChunks: number;
  bufferedDurationMs: number;
}
```

---

## Overflow Strategy

When buffer exceeds safe threshold:

- Pause uploads temporarily.
- Continue recording locally.
- Increase retry interval.
- Warn UI if storage pressure grows.

---

## Engineering Rules

Upload buffer never drops recorded chunks before persistence.

---

# 12.52 Acceptance Tests

## Live Upload Tests

- Upload begins during recording.
- Recording continues during upload backlog.
- Upload queue drains correctly.

## Heartbeat Tests

- Heartbeats refresh Redis session.
- Missed heartbeats trigger reconnect.
- Session expires after timeout.

## Recovery Tests

- Offline upload resumes correctly.
- ACK offsets preserved.
- Duplicate uploads avoided.

## Progress Tests

- Progress updates after ACK.
- ETA decreases correctly.
- Retry updates reflected in UI.

## Presence Tests

- Recording appears active in workspace.
- Presence expires after inactivity.
- Upload-only sessions remain visible.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 12.3)

1. Recording uploads begin immediately while recording continues.
2. Upload queues are independent from MediaRecorder generation.
3. Heartbeats verify recording liveness every few seconds.
4. WebSocket events broadcast recording progress in real time.
5. Upload buffers retain recorded chunks until acknowledged.
6. Recording presence is stored in Redis with automatic expiration.
7. Network interruptions freeze uploads without stopping recording.
8. Background upload scheduling prioritizes recording continuity.
9. Upload progress is calculated only from acknowledged chunks.
10. Telemetry measures upload performance without storing creator content.

# 12.61 Cursor Intelligence Philosophy

The cursor is **not part of the recorded video**.

It is captured as structured metadata so that TryLipi can recreate cinematic cursor movements similar to **Screen Studio**, **Cursorful**, and **Tella**, while remaining fully editable.

Every movement becomes semantic data.

Examples:

- Cursor path.
- Velocity.
- Acceleration.
- Click position.
- Double click.
- Right click.
- Drag selection.
- Hover duration.
- Scroll wheel.
- Window focus changes.

This enables AI-powered zooms and motion effects without modifying the original recording.

---

## Golden Cursor Intelligence Principles

1. Cursor metadata is stored separately from pixels.
2. Cursor replay is deterministic.
3. Cursor smoothing is reversible.
4. Click animations are generated during rendering.
5. Smart Zoom uses cursor metadata as a primary signal.
6. Window changes become timeline events.
7. Metadata remains editable forever.

---

## Responsibilities

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Cursor Event Service | Receive raw cursor events. |
| Smoothing Engine | Build cinematic paths. |
| Click Engine | Generate click metadata. |
| Keyboard Engine | Capture keyboard events. |
| Window Tracker | Browser/window metadata. |
| Smart Zoom Generator | AI zoom metadata. |

---

# 12.62 Cursor Event Ingestion Service

Every cursor movement is streamed as lightweight metadata.

```text
Browser Pointer API
        │
Cursor Capture Worker
        │
Event Buffer
        │
Metadata Upload Queue
        │
Cursor Event Service
        │
Mongo + OPFS Metadata Store
```

---

## Captured Cursor Events

| Event | Captured |
|-------|----------|
| Move | Yes |
| Click | Yes |
| Double Click | Yes |
| Right Click | Yes |
| Drag Start | Yes |
| Drag Move | Yes |
| Drag End | Yes |
| Scroll | Yes |
| Hover | Yes |

```ts
interface CursorEvent {
  eventId: string;
  sessionId: string;
  timestampUs: number;
  type: CursorEventType;
  x: number;
  y: number;
}
```

---

## Event Buffering Strategy

| State | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| Recording | Buffer every frame/event. |
| Uploading | Batch upload every few seconds. |
| Offline | Persist locally until sync. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor events use the same microsecond recording clock as media streams.

# 12.63 Cursor Smoothing & Trajectory Engine

|-------|---------|

| Motion Spline | Smooth cinematic curve. |
