# 12.69 Metadata Compression & Storage Architecture

Cursor metadata can contain millions of events.

Compression is mandatory.

## Compression Pipeline

```text
Raw Events
     │
Delta Encoder
     │
Run-Length Compression
     │
Binary Metadata Format
     │
OPFS / GCS Storage
```

---

## Compression Techniques

| Technique | Used |
|-----------|------|
| Delta Encoding | Cursor coordinates |
| Timestamp Delta | Event times |
| Run-Length Encoding | Repeated movement |
| Binary Packing | Numeric metadata |
| Chunk Compression | Upload batches |

---

## Storage Layout

```text
metadata/
│
├── cursor.bin
├── keyboard.bin
├── clicks.bin
├── windows.bin
└── zoom_candidates.bin
```

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface MetadataChunk {
  chunkId: string;
  compressedBytes: number;
}
```

---

## Benefits

- Small uploads.
- Fast replay.
- Efficient AI processing.

---

## Engineering Rules

Metadata compression is lossless for timing information.

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 12.4)

1. Cursor metadata is stored separately from recorded pixels.
2. Every interaction uses the unified recording timeline clock.
3. Cursor smoothing generates reversible cinematic trajectories.
4. Click effects are generated during rendering from metadata.
5. Keyboard overlays exist as independent editable timeline tracks.
6. Window tracking captures viewport behavior without storing sensitive browser data.
7. Smart Zoom metadata is generated from interaction signals before AI ranking.
8. Interaction replay reconstructs cursor, keyboard, click, and window layers deterministically.
9. Metadata compression is lossless for timestamps and event ordering.
10. Cursor intelligence metadata remains fully editable after recording import.

# 12.81 Recording Finalization Philosophy

When the creator presses **Stop Recording**, the upload is **not** finished.

The backend begins a production-grade processing pipeline that transforms raw recording assets into a fully editable TryLipi project within seconds.

The objective is:

- Creator clicks **Stop**.
- Processing begins immediately.
- Timeline opens almost instantly.
- AI suggestions start appearing in the background.

This is similar to the experience in **Screen Studio**, **Tella**, and **Loom**, but optimized for a full editor.

---

## Golden Finalization Principles

1. Finalization starts only after manifest verification.
2. Processing is asynchronous.
3. Timeline becomes available before AI processing finishes.
4. AI enhancements never block editing.
5. Every processing stage is resumable.
6. Original recordings remain immutable.
7. Processing artifacts are versioned.

---

## Finalization Responsibilities

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Finalization Service | Transition recording to project. |
| Processing Orchestrator | Schedule workers. |
| FFmpeg Workers | Generate derived assets. |
| AI Pipeline | Vision + Zoom bootstrap. |
| Bootstrap Engine | Create editor snapshot. |

---

Recording infrastructure is horizontally scalable and stateless wherever possible.

- Proxy generation duration.

- Worker queue depth.

---

| OCR Delayed | AI queue congestion. |

# 12.92 Acceptance Tests

## Finalization Tests

- Manifest verification succeeds.
- Project bootstrap generated.
- AI processing starts asynchronously.

## Thumbnail Tests

- Timeline strip generated.
- Poster frame generated.
- Hover previews available.

## Waveform Tests

- Audio peaks generated.
- Multi-resolution cache created.
- Timeline renders waveform immediately.

## AI Bootstrap Tests

- OCR metadata generated.
- Face timeline generated.
- Zoom candidates stored.

## Cleanup Tests

- Temporary chunks removed.
- Failed sessions retained for retry.
- Permanent assets preserved.

---

# Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 12.5)

1. Recording finalization is orchestrated as a resumable DAG.
2. Timeline editing becomes available before AI processing completes.
3. Proxy videos, waveforms and thumbnails are generated immediately after ingestion.
4. OCR, face detection and Smart Zoom bootstrap run asynchronously.
5. Timeline thumbnails and poster frames are separate cached assets.
6. Multi-resolution waveforms are generated once and reused.
7. Cleanup jobs remove temporary artifacts without touching verified recordings.
8. Recording bundles are portable across workspaces.
9. Recording infrastructure scales through stateless services and worker pools.
10. AI metadata versions are independent from recording versions.

# 1.01 Why TryLipi Recording Exists

## Mission Statement

> **"Turn any screen recording into a professionally edited tutorial automatically."**

TryLipi's recorder is **not a Loom clone**.

It is **the first browser-native cinematic recording engine** designed specifically for creators who make:

- YouTube tutorials.
- SaaS demos.
- Coding videos.
- Product walkthroughs.
- AI tool videos.
- Educational courses.
- Startup launch videos.
- Technical documentation videos.

Recording is only **the beginning** of the editing pipeline.

---

## The Problem We're Solving

Today's recording tools stop after capturing pixels.

| Existing Tools | Limitation |
|---------------|------------|
| Loom | Great sharing, weak editing. |
| Tella | Browser recorder, limited automation. |
| Screen Studio | Excellent motion, macOS only. |
| Cursorful | Excellent cursor effects, limited editor. |
| OBS Studio | Powerful but manual workflow. |
| CapCut Desktop | Editing starts after recording. |

### TryLipi's Approach

Recording produces an **AI-editable project**, not just a video.

```text
Screen Recording
      │
Semantic Metadata
      │
Editable Timeline
      │
AI Understanding
      │
Automatic Editing Suggestions
      │
Publish
```

This changes recording from **video capture** into **content generation**.

---

# 1.02 Product Philosophy

The recorder follows six core philosophies.

---

## Philosophy 1 — Browser First

Everything works inside Chrome/Edge.

No:

- Native application.
- Chrome extension.
- Electron dependency.
- macOS-specific APIs.

Only browser capabilities.

**Reason**

Windows users should receive the same premium experience as Mac users.

---

## Philosophy 2 — Metadata Over Pixels

Don't burn effects into recordings.

Instead capture metadata.

```text
Video
Cursor Metadata
Keyboard Metadata
Scroll Metadata
Window Metadata
Zoom Metadata
Face Metadata
OCR Metadata
```

Everything stays editable.

---

## Philosophy 3 — AI Assisted, Never AI Locked

AI generates suggestions.

Creators always keep control.

Examples:

- Suggested zooms.
- Suggested cuts.
- Suggested highlights.
- Suggested captions.

Nothing is destructive.

---

## Philosophy 4 — Local First Recording

Recording never depends on internet quality.

Capabilities:

- Offline recording.
- Background uploads.
- Resume uploads.
- Local cache.

Inspired by Figma's offline philosophy.

---

## Philosophy 5 — Cinematic Automation

The recorder automatically creates motion that creators usually keyframe manually.

Examples:

- Cursor zoom.
- Camera pan.
- Auto framing.
- Click spotlight.
- Window focus.

Inspired by Screen Studio.

---

## Philosophy 6 — Recording Equals Editing Project

Every recording immediately becomes:

```text
Project
│
├── Timeline
├── Assets
├── Cursor Layer
├── Audio Tracks
├── Metadata Tracks
└── AI Suggestions
```

No conversion step.

---

# 1.13 Acceptance Principles

A TryLipi recording is considered valid only if all foundational guarantees hold.

## Functional Acceptance

- Screen recording starts within one countdown cycle.
- Webcam synchronization is frame accurate.
- Audio stays synchronized.
- Cursor metadata aligns with recorded frames.
- Recording survives refresh if upload recovery is enabled.

---

## Reliability Acceptance

- Offline recording succeeds.
- Live upload resumes after reconnect.
- Processing generates an editable project.
- Timeline opens before AI finishes.

---

## UX Acceptance

- No unnecessary permission prompts.
- Recording controls remain responsive during uploads.
- Creator always knows recording state.
- Upload progress is deterministic.

---

# 1.14 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 1.1)

## Architecture Rules

1. TryLipi recording is browser-first and platform-independent.
2. Recording generates editable metadata instead of destructive visual effects.
3. Every recording becomes a TryLipi project immediately after processing.
4. Recording lifecycle follows a deterministic state machine.
5. Recording sessions are immutable identities across uploads and processing.
6. Metadata and media always use the same recording timeline clock.
7. Capture, upload, processing and AI are separate runtimes communicating through metadata.
8. Browser capabilities determine runtime configuration during initialization.
9. Offline recording is a first-class feature, not a fallback.
10. AI suggestions enhance recordings without locking creators into automated edits.

# 1.21 Browser Recording Runtime Philosophy

The **Recording Runtime** is the operating system that manages everything while a recording is active.

It is responsible for:

- Initializing browser capture APIs.
- Managing media streams.
- Capturing metadata.
- Coordinating upload workers.
- Synchronizing timestamps.
- Handling pause/resume.
- Recovering from interruptions.

It **never edits video**. It only produces synchronized recording assets.

---

## Runtime Design Principles

1. One runtime controls one recording session.
2. Capture is isolated from uploads.
3. Metadata capture never blocks media capture.
4. Workers communicate through messages only.
5. Runtime survives UI re-renders.
6. Recording state is recoverable after refresh.
7. Every subsystem is independently restartable.

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime Module | Responsibility |
|---------------|----------------|
| Runtime Orchestrator | Coordinates all recording subsystems. |
| Capture Manager | Screen/webcam/audio capture lifecycle. |
| Metadata Manager | Cursor, keyboard, window events. |
| Upload Runtime | Progressive uploads. |
| Worker Manager | Encoding/upload workers. |
| Diagnostics Runtime | Metrics and logging. |

---

# 1.22 Recording Runtime Boot Sequence

Recording startup follows a deterministic initialization sequence.

## Boot Sequence Diagram

```text
User Clicks Record
        │
Permission Manager
        │
Device Discovery
        │
Session Initialization
        │
Worker Initialization
        │
Stream Initialization
        │
Metadata Initialization
        │
Countdown
        │
Recording Begins
```

---

## Startup Stages

| Stage | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Permission Check | Screen, webcam, microphone permissions. |
| Device Discovery | Enumerate available devices. |
| Session Bootstrap | Create runtime session. |
| Worker Bootstrap | Spawn recording workers. |
| Stream Bootstrap | Connect media streams. |
| Metadata Bootstrap | Cursor/keyboard listeners. |
| Countdown | UI preparation. |
| Recording | Runtime enters active state. |

---

## Startup Timing Budget

| Operation | Target Time |
|-----------|-------------|
| Permission Validation | Less than 80 ms |
| Device Enumeration | Less than 50 ms |
| Worker Startup | Less than 60 ms |
| Stream Creation | Less than 120 ms |
| Runtime Ready | Less than 300 ms |

---

## Runtime Boot Interface

```ts
interface RecordingBootResult {
  sessionId: string;
  initializedStreams: string[];
  runtimeReady: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recording countdown cannot begin until runtime initialization succeeds.

---

The Runtime Orchestrator is the brain of the recording engine.

```text
Recording Runtime

 ┌──────┼───────────────┐

Capture Metadata Upload Runtime
 │      │               │
Workers Event Bus Diagnostics
```

```ts
interface RecordingRuntime {

  clockManager: RecordingClock;
```

## Responsibilities

| Component | Responsibility |
|----------|----------------|

| CaptureManager | Media streams. |

---

## Engineering Rules

# 1.25 Capture Session Initialization

Every recording session initializes capture independently.

## Initialization Pipeline

```text
Session Created
      │
Screen Capture
      │
Camera Capture
      │
Audio Capture
      │
Metadata Capture
      │
Capture Registry Ready
```

---

## Initialization Order

| Priority | Stream |
|----------|--------|
| Highest | Screen |
| High | Microphone |
| High | Webcam |
| Medium | System Audio |
| Medium | Cursor |
| Medium | Keyboard |
| Low | Window Metadata |

---

Checks include:

- Permission granted.
- Device available.
- Codec supported.
- Resolution accepted.
- Audio sample rate supported.

## Capture Session Interface

---

# 1.26 Worker Graph & Thread Architecture

Recording work is distributed across workers.

## Worker Graph

```text
Main UI Thread
      │
 ┌────┼───────────────┐
 │    │               │
Capture Upload Metadata
Worker Worker Worker
 │    │               │
Encoder Compression Sync
```

---

## Worker Responsibilities

| Worker | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| Capture Worker | Receive MediaRecorder blobs. |
| Upload Worker | Upload chunk queue. |
| Metadata Worker | Cursor/keyboard batching. |
| Compression Worker | Compress metadata. |
| Thumbnail Worker | Preview generation (optional). |

---

## Worker Communication

```text
Main Thread
     │
postMessage()
     │
Worker
     │
Structured Clone
     │
Shared Runtime Events
```

---

## Worker Interface

```ts
interface RuntimeWorkerMessage {
  type: RuntimeWorkerEventType;
  payload: unknown;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Heavy processing never runs on the UI thread during recording.

---

# 1.27 Recording Clock Synchronization Engine

Everything shares one recording clock.

## Clock Architecture

```text
Recording Start
      │
Clock Origin
      │
Microsecond Timer
      │
All Streams Timestamped
```

---

## Clock Sources

| Source | Usage |
|--------|-------|
| Recording Origin | Global reference. |
| Media Timestamp | Video/audio frames. |
| Performance Timer | Metadata events. |
| Chunk Timestamp | Upload ordering. |

---

## Clock Interface

```ts
interface RecordingClock {
  originTimestampUs: number;
  currentTimestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Synchronization Guarantees

- Cursor aligns with video.
- Audio aligns with screen.
- Webcam aligns with cursor.
- Keyboard aligns with clicks.

---

## Engineering Rules

Recording clock is monotonic and never rewinds.

---

# 1.28 Recording Buffer Management

Buffers isolate recording from uploads.

## Buffer Architecture

```text
MediaRecorder
      │
Memory Buffer
      │
Upload Queue
      │
OPFS Backup Buffer
      │
Cloud Upload
```

---

## Buffer Layers

| Buffer | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| Memory Buffer | Immediate chunks. |
| OPFS Buffer | Offline persistence. |
| Upload Queue | Pending uploads. |
| Retry Queue | Failed uploads. |

---

## Buffer Flow

```text
Chunk Created
     │
Memory Buffer
     │
Uploaded?
 ├── Yes → Release
 └── No  → Persist OPFS
```

---

## Buffer Interface

```ts
interface RecordingBuffer {
  pendingChunks: number;
  persistedChunks: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Chunks remain buffered until server acknowledgement.

---

```text
├── Webcam
```

## Registry Metadata

# 1.30 Recording Runtime Event Bus

All runtime communication flows through an internal event bus.

## Event Bus Diagram

```text
Capture Runtime
Metadata Runtime
Upload Runtime
Diagnostics Runtime
       │
 Runtime Event Bus
       │
UI + Workers + Sync Runtime
```

---

## Event Categories

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Session Events | recording.started |
| Stream Events | stream.connected |
| Upload Events | chunk.acknowledged |
| Metadata Events | cursor.batch.ready |
| Worker Events | upload.retry |
| Diagnostics Events | memory.warning |

---

## Event Bus Interface

```ts
interface RecordingRuntimeEvent {
  eventId: string;
  category: RuntimeEventCategory;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Event Ordering Rules

1. Events are timestamped.
2. Events are immutable.
3. Events are replayable for debugging.

---

## Engineering Rules

Runtime event ordering is deterministic across workers.

---

# 1.31 Failure Recovery During Recording

Runtime failures are isolated whenever possible.

## Failure Recovery Pipeline

```text
Failure Detected
      │
Recovery Manager
      │
Retry Strategy
      │
Runtime Continues
```

---

## Recoverable Failures

| Failure | Recovery |
|---------|----------|
| Webcam disconnected | Retry device. |
| Upload failed | Retry queue. |
| Network offline | Persist OPFS. |
| Worker crashed | Restart worker. |
| UI refresh | Resume runtime session. |

---

## Fatal Failures

| Failure | Action |
|---------|--------|
| Screen permission revoked | Stop recording safely. |
| Storage exhausted | Pause recording. |
| Recording clock corruption | Abort session. |

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface RuntimeRecoveryState {
  recoveryMode: RecoveryMode;
  restartWorkerIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery attempts occur before terminating a recording session.

---

# 1.32 Runtime Diagnostics

Developer Mode exposes runtime health during recording.

## Runtime Metrics

- Active streams.
- Recording FPS.
- Chunk generation rate.
- Upload queue depth.
- Worker memory usage.
- Recording duration.
- Buffer utilization.
- Event bus throughput.

---

## Runtime Warning Events

| Warning | Trigger |
|---------|---------|
| Worker Restarted | Worker crashed and restarted. |
| Buffer Pressure | Upload slower than recording. |
| Clock Drift | Timestamp anomaly detected. |
| Stream Lost | Webcam/mic disconnected. |
| Memory Threshold | Buffer approaching limit. |

---

## Runtime Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface RecordingRuntimeDiagnostics {
  activeWorkers: number;
  activeStreams: number;
  queuedChunks: number;
}
```

---

# 1.33 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 1.2)

## Runtime Architecture Rules

1. Runtime initialization completes before countdown starts.
2. Runtime Orchestrator is the single coordinator of all recording subsystems.
3. Media streams remain isolated until backend reconstruction.
4. Heavy recording work executes in Web Workers instead of the UI thread.
5. Every stream uses the shared microsecond recording clock.
6. Memory, OPFS and upload queues form a three-layer buffering system.
7. Media Stream Registry is the authoritative runtime source for capture streams.
8. Runtime Event Bus is immutable, timestamped and replayable.
9. Recovery mechanisms restart isolated subsystems before terminating recording.
10. Runtime diagnostics expose health without affecting recording performance.

---

# 1.41 Production Recording Runtime Philosophy

Development and production recording runtimes are different systems.

A production runtime must survive:

- Browser refresh.
- Network loss.
- Webcam disconnect.
- Microphone unplug.
- Tab switching.
- Memory pressure.
- Long (2–8 hour) recordings.

The runtime is designed to be **fault-tolerant**, not just functional.

---

## Golden Production Principles

1. Recording is never dependent on UI rendering.
2. Upload failures never stop recording.
3. Device failures recover whenever possible.
4. Runtime state is continuously checkpointed.
5. Browser capabilities are negotiated before recording.
6. Performance adapts dynamically.
7. Recovery is automatic whenever safe.

---

## Runtime Layers

```text
User Interface
      │
Recording Runtime
      │
Capability Layer
      │
Capture Layer
      │
Recovery Layer
      │
Upload Layer
      │
Backend Session
```

Each layer can fail independently without crashing the whole recorder.

---

# 1.42 Browser Capability Negotiation Engine

Before recording begins, TryLipi discovers exactly what the browser supports.

This avoids runtime surprises.

## Capability Negotiation Pipeline

```text
Browser Loaded
      │
Feature Detector
      │
Capability Registry
      │
Recording Configuration
      │
Runtime Bootstrap
```

---

## Capabilities Checked

| Capability | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| `getDisplayMedia` | Screen recording availability. |
| `getUserMedia` | Webcam & microphone. |
| System Audio Capture | Browser/system audio support. |
| `MediaRecorder` | Recording chunks. |
| `WebCodecs` | Hardware encoding/decoding. |
| `AudioWorklet` | Audio processing. |
| `OffscreenCanvas` | Worker rendering. |
| OPFS | Offline recording storage. |
| Service Worker | Background uploads. |
| SharedArrayBuffer | High-performance processing (optional). |

---

## Capability Registry

```ts
interface BrowserCapabilities {
  supportsWebCodecs: boolean;
  supportsOPFS: boolean;
  supportsSystemAudio: boolean;
  supportsOffscreenCanvas: boolean;
  supportsAudioWorklet: boolean;
}
```

---

## Capability Levels

| Level | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Tier A** | Full feature set available. |
| **Tier B** | Recording supported with minor limitations. |
| **Tier C** | Basic recording only. |
| **Tier D** | Unsupported browser. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Capability negotiation runs exactly once per browser session and is cached until refresh.

---

# 1.43 Permission Architecture & Security Model

Permissions are the foundation of browser recording.

TryLipi requests only what is needed.

## Permission Lifecycle

```text
Idle
 │
Permission Request
 │
Granted
 │
Validated
 │
Recording Active
 │
Permission Revoked?
 │
Recovery / Stop
```

---

## Permission Types

| Permission | Required |
|------------|----------|
| Screen Capture | Required |
| Microphone | Optional |
| Webcam | Optional |
| System Audio | Optional |
| Clipboard | Never required for recording |
| Notifications | Never required |

---

## Permission States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Unknown | Not requested yet. |
| Prompt | Browser prompt visible. |
| Granted | Permission active. |
| Denied | User rejected. |
| Revoked | Lost during recording. |

---

## Permission Manager Interface

```ts
interface RecordingPermissionState {
  screen: PermissionStatus;
  microphone: PermissionStatus;
  webcam: PermissionStatus;
  systemAudio: PermissionStatus;
}
```

---

## Permission Recovery Strategy

| Event | Action |
|-------|--------|
| Webcam revoked | Disable webcam track. |
| Mic revoked | Continue recording silently. |
| Screen revoked | Safely stop recording. |
| System audio unavailable | Continue without system audio. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Permissions are never silently re-requested during an active recording.

---

# 1.44 Runtime Performance Budgets

Performance budgets prevent recordings from degrading user experience.

## Performance Budget Philosophy

Every recording runtime has measurable budgets.

If exceeded, adaptive systems respond automatically.

---

## Runtime Budget Table

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Runtime Startup | Under 300 ms |
| Frame Processing | Less than 4 ms/frame |
| Metadata Capture | Less than 1 ms/event |
| Upload Scheduling | Less than 2 ms/chunk |
| Cursor Capture | 120 Hz maximum |
| UI Thread Blocking | Under 8 ms/frame |
| Memory Growth | Stable over long recordings |

---

## Resource Budgets

| Resource | Budget |
|----------|--------|
| Main Thread CPU | Under 20% |
| Worker CPU | Adaptive |
| Memory Buffer | Dynamic |
| Upload Queue | Adaptive |
| Metadata Queue | Compressed every few seconds |

---

## Budget Monitoring

```text
Recording Runtime
      │
Performance Monitor
      │
Threshold Detector
      │
Adaptive Runtime
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance budgets are enforced continuously during recording.

---

# 1.45 Adaptive Quality & Recording Profiles

Recording quality adapts to the creator's device.

## Recording Profiles

| Profile | Resolution | FPS |
|---------|------------|-----|
| Ultra | 4K | 60 FPS |
| High | 1440p | 60 FPS |
| Creator Default | 1080p | 60 FPS |
| Balanced | 1080p | 30 FPS |
| Lightweight | 720p | 30 FPS |

---

## Adaptive Decision Factors

- CPU utilization.
- Memory pressure.
- Browser capabilities.
- Upload bandwidth.
- Battery status (laptops).
- Thermal throttling signals (where available).

---

## Adaptive Runtime Pipeline

```text
Runtime Metrics
      │
Quality Decision Engine
      │
Recording Profile Update
```

---

## Quality Interface

```ts
interface RecordingProfile {
  resolution: "720p" | "1080p" | "1440p" | "4K";
  fps: 30 | 60;
  bitrateMbps: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Quality can scale down automatically but never scale up during an active recording.

---

# 1.46 Device Hot-Swap & Stream Recovery

Creators frequently unplug microphones or switch webcams mid-recording.

TryLipi supports graceful recovery.

## Device Recovery Pipeline

```text
Device Lost
    │
Device Monitor
    │
Recovery Engine
    │
Reconnect Stream
    │
Timeline Continues
```

---

## Recoverable Device Events

| Event | Recovery |
|-------|----------|
| Webcam disconnected | Wait for reconnect. |
| Webcam changed | Switch stream. |
| Mic unplugged | Retry preferred mic. |
| Bluetooth headset connected | Offer switch. |
| External display removed | Stop affected stream safely. |

---

## Stream Recovery States

```text
ACTIVE
 │
LOST
 │
RECOVERING
 │
RESTORED
```

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface StreamRecoveryEvent {
  streamId: string;
  recoveryReason: StreamRecoveryReason;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovered streams preserve timeline synchronization using the recording clock.

---

# 1.47 Crash Recovery & Session Restoration

A browser refresh should not destroy a recording whenever possible.

## Crash Recovery Architecture

```text
Recording Runtime
      │
Checkpoint Engine
      │
OPFS Snapshot
      │
Browser Refresh
      │
Restore Runtime
```

---

## Checkpoint Contents

| Resource | Saved |
|----------|-------|
| Session ID | Yes |
| Active Streams | Metadata only |
| Uploaded Chunk Index | Yes |
| Pending Chunks | Yes |
| Cursor Metadata Offset | Yes |
| Recording Clock Offset | Yes |

---

## Recovery Timeline

```text
Refresh
 │
Restore Session
 │
Recover Buffers
 │
Resume Upload
 │
Continue Processing
```

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface RuntimeCheckpoint {
  sessionId: string;
  lastChunkIndex: number;
  recordingOffsetUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Checkpointing occurs periodically without interrupting recording.

---

# 1.48 Runtime Observability & Diagnostics

Every recording exposes internal runtime health for debugging.

## Observability Architecture

```text
Runtime Metrics
      │
Diagnostics Collector
      │
Developer Console
      │
Analytics Pipeline
```

## Runtime Metrics

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Recording | FPS, dropped frames, duration. |
| Upload | Throughput, retries, ACK latency. |
| Memory | Buffer usage, heap size. |
| Workers | Active workers, restarts. |
| Metadata | Cursor events/sec, keyboard events. |
| Browser | Capability tier, device info. |

---

## Debug Dashboard Widgets

- Recording duration.
- Live FPS graph.
- Upload queue graph.
- Memory usage graph.
- Worker status panel.
- Capability matrix.
- Active stream registry.

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface RecordingRuntimeMetrics {
  fps: number;
  droppedFrames: number;
  uploadQueueDepth: number;
  memoryUsageMB: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

---

# 1.49 Error Taxonomy & Recovery Policies

Every runtime failure belongs to a predefined category.

## Error Categories

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Permission | Permission denied/revoked. |
| Device | Camera lost, microphone unavailable. |
| Browser | API unsupported. |
| Network | Upload timeout. |
| Storage | OPFS quota exceeded. |
| Worker | Worker crash. |
| Runtime | Clock drift, synchronization issue. |

---

## Severity Levels

| Severity | Runtime Behavior |
|----------|------------------|
| INFO | Log only. |
| WARNING | Recover automatically. |
| ERROR | Retry subsystem. |
| CRITICAL | Safely stop recording. |

---

## Recovery Policy Matrix

| Error | Policy |
|-------|--------|
| Upload timeout | Retry queue. |
| Worker crash | Restart worker. |
| Cursor capture failure | Continue recording. |
| Webcam lost | Recover stream. |
| Screen permission revoked | Finalize recording immediately. |
| Storage full | Pause recording and notify creator. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Critical failures always prioritize preserving recorded data before stopping capture.

---

# 1.50 Acceptance Test Matrix

Chapter 1 defines the minimum production acceptance criteria for the recorder.

## Startup Tests

- Runtime initializes under performance budget.
- Capability negotiation succeeds.
- Permissions validated before countdown.
- Required streams initialized correctly.

---

## Runtime Tests

- Recording clock remains monotonic.
- Worker communication succeeds.
- Event ordering deterministic.
- Stream registry updates correctly.

---

## Recovery Tests

- Webcam reconnect works.
- Upload resumes after reconnect.
- Session restores after refresh.
- Pending chunks preserved.

---

## Performance Tests

| Scenario | Expected Result |
|----------|-----------------|
| 2-hour recording | Stable memory growth. |
| Network offline for 5 minutes | Upload resumes later. |
| 60 FPS recording | No UI jank. |
| High cursor activity | Metadata remains synchronized. |

---

## Security Tests

- Permission revocation handled correctly.
- Sensitive APIs never accessed without consent.
- Recording stops safely when screen permission ends.

# 1.52 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 1.3)

## Production Runtime Rules

2. Permissions are explicit, minimal, and independently recoverable.
3. Performance budgets are continuously monitored during recording.
4. Recording profiles adapt downward based on runtime pressure.
5. Device hot-swapping preserves synchronization whenever possible.
6. Runtime checkpoints enable session restoration after browser refresh.
7. Diagnostics provide complete runtime visibility without affecting capture performance.
8. Every runtime error belongs to a predefined recovery category.
9. Critical failures always preserve recorded media before shutdown.
10. Chapter 1 defines the foundational runtime contract for every subsequent recording subsystem.

# 2.01 Browser Recording Runtime Philosophy

## Mission Statement

The Browser Recording Runtime is the **lowest-level execution engine** responsible for capturing pixels, audio, cursor metadata, keyboard events, and browser interactions from inside Chrome or Edge.

Unlike traditional screen recorders, TryLipi's runtime is designed around **metadata-first recording**.

Every recording simultaneously generates:

* Video stream.
* Webcam stream.
* Microphone stream.
* System audio stream.
* Cursor metadata.
* Keyboard metadata.
* Window metadata.
* Recording timeline metadata.

The runtime never edits media. It only captures synchronized assets for the editor.

---

## Golden Runtime Principles

1. Browser-native implementation only.
2. Independent capture pipelines for every stream.
3. Microsecond-level synchronization.
4. Zero-copy media flow whenever possible.
5. Metadata captured separately from pixels.
6. Progressive upload support.
7. Offline-first recording support.

---

## Recording Runtime Responsibilities

| Module                 | Responsibility                         |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Screen Capture Runtime | Capture screen/window/tab stream.      |
| Webcam Runtime         | Capture webcam stream.                 |
| Audio Runtime          | Capture microphone/system audio.       |
| Metadata Runtime       | Cursor, keyboard and window events.    |
| Recording Runtime      | Manage MediaRecorder lifecycle.        |
| Upload Runtime         | Progressive chunk upload.              |
| Diagnostics Runtime    | Runtime metrics and health monitoring. |

---

# 2.02 Browser Media Capture API Stack

TryLipi combines multiple browser APIs into one unified recording runtime.

## Browser Capture Stack

```text
Browser Recording Runtime
│
├── navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()
│
├── navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()
│
├── MediaRecorder
│
├── WebCodecs
│
├── CaptureController
│
├── AudioWorklet
│
├── OffscreenCanvas
│
├── Pointer Events API
│
├── Keyboard Events API
│
└── MutationObserver (Browser Tab Mode)
```

---

## Core APIs Used

### getDisplayMedia()

Captures:

* Entire screen.
* Browser window.
* Individual browser tab.
* Multiple monitor selection.

### getUserMedia()

Captures:

* Webcam.
* Microphone.
* Multiple devices.
* Virtual devices.

### MediaRecorder

Responsible for:

* Encoding captured streams.
* Generating recording chunks.
* Streaming chunks every few seconds.

### WebCodecs

Provides:

* Hardware accelerated encoding.
* Decoding proxy frames.
* Thumbnail generation.
* Future live compositing.

### AudioWorklet

Used for:

* Audio mixing.
* Noise suppression.
* Waveform generation.
* Audio diagnostics.

---

## API Capability Categories

| Category             | APIs                              |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Video Capture        | getDisplayMedia(), getUserMedia() |
| Audio Capture        | getUserMedia(), AudioWorklet      |
| Recording            | MediaRecorder                     |
| Encoding             | WebCodecs                         |
| Rendering            | OffscreenCanvas                   |
| Metadata             | Pointer Events, Keyboard Events   |
| Browser Intelligence | MutationObserver                  |

---

# 2.03 CaptureController & Recording Session Bootstrap

Every recording begins by creating a **Capture Session**.

## Recording Bootstrap Flow

```text
Creator Clicks Record
        │
Permission Manager
        │
CaptureController
        │
Media Streams Created
        │
Recording Runtime Bootstrapped
        │
Countdown Starts
        │
Recording Begins
```

---

## CaptureController Responsibilities

| Responsibility    | Description               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| Session Bootstrap | Creates runtime session.  |
| Stream Lifecycle  | Starts and stops streams. |
| Pause / Resume    | Runtime control.          |
| Focus Management  | Browser tab focus.        |
| Abort Recording   | Safe shutdown.            |

---

## Capture Session Object

```ts
interface CaptureSession {
  sessionId: string;
  screenStream?: MediaStream;
  webcamStream?: MediaStream;
  microphoneStream?: MediaStream;
  systemAudioStream?: MediaStream;
}
```

---

## Bootstrap Validation

Before countdown starts:

* Screen permission granted.
* Required streams available.
* Codec negotiated.
* Recording profile selected.
* Runtime workers initialized.

---

## Engineering Rules

CaptureSession is immutable after recording starts.

---

# 2.04 MediaRecorder Recording Pipeline

MediaRecorder is the primary recording engine for v1 of TryLipi.

## Recording Pipeline

```text
Media Streams
      │
MediaRecorder
      │
Encoded Blob Chunks
      │
Chunk Queue
      │
Upload Runtime
      │
Backend Recording Session
```

---

## Recording Flow

1. Streams attached.
2. MediaRecorder configured.
3. Recording started.
4. Chunks emitted periodically.
5. Upload runtime consumes chunks.
6. Recording finalized.

---

## MediaRecorder States

```text
INACTIVE
    │
STARTING
    │
RECORDING
    │
PAUSED
    │
RECORDING
    │
STOPPING
    │
INACTIVE
```

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface MediaRecorderRuntime {
  recorder: MediaRecorder;
  status: RecordingState;
  chunkIntervalMs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

MediaRecorder never communicates directly with upload services.

---

# 2.05 MediaRecorder Chunk Lifecycle

Chunks are immutable recording units.

## Chunk Lifecycle

```text
Frame Buffer
     │
MediaRecorder Chunk
     │
Chunk Queue
     │
Compression
     │
Upload Queue
     │
ACK Received
     │
Chunk Released
```

---

## Chunk States

| State     | Meaning                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------- |
| Generated | MediaRecorder emitted chunk. |
| Queued    | Waiting upload.              |
| Uploading | Upload active.               |
| Uploaded  | Backend acknowledged.        |
| Persisted | Safe to release locally.     |

---

## Chunk Metadata

```ts
interface RecordingChunk {
  sessionId: string;
  streamId: string;
  chunkIndex: number;
  durationMs: number;
  checksum: string;
}
```

---

## Chunk Timing Policy

| Recording Mode | Chunk Duration            |
| -------------- | ------------------------- |
| WiFi           | 4 seconds                 |
| Mobile Network | 2 seconds                 |
| Slow Network   | Adaptive 1 second         |
| Offline        | Unlimited local buffering |

---

## Engineering Rules

Chunks are immutable after generation.

---

# 2.06 WebCodecs vs MediaRecorder Architecture

TryLipi supports both APIs.

## Why Both Exist

| MediaRecorder           | WebCodecs                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Stable browser support. | Fine-grained encoding control. |
| Easy chunk generation.  | Hardware accelerated pipeline. |
| Simpler recording.      | Custom encoding workflows.     |

---

## Runtime Decision Tree

```text
Browser Supports WebCodecs?
        │
     Yes ─────► Hybrid Runtime
        │
      No
        │
MediaRecorder Runtime
```

---

## Hybrid Runtime

```text
Capture Streams
      │
MediaRecorder
      │
Upload Chunks

Capture Streams
      │
WebCodecs
      │
Preview Frames
```

MediaRecorder records.

WebCodecs powers advanced features.

---

## WebCodecs Responsibilities

* Thumbnail generation.
* Proxy decoding.
* Smart Zoom previews.
* AI frame sampling.
* Background rendering.

---

## Engineering Rules

MediaRecorder remains the canonical recording engine until WebCodecs recording is production-ready across browsers.

---

2. MediaRecorder is the canonical recording engine for V1.
3. WebCodecs complements MediaRecorder for advanced processing.
4. CaptureSession owns all active media streams.
5. Recording chunks are immutable upload units.
6. Every stream is represented inside the Recording Stream Graph.
7. Media constraints are negotiated before stream creation.
8. Codec selection follows browser capability negotiation.
9. Bootstrap APIs orchestrate asynchronous browser capture APIs.
10. Chromium browsers (Chrome/Edge) define the primary production support target.

# 2.21 Hybrid Recording Runtime Philosophy

## Why MediaRecorder Alone Isn't Enough

MediaRecorder is excellent for **capturing recordings**, but it is limited for:

* Live thumbnail generation.
* AI frame sampling.
* Smart Zoom previews.
* Webcam compositing.
* GPU accelerated rendering.
* Future live effects.

TryLipi therefore uses a **Hybrid Runtime**.

### Hybrid Runtime Architecture

```text
Screen / Camera / Audio Streams
            │
     Browser Capture APIs
            │
     ┌──────┴────────┐
     │               │
MediaRecorder     WebCodecs Runtime
     │               │
Recording Chunks   Frame Processing
     │               │
Upload Runtime     Preview Renderer
     │               │
Backend           Live UI + AI Runtime
```

**MediaRecorder** records.

**WebCodecs** processes frames in parallel.

---

## Responsibilities Split

| Runtime               | Responsibility                                      |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| MediaRecorder Runtime | Generate uploadable video chunks.                   |
| WebCodecs Runtime     | Decode frames and encode preview assets.            |
| Offscreen Runtime     | Render overlays inside workers.                     |
| Audio Runtime         | Process microphone and system audio.                |
| Preview Runtime       | Render creator preview without affecting recording. |

---

## Golden Hybrid Principles

1. Recording pipeline is independent from preview pipeline.
2. Frame processing never blocks MediaRecorder.
3. WebCodecs can be disabled without breaking recording.
4. Preview rendering uses GPU when available.
5. AI consumes decoded frames—not recording chunks.

---

# 2.22 WebCodecs Processing Pipeline

WebCodecs provides low-level access to browser encoders and decoders.

## Processing Pipeline

```text
Captured Video Frames
          │
VideoFrame Objects
          │
VideoDecoder
          │
Frame Processor
          │
VideoEncoder
          │
Preview / AI / Export Pipeline
```

---

## Why TryLipi Uses WebCodecs

| Feature              | Why WebCodecs                            |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Frame Access         | Read individual frames.                  |
| Hardware Encoding    | GPU acceleration.                        |
| Decoding Speed       | Faster than HTMLVideoElement extraction. |
| Thumbnail Generation | Frame-accurate previews.                 |
| AI Sampling          | Extract frames every N milliseconds.     |
| Live Effects         | Render transformed frames.               |

---

## WebCodecs Objects

```ts
interface WebCodecsRuntime {
  decoder: VideoDecoder;
  encoder: VideoEncoder;
  initialized: boolean;
}
```

---

## Decoder Lifecycle

```text
VideoFrame Source
      │
Decoder Configured
      │
Frame Decoded
      │
Frame Delivered
      │
Frame Released
```

---

## Encoder Lifecycle

```text
Processed Frame
      │
VideoEncoder
      │
Encoded Chunk
      │
Preview Buffer
```

---

## Engineering Rules

VideoFrames must always be closed after processing to avoid GPU memory leaks.

---

# 2.23 Zero-Copy Media Flow Architecture

Zero-copy architecture minimizes memory duplication.

## Traditional Flow (Avoid)

```text
Media Stream
    │
Blob
    │
Canvas
    │
ImageBitmap
    │
VideoFrame
```

Multiple copies = expensive.

---

## TryLipi Zero-Copy Flow

```text
MediaStreamTrack
       │
VideoFrame
       │
GPU Processing
       │
Renderer
       │
Preview
```

Frames travel directly between APIs whenever possible.

---

## Zero-Copy Layers

| Layer                        | Copy Count       |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Capture → VideoFrame         | 0                |
| VideoFrame → OffscreenCanvas | 0                |
| VideoFrame → Encoder         | 0                |
| VideoFrame → AI Sampler      | Shared reference |

---

## Memory Ownership Rules

| Resource    | Owner             |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| MediaStream | Capture Runtime   |
| VideoFrame  | Processing Worker |
| ImageBitmap | Preview Renderer  |
| Blob        | Upload Runtime    |

---

## Zero-Copy Interface

```ts
interface VideoFrameReference {
  timestampUs: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Never convert VideoFrames into ImageData unless pixel manipulation is required.

---

# 2.24 OffscreenCanvas Rendering Engine

OffscreenCanvas powers worker-side rendering.

## Rendering Architecture

```text
VideoFrame
     │
OffscreenCanvas Worker
     │
GPU Render Pass
     │
Preview Bitmap
     │
UI Thread
```

---

## Rendering Responsibilities

| Task                    | Worker          |
| ----------------------- | --------------- |
| Webcam compositing      | OffscreenCanvas |
| Cursor preview          | OffscreenCanvas |
| Click ripple preview    | OffscreenCanvas |
| Safe-area guides        | OffscreenCanvas |
| Background blur preview | OffscreenCanvas |

---

## Rendering Pipeline

```text
Frame Received
     │
Draw Screen
     │
Draw Webcam
     │
Draw Cursor
     │
Draw Guides
     │
Transfer Frame
```

---

## Renderer Layers

```text
Canvas Renderer
│
├── Screen Layer
├── Webcam Layer
├── Cursor Layer
├── Overlay Layer
└── Debug Layer
```

---

## Renderer Interface

```ts
interface PreviewRendererState {
  canvasWidth: number;
  canvasHeight: number;
  fps: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

The UI thread receives rendered frames, not drawing instructions.

---

# 2.25 AudioWorklet Recording Pipeline

AudioWorklet processes live audio independently of MediaRecorder.

## Audio Runtime Pipeline

```text
Microphone
System Audio
      │
MediaStreamAudioSourceNode
      │
AudioWorkletProcessor
      │
Processed Audio Stream
      │
Recording + Waveform Runtime
```

---

## Audio Responsibilities

| Responsibility    | Description                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Mixing            | Combine mic/system audio.     |
| Metering          | Live volume meters.           |
| Waveform Sampling | Timeline waveform generation. |
| Noise Analysis    | Runtime diagnostics.          |
| Silence Detection | AI assistant input.           |

---

## Audio Graph

```text
Mic Source
     │
Gain Node
     │
AudioWorklet
     │
Destination
```

---

## Audio Metadata Produced

| Metadata         | Usage                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Peak Levels      | UI meters.            |
| RMS Levels       | Waveforms.            |
| Silence Segments | AI chapter detection. |
| Sample Count     | Diagnostics.          |

---

## Audio Interface

```ts
interface AudioWorkletFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  peak: number;
  rms: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

AudioWorklet timing uses the recording clock instead of AudioContext time.

---

# 2.26 Recording Worker Graph Architecture

Every heavy subsystem runs inside dedicated workers.

## Worker Graph

```text
Main Thread
     │
 ┌───┼───────────────┬──────────────┐
 │   │               │              │
Capture Metadata   Preview      Upload
Worker   Worker     Worker       Worker
 │          │           │            │
Compression AI Sampler Waveform Retry Queue
Worker      Worker      Worker
```

---

## Worker Responsibilities

| Worker             | Responsibility              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| Capture Worker     | MediaRecorder events.       |
| Metadata Worker    | Cursor & keyboard batching. |
| Preview Worker     | OffscreenCanvas rendering.  |
| Upload Worker      | Upload scheduling.          |
| Compression Worker | Metadata compression.       |
| AI Sampling Worker | Frame extraction.           |
| Audio Worker       | Waveforms & metering.       |

---

## Worker Communication Model

```text
Runtime Event Bus
      │
Structured Messages
      │
Dedicated Workers
```

Workers never communicate directly.

---

## Worker Message Interface

```ts
interface RecordingWorkerMessage {
  type: RecordingWorkerEventType;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Workers remain stateless whenever possible; runtime state lives in the Runtime Orchestrator.

---

```text
Screen Frame
Webcam Frame

Click Metadata

Preview Compositor
      │
OffscreenCanvas
      │
Preview Surface
```

| ----------- | ----------------------- |
| Screen      | Base recording preview. |
| Webcam      | Bubble camera.          |

| Clicks      | Ripple preview.         |
| Safe Guides | Recording overlays.     |

| Clean Preview        | Hide guides.          |

## Preview Interface

```ts
interface RecordingPreviewFrame {

  rendered: boolean;
}
```

## Engineering Rules

# 2.28 Frame Synchronization & Timestamp Engine

All frames are synchronized using a unified timeline.

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
VideoFrame
Cursor Event
Keyboard Event
Audio Frame
       │
Timestamp Engine
       │
Unified Recording Timeline
```

---

## Timestamp Sources

| Source                   | Precision    |
| ------------------------ | ------------ |
| VideoFrame Timestamp     | Microseconds |
| Audio Frame Timestamp    | Microseconds |
| Cursor Event Timestamp   | Microseconds |
| Keyboard Event Timestamp | Microseconds |

---

## Synchronization Rules

* Screen drives primary timeline.
* Webcam aligns to screen.
* Audio aligns to screen.
* Metadata aligns to screen.

---

## Timeline Alignment Interface

```ts
interface RuntimeTimestamp {
  timelineUs: number;
  frameNumber: number;
}
```

---

## Drift Handling

| Drift Type   | Recovery             |
| ------------ | -------------------- |
| Webcam drift | Offset correction.   |
| Audio drift  | Timestamp alignment. |
| Cursor drift | Event interpolation. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline timestamps are monotonic across every runtime subsystem.

# 2.29 Shared Memory & Message Transport Layer

Workers exchange lightweight messages.

## Message Transport Architecture

```text
Runtime Event Bus
      │
Message Queue
      │
Dedicated Workers
      │
Shared Buffers (Optional)
```

## Transport Types

| Transport            | Usage                                        |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Structured Clone     | Standard messages.                           |
| Transferable Objects | VideoFrames, ArrayBuffers.                   |
| SharedArrayBuffer    | High-performance preview runtime (optional). |

## Transport Priority

| Priority | Message               |
| -------- | --------------------- |
| High     | Recording chunks.     |
| High     | Recording timestamps. |
| Medium   | Cursor batches.       |
| Medium   | Preview frames.       |
| Low      | Diagnostics events.   |

---

## Interface

```ts
interface RuntimeTransportMessage {
  eventType: string;
  transferable: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Large binary payloads must be transferred—not cloned.

# 2.31 Acceptance Principles

## Runtime Acceptance Tests

### WebCodecs Tests

* Decoder initializes.
* Encoder initializes.
* Frames decoded successfully.
* Frames released correctly.

### OffscreenCanvas Tests

* Preview renders in worker.
* Webcam composited correctly.
* Cursor overlay visible.

### AudioWorklet Tests

* Peak levels generated.
* RMS generated.
* Waveform samples produced.

### Worker Tests

* Worker restart succeeds.
* Messages ordered correctly.
* No worker blocks UI thread.

### Synchronization Tests

* Cursor aligned to frames.
* Audio aligned to video.
* Webcam aligned to screen.

---

# 2.32 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 2.2)

1. TryLipi uses a hybrid MediaRecorder + WebCodecs runtime architecture.
2. MediaRecorder is responsible for canonical recording chunks.
3. WebCodecs powers frame processing, previews, AI sampling and future rendering.
4. Zero-copy media flow is preferred throughout the runtime.
5. OffscreenCanvas performs all heavy preview rendering inside workers.
6. AudioWorklet is the authoritative live audio processing engine.
7. Recording workers communicate exclusively through the Runtime Event Bus.
8. Live preview rendering is isolated from recording capture quality.
9. Every media frame and metadata event shares a unified recording timestamp.
10. Transferable objects are preferred over cloned binary payloads for runtime performance.

# 2.41 Production Runtime Philosophy

A production recording runtime must survive **real creator workflows**, not ideal demos.

Typical creator sessions include:

* Recording for 2–8 hours continuously.
* Switching Wi-Fi networks.
* Locking and unlocking the laptop.
* Connecting or disconnecting microphones.
* Opening multiple Chrome tabs.
* Using Figma, VS Code, ChatGPT, and YouTube simultaneously.

The runtime is designed to **continue recording safely under resource pressure**.

---

## Golden Production Runtime Principles

1. Recording quality is prioritized over preview quality.
2. Runtime degrades gracefully under pressure.
3. Every subsystem can restart independently.
4. Browser lifecycle events are recoverable.
5. Memory usage remains bounded during long recordings.
6. Uploads never interrupt recording capture.
7. Diagnostics are always available.

---

## Runtime Protection Layers

```text
Recording Runtime
│
├── Memory Guard
├── Worker Supervisor
├── Upload Supervisor
├── Device Supervisor
├── Lifecycle Supervisor
└── Diagnostics Supervisor
```

Each supervisor monitors one runtime subsystem.

---

# 2.42 Memory Management Architecture

Memory is the biggest challenge for browser-native recording.

## Memory Ownership Model

```text
Browser Memory
│
├── Media Streams
├── VideoFrames
├── Audio Buffers
├── Upload Queue
├── Preview Buffers
└── Metadata Cache
```

Every resource has a single owner.

---

## Memory Pools

| Pool          | Purpose                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Capture Pool  | Active MediaStreams.                  |
| Frame Pool    | Decoded VideoFrames.                  |
| Preview Pool  | Rendered preview frames.              |
| Upload Pool   | Pending recording chunks.             |
| Metadata Pool | Cursor/keyboard batches.              |
| Cache Pool    | Temporary thumbnails and diagnostics. |

---

## Memory Lifecycle

```text
Allocated
    │
Active
    │
Transferred
    │
Released
    │
Garbage Collection Eligible
```

---

## Memory Budget Targets

| Resource       | Target Budget                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| VideoFrames    | Maximum 3 active frames per stream. |
| Preview Frames | Double buffered only.               |
| Upload Queue   | Adaptive.                           |
| Metadata Queue | Compressed every few seconds.       |
| Thumbnails     | Generated lazily.                   |

---

## Memory Leak Prevention Rules

* Close `VideoFrame` immediately after rendering.
* Revoke temporary object URLs.
* Release `ImageBitmap` after transfer.
* Dispose unused `MediaStreamTrack` objects.
* Flush metadata buffers after upload.

---

## Engineering Rules

No runtime object may retain a reference after its timestamp window has passed.

---

# 2.43 Long Recording Runtime Strategy

TryLipi supports **unlimited recording duration** (storage permitting).

## Long Recording Architecture

```text
Recording Runtime
      │
Rolling Chunk Generator
      │
OPFS Persistence
      │
Upload Queue
      │
Chunk Cleanup
```

---

## Long Recording Strategy

| Strategy             | Purpose                 |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Rolling Chunks       | Prevent huge blobs.     |
| OPFS Persistence     | Crash recovery.         |
| Incremental Upload   | Continuous cloud sync.  |
| Metadata Compression | Stable memory usage.    |
| Upload ACK Cleanup   | Remove uploaded chunks. |

---

## Duration Milestones

| Recording Length | Runtime Behavior                   |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 10 minutes       | Standard runtime.                  |
| 30 minutes       | Metadata compression enabled.      |
| 1 hour           | Thumbnail generation becomes lazy. |
| 2 hours          | Waveform batching enabled.         |
| 4+ hours         | Diagnostics sampling reduced.      |

---

## Chunk Cleanup Pipeline

```text
Chunk Uploaded
      │
ACK Received
      │
Safe Persistence Verified
      │
Release Local Memory
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recording duration never changes runtime architecture—only optimization policies.

---

# 2.44 Background Tab & Browser Lifecycle Handling

Browsers throttle inactive tabs.

TryLipi must continue recording safely.

## Browser Lifecycle Events

| Event                | Runtime Action                |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Tab Hidden           | Reduce preview rendering.     |
| Tab Visible          | Restore preview FPS.          |
| Window Minimized     | Continue recording.           |
| Browser Backgrounded | Preserve recording workers.   |
| Focus Returned       | Resume diagnostics frequency. |

---

## Lifecycle Event Flow

```text
Visibility Change
       │
Lifecycle Manager
       │
Preview Runtime
       │
Diagnostics Runtime
```

Recording continues even if preview pauses.

---

## Page Visibility States

```text
VISIBLE
   │
HIDDEN
   │
VISIBLE
```

Recording state remains unchanged.

---

## Background Optimization

| Component        | Optimization              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| Preview Renderer | Lower FPS.                |
| Diagnostics      | Lower sampling frequency. |
| Metadata Capture | No change.                |
| Upload Runtime   | Continue normally.        |

---

## Engineering Rules

Page visibility events must never stop MediaRecorder unless required by browser policy.

---

# 2.45 Runtime Failure Recovery Engine

Every runtime failure has an automatic recovery strategy.

## Recovery Architecture

```text
Failure Detected
      │
Runtime Supervisor
      │
Recovery Strategy
      │
Resume Recording
```

---

## Failure Categories

| Category        | Recovery                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------- |
| Upload Failure  | Retry upload queue.        |
| Worker Crash    | Restart worker.            |
| Webcam Lost     | Attempt reconnect.         |
| Mic Lost        | Retry preferred device.    |
| Preview Failure | Restart preview worker.    |
| OPFS Failure    | Switch to memory fallback. |

---

## Worker Recovery Flow

```text
Worker Crash
     │
Supervisor Detects
     │
Spawn Replacement Worker
     │
Restore Worker State
```

---

## Runtime Recovery State

```ts
interface RuntimeRecoveryState {
  recoveryMode: RecoveryMode;
  restartedWorkers: string[];
  recoveredAtUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery never resets the recording clock.

---

| System Audio            | ✅      | ✅    | ✅     | ❌       | ❌      |
| WebCodecs               | ✅      | ✅    | ✅     | ⚠️      | ⚠️     |

| -------- | -------------------------------- |
| Windows  | Primary TryLipi target.          |

### User Stops Screen Sharing

```text
Screen Track Ends
      │
Finalize Recording
      │
Upload Remaining Chunks
      │
Open Editor
```

### Webcam Permission Revoked

Continue recording without webcam.

### Microphone Changes

Prompt creator to switch devices.

---

## Engineering Rules

Browser-specific workarounds live inside capability adapters—not business logic.

# 2.48 Recording Performance Budgets

Performance budgets guarantee consistent creator experience.

## Runtime Budget Table

| Metric                 | Budget               |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| Startup Time           | Under 300 ms         |
| Preview Latency        | Under 50 ms          |
| Cursor Capture Latency | Under 4 ms           |
| Upload Scheduling      | Under 2 ms/chunk     |
| Worker Restart         | Under 150 ms         |
| Memory Growth          | Stable over 4+ hours |

---

## CPU Budget Allocation

| Runtime             | CPU Target        |
| ------------------- | ----------------- |
| Capture Runtime     | Highest priority. |
| Upload Runtime      | Medium priority.  |
| Preview Runtime     | Adaptive.         |
| Diagnostics Runtime | Lowest priority.  |

---

## Adaptive Budget Decisions

When CPU exceeds threshold:

1. Lower preview FPS.
2. Reduce diagnostics sampling.
3. Pause thumbnail worker.
4. Compress metadata sooner.

Recording quality never changes automatically.

---

## Engineering Rules

Capture runtime always has highest scheduling priority.

# 3.01 Screen Capture Engine Philosophy

## Mission Statement

The **Screen Capture Engine** is responsible for acquiring visual content from the user's desktop while preserving enough metadata for AI-powered editing, Smart Zoom, DOM Tracking, cursor intelligence, and cinematic camera movement.

Unlike traditional screen recorders that capture only pixels, TryLipi captures both **visual streams** and **display context metadata**.

Every capture session records:

* Display pixels.
* Window geometry.
* Display resolution.
* Device pixel ratio.
* Refresh rate.
* Browser tab metadata (when permitted).
* Viewport metadata.
* Monitor topology.

This metadata powers later AI editing features without requiring another recording pass.

---

## Golden Screen Capture Principles

1. Browser-native capture only.
2. Multi-monitor aware runtime.
3. Capture mode determines metadata availability.
4. Original screen pixels remain immutable.
5. Resolution independence through metadata scaling.
6. Display metadata is synchronized with the recording timeline.
7. Capture engine works independently from webcam and audio engines.

---

## Responsibilities

| Module                   | Responsibility                              |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| Display Capture Runtime  | Entire screen capture.                      |
| Window Capture Runtime   | Single application window capture.          |
| Browser Tab Runtime      | Browser tab capture with semantic metadata. |
| Monitor Registry         | Multi-display topology.                     |
| Constraint Engine        | Resolution/FPS negotiation.                 |
| Display Metadata Runtime | DPI, viewport and display metadata.         |

---

# 3.02 DisplayMedia API Architecture

The entire Screen Capture Engine is built on `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()`.

## Capture API Pipeline

```text
User Selects Screen
        │
getDisplayMedia()
        │
MediaStream
        │
Screen Capture Runtime
        │
Recording Runtime
        │
MediaRecorder + WebCodecs
```

---

## DisplayMedia Responsibilities

The API can capture:

* Entire display.
* Single application window.
* Browser tab.
* Browser tab with system audio.
* External monitor.

---

## DisplayMedia Request Flow

```text
Creator Clicks Record
       │
Permission Manager
       │
DisplayMedia Request
       │
Browser Picker
       │
Selected Source
       │
Capture Runtime Initialized
```

---

## DisplayMedia Stream Interface

```ts
interface DisplayCaptureStream {
  streamId: string;
  mediaStream: MediaStream;
  captureMode: DisplayCaptureMode;
}
```

---

## DisplayMedia Lifecycle

```text
REQUESTED
    │
GRANTED
    │
ACTIVE
    │
PAUSED
    │
ENDED
```

---

## Engineering Rules

DisplayMedia streams are immutable after permission is granted.

---

# 3.03 Screen Capture Modes

TryLipi supports multiple visual capture experiences.

## Supported Capture Modes

| Mode                | Description                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Entire Screen       | Full monitor recording.                    |
| Application Window  | Single application.                        |
| Browser Tab         | Individual Chrome/Edge tab.                |
| Browser Tab + Audio | Tab recording with audio.                  |
| Multi-Monitor       | Multiple displays simultaneously (future). |

---

## Capture Mode Hierarchy

```text
Display Capture
│
├── Entire Screen
├── Window Capture
├── Browser Tab Capture
└── Multi-Monitor Capture
```

---

## Entire Screen Mode

Captures:

* Everything visible.
* Multiple applications.
* Cursor across desktop.
* Notifications (user-controlled).

Best for:

* Desktop tutorials.
* VS Code.
* Figma.
* AI tools.

---

## Window Capture Mode

Captures one application only.

Benefits:

* Cleaner recording.
* Privacy friendly.
* Smaller metadata scope.
* Automatic window cropping.

---

## Browser Tab Mode

Special mode enabling future DOM tracking.

Benefits:

* Semantic metadata.
* Scroll metadata.
* Viewport metadata.
* DOM element tracking.
* Tab audio.

---

## Capture Mode Interface

```ts
type DisplayCaptureMode =
  | "screen"
  | "window"
  | "browser_tab"
  | "browser_tab_audio"
  | "multi_monitor";
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Capture mode is immutable for the lifetime of a recording session.

---

# 3.04 Multi-Monitor Recording Runtime

Creators often use multiple displays.

TryLipi is designed to understand monitor topology.

## Multi-Monitor Architecture

```text
Monitor Registry
│
├── Display A
├── Display B
├── Display C
└── Active Capture Display
```

---

## Monitor Metadata Captured

| Metadata           | Purpose                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| Display ID         | Unique monitor identity.     |
| Resolution         | Native display size.         |
| Refresh Rate       | Performance tuning.          |
| Device Pixel Ratio | Retina scaling.              |
| Orientation        | Landscape/portrait.          |
| Position           | Virtual desktop coordinates. |

---

## Monitor Registry Interface

```ts
interface MonitorDescriptor {
  displayId: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  devicePixelRatio: number;
}
```

---

## Display Coordinate Space

```text
Virtual Desktop
│
├── Display A (0,0)
├── Display B (1920,0)
└── Display C (-1080,0)
```

Cursor metadata references this coordinate space.

---

## Multi-Monitor Recording Strategies

| Strategy                       | Description     |
| ------------------------------ | --------------- |
| Single Active Monitor          | Default.        |
| Dynamic Monitor Switching      | Future feature. |
| Parallel Multi-Monitor Capture | Future feature. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Monitor coordinates remain normalized into a virtual desktop coordinate system.

---

# 3.05 Browser Tab Recording Architecture

This is the most important capture mode for TryLipi.

# 3.08 Resolution & FPS Negotiation

## Resolution Negotiation

| Profile         | Resolution |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| Ultra           | 3840×2160  |
| Creator Default | 1920×1080  |
| Balanced        | 1600×900   |
| Lightweight     | 1280×720   |

---

## FPS Negotiation

| Profile         | FPS    |
| --------------- | ------ |
| Ultra           | 60 FPS |
| Creator Default | 60 FPS |
| Balanced        | 30 FPS |
| Low Power       | 24 FPS |

---

## Negotiation Pipeline

```text
Browser Capability
      │
Recording Profile
      │
Constraint Engine
      │
Capture Stream
```

---

## Dynamic Downscaling Rules

Downscale only when:

* Browser cannot provide requested FPS.
* Device memory pressure is high.
* Creator explicitly selected lower quality.

Recording quality is never silently increased.

---

## Engineering Rules

Capture resolution remains constant throughout a recording session.

# 3.21 Cursor Capture Integration Philosophy

## Mission Statement

Screen recording without cursor intelligence is only **pixel capture**.

TryLipi captures the cursor as an independent metadata stream synchronized with screen pixels.

The cursor becomes a first-class timeline object that powers:

* Smart Zoom.
* Click Ripples.
* Cursor Spotlight.
* AI Tutorial Generation.
* Camera Motion.
* Interaction Heatmaps.

---

## Dual Capture Architecture

```text
Display Pixels
      │
Screen Recording Track

Cursor Events
      │
Cursor Metadata Track

Timeline Renderer
      │
AI + Editor
```

Pixels and cursor metadata remain separate until rendering.

---

## Cursor Capture Responsibilities

| Runtime                | Responsibility                   |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Pointer Listener       | High-frequency cursor events.    |
| Coordinate Mapper      | Screen coordinate normalization. |
| Velocity Engine        | Cursor speed calculation.        |
| Interaction Tracker    | Click, drag, hover metadata.     |
| Cursor Timeline Writer | Metadata timeline generation.    |

---

## Cursor Metadata Captured

| Metadata     | Purpose                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------- |
| X Coordinate | Cursor position.          |
| Y Coordinate | Cursor position.          |
| Velocity     | Motion smoothing.         |
| Acceleration | Smart Zoom prediction.    |
| Click State  | Ripple animation.         |
| Drag State   | Drag visualization.       |
| Timestamp    | Timeline synchronization. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor metadata is captured even when cursor rendering is hidden from the recorded pixels.

---

# 3.22 High-DPI Scaling & Coordinate Normalization

## Why High-DPI Matters

Modern displays use device scaling.

Examples:

| Display              | DPR  |
| -------------------- | ---- |
| Standard Monitor     | 1.0  |
| Windows 125% Scaling | 1.25 |
| Windows 150% Scaling | 1.5  |
| Retina MacBook       | 2.0  |
| 4K Monitor (200%)    | 2.0  |

Cursor coordinates and pixels do not naturally align.

---

## Coordinate Spaces

```text
Physical Pixels
       │
Device Pixel Ratio
       │
Logical CSS Pixels
       │
Normalized Timeline Coordinates
```

TryLipi stores normalized coordinates.

---

## Coordinate Conversion Pipeline

```text
Pointer Event
      │
Physical Pixel Coordinates
      │
Normalize Using DPR
      │
Viewport Coordinates
      │
Recording Timeline Coordinates
```

---

## Coordinate Interface

```ts
interface NormalizedCursorPosition {
  normalizedX: number;
  normalizedY: number;
  devicePixelRatio: number;
}
```

---

## High-DPI Scaling Formula

```text
normalizedX = physicalX / (viewportWidth × DPR)
normalizedY = physicalY / (viewportHeight × DPR)
```

Stored values range from **0 → 1**.

---

## Why Normalize?

Benefits:

* Resolution-independent cursor replay.
* Same metadata works for 720p, 1080p and 4K exports.
* Camera Motion uses normalized positions.
* Smart Zoom becomes resolution agnostic.

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline stores normalized coordinates — renderer converts back into export resolution.

---

## Engineering Rules

# 3.26 Capture Interruptions & Recovery Runtime

Screen sharing can stop unexpectedly.

TryLipi handles interruptions gracefully.

## Interruption Sources

| Source             | Example                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| User Stops Sharing | Browser "Stop Sharing".     |
| Monitor Removed    | External display unplugged. |
| Permission Revoked | Screen permission removed.  |
| Window Closed      | Captured window exits.      |
| Browser Crash      | Unexpected termination.     |

---

## Recovery Pipeline

```text
Interruption Detected
       │
Capture Supervisor
       │
Recovery Strategy
       │
Continue / Finalize Recording
```

---

## Recovery Strategies

| Failure            | Runtime Action                     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| Window Closed      | End capture safely.                |
| Monitor Lost       | Ask creator to choose new display. |
| Permission Revoked | Finalize recording immediately.    |
| Browser Hidden     | Continue capture if supported.     |

---

## Capture Interruption States

```text
ACTIVE
   │
INTERRUPTED
   │
RECOVERING
   │
RESTORED
```

---

## Recovery Interface

```ts
interface CaptureRecoveryEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  reason: CaptureInterruptionReason;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery preserves recording timeline continuity whenever capture resumes.

---
