# 3.41 Production Screen Capture Philosophy

## Mission Statement

The Screen Capture Engine must work reliably across thousands of different creator environments.

Production recording must survive:

* Windows laptops with 125% or 150% scaling.
* Ultrawide monitors.
* Dual and triple monitor setups.
* High refresh rate displays (120 Hz / 144 Hz / 240 Hz).
* Laptop display changes.
* Display sleep/wake cycles.
* Browser zoom changes.
* Chrome updates without breaking recording.

The capture runtime is designed to **preserve recording integrity first, preview quality second**.

---

## Golden Production Principles

1. Screen capture never blocks MediaRecorder.
2. Display metadata is continuously synchronized.
3. Capture interruptions are recoverable whenever browser policies allow.
4. Preview rendering degrades before capture quality.
5. Multi-monitor environments are normalized into a single coordinate space.
6. Sensitive browser content can be hidden from previews.
7. Capture runtime is deterministic across Chrome and Edge.

---

## Production Runtime Layers

```text
Screen Capture Runtime
│
├── Display Runtime
├── Viewport Runtime
├── Cursor Runtime
├── Privacy Runtime
├── Recovery Runtime
├── Diagnostics Runtime
└── Performance Runtime
```

Each runtime can be monitored independently.

---

# 3.42 Capture Performance Optimization Engine

Recording must remain smooth even during heavy desktop activity.

## Performance Optimization Pipeline

```text
Display Stream
      │
Performance Monitor
      │
Optimization Engine
      │
Capture Runtime
```

---

## Optimization Inputs

| Metric             | Usage                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Frame Rate         | Detect dropped frames.    |
| Display Resolution | Adjust preview rendering. |
| GPU Availability   | Rendering decisions.      |
| CPU Usage          | Preview optimization.     |
| Memory Pressure    | Buffer optimization.      |

---

## Optimization Outputs

| Optimization                      | Purpose                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Reduce Preview FPS                | Preserve recording quality. |
| Disable Live Thumbnails           | Reduce GPU usage.           |
| Pause Debug Overlay               | Lower CPU usage.            |
| Compress Metadata More Frequently | Lower memory usage.         |

---

## Preview vs Capture Priority

| Runtime          | Priority |
| ---------------- | -------- |
| Screen Capture   | Highest  |
| MediaRecorder    | Highest  |
| Cursor Metadata  | High     |
| Upload Runtime   | Medium   |
| Preview Renderer | Adaptive |
| Diagnostics      | Lowest   |

---

## Engineering Rules

Preview quality may degrade automatically; recording quality must never degrade automatically.

---

# 3.43 Privacy Filter & Sensitive Content Runtime

Creators often share their entire desktop.

TryLipi includes a privacy-aware runtime for previews and AI processing.

## Privacy Runtime Philosophy

Privacy filters are **non-destructive overlays**.

The original recording remains untouched.

Privacy filtering happens only for:

* Live preview.
* AI processing.
* Shared review links (optional).

---

## Sensitive Content Categories

| Category              | Detection Strategy      |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Email Addresses       | OCR + Regex             |
| Phone Numbers         | OCR + Pattern Detection |
| Password Fields       | DOM + OCR               |
| API Keys              | OCR + Entropy Detection |
| Access Tokens         | OCR + Pattern Detection |
| Credit Card Numbers   | OCR + Validation Rules  |
| Aadhaar / PAN (India) | OCR + Pattern Detection |

---

## Privacy Pipeline

```text
Screen Frame
      │
OCR Runtime
      │
Sensitive Region Detector
      │
Blur Mask Layer
      │
Preview Renderer
```

---

## Blur Region Metadata

```ts
interface SensitiveRegion {
  id: string;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  category: SensitiveContentType;
}
```

---

## Privacy Modes

| Mode          | Behavior                     |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Off           | No filtering.                |
| Preview Only  | Blur only preview.           |
| AI Only       | Hide regions from AI models. |
| Shared Review | Blur in shared links.        |

---

## Engineering Rules

Privacy filters never modify the source recording file.

---

# 3.44 Dynamic Resolution & Refresh Rate Handling

Displays can change while recording.

The runtime tracks display characteristics as timeline metadata.

## Resolution Change Pipeline

```text
Display Change
      │
Display Observer
      │
Geometry Event
      │
Timeline Metadata
```

---

## Supported Geometry Changes

| Event                     | Runtime Behavior          |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Window Resize             | Metadata event.           |
| Display Resolution Change | Metadata snapshot.        |
| Browser Zoom Change       | Metadata event.           |
| Display Rotation          | Metadata snapshot.        |
| DPR Change                | Coordinate recalculation. |

---

## Refresh Rate Metadata

Captured values include:

* 60 Hz
* 90 Hz
* 120 Hz
* 144 Hz
* 165 Hz
* 240 Hz

Refresh rate influences preview interpolation—not recording timestamps.

---

## Display Geometry Snapshot

```ts
interface DisplayGeometrySnapshot {
  timestampUs: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  refreshRate: number;
  devicePixelRatio: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Resolution changes create metadata snapshots instead of restarting capture.

---

# 3.45 Screen Capture Failure Recovery Runtime

Screen capture interruptions require deterministic recovery.

## Failure Recovery Pipeline

```text
Capture Failure
      │
Capture Supervisor
      │
Recovery Decision Engine
      │
Recover / Finalize
```

---

## Failure Categories

| Failure                    | Recovery                               |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Screen Sharing Ended       | Finalize recording safely.             |
| Window Closed              | End capture.                           |
| Display Disconnected       | Offer replacement display if possible. |
| Browser Permission Revoked | Finalize recording immediately.        |
| Display Sleep              | Attempt stream recovery.               |

---

## Recovery State Machine

```text
ACTIVE
   │
FAILED
   │
RECOVERING
   │
RESTORED
```

---

## Recovery Metadata Event

```ts
interface ScreenCaptureRecoveryEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  reason: ScreenCaptureFailureReason;
  recovered: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery never changes the recording session ID or timeline clock.

---

# 3.46 Browser Edge Cases & Platform Behavior

Real-world browsers behave differently.

This chapter standardizes runtime behavior.

## Chromium Family Support

| Browser | Status |
| ------- | ------ |
| Chrome  | Tier A |
| Edge    | Tier A |
| Brave   | Tier A |
| Arc     | Tier A |
| Opera   | Tier B |

---

## Firefox Limitations

Known limitations:

* System audio unavailable.
* WebCodecs partially supported.
* OffscreenCanvas worker behavior differs.
* CaptureController support limited.

Runtime gracefully disables unsupported features.

---

## Safari Limitations

Known limitations:

* System audio unavailable.
* Browser tab audio unavailable.
* WebCodecs incomplete.
* OPFS partial support.

Safari receives a compatibility runtime.

---

## Windows Edge Cases

| Scenario           | Runtime Behavior                         |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| HDR Display        | Capture SDR stream unless HDR supported. |
| Mixed DPI Monitors | Normalize coordinates.                   |
| Display Sleep      | Attempt recovery.                        |
| GPU Driver Reset   | Restart preview renderer only.           |

---

## Engineering Rules

Browser-specific workarounds live inside capability adapters, never inside editor logic.

---

# 3.47 Screen Capture Diagnostics & Telemetry

The Screen Capture Engine exposes detailed runtime telemetry.

## Diagnostics Architecture

```text
Screen Runtime
      │
Telemetry Collector
      │
Runtime Dashboard
      │
Developer Console
```

---

## Metrics Captured

### Display Metrics

* Capture resolution.
* Refresh rate.
* DPR.
* Viewport size.
* Monitor ID.

### Performance Metrics

* Capture FPS.
* Dropped frames.
* Capture latency.
* Preview latency.

### Recovery Metrics

* Capture interruptions.
* Recovery attempts.
* Successful recoveries.

---

## Runtime Events

| Event                      | Description                |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `display.capture.started`  | Capture began.             |
| `display.capture.failed`   | Capture interruption.      |
| `display.geometry.changed` | Resolution or DPR changed. |
| `display.recovered`        | Capture restored.          |

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface ScreenCaptureDiagnostics {
  captureFPS: number;
  droppedFrames: number;
  refreshRate: number;
  activeDisplayId: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Telemetry sampling frequency automatically decreases during long recordings.

---

# 3.48 Performance Budget Enforcement

Performance budgets are enforced continuously.

## Capture Budgets

| Metric                 | Budget            |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| Capture Latency        | Under 16 ms/frame |
| Preview Latency        | Under 50 ms       |
| Geometry Event Latency | Under 5 ms        |
| Cursor Mapping Latency | Under 2 ms        |
| Display Metadata Write | Under 1 ms        |

---

## Runtime Thresholds

| Threshold            | Runtime Action             |
| -------------------- | -------------------------- |
| GPU Busy             | Lower preview FPS.         |
| CPU Busy             | Pause debug overlays.      |
| Memory Warning       | Compress metadata buffers. |
| Display Change Storm | Batch geometry events.     |

---

## Optimization Priority

1. Recording capture.
2. Cursor metadata.
3. Upload queue.
4. Preview renderer.
5. Diagnostics.

---

## Engineering Rules

Screen capture runtime always has priority over live preview rendering.

---

# 6.01 Cursor Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The cursor is the narrator of every tutorial.**

Almost every software tutorial is driven by the cursor.

Where the cursor moves determines:

* What viewers pay attention to.
* When Smart Zoom should trigger.
* Which UI element is important.
* When camera movement begins.
* What AI considers an interaction.

Instead of treating the cursor as pixels inside the recording, TryLipi records it as an **independent semantic interaction stream**.

---

## Cursor as an Independent Recording Layer

```text
Screen Pixels
      │
Cursor Metadata Stream
      │
Interaction Timeline
      │
AI + Editor Renderer
```

This architecture enables creators to completely redesign cursor appearance after recording.

---

## Cursor Intelligence Responsibilities

| Runtime Module      | Responsibility                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Pointer Runtime     | Raw pointer capture.             |
| Motion Runtime      | Cursor trajectory.               |
| Velocity Runtime    | Cursor speed analysis.           |
| Interaction Runtime | Hover, drag, click metadata.     |
| Timeline Runtime    | Cursor metadata synchronization. |
| Rendering Runtime   | Cursor styling after recording.  |

---

## Golden Cursor Principles

1. Cursor metadata is independent from pixels.
2. Cursor sampling uses the recording clock.
3. Cursor replay is resolution independent.
4. Motion is continuous—not click based.
5. Every cursor event is timestamped.
6. Rendering happens after recording.
7. AI consumes metadata—not rendered cursor pixels.

---

# 6.02 Why Cursor Is a First-Class Timeline Object

Traditional screen recorders permanently bake the cursor into video frames.

TryLipi separates them.

## Traditional Architecture

```text
Screen Recording
      │
Cursor Burned Into Pixels
      │
Video
```

Impossible to edit later.

---

## TryLipi Architecture

```text
Screen Recording
      │
Screen Track

Cursor Runtime
      │
Cursor Metadata Track

Timeline Renderer
      │
Rendered Cursor Layer
```

Cursor becomes editable.

---

## Editing Possibilities Enabled

| Feature             | Enabled |
| ------------------- | ------- |
| Change Cursor Size  | ✅       |
| Change Cursor Color | ✅       |
| Add Spotlight       | ✅       |
| Click Ripple        | ✅       |
| Cursor Shadow       | ✅       |
| Cursor Tail         | ✅       |
| Cursor Glow         | ✅       |
| AI Cursor Highlight | ✅       |

---

## Timeline Layer Model

```text
Timeline
│
├── Screen Track
├── Webcam Track
├── Audio Track
├── Cursor Track
├── Keyboard Track
├── Zoom Track
└── Metadata Track
```

Cursor Track is rendered dynamically.

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor appearance is never permanently embedded into recorded pixels.

---

# 6.03 Pointer Capture Runtime Architecture

The Pointer Runtime captures every meaningful cursor movement.

## Pointer Runtime Pipeline

```text
Pointer Events API
        │
Pointer Runtime
        │
Sampling Engine
        │
Coordinate Normalizer
        │
Cursor Metadata Queue
        │
Timeline Writer
```

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Component         | Responsibility              |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| Pointer Listener  | Browser pointer events.     |
| Coordinate Mapper | Normalize coordinates.      |
| Timestamp Writer  | Recording clock timestamps. |
| Motion Analyzer   | Detect movement.            |
| Metadata Writer   | Cursor timeline events.     |

---

## Pointer Event Sources

Captured browser events include:

* `pointermove`
* `pointerdown`
* `pointerup`
* `pointerenter`
* `pointerleave`
* `pointercancel`

---

## Pointer Runtime Interface

```ts
interface PointerRuntimeState {
  pointerActive: boolean;
  samplingRateHz: number;
  lastTimestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Runtime Lifecycle

```text
IDLE
  │
LISTENING
  │
SAMPLING
  │
PAUSED
  │
STOPPED
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Pointer Runtime continues sampling even if preview rendering is paused.

---

# 6.04 Cursor Coordinate Systems

Coordinates must work across monitors, resolutions and exports.

## Four Coordinate Spaces

```text
Physical Pixels
       │
CSS Pixels
       │
Viewport Coordinates
       │
Normalized Timeline Coordinates
```

Each serves a different runtime.

---

## Coordinate Definitions

| Coordinate Space       | Usage                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Physical Pixels        | Browser pointer events. |
| CSS Pixels             | DOM interactions.       |
| Viewport Coordinates   | Browser tab mode.       |
| Normalized Coordinates | Timeline storage.       |

---

## Normalization Formula

```text
normalizedX = x / viewportWidth
normalizedY = y / viewportHeight
```

Stored between `0.0` and `1.0`.

---

## Why Normalize?

Benefits:

* 720p → 4K exports.
* Vertical video exports.
* Cropped videos.
* Camera panning.
* Smart Zoom.

---

## Coordinate Interface

```ts
interface CursorCoordinates {
  physicalX: number;
  physicalY: number;
  normalizedX: number;
  normalizedY: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline stores normalized coordinates as the canonical representation.

---

# 6.05 High-Frequency Pointer Sampling Engine

Smooth cursor motion requires high-frequency sampling.

## Sampling Philosophy

Recording FPS is **not** cursor FPS.

Cursor metadata may be sampled faster than rendered video.

---

## Sampling Pipeline

```text
Pointer Event
      │
Sampling Scheduler
      │
Cursor Sample
      │
Motion Buffer
      │
Timeline Metadata
```

---

## Sampling Rates

| Recording Mode      | Cursor Sampling        |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- |
| 30 FPS Video        | 90 Hz Cursor           |
| 60 FPS Video        | 120 Hz Cursor          |
| High Precision Mode | 240 Hz Cursor Metadata |

---

## Why Oversample?

Enables:

* Smooth easing.
* Motion interpolation.
* AI movement prediction.
* Slow-motion exports.

---

## Sampling Metadata

```ts
interface CursorSample {
  timestampUs: number;
  x: number;
  y: number;
}
```

---

## Sample Buffer Strategy

```text
Live Samples
      │
Rolling Motion Buffer
      │
Compressed Timeline Events
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Sampling frequency is independent of recording frame rate.

---

# 6.06 Cursor Motion Tracking Engine

Motion is reconstructed as trajectories.

## Motion Pipeline

```text
Cursor Samples
      │
Motion Tracker
      │
Trajectory Builder
      │
Timeline Motion Segments
```

---

## Motion Segment Model

| Segment | Description                |
| ------- | -------------------------- |
| Move    | Continuous movement.       |
| Hover   | Stationary cursor.         |
| Drag    | Pointer held while moving. |
| Idle    | No movement.               |

---

## Motion State Machine

```text
IDLE
 │
MOVE
 │
HOVER
 │
DRAG
 │
MOVE
```

---

## Trajectory Metadata

```ts
interface CursorTrajectorySegment {
  startUs: number;
  endUs: number;
  pathLengthPx: number;
}
```

---

## Motion Compression

Instead of saving every point forever:

* Raw samples buffered.
* Simplified trajectory stored.
* High precision retained for AI.

---

## Engineering Rules

Motion segments preserve original timestamps even after compression.

---

# 6.07 Cursor Velocity & Acceleration Model

Cursor behavior reveals user intent.

## Velocity Pipeline

```text
Cursor Samples
      │
Distance Calculator
      │
Velocity Engine
      │
Acceleration Engine
      │
Intent Metadata
```

---

## Velocity Metrics

| Metric           | Purpose              |
| ---------------- | -------------------- |
| Instant Velocity | Cursor speed.        |
| Average Velocity | Motion smoothing.    |
| Peak Velocity    | Camera anticipation. |
| Acceleration     | Zoom prediction.     |

---

## Velocity Formula

```text
velocity = distance / deltaTime
```

---

## Acceleration Formula

```text
acceleration = deltaVelocity / deltaTime
```

---

## Motion Categories

| Category          | Velocity  |
| ----------------- | --------- |
| Precise Hover     | Very Low  |
| UI Exploration    | Low       |
| Normal Navigation | Medium    |
| Fast Navigation   | High      |
| Flick Motion      | Very High |

---

## AI Uses

Velocity helps predict:

* Zoom destination.
* Click importance.
* Camera movement timing.

---

## Engineering Rules

Velocity is derived metadata—not a primary timeline event.

---

# 6.08 Cursor Interaction Timeline

Every interaction becomes a semantic event.

## Timeline Event Flow

```text
Pointer Runtime
      │
Interaction Detector
      │
Timeline Event
```

---

## Cursor Event Types

| Event          | Stored |
| -------------- | ------ |
| Move           | ✅      |
| Hover Begin    | ✅      |
| Hover End      | ✅      |
| Drag Begin     | ✅      |
| Drag End       | ✅      |
| Enter Viewport | ✅      |
| Leave Viewport | ✅      |

---

## Interaction Timeline Example

```text
0.0s   Hover Button
0.6s   Move
1.1s   Hover Input
2.0s   Drag Slider
3.4s   Idle
```

---

## Timeline Interface

```ts
interface CursorTimelineEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  type: CursorEventType;
}
```

---

## Timeline Synchronization

Cursor events align with:

* Screen frames.
* Audio.
* Keyboard events.
* DOM events.
* Smart Zoom timeline.

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor timeline is immutable once recording finishes.

---

# 6.09 Cursor Metadata Data Model

Cursor metadata is stored separately from rendering.

## Cursor Metadata Schema

```text
Cursor Metadata
│
├── Position
├── Velocity
├── Acceleration
├── Motion Segment
├── Interaction State
├── Display Mapping
└── Viewport Mapping
```

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface CursorMetadataFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  normalizedX: number;
  normalizedY: number;
  velocity: number;
  interactionState: CursorInteractionState;
}
```

---

## Compression Strategy

| Layer           | Storage           |
| --------------- | ----------------- |
| Raw Samples     | Temporary buffer. |
| Motion Segments | Timeline storage. |
| AI Samples      | Optional archive. |

---

## Metadata Timeline Track

```text
Cursor Timeline
│
├── Motion Events
├── Hover Events
├── Drag Events
├── Velocity Samples
└── Display Mapping Events
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor metadata is versioned independently from video exports.

---

# 6.10 Runtime Cursor APIs

Chapter 6 introduces the Cursor Intelligence Runtime APIs.

## Runtime APIs

| API                     | Purpose                  |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `startCursorCapture()`  | Begin pointer runtime.   |
| `stopCursorCapture()`   | End pointer runtime.     |
| `pauseCursorCapture()`  | Pause metadata sampling. |
| `resumeCursorCapture()` | Resume sampling.         |
| `getCursorTrajectory()` | Retrieve motion path.    |
| `getCursorMetadata()`   | Timeline metadata.       |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface CursorRuntimeAPI {
  samplingRateHz: number;
  active: boolean;
}
```

---

## Cursor Runtime Events

```text
cursor.capture.started
cursor.capture.paused
cursor.capture.resumed
cursor.motion.segment
cursor.hover.started
cursor.hover.ended
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Cursor Runtime APIs expose metadata only—not rendered cursor graphics.

---

# 6.11 Acceptance Principles

## Pointer Runtime Tests

* Pointer events captured continuously.
* Sampling frequency maintained.
* Timeline timestamps monotonic.

### Motion Tests

* Hover detected correctly.
* Drag segments detected correctly.
* Motion compression preserves trajectory.

### Coordinate Tests

* High-DPI normalization correct.
* Multi-monitor mapping correct.
* Browser zoom normalization correct.

### Timeline Tests

* Cursor aligned with recording clock.
* Metadata replay deterministic.

---

# 6.12 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 6.1)

1. Cursor is a first-class semantic timeline object.
2. Cursor metadata is stored independently from recorded pixels.
3. Pointer Runtime samples independently of recording FPS.
4. Timeline stores normalized coordinates only.
5. Motion is reconstructed from trajectories instead of rendered pixels.
6. Velocity and acceleration are derived metadata for AI systems.
7. Cursor interactions become immutable semantic timeline events.
8. Rendering is separated completely from capture.
9. Cursor metadata synchronizes with the global recording clock.
10. Chapter 6.1 establishes the foundational Cursor Intelligence architecture used by Smart Zoom, Camera Motion, Click Intelligence, DOM Tracking, and AI Tutorial Generation.

# 6.21 Semantic Cursor Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **A cursor movement is not just movement. It is intent.**

Creators don't move a cursor randomly.

Every cursor behavior communicates something:

* Hovering means "look here."
* Clicking means "this is important."
* Dragging means "I'm demonstrating a workflow."
* Rapid movement usually means navigation.
* Slow movement usually means explanation.

TryLipi transforms raw pointer data into **semantic interaction events**.

---

## Cursor Intelligence Pipeline

```text
Pointer Samples
      │
Behavior Analysis Engine
      │
Interaction Classifier
      │
Intent Engine
      │
Semantic Timeline
      │
AI + Smart Zoom + Camera Motion
```

---

## Intelligence Layers

| Layer             | Output                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Motion Layer      | Velocity & trajectory.                    |
| Interaction Layer | Hover, click, drag.                       |
| Intent Layer      | Explain, navigate, demonstrate.           |
| AI Layer          | Zoom, camera movement, tutorial chapters. |

---

## Golden Semantic Principles

1. Clicks are semantic events, not pixels.
2. Hover duration determines attention.
3. Drag paths become editable timeline objects.
4. Intent is inferred from interaction context.
5. Cursor behavior feeds AI systems directly.
6. Every semantic event remains editable.

---

# 6.22 Click Detection Engine

Clicks are among the most important events in a tutorial.

## Click Detection Pipeline

```text
pointerdown
     │
Pointer State Machine
     │
Click Detector
     │
Semantic Click Event
     │
Timeline Writer
```

---

## Click Lifecycle

```text
IDLE
 │
PRESS
 │
RELEASE
 │
CLICK CONFIRMED
```

---

## Click Metadata

| Metadata    | Purpose                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------- |
| Button      | Left, right, middle.    |
| Position    | Normalized coordinates. |
| Timestamp   | Recording timeline.     |
| Duration    | Click hold length.      |
| Click Count | Single / Double.        |

---

## Click Event Interface

```ts
interface CursorClickEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  button: "left" | "right" | "middle";
  normalizedX: number;
  normalizedY: number;
  holdDurationMs: number;
}
```

---

## Click Classification

| Interaction  | Detection Rule               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- |
| Single Click | One press/release cycle.     |
| Double Click | Two clicks inside threshold. |
| Long Press   | Hold exceeds threshold.      |
| Right Click  | Secondary pointer button.    |
| Middle Click | Middle button.               |

---

## Click Confidence Model

Each click receives a confidence score based on timing consistency.

Used later for:

* Smart Zoom confidence.
* Tutorial segmentation.
* Click ripple rendering.

---

## Engineering Rules

A click event is finalized only after release, not on press.

# 6.31 Acceptance Principles

## Click Detection Tests

* Single click detected correctly.
* Double click classified correctly.
* Long press detected correctly.
* Right click separated.

### Hover Tests

* Hover duration measured correctly.
* Hover radius respected.
* Hover ends immediately after movement threshold.

### Drag Tests

* Drag start threshold respected.
* Trajectory reconstructed correctly.
* Drop event generated.

### Idle Tests

* Reading pauses detected.
* Long idle segments generated.

### Intent Tests

* Hover → Focus intent.
* Click CTA → CTA intent.
* Drag slider → Workflow intent.
* Navigation classified correctly.

---

# 6.32 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 6.2)

1. Cursor behavior is transformed into semantic interaction events.
2. Clicks, hovers, drags, and idle periods become independent timeline objects.
3. Hover duration is a primary attention signal for AI systems.
4. Drag trajectories remain editable timeline metadata.
5. Cursor prediction is used only for rendering and AI—not recording data.
6. Interaction classification is deterministic and replayable.
7. AI Intent events are layered above interaction events.
8. Cursor Timeline contains multiple semantic layers synchronized to one recording clock.
9. Every semantic cursor event is immutable after recording completes.
10. Chapter 6.2 establishes the AI Interaction Intelligence layer that powers Smart Zoom, Camera Motion, Tutorial Generation, and Screen Studio cursor effects.

# 6.31 Cursor Rendering Philosophy

## Mission Statement

The **Cursor Rendering Engine** transforms invisible cursor metadata into cinematic cursor animations during playback and export.

This is where TryLipi competes directly with **Cursorful** and **Screen Studio**.

> **Recording captures intent. Rendering creates emotion.**

The renderer is responsible for making cursor movement feel:

* Smooth.
* Premium.
* Cinematic.
* Easy to follow.
* Attention-guiding.

Importantly:

**Nothing is rendered during recording.** Rendering happens only during preview, editing, or export.

---

## Capture vs Render Architecture

```text
Recording Phase
│
├── Cursor Metadata
├── Motion Metadata
├── Click Metadata
└── Intent Metadata

Playback / Export Phase
│
├── Cursor Renderer
├── Spotlight Renderer
├── Ripple Renderer
├── Tail Renderer
└── Motion Smoother
```

---

## Cursor Rendering Layers

```text
Cursor Rendering Engine
│
├── Base Cursor Layer
├── Spotlight Layer
├── Click Layer
├── Motion Trail Layer
├── Glow Layer
├── Shadow Layer
└── Accessibility Layer
```

Each layer is optional and editable.

---

## Golden Rendering Principles

1. Rendering is non-destructive.
2. Cursor appearance is editable after recording.
3. Animations are frame-independent.
4. GPU rendering is preferred.
5. Effects never modify cursor metadata.
6. Export renderer and preview renderer produce identical results.
7. Every animation is timeline driven.

---

The rendering engine converts metadata into visuals.

## Rendering Pipeline

```text
      │
Interpolation Engine
      │

      │
Effects Engine
      │
Preview / Export Frame
```

---

| Module            | Responsibility                |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Position Renderer | Cursor location.              |
| Rotation Renderer | Pointer orientation (future). |
| Scale Renderer    | Dynamic cursor size.          |
| Shadow Renderer   | Depth.                        |
| Glow Renderer     | Focus emphasis.               |
| Theme Renderer    | Cursor style presets.         |

---

```text

       │
Cursor Metadata Lookup
       │
Interpolation
       │
Effects Applied
       │
Frame Rendered
```

---

## Cursor Render Interface

```ts
interface CursorRenderFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  renderX: number;
  renderY: number;
  scale: number;
  opacity: number;
}
```

---

## Interpolation Strategy

Instead of jumping between recorded samples:

* Linear interpolation.
* Cubic interpolation.
* Velocity-aware interpolation.
* Bezier motion smoothing.

---

## Engineering Rules

Renderer consumes normalized coordinates only.

## Engineering Rules

# 6.34 Cursor Tail & Motion Trail Engine

```text
      │
```

```text

●────●────●────●────●
     ▲
   Current Cursor
```

| Idle     | No trail.             |

| Medium   | Medium trail.         |

Uses:

* Catmull-Rom splines.
* Cubic Bezier interpolation.
* Velocity easing.

## Engineering Rules

Trail geometry is generated procedurally—not stored.

# 6.38 Cursor Rendering Performance Runtime

Cursor rendering must remain extremely lightweight.

## Rendering Pipeline Optimization

```text
Cursor Metadata
      │
Interpolation Cache
      │
GPU Renderer
      │
Preview Surface
```

---

## Performance Optimizations

| Optimization         | Benefit                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| GPU rendering        | Smooth cursor motion.    |
| Cached interpolation | Lower CPU usage.         |
| Trail batching       | Fewer draw calls.        |
| Spotlight masking    | Single compositing pass. |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric             | Target           |
| ------------------ | ---------------- |
| Cursor Render Cost | Under 1 ms/frame |
| Ripple Render      | Under 0.5 ms     |
| Spotlight Render   | Under 1 ms       |
| Trail Render       | Under 0.8 ms     |

---

## Adaptive Rendering

When preview FPS drops:

1. Reduce spotlight blur quality.
2. Reduce trail sample density.
3. Lower ripple particle count.

Cursor motion remains smooth.

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance optimizations never reduce cursor metadata fidelity.

---

# 6.41 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 6.3)

1. Cursor rendering is completely separated from cursor capture.
2. Spotlight, ripples and trails are procedural rendering layers.
3. Cursor appearance is editable after recording.
4. Motion interpolation uses normalized timeline coordinates.
5. Screen Studio animations are generated from semantic cursor metadata.
6. AI importance influences spotlight, ripple and camera behavior.
7. Rendering budgets prioritize smooth cursor playback over decorative effects.
8. Cursor themes are reusable project-level assets.
9. Diagnostics expose capture, rendering and AI interaction metrics independently.
10. Chapter 06 defines the complete production Cursor Intelligence Engine for TryLipi.

# 7.01 Keyboard Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **A keyboard tells the story of what the creator is doing.**

Mouse interactions explain **where** attention is.

Keyboard interactions explain **what** action happened.

Examples:

* `Ctrl + K` → Search opened.
* `Ctrl + Shift + P` → Command Palette.
* `Cmd + B` → Sidebar toggle.
* `Ctrl + S` → Save action.
* `Enter` → Confirmation.
* `Esc` → Cancel.

TryLipi captures keyboard activity as a **semantic interaction stream**, synchronized with cursor, screen, audio, and viewport metadata.

---

## Keyboard Intelligence Architecture

```text
Keyboard Events API
        │
Keyboard Runtime
        │
Shortcut Detector
        │
Input Intelligence
        │
Semantic Timeline
        │
AI + Editor + Effects
```

---

## Keyboard Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime Module    | Responsibility                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Keyboard Listener | Browser keyboard events.        |
| Shortcut Engine   | Detect hotkeys.                 |
| Modifier Engine   | Ctrl, Cmd, Shift, Alt tracking. |
| Input Engine      | Text typing metadata.           |
| Timeline Writer   | Keyboard timeline events.       |
| Rendering Engine  | Visual keystroke overlays.      |

---

## Golden Keyboard Principles

1. Keyboard metadata is independent from pixels.
2. Key presses are timestamped using the recording clock.
3. Shortcuts are semantic actions.
4. Typed text is treated differently from shortcuts.
5. Sensitive text is never stored by default.
6. Keyboard overlays are rendered after recording.
7. AI consumes semantic keyboard events—not visual overlays.

---

# 7.02 Keyboard Capture Runtime Architecture

The Keyboard Runtime continuously listens for browser keyboard events during recording.

## Runtime Pipeline

```text
keydown / keyup
        │
Keyboard Runtime
        │
Key State Tracker
        │
Shortcut Detector
        │
Keyboard Metadata Queue
        │
Timeline Writer
```

---

## Browser Events Captured

| Event         | Purpose                                 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `keydown`     | Key pressed.                            |
| `keyup`       | Key released.                           |
| `keypress`    | Legacy compatibility only.              |
| `beforeinput` | Rich text detection (Browser Tab Mode). |
| `input`       | Text input detection.                   |

---

## Runtime State Machine

```text
IDLE
 │
LISTENING
 │
KEY PRESSED
 │
KEY RELEASED
 │
IDLE
```

---

## Keyboard Runtime Interface

```ts
interface KeyboardRuntimeState {
  listening: boolean;
  activeKeys: Set<string>;
  modifierState: ModifierKeyState;
}
```

---

## Event Sampling Philosophy

Unlike cursor sampling:

* Keyboard events are event-driven.
* No polling.
* Every key transition becomes a timeline event.

---

## Engineering Rules

Keyboard Runtime must remain active even when preview rendering is paused.

---

# 7.03 Keyboard Event Lifecycle

Each keyboard interaction follows a deterministic lifecycle.

## Key Lifecycle

```text
KEYDOWN
   │
Active Key Registry
   │
Modifier Evaluation
   │
Shortcut Evaluation
   │
Timeline Event
   │
KEYUP
```

---

## Event Timeline Example

```text
0.0s KeyDown Ctrl
0.1s KeyDown K
0.1s Shortcut Detected
0.2s KeyUp K
0.3s KeyUp Ctrl
```

---

## Event Types

| Event              | Description              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| Key Press          | Initial press.           |
| Key Release        | Key released.            |
| Key Hold           | Held beyond threshold.   |
| Repeat Key         | Auto-repeat detected.    |
| Shortcut Triggered | Semantic shortcut event. |

---

## Keyboard Timeline Event

```ts
interface KeyboardTimelineEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  eventType: KeyboardEventType;
  key: string;
}
```

---

## Key Hold Detection

| Duration         | Classification |
| ---------------- | -------------- |
| Less than 150 ms | Tap            |
| 150–500 ms       | Hold           |
| More than 500 ms | Long Hold      |

---

## Engineering Rules

Key repeat events are compressed into a single semantic hold event where appropriate.

---

# 7.04 Modifier Key Intelligence Engine

Modifier keys change the meaning of every interaction.

## Modifier Runtime

```text
Modifier Keys
     │
Modifier Tracker
     │
Active Modifier State
     │
Shortcut Engine
```

---

## Supported Modifier Keys

| Platform | Keys                     |
| -------- | ------------------------ |
| Windows  | Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Win    |
| macOS    | Cmd, Shift, Option, Ctrl |
| Linux    | Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Super  |

---

## Modifier State Machine

```text
NONE
 │
CTRL
 │
CTRL+SHIFT
 │
CTRL+SHIFT+P
 │
NONE
```

---

## Modifier Metadata

```ts
interface ModifierKeyState {
  ctrl: boolean;
  shift: boolean;
  alt: boolean;
  meta: boolean;
}
```

---

## Platform Normalization

TryLipi normalizes shortcuts internally.

| Windows | macOS | Canonical Action |
| ------- | ----- | ---------------- |
| Ctrl+C  | Cmd+C | Copy             |
| Ctrl+V  | Cmd+V | Paste            |
| Ctrl+S  | Cmd+S | Save             |
| Ctrl+Z  | Cmd+Z | Undo             |

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline stores normalized shortcut actions while preserving original platform metadata.

---

# 7.05 Shortcut Detection Engine

The Shortcut Engine converts multiple simultaneous keys into semantic actions.

## Detection Pipeline

```text
Key Events
    │
Modifier Engine
    │
Shortcut Matcher
    │
Shortcut Metadata Event
```

---

## Shortcut Categories

| Category   | Examples             |
| ---------- | -------------------- |
| Navigation | Ctrl+Tab, Alt+Tab    |
| Editing    | Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V       |
| IDE        | Ctrl+Shift+P, Ctrl+` |
| Browser    | Ctrl+L, Ctrl+R       |
| Design     | Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G |
| AI Tools   | Ctrl+K, Cmd+K        |

---

## Shortcut Registry

```ts
interface ShortcutDefinition {
  id: string;
  keys: string[];
  semanticAction: ShortcutAction;
}
```

---

## Detection Example

```text
Ctrl
 │
Ctrl + Shift
 │
Ctrl + Shift + P
 │
Command Palette Opened
```

---

## Multi-Key Detection Rules

* Order-independent matching.
* Modifier normalization.
* Hold tolerance.
* Platform mapping.

---

## Engineering Rules

Shortcut events become semantic timeline objects independent of raw key events.

---

# 7.06 Text Input Intelligence Engine

Typing is different from shortcuts.

TryLipi separates **commands** from **content creation**.

## Input Intelligence Pipeline

```text
Input Events
     │
Text Input Detector
     │
Input Metadata
     │
Timeline Event
```

---

## Input Categories

| Category       | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| Plain Text     | Typing text.     |
| Password Input | Sensitive field. |
| Search Input   | Search bars.     |
| Code Input     | IDE typing.      |
| Command Input  | Terminal typing. |

---

## Metadata Captured

| Metadata        | Stored              |
| --------------- | ------------------- |
| Input Started   | Yes                 |
| Input Ended     | Yes                 |
| Character Count | Yes                 |
| Typing Duration | Yes                 |
| Typing Speed    | Yes                 |
| Actual Text     | Optional / Redacted |

---

## Text Input Interface

```ts
interface TextInputMetadata {
  timestampUs: number;
  inputType: TextInputType;
  characterCount: number;
}
```

---

## Privacy Modes

| Mode           | Behavior                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Metadata Only  | Store counts, not characters. |
| Developer Mode | Store code text.              |
| Browser Mode   | Respect sensitive inputs.     |
| Password Mode  | Never store text.             |

---

## Engineering Rules

Sensitive text is redacted before timeline storage unless explicitly permitted.

---

# 7.07 Keyboard Timeline Architecture

Keyboard becomes its own editable timeline.

## Timeline Structure

```text
Keyboard Timeline
│
├── Key Events
├── Modifier Events
├── Shortcut Events
├── Text Input Events
└── Hold Events
```

---

## Timeline Synchronization

Keyboard aligns with:

* Screen timeline.
* Cursor timeline.
* Audio timeline.
* DOM timeline.
* Smart Zoom timeline.

---

## Timeline Example

```text
0.5s Ctrl+K
1.4s Type "Settings"
3.0s Enter
4.2s Ctrl+Shift+P
```

---

## Timeline Interface

```ts
interface KeyboardTimelineFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  shortcut?: ShortcutAction;
  inputType?: TextInputType;
}
```

---

## Timeline Compression Strategy

* Merge repeated key events.
* Group continuous typing sessions.
* Preserve shortcut boundaries.
* Keep semantic timing.

---

## Engineering Rules

Keyboard timeline is immutable after recording finishes.

---

# 7.08 Keyboard Metadata Schema

Keyboard metadata is stored independently from rendering.

## Metadata Model

```text
Keyboard Metadata
│
├── Raw Key Events
├── Modifier State
├── Shortcut Events
├── Input Metadata
├── Hold Metadata
└── Platform Metadata
```

---

## Canonical Schema

```ts
interface KeyboardMetadataFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  key: string;
  modifiers: ModifierKeyState;
  semanticAction?: ShortcutAction;
}
```

---

## Metadata Layers

| Layer              | Purpose                |
| ------------------ | ---------------------- |
| Raw Keys           | Debugging & replay.    |
| Semantic Shortcuts | AI & editor.           |
| Typing Metadata    | Analytics.             |
| Platform Metadata  | Windows/macOS mapping. |

---

## Storage Strategy

* Raw keys compressed.
* Semantic events preserved.
* Sensitive content removed.
* Timeline indexed by timestamp.

---

## Engineering Rules

Semantic keyboard metadata is the primary API consumed by AI systems.

---

# 7.09 Runtime Keyboard APIs

Chapter 7 introduces the Keyboard Intelligence Runtime APIs.

## Runtime APIs

| API                          | Purpose                   |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `startKeyboardCapture()`     | Begin keyboard runtime.   |
| `stopKeyboardCapture()`      | Stop keyboard runtime.    |
| `subscribeShortcutEvents()`  | Semantic shortcut stream. |
| `subscribeTextInputEvents()` | Typing metadata stream.   |
| `getKeyboardTimeline()`      | Replay timeline events.   |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface KeyboardRuntimeAPI {
  activeKeys: string[];
  modifiers: ModifierKeyState;
}
```

---

## Runtime Events

```text
keyboard.started
keyboard.shortcut.detected
keyboard.text.started
keyboard.text.ended
keyboard.key.held
keyboard.stopped
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Keyboard APIs expose metadata only—not rendered overlays.

---

# 7.10 Acceptance Principles

## Keyboard Capture Tests

* KeyDown captured correctly.
* KeyUp captured correctly.
* Hold duration calculated.
* Repeat keys compressed.

### Modifier Tests

* Ctrl state tracked.
* Shift state tracked.
* Alt state tracked.
* Cmd normalized on macOS.

### Shortcut Tests

* Ctrl+K detected.
* Ctrl+Shift+P detected.
* Cmd+C normalized.
* Alt+Tab ignored when browser focus lost.

### Input Tests

* Typing sessions grouped.
* Character counts accurate.
* Password fields redacted.
* Code typing supported.

---

# 7.11 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 7.1)

1. Keyboard is a first-class semantic interaction stream.
2. Shortcut events are separate from raw key events.
3. Modifier keys are normalized across operating systems.
4. Text input metadata is privacy-aware by default.
5. Keyboard timeline synchronizes with every recording subsystem.
6. Continuous typing is grouped into semantic input sessions.
7. Sensitive inputs are redacted before storage unless explicitly enabled.
8. Keyboard overlays are rendered after recording.
9. Semantic keyboard metadata powers AI Tutorial Generation, Smart Zoom, and workflow detection.
10. Chapter 7.1 establishes the foundational Keyboard Intelligence Runtime for all interaction-aware editing features.

# 7.21 Keyboard Visualization Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Viewers should understand keyboard actions instantly without looking at the keyboard.**

Professional tutorial videos don't just show keys being pressed—they **teach shortcuts visually**.

TryLipi renders keyboard interactions into beautiful animated overlays inspired by:

* Screen Studio.
* Cursorful.
* Apple Keynote presentations.
* Raycast demos.
* Arc Browser product videos.

Keyboard visualization is completely **timeline-driven** and generated after recording.

---

## Keyboard Rendering Architecture

```text
Keyboard Timeline
        │
Keystroke Renderer
        │
Shortcut Card Engine
        │
Animation Engine
        │
Overlay Compositor
        │
Preview / Export
```

---

## Keyboard Rendering Layers

```text
Keyboard Rendering Engine
│
├── Keycap Layer
├── Shortcut Card Layer
├── Modifier Layer
├── Typing Layer
├── Terminal Layer
├── Accessibility Layer
└── Branding Layer
```

Each layer is independently customizable.

---

## Golden Visualization Principles

1. Keyboard overlays never block important UI.
2. Modifier keys animate independently.
3. Shortcut combinations appear as a grouped card.
4. Typing appears progressively—not instantly.
5. Terminal typing mimics human typing speed.
6. Overlays remain editable after recording.
7. Export rendering matches preview rendering exactly.

---

# 7.22 Keystroke Overlay Rendering Engine

The Keystroke Renderer converts semantic keyboard events into animated visual keycaps.

## Rendering Pipeline

```text
Keyboard Timeline
       │
Key Event Resolver
       │
Overlay Generator
       │
Animation Engine
       │
Compositor
```

---

## Keycap Lifecycle

```text
KEYDOWN
   │
Key Appears
   │
Pressed Animation
   │
Held State
   │
Release Animation
   │
Fade Out
```

---

## Keycap States

| State     | Description          |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| Appearing | Fade + Scale In      |
| Pressed   | Active highlight     |
| Held      | Persistent highlight |
| Released  | Ease Out animation   |
| Expired   | Removed from overlay |

---

## Keycap Metadata

```ts
interface RenderedKeycap {
  key: string;
  pressed: boolean;
  held: boolean;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Overlay Placement Modes

| Mode                 | Usage                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Bottom Center        | Default tutorial layout. |
| Bottom Left          | Coding videos.           |
| Floating Near Cursor | Advanced mode.           |
| Custom Position      | Creator-defined layout.  |

---

## Animation Timing

| Animation    | Duration   |
| ------------ | ---------- |
| Fade In      | 120 ms     |
| Press Bounce | 80 ms      |
| Hold Glow    | Continuous |
| Fade Out     | 180 ms     |

---

## Engineering Rules

Each active keycap is rendered independently and synchronized with the keyboard timeline.

---

4. IDE workflows receive specialized semantic overlays.
5. Terminal typing uses dedicated rendering behavior.
6. Overlay layout engine prevents collisions with other visual layers.
7. Themes are reusable rendering presets.
8. Preview and export rendering are pixel-identical.
9. Keyboard overlays remain editable until final export.

# 7.31 AI Workflow Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

A tutorial is not a random sequence of keys.

It is a **workflow**.

Example:

```text
Ctrl + Shift + P
↓
Search "Git Clone"
↓
Enter
↓
Paste Repository URL
↓
Enter
```

This is one workflow called **Clone Git Repository**.

TryLipi detects workflows automatically from keyboard, cursor, viewport, OCR and DOM metadata.

---

## Workflow Intelligence Pipeline

```text
Keyboard Timeline
       │
Cursor Timeline
       │
Viewport Timeline
       │
Application Context
       │
Workflow Detector
       │
Semantic Workflow Timeline
```

---

## Why Workflow Intelligence Exists

Instead of showing:

* Ctrl+K
* Type "settings"
* Enter

AI understands:

> "Creator opened Search Settings."

This powers:

* AI Chapters.
* Auto Captions.
* Tutorial Summary.
* Step Generation.
* Smart Zoom.

---

## Golden Workflow Principles

1. Workflows consist of multiple interactions.
2. Keyboard alone is insufficient.
3. Cursor context improves confidence.
4. Application context changes shortcut meaning.
5. Workflow events remain editable.
6. AI never replaces raw timeline metadata.
7. Every workflow references the global recording timeline.

---

# 7.37 Keyboard Performance Optimization Runtime

Keyboard visualization should be extremely lightweight.

## Optimization Pipeline

```text
Keyboard Timeline
      │
Overlay Optimizer
      │
Renderer
```

---

## Optimization Strategies

| Strategy                   | Benefit                     |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Overlay Pooling            | Reuse keycap objects.       |
| Animation Cache            | Lower layout recalculation. |
| Shortcut Card Cache        | Reuse combinations.         |
| Typing Session Compression | Fewer render updates.       |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric                      | Target           |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Key Overlay Render          | Under 0.5 ms     |
| Shortcut Card Render        | Under 0.8 ms     |
| Typing Animation Update     | Under 1 ms       |
| Total Keyboard Overlay Cost | Under 2 ms/frame |

---

## Adaptive Rendering

When preview FPS drops:

1. Reduce shadow blur.
2. Disable key glow.
3. Reduce animation oversampling.
4. Keep shortcut timing unchanged.

---

## Engineering Rules

Optimization affects visuals only—not semantic timeline accuracy.

# 8.01 Smart Zoom Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The camera should know where the viewer should look before the viewer realizes it.**

Smart Zoom is the defining feature of premium tutorial videos.

Instead of creators manually adding zoom keyframes, TryLipi automatically understands:

* What the creator clicked.
* What the creator hovered.
* What UI element is important.
* What keyboard shortcut triggered a workflow.
* Where attention should move next.

Smart Zoom transforms a static screen recording into a **cinematic, AI-directed experience**.

---

## Smart Zoom Vision

Traditional screen recordings capture an entire desktop.

TryLipi captures attention.

### Traditional Recording

```text id="lr7mmc"
Entire Screen
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│                              │
│  Everything equally visible   │
│                              │
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

### TryLipi Smart Zoom

```text id="bsgnpt"
Entire Screen
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│                              │
│        🔍 Focus Region        │
│                              │
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

The viewer's attention follows AI-generated camera movement.

---

## What Smart Zoom Understands

| Signal            | Zoom Usage                 |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| Cursor Hover      | Candidate focus region.    |
| Cursor Click      | Primary zoom trigger.      |
| Drag Interaction  | Follow cursor path.        |
| Keyboard Shortcut | Zoom workflow destination. |
| DOM Element       | Semantic zoom target.      |
| OCR Text Region   | Zoom important text.       |
| AI Workflow Event | Zoom entire interaction.   |

---

## Golden Smart Zoom Principles

1. Zoom is metadata—not pixels.
2. Zoom never changes source recording.
3. Camera movement is generated after recording.
4. Zoom targets are semantic objects.
5. Cursor and DOM jointly determine focus.
6. Zoom is timeline-driven.
7. Every zoom is editable.

---

| Click            | Immediate zoom. |
| Hover            | Delayed zoom.   |
| Workflow Event   | Section zoom.   |
| OCR Heading      | Title emphasis. |
| DOM Focus        | Element zoom.   |
| AI Tutorial Step | Chapter zoom.   |

---

## Trigger States

```text id="ey6h5t"
IDLE
 │
CANDIDATE
 │
CONFIRMED
 │
ZOOM ACTIVE
 │
RELEASE
```

---

## Trigger Confidence

```ts id="p24j6i"
interface ZoomTrigger {
  triggerType: ZoomTriggerType;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## AI Delay Strategy

| Interaction | Delay                           |
| ----------- | ------------------------------- |
| Click       | 80–120 ms                       |
| Hover       | 300–600 ms                      |
| Workflow    | Immediate after workflow starts |
| OCR         | Adaptive                        |

---

## Engineering Rules

AI triggers produce timeline events—not rendered animations.

---

# 8.07 Zoom Timeline Architecture

| Zoom Started  | Begin camera movement. |
| Zoom Updated  | Target changed.        |
| Zoom Held     | Maintain framing.      |
| Zoom Released | Return camera.         |

```text id="hdtz5a"
5.0s Zoom Start
5.3s Ease In
6.8s Hold
7.4s Ease Out
```

```ts id="i65w5t"
interface ZoomTimelineEvent {

```

---

## Timeline Synchronization

Zoom aligns with:

* Cursor.
* Keyboard.
* Audio.
* DOM.
* Camera Motion.

---

## Engineering Rules

Zoom Timeline is immutable after recording generation.

## Engineering Rules

# 8.10 Acceptance Principles

## Focus Detection Tests

* Click creates focus region.
* Hover creates delayed focus.
* DOM elements generate semantic focus.

### Cursor Zoom Tests

* Click zoom synchronized.
* Hover zoom delayed correctly.
* Drag zoom follows cursor.

### DOM Zoom Tests

* Buttons zoom precisely.
* Inputs zoom correctly.
* Hidden DOM ignored.

### Timeline Tests

* Zoom timeline synchronized.
* Zoom release generated.
* Multiple zooms do not overlap incorrectly.

---

# 8.11 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 8.1)

1. Smart Zoom is an AI-generated camera system—not a pixel crop.
2. Focus Regions are the canonical zoom targets.
3. Cursor behavior is the primary Smart Zoom signal.
4. DOM metadata overrides cursor metadata when available.
5. AI Zoom Triggers create semantic zoom events.
6. Zoom Timeline is independent from screen recording.
7. Zoom metadata is resolution-independent and editable.
8. Editor overrides never modify original AI events.
9. Smart Zoom synchronizes with cursor, keyboard, DOM, OCR and workflow timelines.
10. Chapter 8.1 establishes the foundational AI Smart Zoom Engine that powers cinematic tutorial recordings in TryLipi.

# 8.21 AI Zoom Heuristics Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Not every interaction deserves a zoom. AI must decide what actually matters.**

The Heuristics Engine evaluates every interaction and decides whether it is worthy of camera attention.

Instead of blindly zooming every click, TryLipi evaluates:

* Cursor behavior.
* Hover duration.
* Keyboard shortcuts.
* DOM importance.
* OCR importance.
* Workflow importance.
* Previous zoom history.

---

## Heuristic Decision Pipeline

```text
Interaction Timeline
        │
Feature Extraction
        │
Heuristic Engine
        │
Importance Score
        │
Zoom Decision
```

---

## Signals Evaluated

| Signal            | Importance |
| ----------------- | ---------- |
| Click Event       | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐      |
| Hover Duration    | ⭐⭐⭐⭐       |
| Keyboard Shortcut | ⭐⭐⭐⭐       |
| DOM Role          | ⭐⭐⭐⭐       |
| OCR Heading       | ⭐⭐⭐        |
| Cursor Velocity   | ⭐⭐         |
| Scroll Event      | ⭐⭐         |
| Idle After Hover  | ⭐⭐⭐        |

---

## Importance Scoring Model

```text
Interaction
      │
Attention Score
      │
Zoom Candidate
      │
Zoom Trigger / Ignore
```

---

## Example Decisions

| Interaction              | Zoom?           |
| ------------------------ | --------------- |
| Click "Publish"          | ✅ Strong Zoom   |
| Hover Pricing Card       | ✅ Medium Zoom   |
| Rapid Cursor Movement    | ❌ Ignore        |
| Scroll Through Feed      | ❌ Ignore        |
| Ctrl + Shift + P         | ✅ Workflow Zoom |
| Hover Tiny Icon for 80ms | ❌ Ignore        |

---

## Engineering Rules

The Heuristics Engine creates zoom candidates, not camera animations.

---

# 8.22 OCR-Aware Zoom Engine

OCR allows Smart Zoom outside browser tabs.

## Why OCR Matters

Desktop applications like:

* VS Code
* Cursor IDE
* Figma
* Photoshop
* PowerPoint

have no DOM.

OCR becomes the semantic layer.

---

## OCR Zoom Pipeline

```text
Screen Frames
      │
OCR Engine
      │
Text Regions
      │
Importance Detector
      │
Focus Region Generator
```

---

## OCR Region Types

| Region          | Zoom Usage            |
| --------------- | --------------------- |
| Heading         | Large emphasis zoom.  |
| Button Label    | Action zoom.          |
| Price           | Marketing emphasis.   |
| Error Message   | Tutorial explanation. |
| Terminal Output | Command output zoom.  |
| AI Response     | Reading zoom.         |

---

## OCR Metadata

```ts
interface OCRFocusRegion {
  text: string;
  confidence: number;
  bounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

## OCR Attention Rules

| Text Pattern    | Zoom Behavior          |
| --------------- | ---------------------- |
| Large Heading   | Focus immediately.     |
| Success Message | Hold zoom briefly.     |
| Error Banner    | Strong emphasis zoom.  |
| Version Number  | Small contextual zoom. |

---

## OCR Reading Zoom

Reading mode creates a slightly wider framing around paragraphs instead of individual words.

---

## Engineering Rules

OCR regions become Focus Regions with semantic text metadata attached.

```text
Workflow Active
```

# 8.24 Adaptive Zoom Strength Engine

Zoom amount depends on context.

## Adaptive Zoom Philosophy

A tiny checkbox shouldn't receive the same zoom as an entire pricing card.

---

## Zoom Strength Pipeline

```text
Focus Region
      │
Region Analyzer
      │
Context Analyzer
      │
Zoom Strength Calculator
```

---

## Zoom Strength Levels

| Level | Usage              |
| ----- | ------------------ |
| 1.0x  | No zoom            |
| 1.2x  | Gentle emphasis    |
| 1.4x  | UI interaction     |
| 1.6x  | Button/Form focus  |
| 2.0x  | Tiny UI target     |
| 2.5x  | OCR text emphasis  |
| 3.0x  | Accessibility mode |

---

## Adaptive Inputs

| Input             | Effect                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Region Size       | Smaller region → larger zoom.             |
| Cursor Confidence | Higher confidence → stronger zoom.        |
| OCR Importance    | Headings receive moderate zoom.           |
| DOM Role          | CTA buttons receive stronger zoom.        |
| Workflow Context  | Larger workflow regions use smaller zoom. |

---

## Zoom Strength Interface

```ts
interface ZoomStrength {
  scale: number;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Accessibility Scaling

Accessibility mode increases zoom strength globally while preserving camera composition.

---

## Engineering Rules

Zoom strength is calculated independently from easing and animation.

---

# 8.25 Viewport-Aware Zoom Runtime

Browser tabs have viewport metadata.

Smart Zoom uses it to maintain framing consistency.

## Viewport Zoom Pipeline

```text
Viewport Timeline
      │
Viewport Analyzer
      │
Zoom Region Adjuster
      │
Camera Renderer
```

---

## Viewport Signals

| Signal             | Usage                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Browser Zoom Level | Coordinate normalization. |
| Scroll Position    | Camera offset.            |
| Viewport Size      | Zoom bounds.              |
| DPR                | Scaling correction.       |
| Browser Resize     | Recalculate framing.      |

---

## Scroll-Aware Zoom

```text
Scroll
 │
Viewport Updated
 │
Camera Offset Updated
 │
Zoom Maintained
```

The camera follows scrolling content without jitter.

---

## Browser Resize Handling

When viewport changes:

* Preserve target element.
* Recalculate normalized coordinates.
* Animate framing correction.

---

## Viewport Interface

```ts
interface ViewportZoomContext {
  viewportWidth: number;
  viewportHeight: number;
  scrollOffsetY: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Viewport changes modify camera framing—not focus region identity.

# 8.26 Multi-Target Camera Engine

Sometimes multiple UI elements matter simultaneously.

## Multi-Target Philosophy

Example:

Compare pricing plans.

Cursor moves between two cards.

Camera should frame both.

---

## Multi-Target Pipeline

```text
Focus Region A
Focus Region B
Focus Region C
       │
Region Grouper
       │
Camera Framing Generator
```

---

## Multi-Target Strategies

| Strategy        | Usage                         |
| --------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Bounding Zoom   | Fit all regions.              |
| Sequential Zoom | Zoom one after another.       |
| Split Attention | Alternate focus smoothly.     |
| Comparison Mode | Maintain two targets visible. |

---

## Bounding Box Strategy

```text
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ Region A         Region B│
│                          │
│    Camera Fits Both      │
└──────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Multi-Target Metadata

```ts
interface MultiTargetZoom {

  framingBounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

* Pricing comparison.
* Before/after UI.
* Multiple charts.
* Two editors side-by-side.

---

## Engineering Rules

Multi-target framing preserves all important regions inside safe margins.

# 8.27 Zoom Priority Resolution Engine

Multiple zoom candidates may overlap.

A priority engine resolves conflicts.

## Resolution Pipeline

```text
Zoom Candidates
      │
Priority Engine
      │
Winning Zoom
      │
Zoom Timeline
```

---

## Priority Sources

| Source           | Priority |
| ---------------- | -------- |
| Manual Zoom      | Highest  |
| AI Workflow Zoom | High     |
| DOM Focus Zoom   | High     |
| Click Zoom       | Medium   |
| Hover Zoom       | Medium   |
| OCR Zoom         | Low      |
| Prediction Zoom  | Lowest   |

---

## Conflict Example

```text
Hover Button
Click Button
DOM Button
```

Priority Engine chooses DOM + Click combined zoom.

---

## Priority Rules

1. Manual overrides AI.
2. Workflow overrides isolated clicks.
3. DOM overrides cursor-only focus.
4. OCR supplements existing focus.

---

## Resolution Metadata

```ts
interface ZoomPriorityDecision {
  selectedZoomId: string;
  ignoredZoomIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Ignored zoom candidates remain stored for editor inspection.

---

| ------------------ | ------ |

| Hover Duration     | High   |

Example:

```text
Score: 0.94

Reasons:
```

## Engineering Rules

Confidence scores are stored alongside every AI-generated zoom event.

# 8.31 Cinematic Camera Rendering Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Smart Zoom is not cropping. It is virtual cinematography.**

Every zoom generated by TryLipi behaves like a professional camera operator.

Instead of instantly enlarging a UI element, the camera:

* Anticipates movement.
* Accelerates smoothly.
* Settles naturally.
* Holds attention.
* Returns gracefully.

The goal is to make software tutorials feel like product launch videos from Apple, Linear, Arc Browser and Screen Studio.

---

## Camera Rendering Pipeline

```text
Zoom Timeline
     │
Camera Timeline
     │
Camera Path Generator
     │
Easing Engine
     │
Frame Compositor
     │
Preview / Export
```

---

## Rendering Responsibilities

| Module              | Responsibility                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Camera Renderer     | Render virtual camera transform. |
| Framing Engine      | Maintain subject visibility.     |
| Easing Engine       | Natural zoom transitions.        |
| Motion Interpolator | Smooth camera path.              |
| Composition Engine  | Safe margins and balance.        |
| Export Renderer     | Pixel-identical final output.    |

---

## Camera Coordinate Model

Every rendered frame is computed from:

```text
Virtual Camera
│
├── Center Position (X,Y)
├── Zoom Scale
├── Rotation (Future)
├── Safe Margin
└── Aspect Ratio
```

No pixels are modified until export rendering.

---

## Golden Camera Principles

1. Camera movement is timeline-driven.
2. Zoom scale and position animate independently.
3. Camera never jumps unless manually configured.
4. Motion is resolution-independent.
5. Preview and export use identical camera math.
6. Camera always preserves focus region visibility.
7. AI-generated paths remain editable.

---

# 8.32 Camera Path Generation Engine

The Camera Path Engine converts focus regions into cinematic movement.

## Camera Path Pipeline

```text
Focus Region Timeline
        │
Target Position Generator
        │
Path Planner
        │
Camera Keyframes
        │
Interpolated Camera Path
```

---

## Camera Keyframe Model

| Keyframe | Purpose                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------ |
| Start    | Current camera position.       |
| Target   | Focus region center.           |
| Hold     | Maintain framing.              |
| Exit     | Return or move to next target. |

---

## Example Camera Path

```text
Screen Center
      │
      ▼
Button Focus
      │
      ▼
Sidebar Focus
      │
      ▼
Return Wide View
```

---

## Camera Path Interface

```ts
interface CameraKeyframe {
  timestampUs: number;
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
  zoomScale: number;
}
```

---

## Path Planning Rules

* Never cut through UI unexpectedly.
* Maintain continuous motion.
* Shortest visually pleasing path.
* Respect camera velocity limits.

---

## Path Types

| Path            | Usage                          |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Direct Path     | Single interaction.            |
| Curved Path     | Long cursor movement.          |
| Sequential Path | Multiple workflow steps.       |
| Comparison Path | Alternate between two regions. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera paths are generated before easing is applied.

---

# 8.33 Zoom Animation & Easing Engine

This engine makes camera motion feel premium.

## Easing Pipeline

```text
Camera Keyframes
       │
Animation Engine
       │
Easing Curve
       │
Rendered Camera Motion
```

---

## Zoom Animation Lifecycle

```text
Candidate
   │
Ease In
   │
Acceleration
   │
Hold
   │
Ease Out
```

---

## Supported Easing Curves

| Curve             | Usage                       |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| Linear            | Debug mode.                 |
| Ease Out Cubic    | Default tutorial zoom.      |
| Ease In Out Quint | Long transitions.           |
| Ease Out Expo     | Fast CTA zoom.              |
| Spring            | Interactive hover emphasis. |
| Elastic           | Optional creator effect.    |

---

## Animation Timing Presets

| Preset     | Duration |
| ---------- | -------- |
| Instant    | 120 ms   |
| Fast       | 220 ms   |
| Standard   | 320 ms   |
| Cinematic  | 450 ms   |
| Slow Focus | 700 ms   |

---

## Zoom Hold Strategy

The hold duration depends on interaction context.

| Interaction | Hold                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------- |
| Click       | 300–500 ms              |
| Hover       | Hover duration + buffer |
| Reading     | Dynamic                 |
| Workflow    | Entire workflow segment |

---

## Engineering Rules

Easing modifies camera motion only—not zoom metadata timestamps.

---

# 8.34 Motion Interpolation & Camera Smoothing

Raw focus changes create jitter.

The Motion Interpolator removes it.

## Smoothing Pipeline

```text
Camera Keyframes
       │
Interpolator
       │
Bezier Curve
       │
Smoothed Camera Frames
```

---

## Interpolation Strategies

| Strategy        | Usage                 |
| --------------- | --------------------- |
| Linear          | Debug mode.           |
| Cubic Bezier    | Default.              |
| Catmull-Rom     | Long paths.           |
| Velocity-Aware  | Cursor following.     |
| Adaptive Spline | Workflow transitions. |

---

## Jitter Removal

Small cursor oscillations should not create camera movement.

### Threshold Example

```text
Cursor Wiggle
⬅➡⬅➡⬅➡

Camera
────────────
No Movement
```

---

## Camera Dead Zone

A configurable dead zone ignores tiny movements around the current focus.

| Dead Zone Radius | Behavior               |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| 0 px             | Follow everything.     |
| 12 px            | Ignore micro movement. |
| 20 px            | Reading stability.     |
| Dynamic          | AI-controlled.         |

---

## Motion Interpolation Interface

```ts
interface CameraInterpolation {
  smoothingRadius: number;
  deadZoneRadius: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera smoothing never changes focus region identity.

---

# 8.35 Safe Framing & Composition Engine

The camera should never crop important UI.

## Composition Pipeline

```text
Focus Region
      │
Safe Area Calculator
      │
Composition Engine
      │
Camera Target
```

---

## Safe Margin Philosophy

Every focus region receives padding.

```text
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│         Safe Margin           │
│  ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│  │      Focus Region       │  │
│  └────────────────────────┘  │
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Composition Rules

| Rule               | Purpose                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| Minimum Padding    | Avoid tight crops.           |
| Maximum Zoom       | Prevent over-zoom.           |
| Edge Protection    | Keep target inside viewport. |
| Overlay Protection | Avoid webcam/captions.       |

---

## Aspect Ratio Awareness

| Export | Behavior                 |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| 16:9   | Wide framing.            |
| 9:16   | Vertical reframing.      |
| 1:1    | Center-balanced framing. |
| 4:5    | Social media framing.    |

---

## Composition Metadata

```ts
interface CameraComposition {
  paddingPx: number;
  aspectRatio: string;
}
```

---

## Accessibility Composition

Accessibility mode increases margins around text-heavy regions.

---

## Engineering Rules

Composition adjustments happen after zoom strength calculation.

---

# 8.36 Export Rendering Pipeline

Preview and export must be identical.

## Export Pipeline

```text
Smart Zoom Timeline
        │
Camera Renderer
        │
Frame Crop Generator
        │
GPU Compositor
        │
Video Encoder
```

---

## Rendering Stages

| Stage               | Responsibility     |
| ------------------- | ------------------ |
| Camera Transform    | Virtual viewport.  |
| Cursor Rendering    | Cursor layer.      |
| Spotlight Rendering | Spotlight layer.   |
| Overlay Rendering   | Keyboard/captions. |
| Final Composite     | Export frame.      |

---

## Export Determinism

Given identical metadata:

* Preview frame N.
* Export frame N.

Must be pixel-identical.

---

## Resolution Independence

The same metadata renders correctly to:

| Resolution  | Supported |
| ----------- | --------- |
| 720p        | ✅         |
| 1080p       | ✅         |
| 1440p       | ✅         |
| 4K          | ✅         |
| 8K (Future) | Planned   |

---

## Export Interface

```ts
interface SmartZoomRenderJob {
  exportResolution: ExportResolution;
  zoomTimeline: ZoomTimelineEvent[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Export renderer consumes semantic metadata only.

## Diagnostics Interface


# 8.38 Performance Optimization Runtime

Smart Zoom must remain smooth even in 4K recordings.

## Optimization Pipeline

```text
Zoom Timeline
      │
Optimization Engine
      │
Camera Renderer
```

---

## Optimization Strategies

| Strategy             | Benefit              |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Keyframe Caching     | Faster rendering.    |
| Path Caching         | Reuse interpolation. |
| Focus Region Cache   | Avoid recomputation. |
| GPU Camera Transform | Low CPU usage.       |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric                | Target             |
| --------------------- | ------------------ |
| Camera Transform      | Under 1 ms/frame   |
| Zoom Interpolation    | Under 0.5 ms/frame |
| Focus Lookup          | Under 0.2 ms/frame |
| Total Smart Zoom Cost | Under 2 ms/frame   |

---

## Adaptive Rendering

When preview FPS drops:

1. Reduce interpolation density.
2. Lower blur quality.
3. Cache camera paths.
4. Preserve camera timing.

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance optimization never changes camera timing or focus region selection.

# 9.01 Camera Panning Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Smart Zoom decides the camera's lens. Camera Panning decides the camera's movement.**

A professional tutorial does not keep the zoom fixed.

The camera smoothly follows the creator's interaction across the screen, creating the feeling that an invisible camera operator is filming the workflow in real time.

TryLipi's Camera Panning Engine generates this motion automatically.

---

## Smart Zoom vs Camera Panning

| Smart Zoom                           | Camera Panning                               |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| Controls zoom level.                 | Controls camera position.                    |
| Decides how close to zoom.           | Decides where the camera moves.              |
| Focuses attention.                   | Maintains attention while interaction moves. |
| Triggered by important interactions. | Continuously follows important interactions. |

---

## Virtual Camera Philosophy

The recorded screen is treated as a large virtual stage.

The camera moves across that stage.

```text
Virtual Screen Canvas
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                            │
│     Cursor moves here  →   Camera follows  │
│                                            │
│   UI Panel A         UI Panel B            │
│                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Nothing inside the recording changes.

Only the virtual camera viewport changes.

---

## Responsibilities of Camera Panning Engine

| Module               | Responsibility                                  |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Camera Runtime       | Maintain virtual camera state.                  |
| Cursor Follow Engine | Follow cursor intelligently.                    |
| Focus Tracker        | Lock camera to important UI.                    |
| Path Generator       | Generate cinematic movement.                    |
| Timeline Engine      | Store camera motion metadata.                   |
| Renderer             | Render camera transforms during preview/export. |

---

## Golden Camera Principles

1. Camera movement is independent from Smart Zoom.
2. Camera always moves smoothly.
3. Camera never follows every cursor pixel.
4. Camera movement is timeline-driven.
5. Camera can follow cursor, DOM or workflow focus.
6. Camera metadata is resolution-independent.
7. Every camera movement remains editable.

---

# 9.02 Virtual Camera Runtime Architecture

The Camera Runtime owns the virtual camera state throughout the recording.

## Runtime Architecture

```text
Cursor Timeline
Focus Timeline
Zoom Timeline
Workflow Timeline
        │
Virtual Camera Runtime
        │
Camera Timeline
        │
Renderer
```

---

## Camera Runtime Layers

```text
Virtual Camera Runtime
│
├── Camera Position
├── Camera Velocity
├── Camera Target
├── Camera Zoom
├── Camera Constraints
└── Camera State
```

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime            | Responsibility         |
| ------------------ | ---------------------- |
| Position Runtime   | Current camera center. |
| Target Runtime     | Desired destination.   |
| Motion Runtime     | Camera velocity.       |
| Constraint Runtime | Clamp camera movement. |
| Timeline Runtime   | Record camera states.  |

---

## Virtual Camera State

```ts
interface VirtualCameraState {
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
  zoomScale: number;
  velocityX: number;
  velocityY: number;
}
```

---

## Camera Coordinate Space

Everything uses normalized coordinates.

```text
0.0 ─────────────────────────► 1.0
```

Works across:

* 720p
* 1080p
* 1440p
* 4K
* Vertical exports

---

## Camera Lifecycle

```text
IDLE
 │
FOLLOW TARGET
 │
TRACK TARGET
 │
HOLD
 │
TRANSITION
 │
RETURN
```

---

## Engineering Rules

The Camera Runtime is the single source of truth for virtual camera position.

---

# 9.03 Cursor Follow Engine

Cursor following is the heart of Camera Panning.

## Cursor Follow Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
      │
Motion Analyzer
      │
Follow Decision Engine
      │
Camera Target
      │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Why Not Follow Every Cursor Movement?

If the camera mirrored every cursor movement, tutorials would become nauseating.

Instead, the engine filters cursor motion.

---

## Cursor Follow Stages

| Stage                | Behavior               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Cursor Starts Moving | Observe velocity.      |
| Stable Direction     | Begin camera movement. |
| Cursor Stops         | Ease into hold state.  |
| Tiny Cursor Wiggle   | Ignore.                |

---

## Cursor Follow State Machine

```text
WAITING
   │
TRACKING
   │
FOLLOWING
   │
HOLDING
   │
WAITING
```

---

## Follow Modes

| Mode             | Usage                         |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Soft Follow      | Slow cursor following.        |
| Teaching Follow  | Cursor centered gently.       |
| Cinematic Follow | Delayed smooth camera motion. |
| Locked Follow    | Cursor always centered.       |
| Disabled         | Static framing.               |

---

## Cursor Follow Metadata

```ts
interface CursorFollowEvent {
  cursorEventId: string;
  followMode: CursorFollowMode;
  followStrength: number;
}
```

---

## Cursor Velocity Threshold

| Cursor Speed     | Camera Behavior                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Idle             | Hold camera.                         |
| Slow Movement    | Begin soft follow.                   |
| Medium           | Smooth follow.                       |
| Fast Flick       | Delay follow.                        |
| Rapid Navigation | Ignore until destination stabilizes. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera follows cursor intent—not cursor pixels.

---

# 9.04 Focus Tracking Engine

The Focus Tracker locks the camera onto important regions.

## Focus Tracking Pipeline

```text
Focus Regions
      │
Tracking Engine
      │
Camera Lock Target
      │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Tracking Targets

| Target Type     | Example                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------- |
| Cursor Target   | Cursor hover.             |
| DOM Target      | Button/Input.             |
| OCR Target      | Heading/Text block.       |
| Workflow Target | Sidebar, Modal, Terminal. |
| Manual Target   | User-created focus.       |

---

## Focus Lock Lifecycle

```text
FOCUS CREATED
     │
CAMERA LOCKS
     │
FOLLOW TARGET
     │
TARGET LOST
     │
RELEASE
```

---

## Lock Strength

| Lock Type     | Usage                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Soft Lock     | Cursor may drift slightly.    |
| Strong Lock   | Camera stays fixed on region. |
| Workflow Lock | Entire workflow duration.     |
| Manual Lock   | Editor override.              |

---

## Focus Tracking Interface

```ts
interface CameraFocusLock {
  focusRegionId: string;
  lockStrength: number;
  durationMs: number;
}
```

---

## Dynamic Focus Updates

If a DOM element moves during scrolling:

* Camera keeps following.
* Focus region updates.
* No visual jump.

---

## Engineering Rules

Focus tracking references Focus Region IDs instead of raw coordinates whenever possible.

---
