Camera movement becomes its own editable timeline.

## Timeline Structure

```text
Timeline
│
├── Screen Track
├── Cursor Track
├── Zoom Track
├── Camera Track
├── Keyboard Track
└── DOM Track
```

---

## Camera Timeline Events

| Event                 | Description        |
| --------------------- | ------------------ |
| Camera Move Started   | Transition begins. |
| Camera Target Updated | New destination.   |
| Camera Hold Started   | Hold framing.      |
| Camera Released       | Transition out.    |

---

## Timeline Example

```text
5.0s Camera Start
5.3s Move Right
6.1s Hold
7.0s Move Down
8.2s Hold
```

---

## Camera Timeline Interface

```ts
interface CameraTimelineEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
}
```

---

## Timeline Synchronization

Camera aligns with:

* Smart Zoom timeline.
* Cursor timeline.
* Keyboard timeline.
* Audio timeline.
* Workflow timeline.

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera Timeline stores only semantic camera transforms.

---

# 9.06 Camera State Machine

The runtime maintains deterministic camera behavior.

## State Machine

```text
IDLE
 │
TARGET ACQUIRED
 │
MOVING
 │
TRACKING
 │
HOLD
 │
RELEASE
 │
RETURN
```

---

## State Definitions

| State           | Description                 |
| --------------- | --------------------------- |
| Idle            | Camera static.              |
| Target Acquired | Focus identified.           |
| Moving          | Camera transitioning.       |
| Tracking        | Following active target.    |
| Hold            | Stable framing.             |
| Release         | Leaving target.             |
| Return          | Returning to wider framing. |

---

## Transition Rules

* New higher-priority target interrupts Hold.
* Manual camera overrides AI.
* Workflow lock prevents interruptions unless manual.

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface CameraStateEvent {
  state: CameraState;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera states are deterministic for identical timeline metadata.

---

# 9.07 Camera Metadata Schema

Camera metadata is stored independently from rendering.

## Metadata Model

```text
Camera Metadata
│
├── Position
├── Target
├── Velocity
├── Zoom Reference
├── State
└── Constraints
```

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface CameraMetadataFrame {
  timestampUs: number;
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
  zoomScale: number;
  state: CameraState;
}
```

---

## Metadata Relationships

| Metadata        | References        |
| --------------- | ----------------- |
| Camera Position | Focus Region      |
| Camera Zoom     | Zoom Timeline     |
| Camera State    | Cursor Timeline   |
| Camera Target   | Workflow Timeline |

---

## Storage Strategy

* Normalized coordinates only.
* Timeline indexed.
* Delta compression.
* Versioned metadata.

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera metadata is immutable after recording generation.

---

---

# 9.09 Acceptance Principles

## Cursor Follow Tests

* Camera ignores tiny cursor wiggles.
* Slow cursor triggers smooth follow.
* Fast flick delays follow.
* Hold begins after cursor stops.

### Focus Tracking Tests

* DOM target lock.
* OCR target lock.
* Workflow target lock.
* Manual override.

### Timeline Tests

* Camera timeline synchronized.
* Multiple targets handled.
* State transitions deterministic.

### Metadata Tests

* Camera metadata normalized.
* Camera state versioned.
* Resolution-independent replay.

---

# 9.10 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 9.1)

1. Camera Panning is a virtual camera movement engine independent of Smart Zoom.
2. Cursor Follow tracks semantic cursor intent instead of raw cursor pixels.
3. Focus Tracking locks the camera onto semantic Focus Regions.
4. Camera Timeline is a first-class timeline track synchronized with all interaction systems.
5. Camera movement is generated using normalized coordinates only.
6. Workflow locks prevent unnecessary camera interruptions.
7. Manual editor locks override AI-generated tracking.
8. Camera metadata is immutable after recording generation.
9. Runtime APIs expose semantic camera transforms only.
10. Chapter 9.1 establishes the foundational Virtual Camera Runtime powering all cinematic movement in TryLipi.

# 9.21 AI Camera Heuristics Engine

## Mission Statement

> **The camera should move only when movement improves comprehension.**

A professional camera operator doesn't follow every interaction.

Instead, the camera asks:

* Is this interaction important?
* Will movement help the viewer?
* Is the interaction already visible?
* Should the camera wait?

The AI Camera Heuristics Engine answers those questions.

---

## Camera Decision Pipeline

```text
Interaction Timeline
        │
Camera Feature Extractor
        │
AI Camera Heuristics
        │
Movement Candidate
        │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Signals Evaluated

| Signal           | Camera Usage             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ |
| Click Importance | Strong movement trigger. |
| Hover Duration   | Candidate tracking.      |
| Cursor Velocity  | Delay or follow.         |
| DOM Importance   | High-priority framing.   |
| Workflow Context | Long camera lock.        |
| OCR Heading      | Reading movement.        |
| Scroll Activity  | Scroll tracking.         |

---

## Camera Importance Score

```text
Interaction
      │
Movement Score
      │
Pan Candidate
      │
Move / Hold
```

---

## Example Decisions

| Interaction                | Camera Decision           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Click tiny button          | Move camera.              |
| Cursor flick across screen | Ignore movement.          |
| Hover pricing section      | Slowly pan.               |
| Open sidebar               | Move left and hold.       |
| Scroll documentation       | Follow viewport smoothly. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Heuristics create camera candidates, not rendered movement.

---

# 9.22 Predictive Camera Motion Engine

The camera anticipates cursor intent before the cursor reaches its destination.

## Why Prediction Matters

Without prediction:

* Cursor reaches button.
* Camera reacts afterward.
* Motion feels late.

With prediction:

* Cursor approaches button.
* Camera begins moving early.
* Motion feels cinematic.

---

## Prediction Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
      │
Velocity Analyzer
      │
Trajectory Predictor
      │
Predicted Camera Target
      │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Prediction Windows

| Window | Usage                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| 50 ms  | Rendering smoothing. |
| 120 ms | Hover anticipation.  |
| 200 ms | Camera preparation.  |
| 300 ms | Workflow prediction. |

---

## Prediction Inputs

* Cursor velocity.
* Cursor acceleration.
* Previous trajectory.
* Hover history.
* DOM destination.
* Workflow context.

---

## Prediction Metadata

```ts
interface CameraPrediction {
  predictedCenterX: number;
  predictedCenterY: number;
  predictionConfidence: number;
}
```

---

## Prediction Strategies

| Strategy                   | Usage              |
| -------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Velocity Prediction        | Cursor following.  |
| DOM Destination Prediction | Button click.      |
| Workflow Prediction        | Sidebar opening.   |
| Scroll Prediction          | Reading documents. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Predicted camera paths never overwrite recorded interaction metadata.

---

# 9.23 Multi-Target Camera Panning Engine

Many tutorials involve multiple important UI elements simultaneously.

## Multi-Target Pipeline

```text
Focus Region A
Focus Region B
Focus Region C
       │
Grouping Engine
       │
Camera Framing Planner
       │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Multi-Target Modes

| Mode             | Usage                   |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| Comparison Mode  | Pricing cards.          |
| Sequential Mode  | Multi-step workflow.    |
| Bounding Mode    | Fit multiple regions.   |
| Guided Tour Mode | Visit regions in order. |

---

## Comparison Camera Example

```text
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ Sidebar       Preview Window  │
│                               │
│  Camera frames both together  │
└───────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Guided Tour Example

```text
Search Bar
    │
Sidebar
    │
Editor
    │
Preview Panel
```

Camera visits each area in sequence.

---

## Multi-Target Metadata

```ts
interface CameraGroupTarget {
  regionIds: string[];
  groupBounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

## AI Uses

* Before/after comparisons.
* Dashboard walkthroughs.
* IDE split editors.
* Analytics dashboards.

---

## Engineering Rules

Bounding regions include safe composition margins before camera framing.

---

# 9.24 Scroll-Aware Camera Runtime

Scrolling is one of the hardest interactions to film smoothly.

## Scroll Camera Philosophy

The camera follows content—not scrolling velocity.

---

## Scroll Pipeline

```text
Scroll Timeline
      │
Viewport Tracker
      │
Scroll Motion Analyzer
      │
Camera Offset Generator
```

---

## Scroll Behaviors

| Scroll Type     | Camera Behavior       |
| --------------- | --------------------- |
| Reading Scroll  | Smooth follow.        |
| Rapid Scroll    | Delay until stop.     |
| Tiny Scroll     | Ignore.               |
| Jump Navigation | Immediate reposition. |

---

## Reading Mode

```text
Document Scroll
     │
Camera Tracks Text Block
     │
Reader Never Loses Context
```

---

## Scroll Anchoring

The camera anchors to semantic content instead of raw pixel offsets whenever possible.

---

## Scroll Metadata

```ts
interface ScrollCameraEvent {
  scrollOffsetY: number;
  cameraOffsetY: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Scroll tracking uses viewport metadata instead of cursor position whenever scrolling is active.

---

# 9.25 Workflow Camera Engine

Long workflows require persistent cinematic framing.

## Workflow Camera Pipeline

```text
Workflow Timeline
      │
Workflow Camera Planner
      │
Camera Lock
      │
Transition Planner
```

---

## Workflow Camera States

| State             | Description           |
| ----------------- | --------------------- |
| Enter Workflow    | Camera transitions.   |
| Workflow Active   | Camera holds context. |
| Interaction Shift | Camera pans locally.  |
| Workflow Exit     | Return or transition. |

---

## Workflow Types

| Workflow           | Camera Strategy             |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| VS Code Editing    | Follow editor panel.        |
| Git Clone          | Follow terminal.            |
| AI Prompting       | Follow prompt + response.   |
| Dashboard Analysis | Follow charts sequentially. |
| Checkout Flow      | Follow payment form.        |

---

## Workflow Metadata

```ts
interface WorkflowCameraLock {
  workflowId: string;
  cameraMode: WorkflowCameraMode;
}
```

---

## Persistent Workflow Framing

Camera avoids unnecessary zoom/pan resets inside one workflow.

---

## Engineering Rules

Workflow locks have higher priority than hover-based camera movement.

---

# 9.26 Viewport Transition Engine

Camera transitions between viewport contexts gracefully.

## Transition Pipeline

```text
Viewport Change
      │
Transition Generator
      │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Transition Types

| Transition              | Example                |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Scroll Transition       | Reading documentation. |
| Modal Transition        | Dialog appears.        |
| Sidebar Transition      | Navigation opens.      |
| Tab Transition          | Browser switches tab.  |
| Split Layout Transition | IDE layout changes.    |

---

## Transition Animation

```text
Old Target
    │
Ease Out
    │
Mid Transition
    │
Ease In
    │
New Target
```

---

## Transition Metadata

```ts
interface ViewportTransition {
  fromRegionId: string;
  toRegionId: string;
  durationMs: number;
}
```

---

## Dynamic Viewport Changes

Supports:

* Browser resize.
* Split pane resize.
* Responsive layouts.
* DevTools open/close.

---

## Engineering Rules

Viewport transitions preserve visual continuity whenever possible.

---

# 9.27 Camera Priority Resolution Engine

Multiple camera requests compete for control.

## Resolution Pipeline

```text
Camera Candidates
      │
Priority Resolver
      │
Winning Camera Target
```

---

## Camera Priority Order

| Priority | Source                 |
| -------- | ---------------------- |
| Highest  | Manual Camera Keyframe |
| High     | Workflow Lock          |
| High     | DOM Focus              |
| Medium   | Click Follow           |
| Medium   | Hover Follow           |
| Low      | OCR Reading            |
| Lowest   | Prediction             |

---

## Conflict Example

```text
Hover Input
Click Button
Workflow Lock
```

Workflow Lock keeps camera stable until completion.

---

## Resolution Metadata

```ts
interface CameraPriorityDecision {
  selectedTargetId: string;
  rejectedTargetIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Rejected camera candidates remain visible inside editor diagnostics.

---

# 9.28 Camera Confidence Model

Every AI camera movement has an explainable confidence score.

## Confidence Pipeline

```text
Interaction Signals
      │
Confidence Calculator
      │
Camera Confidence
```

---

## Confidence Inputs

| Signal            | Weight |
| ----------------- | ------ |
| Workflow Context  | High   |
| Click Confidence  | High   |
| Hover Duration    | High   |
| DOM Confidence    | High   |
| OCR Confidence    | Medium |
| Cursor Prediction | Medium |
| Scroll Context    | Medium |

---

## Confidence Levels

| Score      | Meaning                    |
| ---------- | -------------------------- |
| 0.90–1.00  | Automatic camera move.     |
| 0.75–0.90  | Strong movement candidate. |
| 0.50–0.75  | Gentle follow candidate.   |
| Below 0.50 | Hold camera.               |

---

## Explainability Metadata

```ts
interface CameraConfidence {
  score: number;
  reasons: string[];
}
```

---

## Example Explanation

```text
Camera Confidence: 0.93

Reasons
• Workflow active
• CTA button clicked
• Cursor stabilized
```

Useful for debugging AI camera decisions.

---

## Engineering Rules

Every AI-generated camera movement stores explainability metadata.

---

}

```text
camera.candidate.created
camera.prediction.generated
camera.workflow.locked
camera.priority.resolved
camera.transition.created
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Runtime APIs expose semantic camera metadata—not rendered transforms.

---

# 9.30 Acceptance Principles

## Heuristic Tests

* Important clicks generate movement.
* Tiny cursor wiggles ignored.
* Workflow lock respected.

### Prediction Tests

* Camera anticipates cursor destination.
* Prediction disabled when confidence low.
* DOM prediction preferred over cursor-only prediction.

### Scroll Tests

* Reading scroll smooth.
* Rapid scroll delayed.
* Jump navigation repositioned.

### Workflow Tests

* VS Code workflow lock.
* Terminal workflow lock.
* AI chat workflow lock.

### Multi-Target Tests

* Pricing comparison framed.
* IDE split editor framed.
* Sequential guided tour generated.

---

# 9.31 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 9.2)

1. AI Camera Heuristics decide when camera movement improves comprehension.
2. Predictive Camera Motion anticipates interactions without modifying recorded metadata.
3. Multi-Target Camera Engine frames multiple semantic regions simultaneously.
4. Scroll-Aware Camera follows viewport content instead of raw scroll velocity.
5. Workflow Camera Locks maintain stable framing across long interaction sequences.
6. Viewport Transition Engine preserves continuity across layout changes.
7. Camera Priority Resolution guarantees deterministic movement selection.
8. Camera Confidence Scores make every AI movement explainable.
9. Manual editor camera tracks override AI-generated movement.
10. Chapter 9.2 establishes the AI Context-Aware Camera Motion system powering TryLipi's cinematic software tutorials.

# 9.31 Cinematic Camera Rendering Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The camera should feel like it has physical weight.**

A robotic camera instantly jumps between positions.

A cinematic camera behaves like a stabilized handheld gimbal:

* Smooth acceleration.
* Momentum.
* Controlled deceleration.
* Natural settling.
* Predictable movement.

This is what makes Screen Studio videos feel expensive.

TryLipi recreates this behavior using a **virtual physics-based camera renderer**.

---

## Rendering Pipeline

```text
Camera Timeline
      │
Motion Renderer
      │
Physics Engine
      │
Composition Engine
      │
Frame Renderer
      │
Preview / Export
```

---

## Camera Rendering Layers

```text
Camera Rendering Engine
│
├── Position Layer
├── Zoom Layer
├── Velocity Layer
├── Rotation Layer (Future)
├── Composition Layer
└── Stabilization Layer
```

Each layer contributes to the final virtual camera transform.

---

## Camera Motion Principles

| Principle            | Purpose                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Smooth Starts        | Prevent abrupt movement. |
| Momentum             | Natural continuation.    |
| Ease Stops           | Comfortable viewing.     |
| Stable Holds         | Prevent drift.           |
| Context Preservation | Never lose important UI. |

---

## Golden Rendering Rules

1. Camera movement is physically simulated.
2. Camera never teleports unless requested.
3. Motion always preserves focus visibility.
4. Camera transforms are resolution-independent.
5. Preview equals export.
6. Camera renderer is deterministic.
7. Physics parameters remain editable.

---

# 9.32 Camera Inertia Engine

The Inertia Engine gives the camera weight and momentum.

## Why Inertia Exists

Without inertia:

```text
Target A
   │
   ▼
Target B
```

The camera snaps.

With inertia:

```text
Target A
   │
Acceleration
   │
Cruise
   │
Deceleration
   │
Target B
```

Movement feels intentional.

---

## Inertia Pipeline

```text
Camera Target
      │
Velocity Generator
      │
Momentum Engine
      │
Camera Position
```

---

## Inertia Components

| Component        | Purpose                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| Initial Velocity | Smooth takeoff.        |
| Momentum         | Continue movement.     |
| Friction         | Slow camera naturally. |
| Deceleration     | Controlled stop.       |

---

## Camera Velocity Graph

```text
Velocity

      /─────────\
_____/           \_____
```

The curve is continuous.

---

## Inertia Metadata

```ts
interface CameraInertia {
  acceleration: number;
  maxVelocity: number;
  friction: number;
}
```

---

## Motion Presets

| Preset    | Feel                      |
| --------- | ------------------------- |
| Instant   | Robotic                   |
| Smooth    | Screen Studio default     |
| Cinematic | Apple keynote style       |
| Floating  | Slow educational mode     |
| Dynamic   | Cursorful-inspired motion |

---

## Engineering Rules

Inertia affects rendered motion only, never timeline timestamps.

---

# 9.33 Spring Physics Motion Engine

Spring physics create premium camera movement.

## Spring Philosophy

Instead of stopping immediately...

The camera gently settles into its destination.

---

## Spring Pipeline

```text
Target Position
      │
Spring Solver
      │
Damped Motion
      │
Camera Position
```

---

## Spring Components

| Parameter | Purpose              |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| Stiffness | Responsiveness.      |
| Damping   | Overshoot reduction. |
| Mass      | Camera weight.       |
| Velocity  | Current motion.      |

---

## Spring Motion Example

```text
Target
  │
Approach
  │
Tiny Overshoot
  │
Settle
```

Overshoot is extremely subtle.

---

## Spring Metadata

```ts
interface CameraSpring {
  stiffness: number;
  damping: number;
  mass: number;
}
```

---

## Spring Presets

| Preset        | Usage            |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| Gentle        | Tutorials        |
| Standard      | Product demos    |
| Tight         | UI walkthroughs  |
| Soft Floating | Education videos |
| Accessibility | Stable movement  |

---

## Engineering Rules

Spring overshoot is disabled near screen edges to avoid cropping.

---

# 9.34 Camera Motion Smoothing & Stabilization Engine

Raw AI targets may still introduce jitter.

This engine removes visual instability.

## Stabilization Pipeline

```text
Camera Targets
      │
Motion Filter
      │
Dead Zone Filter
      │
Trajectory Smoother
      │
Rendered Camera Path
```

---

## Stabilization Layers

| Layer             | Purpose                 |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- |
| Dead Zone         | Ignore tiny movement.   |
| Low-Pass Filter   | Smooth velocity spikes. |
| Curve Smoother    | Bezier interpolation.   |
| Target Stabilizer | Prevent oscillation.    |

---

## Dead Zone Example

```text
Cursor
⬅➡⬅➡⬅➡

Camera
──────────
```

No visible camera movement.

---

## Stabilization Modes

| Mode       | Usage                  |
| ---------- | ---------------------- |
| Static     | Ignore micro movement. |
| Smooth     | Default creator mode.  |
| Cinematic  | Strong smoothing.      |
| Responsive | Faster tracking.       |

---

## Stabilization Metadata

```ts
interface CameraStabilization {
  deadZonePx: number;
  smoothingStrength: number;
}
```

---

## Scroll Stabilization

Reading documents requires stronger smoothing than cursor tutorials.

---

## Engineering Rules

Stabilization preserves semantic camera destinations while smoothing trajectories.

---

# 9.35 Camera Rendering Performance Runtime

Camera rendering must remain smooth in long recordings.

## Performance Pipeline

```text
Camera Timeline
      │
Interpolation Cache
      │
GPU Transform Engine
      │
Preview Renderer
```

---

## Optimization Strategies

| Strategy             | Benefit              |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Camera Path Cache    | Reuse interpolation. |
| GPU Matrix Transform | Low CPU cost.        |
| Focus Region Cache   | Fast lookup.         |
| Motion Segment Cache | Efficient rendering. |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric            | Target             |
| ----------------- | ------------------ |
| Camera Transform  | Under 1 ms/frame   |
| Motion Smoothing  | Under 0.5 ms/frame |
| Path Lookup       | Under 0.2 ms/frame |
| Total Camera Cost | Under 2 ms/frame   |

---

## Adaptive Rendering Strategy

When preview FPS drops:

1. Reduce interpolation density.
2. Cache spring calculations.
3. Lower blur quality.
4. Preserve camera timing.

---

## Memory Strategy

Camera keyframes are delta-compressed for recordings longer than one hour.

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance optimization never changes camera timing or easing curves.

---

# 9.36 Camera Diagnostics & Telemetry Runtime

Developers need visibility into AI camera behavior.

## Diagnostics Architecture

```text
Camera Runtime
      │
Metrics Collector
      │
Developer Dashboard
```

---

## Runtime Metrics

### Camera Metrics

* Active camera transitions.
* Average movement distance.
* Hold duration.
* Transition duration.

### AI Metrics

* Camera candidates generated.
* Candidates rejected.
* Prediction confidence.
* Workflow locks created.

### Rendering Metrics

* Render latency.
* Interpolation latency.
* Stabilization latency.

---

## Diagnostic Events

| Event                          | Description               |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `camera.target.created`        | Focus acquired.           |
| `camera.transition.started`    | Camera movement begins.   |
| `camera.transition.completed`  | Camera settles.           |
| `camera.stabilization.applied` | Smoothing filter applied. |

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface CameraDiagnostics {
  transitionsRendered: number;
  averageRenderLatencyMs: number;
  workflowLocks: number;
}
```

---

## Debug Visualization Mode

Developers can enable overlays showing:

* Camera viewport.
* Focus region.
* Dead zone.
* Velocity vectors.
* Camera path.

Useful during AI tuning.

---

## Engineering Rules

Diagnostics never ship in exported videos.

---

# 9.37 Export Camera Rendering Runtime

Camera rendering becomes part of final video composition.

## Export Pipeline

```text
Camera Timeline
      │
Camera Renderer
      │
Screen Crop Generator
      │
Cursor Renderer
      │
Overlay Renderer
      │
Video Encoder
```

---

## Export Rendering Order

| Layer            | Render Order      |
| ---------------- | ----------------- |
| Screen           | Base layer        |
| Camera Transform | Virtual viewport  |
| Cursor           | Cursor layer      |
| Spotlight        | Cursor spotlight  |
| Keyboard         | Keyboard overlays |
| Captions         | Caption layer     |
| Effects          | Final effects     |

---

## Resolution Independence

Supports identical camera behavior across:

| Resolution    | Status |
| ------------- | ------ |
| 720p          | ✅      |
| 1080p         | ✅      |
| 1440p         | ✅      |
| 4K            | ✅      |
| 9:16 Vertical | ✅      |
| 1:1 Square    | ✅      |

---

## Deterministic Export

Frame `N` in preview equals frame `N` during export.

This guarantees WYSIWYG editing.

---

## Export Metadata

```ts
interface CameraRenderJob {
  resolution: ExportResolution;
  cameraTimeline: CameraTimelineEvent[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Export rendering consumes immutable semantic camera metadata only.

---

```text
Camera Target
      │
Velocity Generator
      │
Momentum Engine
      │
Camera Position
```

---

## Inertia Components

| Component        | Purpose                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| Initial Velocity | Smooth takeoff.        |
| Momentum         | Continue movement.     |
| Friction         | Slow camera naturally. |
| Deceleration     | Controlled stop.       |

---

## Camera Velocity Graph

```text
Velocity

      /─────────\
_____/           \_____
```

The curve is continuous.

---

## Inertia Metadata

```ts
interface CameraInertia {
  acceleration: number;
  maxVelocity: number;
  friction: number;
}
```

---

## Motion Presets

| Preset    | Feel                      |
| --------- | ------------------------- |
| Instant   | Robotic                   |
| Smooth    | Screen Studio default     |
| Cinematic | Apple keynote style       |
| Floating  | Slow educational mode     |
| Dynamic   | Cursorful-inspired motion |

---

## Engineering Rules

Inertia affects rendered motion only, never timeline timestamps.

---

# 9.33 Spring Physics Motion Engine

Spring physics create premium camera movement.

## Spring Philosophy

Instead of stopping immediately...

The camera gently settles into its destination.

---

## Spring Pipeline

```text
Target Position
      │
Spring Solver
      │
Damped Motion
      │
Camera Position
```

---

## Spring Components

| Parameter | Purpose              |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| Stiffness | Responsiveness.      |
| Damping   | Overshoot reduction. |
| Mass      | Camera weight.       |
| Velocity  | Current motion.      |

---

## Spring Motion Example

```text
Target
  │
Approach
  │
Tiny Overshoot
  │
Settle
```

Overshoot is extremely subtle.

---

## Spring Metadata

```ts
interface CameraSpring {
  stiffness: number;
  damping: number;
  mass: number;
}
```

---

## Spring Presets

| Preset        | Usage            |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| Gentle        | Tutorials        |
| Standard      | Product demos    |
| Tight         | UI walkthroughs  |
| Soft Floating | Education videos |
| Accessibility | Stable movement  |

---

## Engineering Rules

Spring overshoot is disabled near screen edges to avoid cropping.

---

# 9.34 Camera Motion Smoothing & Stabilization Engine

Raw AI targets may still introduce jitter.

This engine removes visual instability.

## Stabilization Pipeline

```text
Camera Targets
      │
Motion Filter
      │
Dead Zone Filter
      │
Trajectory Smoother
      │
Rendered Camera Path
```

---

## Stabilization Layers

| Layer             | Purpose                 |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- |
| Dead Zone         | Ignore tiny movement.   |
| Low-Pass Filter   | Smooth velocity spikes. |
| Curve Smoother    | Bezier interpolation.   |
| Target Stabilizer | Prevent oscillation.    |

---

## Dead Zone Example

```text
Cursor
⬅➡⬅➡⬅➡

Camera
──────────
```

No visible camera movement.

---

## Stabilization Modes

| Mode       | Usage                  |
| ---------- | ---------------------- |
| Static     | Ignore micro movement. |
| Smooth     | Default creator mode.  |
| Cinematic  | Strong smoothing.      |
| Responsive | Faster tracking.       |

---

## Stabilization Metadata

```ts
interface CameraStabilization {
  deadZonePx: number;
  smoothingStrength: number;
}
```

---

## Scroll Stabilization

Reading documents requires stronger smoothing than cursor tutorials.

---

## Engineering Rules

Stabilization preserves semantic camera destinations while smoothing trajectories.

---

# 9.35 Camera Rendering Performance Runtime

Camera rendering must remain smooth in long recordings.

## Performance Pipeline

```text
Camera Timeline
      │
Interpolation Cache
      │
GPU Transform Engine
      │
Preview Renderer
```

---

## Optimization Strategies

| Strategy             | Benefit              |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Camera Path Cache    | Reuse interpolation. |
| GPU Matrix Transform | Low CPU cost.        |
| Focus Region Cache   | Fast lookup.         |
| Motion Segment Cache | Efficient rendering. |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric            | Target             |
| ----------------- | ------------------ |
| Camera Transform  | Under 1 ms/frame   |
| Motion Smoothing  | Under 0.5 ms/frame |
| Path Lookup       | Under 0.2 ms/frame |
| Total Camera Cost | Under 2 ms/frame   |

---

## Adaptive Rendering Strategy

When preview FPS drops:

1. Reduce interpolation density.
2. Cache spring calculations.
3. Lower blur quality.
4. Preserve camera timing.

---

## Memory Strategy

Camera keyframes are delta-compressed for recordings longer than one hour.

---

## Engineering Rules

Performance optimization never changes camera timing or easing curves.

---

# 9.36 Camera Diagnostics & Telemetry Runtime

Developers need visibility into AI camera behavior.

## Diagnostics Architecture

```text
Camera Runtime
      │
Metrics Collector
      │
Developer Dashboard
```

---

## Runtime Metrics

### Camera Metrics

* Active camera transitions.
* Average movement distance.
* Hold duration.
* Transition duration.

### AI Metrics

* Camera candidates generated.
* Candidates rejected.
* Prediction confidence.
* Workflow locks created.

### Rendering Metrics

* Render latency.
* Interpolation latency.
* Stabilization latency.

---

## Diagnostic Events

| Event                          | Description               |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `camera.target.created`        | Focus acquired.           |
| `camera.transition.started`    | Camera movement begins.   |
| `camera.transition.completed`  | Camera settles.           |
| `camera.stabilization.applied` | Smoothing filter applied. |

---

## Diagnostics Interface

```ts
interface CameraDiagnostics {
  transitionsRendered: number;
  averageRenderLatencyMs: number;
  workflowLocks: number;
}
```

---

## Debug Visualization Mode

Developers can enable overlays showing:

* Camera viewport.
* Focus region.
* Dead zone.
* Velocity vectors.
* Camera path.

Useful during AI tuning.

---

## Engineering Rules

Diagnostics never ship in exported videos.

---

Camera Renderer

| Keyboard         | Keyboard overlays |

Supports identical camera behavior across:

| Resolution    | Status |
| ------------- | ------ |
| 720p          | ✅      |
| 1080p         | ✅      |
| 1440p         | ✅      |
| 4K            | ✅      |
| 9:16 Vertical | ✅      |
| 1:1 Square    | ✅      |

---

## Deterministic Export

Frame `N` in preview equals frame `N` during export.

This guarantees WYSIWYG editing.

---

## Export Metadata

```ts
interface CameraRenderJob {
  resolution: ExportResolution;
  cameraTimeline: CameraTimelineEvent[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Export rendering consumes immutable semantic camera metadata only.

# 10.01 DOM Tracking Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The browser already knows what every UI element is. TryLipi records that knowledge.**

This chapter is arguably the **largest technical differentiator** between TryLipi and every browser-based screen recorder.

Traditional recorders only capture pixels.

TryLipi captures **semantic UI knowledge**:

* Buttons.
* Inputs.
* Links.
* Cards.
* Menus.
* Dialogs.
* Modals.
* Tooltips.
* Tables.
* Navigation bars.

Every important DOM element becomes an object inside the recording timeline.

---

## Pixels vs DOM Intelligence

### Traditional Browser Recorder

```text
Browser Page
     │
Canvas Pixels
     │
Video
```

Everything is flattened.

---

### TryLipi Browser Recorder

```text
Browser Page
     │
DOM Runtime
     │
Semantic Elements
     │
DOM Timeline
     │
Video + Metadata
```

Now AI knows **what was clicked**, not just **where**.

---

## Why DOM Tracking Is Revolutionary

Without OCR.

Without AI Vision.

Without screenshots.

Browser APIs already expose:

* Element type.
* Accessibility role.
* Bounding box.
* Text.
* State.
* Visibility.
* Parent hierarchy.

TryLipi records these as timeline metadata.

---

## DOM Tracking Responsibilities

| Module               | Responsibility                     |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| DOM Scanner          | Discover elements.                 |
| Element Registry     | Maintain live semantic tree.       |
| Mutation Observer    | Detect DOM changes.                |
| Bounding Box Runtime | Track element geometry.            |
| State Tracker        | Hover, disabled, hidden, selected. |
| Timeline Writer      | Record DOM events.                 |

---

## Golden DOM Principles

1. DOM metadata is independent from pixels.
2. Every tracked element receives a stable semantic ID.
3. Bounding boxes are normalized.
4. DOM changes become timeline events.
5. Hidden elements are versioned, not deleted.
6. AI consumes semantic DOM metadata directly.
7. DOM Tracking works only in Browser Recording Mode.

---

# 10.02 DOM Tracking Runtime Architecture

The DOM Runtime continuously watches the page during recording.

## Runtime Architecture

```text
Browser Document
       │
DOM Scanner
       │
Semantic Registry
       │
Mutation Observer
       │
Bounding Box Runtime
       │
DOM Timeline
```

---

## Runtime Layers

```text
DOM Tracking Runtime
│
├── Scanner Runtime
├── Registry Runtime
├── Mutation Runtime
├── Geometry Runtime
├── State Runtime
└── Timeline Runtime
```

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime          | Purpose                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| Scanner Runtime  | Initial page scan.        |
| Registry Runtime | Semantic element IDs.     |
| Geometry Runtime | Position & size tracking. |
| Mutation Runtime | DOM updates.              |
| Timeline Runtime | Store semantic events.    |

---

## Recording Lifecycle

```text
Page Loaded
     │
Initial DOM Scan
     │
Registry Created
     │
Observe Mutations
     │
Write Timeline Events
     │
Recording Ends
```

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface DOMRuntimeState {
  registryReady: boolean;
  observing: boolean;
  trackedElementCount: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

The DOM Runtime starts immediately after browser recording begins.

---

# 10.03 Live Semantic Element Registry

Every important DOM node becomes a tracked entity.

## Registry Philosophy

Instead of tracking HTML nodes directly...

TryLipi creates immutable semantic IDs.

```text
<button id="save-btn">

↓

dom_btn_000194
```

The semantic ID survives movement and resizing.

---

## Registry Architecture

```text
DOM Node
    │
Element Scanner
    │
Semantic ID Generator
    │
Element Registry
```

---

## Registry Contents

| Metadata           | Stored |
| ------------------ | ------ |
| Semantic ID        | ✅      |
| HTML Tag           | ✅      |
| Accessibility Role | ✅      |
| Bounding Box       | ✅      |
| Parent ID          | ✅      |
| Visibility State   | ✅      |
| Text Snapshot      | ✅      |
| Attributes         | ✅      |

---

## Registry Tree

```text
Page Root
│
├── Header
│   ├── Logo
│   ├── Search Button
│   └── Menu Button
│
├── Sidebar
│
├── Main Content
│
└── Footer
```

Every node receives a semantic identifier.

---

## Registry Interface

```ts
interface DOMElementRecord {
  semanticId: string;
  tagName: string;
  role: string;
  parentId?: string;
}
```

---

## Stable Semantic IDs

IDs never depend on CSS selectors.

Example:

| HTML Changes          | Semantic ID |
| --------------------- | ----------- |
| Class changes         | Same ID     |
| Position changes      | Same ID     |
| Size changes          | Same ID     |
| Parent layout changes | Same ID     |

---

## Engineering Rules

Semantic IDs persist throughout one recording session.

---

# 10.04 Mutation Observer Runtime

Modern web pages constantly change.

TryLipi records those changes.

## Mutation Runtime Pipeline

```text
DOM Changes
     │
Mutation Observer
     │
Mutation Processor
     │
Registry Update
     │
Timeline Event
```

---

## Mutation Types

| Mutation           | Recorded |
| ------------------ | -------- |
| Node Added         | ✅        |
| Node Removed       | ✅        |
| Attribute Changed  | ✅        |
| Text Changed       | ✅        |
| Visibility Changed | ✅        |
| Class Changed      | ✅        |
| Style Changed      | Optional |

---

## Mutation Timeline Example

```text
12.4s Modal Added

13.1s Button Enabled

15.8s Error Message Added

17.0s Modal Removed
```

---

## Mutation Metadata

```ts
interface DOMMutationEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  mutationType: DOMMutationType;
  semanticId: string;
}
```

---

## Intelligent Mutation Filtering

Ignored mutations include:

* Analytics scripts.
* Invisible helper nodes.
* Animation-only wrappers.
* Temporary framework placeholders.

---

## Mutation Priority

| Mutation              | Priority |
| --------------------- | -------- |
| Modal Added           | High     |
| Button Enabled        | High     |
| Tooltip Added         | Medium   |
| Text Counter Updated  | Low      |
| CSS Animation Wrapper | Ignore   |

---

## Engineering Rules

Mutation events update registry versions instead of replacing records.

---

# 10.05 Bounding Box Timeline Engine

DOM geometry changes over time.

TryLipi stores geometry as timeline metadata.

## Geometry Pipeline

```text
Semantic Element
      │
Bounding Box Calculator
      │
Normalized Geometry
      │
Timeline Writer
```

---

## Bounding Box Metadata

| Property | Purpose          |
| -------- | ---------------- |
| X        | Left position    |
| Y        | Top position     |
| Width    | Element width    |
| Height   | Element height   |
| Center   | Camera targeting |
| Rotation | Future support   |

---

## Bounding Box Coordinate Space

```text
Viewport
0,0 ─────────────────────────►

Bounding Box

x,y,width,height
```

All coordinates are normalized.

---

## Geometry Timeline Example

```text
Button

0.0s Position A

4.2s Position B

6.8s Position C
```

Useful for animated layouts.

---

## Geometry Interface

```ts
interface DOMBoundingBox {
  normalizedX: number;
  normalizedY: number;
  normalizedWidth: number;
  normalizedHeight: number;
}
```

---

## Why Bounding Box Timeline Matters

Supports:

* Smart Zoom.
* Camera Panning.
* Spotlight.
* Click Ripples.
* OCR alignment.
* AI Scene Understanding.

---

## Engineering Rules

Bounding Box updates are delta-compressed over time.

---

# 10.06 DOM Element Lifecycle

Every semantic element follows a lifecycle.

## Lifecycle State Machine

```text
DISCOVERED
    │
VISIBLE
    │
UPDATED
    │
HIDDEN
    │
REMOVED
```

---

## Lifecycle States

| State      | Meaning                     |
| ---------- | --------------------------- |
| Discovered | Initial scan found element. |
| Visible    | Currently rendered.         |
| Updated    | Geometry/text changed.      |
| Hidden     | CSS/display hidden.         |
| Removed    | Removed from DOM.           |

---

## Lifecycle Timeline Example

```text
2.1s Button Discovered

2.3s Button Visible

5.2s Button Disabled

7.0s Button Enabled

10.4s Button Removed
```

---

## Lifecycle Interface

```ts
interface DOMLifecycleEvent {
  semanticId: string;
  lifecycleState: DOMLifecycleState;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Hidden vs Removed

Important distinction:

| Hidden           | Removed                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| CSS hidden       | Node deleted               |
| Visibility false | DOM removed                |
| May return       | New lifecycle if recreated |

---

## Engineering Rules

Hidden elements remain addressable until recording ends.

---

# 10.07 DOM Metadata Schema

DOM metadata becomes one of TryLipi's richest timeline datasets.

## Metadata Model

```text
DOM Metadata
│
├── Semantic ID
├── Role
├── Tag
├── Bounding Box Timeline
├── Visibility Timeline
├── Mutation Timeline
├── Parent Hierarchy
└── Text Snapshot
```

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface DOMMetadataFrame {
  semanticId: string;
  timestampUs: number;
  boundingBox: DOMBoundingBox;
  visibility: boolean;
}
```

---

## Metadata Layers

| Layer            | Used By               |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Geometry         | Smart Zoom            |
| Role             | AI Tutorial Generator |
| Text             | Captions              |
| Visibility       | Camera Renderer       |
| Parent Hierarchy | Scene Understanding   |

---

## Compression Strategy

* Static elements stored once.
* Geometry stored as deltas.
* Mutations stored as events.
* Text versioned.

---

## Engineering Rules

Metadata remains resolution-independent and replayable.

---

# 10.08 Runtime DOM APIs

The DOM Runtime exposes APIs for AI and editor systems.

## Runtime APIs

| API                        | Purpose                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `scanDOMTree()`            | Initial semantic scan.   |
| `observeDOMMutations()`    | Start mutation runtime.  |
| `getElementBySemanticId()` | Lookup registry element. |
| `getBoundingBoxTimeline()` | Replay geometry changes. |
| `subscribeDOMEvents()`     | Live semantic events.    |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface DOMRuntimeAPI {
  trackedElements: number;
  mutationObserverActive: boolean;
}
```

---

## Runtime Events

```text
dom.scan.completed
dom.element.discovered
dom.element.updated
dom.element.hidden
dom.element.removed
dom.registry.updated
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Runtime APIs expose semantic metadata only—not raw DOM nodes.

---

# 10.09 Acceptance Principles

## Registry Tests

* Semantic IDs stable.
* Parent hierarchy preserved.
* Accessibility roles captured.

### Mutation Tests

* Node additions detected.
* Visibility changes detected.
* Attribute changes detected.
* Removed nodes versioned correctly.

### Geometry Tests

* Bounding boxes normalized.
* Layout changes tracked.
* Animated UI tracked smoothly.

### Timeline Tests

* Registry synchronized with recording clock.
* Mutation ordering deterministic.
* Geometry replay deterministic.

---

# 10.10 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 10.1)

1. DOM Tracking is TryLipi's browser-only semantic intelligence layer.
2. Every tracked element receives a stable semantic ID.
3. Mutation Observer converts DOM updates into timeline events.
4. Bounding Box Timeline stores normalized geometry over time.
5. DOM Lifecycle distinguishes discovered, visible, hidden and removed states.
6. Geometry updates are delta-compressed for long recordings.
7. DOM metadata is independent from rendered pixels.
8. Runtime APIs expose semantic metadata instead of DOM node references.
9. DOM Timeline synchronizes with cursor, keyboard, camera and zoom timelines.
10. Chapter 10.1 establishes the foundational Semantic DOM Runtime powering AI understanding inside browser recordings.

# 10.21 DOM Interaction Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Every interaction should know which UI element it belongs to.**

The Cursor Engine knows where the pointer moved.

The Keyboard Engine knows what keys were pressed.

The DOM Intelligence Engine answers:

* Which button was clicked?
* Which input received focus?
* Which dropdown opened?
* Which menu item was selected?
* Which tooltip appeared?

Instead of storing pixel coordinates, TryLipi stores **semantic interaction targets**.

---

## Interaction Intelligence Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
Keyboard Timeline
DOM Registry
Mutation Timeline
      │
Interaction Resolver
      │
Semantic DOM Interaction
      │
Interaction Timeline
```

---

## Semantic Interaction Examples

| User Action            | Semantic Output                     |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Click "Publish" button | `button.publish.clicked`            |
| Hover email input      | `input.email.hovered`               |
| Focus search box       | `input.search.focused`              |
| Open language dropdown | `dropdown.language.opened`          |
| Select "English"       | `dropdown.language.option.selected` |

---

## Interaction Categories

| Category               | Examples                   |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Pointer Interaction    | Hover, Click, Double Click |
| Focus Interaction      | Focus / Blur               |
| Input Interaction      | Typing, Paste              |
| Selection Interaction  | Checkbox, Radio            |
| Navigation Interaction | Menu, Tabs                 |
| Visibility Interaction | Modal, Tooltip             |

---

## Golden Interaction Principles

1. Every interaction references a semantic DOM element.
2. Pointer coordinates are secondary metadata.
3. DOM interactions survive layout changes.
4. Timeline stores interaction intent.
5. Interactions are replayable.
6. AI consumes semantic interaction events directly.
7. DOM interactions synchronize with cursor and keyboard timelines.

---

# 10.22 Accessibility Tree Intelligence Engine

Accessibility metadata is one of the richest semantic sources inside browsers.

## Why Accessibility Matters

The browser already exposes semantic roles.

TryLipi captures them.

---

## Accessibility Runtime Pipeline

```text
DOM Node
    │
Accessibility Tree
    │
Role Extractor
    │
Semantic Registry
```

---

## Captured Accessibility Metadata

| Property    | Example         |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| Role        | Button          |
| Label       | "Continue"      |
| Name        | Search          |
| Description | Tooltip text    |
| Checked     | Checkbox state  |
| Disabled    | Button disabled |
| Expanded    | Accordion state |
| Selected    | Tab selected    |

---

## Accessibility Tree Example

```text
Application
│
├── Navigation
│   ├── Home Button
│   ├── Pricing Button
│   └── Login Button
│
├── Main
│   ├── Heading
│   ├── Search Input
│   └── CTA Button
```

---

## Accessibility Metadata Interface

```ts
interface AccessibilityMetadata {
  role: string;
  label: string;
  disabled: boolean;
  expanded: boolean;
}
```

---

## Accessibility Roles Captured

| Role        | Importance |
| ----------- | ---------- |
| button      | High       |
| input       | High       |
| textbox     | High       |
| heading     | High       |
| navigation  | Medium     |
| menuitem    | High       |
| dialog      | High       |
| alert       | High       |
| progressbar | Medium     |
| tooltip     | Medium     |

---

## Why AI Uses Accessibility

Instead of OCR reading `"Continue"`...

AI immediately knows:

> This is a **button** labeled "Continue."

Much higher confidence.

---

## Engineering Rules

Accessibility metadata augments semantic registry records without replacing DOM metadata.

---

# 10.23 Semantic Importance Scoring Engine

Every DOM element receives an AI importance score.

## Importance Philosophy

Not every element deserves camera attention.

---

## Importance Pipeline

```text
DOM Registry
     │
Accessibility Metadata
Cursor Timeline
Keyboard Timeline
Mutation Timeline
     │
Importance Engine
     │
Importance Score
```

---

## Importance Signals

| Signal                | Weight |
| --------------------- | ------ |
| Accessibility Role    | High   |
| Cursor Hover Duration | High   |
| Click Frequency       | High   |
| Keyboard Focus        | High   |
| Visible Heading       | Medium |
| Modal/Dialog          | High   |
| Tooltip               | Medium |
| Footer Link           | Low    |

---

## Importance Levels

| Score      | Meaning                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------- |
| 1.00       | Primary UI element        |
| 0.85       | CTA / Interactive Control |
| 0.70       | Workflow Element          |
| 0.50       | Supporting Content        |
| Below 0.30 | Ignore by default         |

---

## Importance Metadata

```ts
interface DOMImportanceScore {
  semanticId: string;
  score: number;
  reasons: string[];
}
```

---

## Example Scores

| Element            | Score |
| ------------------ | ----- |
| Publish Button     | 0.97  |
| Search Input       | 0.94  |
| Modal Close Button | 0.88  |
| Footer Copyright   | 0.08  |
| Decorative Divider | 0.02  |

---

## AI Consumers

* Smart Zoom.
* Camera Panning.
* Tutorial Chapters.
* Captions.
* Spotlight Effects.

---

## Engineering Rules

Importance scores are versioned timeline metadata, not static properties.

# 10.24 Viewport Synchronization Runtime

The viewport changes continuously during browser recordings.

DOM tracking stays synchronized.

## Synchronization Pipeline

```text
Viewport Timeline
      │
DOM Geometry Runtime
      │
Bounding Box Adjuster
      │
DOM Timeline
```

---

## Viewport Signals

| Signal          | Usage                      |
| --------------- | -------------------------- |
| Scroll Position | Update geometry.           |
| Viewport Resize | Recalculate coordinates.   |
| Zoom Level      | Normalize positions.       |
| DPR             | Device scaling correction. |

---

## Synchronization Lifecycle

```text
Viewport Updated
      │
Geometry Recalculated
      │
Timeline Updated
```

---

## Geometry Synchronization Example

```text
Button
0.0s Y = 0.40

Scroll

2.0s Y = 0.22
```

Semantic ID remains identical.

---

## Synchronization Interface

```ts
interface DOMViewportSync {
  scrollOffsetY: number;
  viewportWidth: number;
  viewportHeight: number;
}
```

---

## Browser Resize Handling

Supports:

* Window resize.
* Responsive layouts.
* DevTools opening.
* Split screen.

---

## Engineering Rules

Viewport synchronization never creates new semantic IDs.

---

## Scroll Tracking Responsibilities

| Responsibility   | Description                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |

| Hidden Elements  | Leaving viewport.           |

```text
0.0s Pricing Card Hidden

Scroll

2.1s Pricing Card Visible

Scroll

7.8s Pricing Card Hidden
```

---

## Sticky Element Detection

Supports:

* Sticky headers.
* Floating action buttons.
* Cookie banners.
* Chat widgets.

Sticky elements maintain viewport-relative coordinates.

---

## Infinite Scroll Detection

Detects:

* Newly loaded cards.
* Feed items.
* Pagination append events.
* Lazy-loaded sections.

---

## Scroll Metadata

```ts
interface ScrollVisibilityEvent {
  semanticId: string;
  visible: boolean;
  timestampUs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Scroll visibility is stored separately from DOM lifecycle visibility.

# 10.26 Shadow DOM Tracking Runtime

Modern applications use Shadow DOM extensively.

TryLipi supports semantic traversal.

## Why Shadow DOM Matters

Frameworks:

* Material UI.
* Ionic.
* Shoelace.
* Lit.
* Web Components.

hide UI inside Shadow Roots.

---

## Shadow DOM Pipeline

```text
Shadow Host
     │
Shadow Root Scanner
     │
Semantic Registry
     │
Timeline Events
```

---

## Traversal Strategy

```text
Document
 │
 Shadow Host
     │
 Shadow Root
     │
 Internal Button
```

The internal button receives its own semantic ID.

---

## Metadata Captured

| Metadata          | Captured |
| ----------------- | -------- |
| Shadow Host       | Yes      |
| Shadow Root Depth | Yes      |
| Internal Role     | Yes      |
| Bounding Box      | Yes      |
| Slot Assignment   | Yes      |

---

## Shadow Metadata Interface

```ts
interface ShadowDOMMetadata {
  hostSemanticId: string;
  shadowDepth: number;
}
```

---

## Why It Matters

Without Shadow DOM traversal:

* MUI Buttons disappear.
* Custom components become invisible.
* AI loses semantic understanding.

---

## Engineering Rules

Shadow DOM elements participate in the same semantic registry.

---

# 10.27 iFrame Tracking Runtime

## iFrame Philosophy

Treat accessible iframes as nested semantic worlds.

Document
  │

  │
Accessible?

## Supported iFrame Types

Main Page
│
├── Sidebar
├── Content
│
└── iframe
    ├── Input
    ├── Button
    └── Modal

interface IFrameMetadata {

## Cross-Origin Strategy

When DOM access is unavailable:

* Track iframe bounds.
* Track visibility.
* Use OCR fallback.
* Cursor interactions mapped to iframe region.

---

## Engineering Rules

Nested DOM timelines merge into the global recording timeline using timestamp synchronization.

# 10.31 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 10.2)

1. DOM Interaction Intelligence maps user actions to semantic UI elements.
2. Accessibility metadata is a first-class AI signal inside browser recordings.
3. Every DOM element receives a dynamic semantic importance score.
4. Viewport synchronization preserves semantic IDs across scrolling and resizing.
5. Scroll visibility is stored independently from lifecycle visibility.
6. Shadow DOM traversal is mandatory for modern component libraries like MUI and Lit.
7. Same-origin iframes participate in the semantic registry; cross-origin iframes fall back to geometry and OCR.
8. DOM Relationship Graphs enable AI understanding of UI structure.
9. Semantic importance drives Smart Zoom, Camera Panning and Tutorial Generation.
10. Chapter 10.2 establishes the Semantic DOM Intelligence layer that makes TryLipi fundamentally different from pixel-only screen recorders.

# 10.31 DOM-Aware Smart Zoom Integration

## Mission Statement

> **Smart Zoom should zoom to UI elements—not approximate cursor positions.**

This section connects **Chapter 08 Smart Zoom** with the DOM Intelligence Engine.

Instead of estimating where attention belongs using cursor coordinates, Smart Zoom now receives **semantic DOM targets** with precise geometry, role, label, hierarchy and importance.

This is TryLipi's biggest browser-only advantage over Screen Studio, Tella and Cursorful.

---

## Integration Architecture

```text
Cursor Timeline
Keyboard Timeline
DOM Timeline
Mutation Timeline
Accessibility Tree
      │
DOM Focus Resolver
      │
Smart Zoom Engine
      │
Zoom Timeline
```

---

## DOM → Smart Zoom Pipeline

| Stage                  | Responsibility                                  |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Element Interaction    | Cursor or keyboard references semantic element. |
| DOM Focus Resolver     | Determines zoom target element.                 |
| Importance Engine      | Calculates zoom priority.                       |
| Focus Region Generator | Creates normalized zoom region.                 |
| Zoom Timeline          | Stores editable zoom event.                     |

---

## Example Flow

```text
User clicks "Publish"

↓

DOM Button Found

↓

Importance Score = 0.97

↓

Focus Region Created

↓

Smart Zoom Timeline Generated
```

The zoom follows the actual button—not where the cursor happened to be.

---

## DOM Focus Resolution Rules

| DOM Role | Zoom Behavior             |
| -------- | ------------------------- |
| Button   | Tight CTA zoom.           |
| Input    | Medium zoom with padding. |
| Dialog   | Large modal framing.      |
| Heading  | Reading zoom.             |
| Dropdown | Expand bounding region.   |
| Tooltip  | Contextual micro zoom.    |

---

## DOM Focus Interface

```ts
interface DOMZoomTarget {
  semanticId: string;
  importanceScore: number;
  focusBounds: DOMBoundingBox;
}
```

---

## Multi-Element DOM Zoom

When interacting with grouped components:

```text
Pricing Card
│
├── Title
├── Price
└── Subscribe Button
```

Camera zooms to the **entire card**, not only the button.

---

## Engineering Rules

Smart Zoom always prefers DOM geometry over cursor geometry when confidence is higher.

---

# 10.35 Performance Optimization Runtime

DOM tracking must support very large web applications.

## Performance Pipeline

```text
DOM Runtime
     │
Optimization Layer
     │
Registry Cache
     │
Timeline Writer
```

---

## Optimization Strategies

| Strategy                   | Benefit                               |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Registry Caching           | Fast semantic lookup.                 |
| Geometry Delta Compression | Smaller timeline.                     |
| Mutation Filtering         | Ignore framework noise.               |
| Importance Memoization     | Avoid rescoring unchanged nodes.      |
| Visibility Windowing       | Track only relevant viewport updates. |

---

## Performance Budgets

| Metric              | Target             |
| ------------------- | ------------------ |
| Initial DOM Scan    | Under 25 ms        |
| Mutation Processing | Under 1 ms/event   |
| Geometry Update     | Under 0.5 ms/frame |
| Registry Lookup     | Under 0.1 ms       |

---

## Large Application Strategy

Supports:

* Gmail.
* Notion.
* Linear.
* GitHub.
* Figma.
* Canva.
* Cursor IDE Web.

Even pages with **20,000+ DOM nodes** remain responsive through selective tracking.

---

## Memory Strategy

* Static nodes stored once.
* Geometry stored as deltas.
* Text versioned only on changes.
* Scene graph snapshots compressed.

---

## Engineering Rules

Optimization never removes semantic events from the recording timeline.

---

# 11.01 OCR Engine Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **OCR is the semantic intelligence layer for everything outside the browser.**

DOM Tracking gives TryLipi perfect semantic understanding inside browser tabs.

OCR extends that intelligence to:

* VS Code
* Cursor IDE
* Terminal
* Figma Desktop
* Photoshop
* Canva Desktop
* PowerPoint
* Excel
* Notion Desktop
* Any desktop application

Instead of recording only pixels, TryLipi understands **text, UI structure and visual hierarchy**.

---

## Why OCR Exists

### Browser Recording Mode

```text id="tzhy8g"
DOM Available

↓

Semantic Elements
```

### Desktop Recording Mode

```text id="ysfhw0"
Pixels Only

↓

OCR Engine

↓

Semantic Text Timeline
```

OCR becomes the replacement for DOM intelligence.

---

## OCR Responsibilities

| Module               | Responsibility            |
| -------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Vision OCR Runtime   | Detect text from frames.  |
| Layout Analyzer      | Detect text blocks.       |
| Text Timeline Engine | Version text over time.   |
| Language Detector    | Identify language/script. |
| Geometry Runtime     | Track text positions.     |
| Semantic Runtime     | Classify detected text.   |

---

## OCR vs DOM

| DOM Engine        | OCR Engine               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| Browser only      | Any application          |
| Perfect semantics | Vision-derived semantics |
| Native roles      | AI-inferred roles        |
| HTML hierarchy    | Visual layout hierarchy  |
| Bounding boxes    | Bounding boxes           |
| Mutation timeline | OCR text timeline        |

Together they cover **100% of recording environments**.

---

## Golden OCR Principles

1. OCR metadata never replaces screen pixels.
2. OCR produces semantic timeline metadata.
3. Text recognition is incremental.
4. Bounding boxes are normalized.
5. OCR is language-independent.
6. OCR integrates with Smart Zoom and Camera Panning.
7. AI consumes OCR metadata before raw pixels whenever possible.

---

# 11.02 OCR Runtime Architecture

The OCR Runtime continuously processes selected video frames.

## Runtime Architecture

```text id="kzn96y"
Screen Capture Engine
        │
Frame Sampler
        │
OCR Runtime
        │
Text Detector
        │
Layout Analyzer
        │
OCR Timeline
```

---

## Runtime Layers

```text id="dwlw5j"
OCR Runtime
│
├── Frame Sampling Runtime
├── OCR Detection Runtime
├── Language Runtime
├── Layout Runtime
├── Timeline Runtime
└── Semantic Runtime
```

---

## OCR Processing Lifecycle

```text id="5zqwy0"
Recording Starts
      │
Sample Frame
      │
Detect Text
      │
Detect Layout
      │
Compare Previous Frame
      │
Write OCR Timeline
```

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime          | Responsibility              |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| Frame Runtime    | Decide which frames to OCR. |
| OCR Runtime      | Detect text.                |
| Geometry Runtime | Detect text bounds.         |
| Timeline Runtime | Store text changes.         |
| Semantic Runtime | Classify detected content.  |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts id="nvuhnl"
interface OCRRuntimeState {
  enabled: boolean;
  sampledFrames: number;
  detectedTextBlocks: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

OCR Runtime operates independently from rendering FPS using intelligent frame sampling.

---

# 11.03 Vision Text Detection Runtime

The Vision Runtime converts pixels into structured text.

## Detection Pipeline

```text id="31e9pk"
Captured Frame
      │
Preprocessing
      │
Vision OCR Model
      │
Text Lines
      │
Bounding Boxes
      │
Confidence Scores
```

---

## Detection Granularity

| Granularity | Example                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------ |
| Character   | A                        |
| Word        | Publish                  |
| Line        | Publish Project          |
| Paragraph   | Documentation text       |
| Block       | Pricing card description |

---

## OCR Output Example

```text id="icvnhy"
Detected Text

Publish Project

Bounds:
x=0.42
y=0.31
w=0.18
h=0.05
```

---

## OCR Detection Metadata

```ts id="mshcl0"
interface OCRDetection {
  text: string;
  confidence: number;
  bounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

## Confidence Bands

| Confidence | Usage                      |
| ---------- | -------------------------- |
| Above 0.95 | Canonical text.            |
| 0.85–0.95  | High-confidence OCR.       |
| 0.70–0.85  | AI verification candidate. |
| Below 0.70 | Ignore unless persistent.  |

---

## Frame Sampling Strategy

| Screen Activity | OCR Sampling    |
| --------------- | --------------- |
| Static Reading  | Low frequency.  |
| Typing          | High frequency. |
| Scroll          | Adaptive.       |
| Modal Appears   | Immediate OCR.  |

---

## Engineering Rules

OCR detects only changed regions whenever possible.

---

# 11.04 Text Timeline Engine

Text changes over time.

TryLipi records those changes semantically.

## Timeline Pipeline

```text id="pylqkn"
OCR Detection
      │
Version Comparator
      │
Text Timeline
```

---

## Timeline Example

```text id="xy8h33"
0.0s "Loading..."

1.2s "Project Created"

3.0s "Deployment Successful"
```

Each text change becomes an event.

---

## Timeline Event Types

| Event         | Description            |
| ------------- | ---------------------- |
| Text Appeared | New text detected.     |
| Text Updated  | Existing text changed. |
| Text Removed  | Region disappeared.    |
| Text Moved    | Geometry changed.      |

---

## Timeline Interface

```ts id="lqig1a"
interface OCRTimelineEvent {
  timestampUs: number;
  textId: string;
  changeType: OCRTextChangeType;
}
```

---

## Incremental Text Detection

Instead of rescanning identical text every frame:

* Compare hashes.
* Compare geometry.
* Compare confidence.
* Emit updates only on changes.

---

## Text Versioning

```text id="i3fiv8"
Button Text

Version 1
Publish

Version 2
Publishing...

Version 3
Published
```

AI understands progression.

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline stores semantic text versions instead of duplicate OCR results.

---

# 11.09 Acceptance Principles

## Detection Tests

* English UI detected.
* Terminal output detected.
* Button text detected.
* Mixed-language UI detected.

### Timeline Tests

* Text updates version correctly.
* Removed text tracked.
* Moved text tracked.

### Layout Tests

* Headings grouped.
* Paragraphs grouped.
* Tables grouped.
* Code blocks grouped.

### Language Tests

* Telugu detected.
* Hindi detected.
* English detected.
* Mixed-language blocks preserved.

---

# 11.10 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 11.1)

1. OCR is the semantic intelligence layer for non-browser applications.
2. OCR Runtime samples frames independently from rendering FPS.
3. Text Timeline versions text instead of duplicating detections.
4. Layout Blocks represent semantic visual structure beyond plain text.
5. Multi-language OCR preserves native scripts without translation.
6. Bounding boxes are normalized and timeline-aware.
7. Confidence scores accompany every OCR detection.
8. OCR metadata integrates with Smart Zoom and Camera Panning.
9. Runtime APIs expose semantic OCR metadata only.
10. Chapter 11.1 establishes the foundational Vision OCR Runtime powering AI understanding across every desktop application.

# 11.21 Semantic OCR Intelligence Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **OCR should understand what text means, not just what text says.**

Raw OCR outputs strings.

Semantic OCR outputs structured knowledge.

Instead of:

```text
Ctrl + Shift + P
```

TryLipi understands:

```text
Keyboard Shortcut
Application: VS Code
Action: Open Command Palette
```

This transforms OCR into an AI-readable timeline.

---

## Semantic OCR Pipeline

```text
Captured Frame
      │
Vision OCR
      │
Layout Detection
      │
Semantic Classifier
      │
OCR Semantic Timeline
```

---

## Semantic Output Categories

| OCR Output       | Semantic Meaning  |
| ---------------- | ----------------- |
| `Ctrl + K`       | Keyboard Shortcut |
| `npm install`    | Terminal Command  |
| `404 Not Found`  | Error Message     |
| `Settings`       | Navigation Item   |
| `Deploy Project` | Primary CTA       |
| `README.md`      | File Name         |

---

## Semantic Intelligence Responsibilities

| Module              | Purpose                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| OCR Parser          | Normalize text.                   |
| Context Analyzer    | Understand surrounding UI.        |
| Semantic Classifier | Assign semantic type.             |
| Workflow Resolver   | Connect OCR with workflow events. |
| Timeline Writer     | Store semantic OCR events.        |

---

## Golden Semantic OCR Principles

1. OCR text is classified, not merely stored.
2. Semantic meaning is versioned separately from raw text.
3. Classification is explainable.
4. OCR semantics integrate with cursor, keyboard and DOM.
5. AI uses semantic OCR before pixel vision.
6. Classification confidence is stored.
7. Raw OCR always remains available.

---

# 11.22 Code Block Detection Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Developers create tutorials around code. OCR must understand code structure.**

Recognizing code as plain text is insufficient.

TryLipi detects:

* Programming language.
* Function names.
* Variables.
* Comments.
* File names.
* Syntax regions.

---

## Code Detection Pipeline

```text
OCR Text
    │
Code Detector
    │
Language Detector
    │
Syntax Region Generator
```

---

| Web      | JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS |
| Backend  | Node.js, Python, Go, Rust         |
| Mobile   | Swift, Kotlin, Dart               |
| Data     | SQL, JSON, YAML                   |
| Shell    | Bash, PowerShell, CMD             |
| Config   | Dockerfile, Nginx, GitHub Actions |

---

```text
const app = express();
```

Output:

| Metadata   | Value                |
| ---------- | -------------------- |
| Type       | Code Block           |
| Language   | TypeScript           |
| Block Role | JavaScript Statement |
| Confidence | 0.98                 |

---

## Code Layout Detection

Recognizes:

* Line numbers.
* Indentation.
* Braces.
* Comments.
* Imports.
* Functions.
* Classes.

---

## Code Metadata Interface

```ts
interface OCRCodeBlock {
  language: ProgrammingLanguage;
  lineCount: number;
  indentationLevel: number;
}
```

---

## AI Uses

* Smart Zoom code.
* Auto captions for code.
* Tutorial summaries.
* Copyable snippets.
* Syntax highlighting during export.

---

## Engineering Rules

Code blocks are semantic layout blocks independent of raw OCR words.

# 11.23 Terminal OCR Intelligence Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Terminal tutorials require command-aware OCR, not sentence OCR.**

OCR must distinguish:

* Commands.
* Output.

* Prompts.
* Progress bars.

* Kubernetes.
* Python.
* SSH.
* Firebase.
* Vercel.

---

* Command chapters.
* Error explanations.

---

## Engineering Rules

Terminal commands are versioned independently from terminal output.

# 11.27 OCR Semantic Classification Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Every OCR block receives semantic meaning.**

---

## Classification Pipeline

```text
OCR Block
    │
Context Engine
    │
Semantic Classifier
    │
Timeline Metadata
```

---

## Semantic Categories

| Category   | Example                                       |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Heading    | "Deploy Project"                              |
| Button     | Publish                                       |
| Navigation | Settings                                      |
| Code       | `npm install`                                 |
| Command    | `git clone`                                   |
| Error      | 404                                           |
| Success    | Deployment Complete                           |
| File Name  | package.json                                  |
| URL        | github.com                                    |
| Email      | [hello@example.com](mailto:hello@example.com) |
| Shortcut   | Ctrl+Shift+P                                  |

---

## Metadata Interface

```ts
interface OCRSemanticLabel {
  semanticType: OCRSemanticType;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Semantic Relationships

Example:

```text
README.md

↓

File Name

↓

Inside Explorer Panel
```

AI understands location and role.

---

## AI Consumers

* Tutorial Generator.
* Scene Understanding.
* Auto Chapters.
* Search Engine.
* Translation.

---

## Engineering Rules

Semantic classification never modifies original OCR output.

# 11.28 OCR Confidence & Correction Engine

## Mission Statement

OCR errors should be corrected deterministically whenever possible.

---

## Correction Pipeline

```text
Raw OCR
    │
Confidence Engine
    │
Dictionary
    │
Context Validator
    │
Corrected OCR
```

---

## Correction Sources

| Source                   | Usage               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------- |
| Programming Keywords     | Fix code OCR.       |
| Terminal Commands        | Fix shell OCR.      |
| Accessibility Dictionary | UI labels.          |
| Previous Timeline        | Stable text reuse.  |
| Language Model           | Context validation. |

---

## Example Corrections

| OCR           | Corrected      |
| ------------- | -------------- |
| `npm instal`  | `npm install`  |
| `packag json` | `package.json` |
| `Settngs`     | `Settings`     |
| `Gthub`       | `GitHub`       |

---

## Confidence Metadata

```ts
interface OCRCorrection {
  originalText: string;
  correctedText: string;
  correctionConfidence: number;
}
```

---

## Safety Rules

Never overwrite low-confidence OCR silently.

Store:

* Original.
* Suggested correction.
* Confidence.

---

## Engineering Rules

Corrections are additive metadata layers.

# 11.31 OCR-Aware Smart Zoom Integration

## Mission Statement

> **Smart Zoom should understand important text before it understands pixels.**

This section connects the **OCR Engine** with the **Smart Zoom Engine** developed in Chapter 08.

Whenever DOM metadata is unavailable (desktop recording), OCR becomes the source of focus regions.

Examples include:

* VS Code editor.
* Cursor IDE prompt.
* Terminal output.
* Figma labels.
* PowerPoint slides.
* PDF viewers.
* Documentation pages.

Smart Zoom receives semantic OCR targets instead of guessing from cursor position.

---

## OCR → Smart Zoom Architecture

```text
Screen Capture
      │
OCR Runtime
      │
Semantic OCR Timeline
      │
Focus Region Resolver
      │
Smart Zoom Engine
      │
Zoom Timeline
```

---

## OCR Zoom Target Pipeline

| Stage                   | Responsibility                          |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| OCR Detection           | Detect text and layout block.           |
| Semantic Classification | Identify heading/button/code/table/etc. |
| Importance Engine       | Score visual importance.                |
| Focus Generator         | Create normalized focus region.         |
| Smart Zoom              | Generate cinematic zoom event.          |

---

## Example Flow — VS Code

```text
Cursor pauses over "package.json"

↓

OCR detects File Name

↓

Importance Score = 0.92

↓

Focus Region Created

↓

Camera Zooms to Explorer Panel
```

---

## OCR Zoom Strategies

| OCR Block Type     | Zoom Behavior                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| Heading            | Reading zoom with padding.         |
| Code Block         | Wider zoom preserving indentation. |
| Terminal Command   | Tight horizontal zoom.             |
| Error Banner       | Strong emphasis zoom.              |
| Table              | Zoom to entire table container.    |
| Toast Notification | Micro zoom with hold.              |

---

## Reading Mode Zoom

For documentation or blog tutorials:

```text
Heading
Paragraph
Paragraph
```

Instead of zooming individual lines, Smart Zoom frames the **entire reading section**.

---

## OCR Focus Metadata

```ts
interface OCRZoomTarget {
  textId: string;
  semanticType: OCRSemanticType;
  importanceScore: number;
  focusBounds: BoundingBox;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

1. OCR Focus Regions become Smart Zoom targets only when DOM metadata is unavailable or confidence is lower.
2. Layout blocks override individual word boxes.
3. Reading mode uses paragraph-level framing.
4. Zoom targets remain editable inside the timeline editor.

---

# 11.32 OCR-Aware Camera Panning Integration

## Mission Statement

> **Camera movement should follow semantic reading flow across the screen.**

Camera Panning integrates OCR layout blocks to create documentary-style movement.

---

## Camera Integration Pipeline

```text
OCR Timeline
     │
Layout Analyzer
     │
Camera Target Planner
     │
Camera Timeline
```

---

## OCR Camera Behaviors

| OCR Event         | Camera Behavior            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| Heading Appears   | Pan to heading.            |
| Paragraph Reading | Slow vertical follow.      |
| Code Block        | Hold entire code region.   |
| Terminal Output   | Follow command execution.  |
| Table Appears     | Center table.              |
| Diagram Labels    | Follow annotation cluster. |

---

## Reading Camera Example

```text
Page Scroll

Heading
Paragraph
Paragraph
Diagram
Paragraph
```

Camera moves gradually downward, matching natural reading rhythm.

---

## Code Tutorial Example

```text
Import Statement

↓

Function

↓

Return Statement
```

Camera pans vertically while maintaining indentation visibility.

---

## Camera Lock Metadata

```ts
interface OCRCameraTarget {
  textId: string;
  lockStrength: number;
  followMode: OCRCameraFollowMode;
}
```

---

## Scroll Synchronization

When the creator scrolls:

* OCR geometry updates.
* Camera follows semantic layout blocks.
* Cursor movement becomes secondary.

---

## Engineering Rules

1. Camera follows semantic layout rather than raw scroll offset.
2. OCR camera locks have lower priority than manual editor keyframes.
3. Code blocks use wider framing than ordinary paragraphs.

---

# 11.33 OCR + DOM Scene Graph Fusion Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Browser recordings and desktop recordings should produce one unified semantic world.**

This is one of the most important architectural chapters in TryLipi.

DOM recordings generate Scene Graphs.

OCR recordings generate Scene Graphs.

AI consumes **one unified Scene Graph API**.

---

## Fusion Architecture

```text
DOM Scene Graph
       │
OCR Scene Graph
       │
Scene Graph Fusion Runtime
       │
Unified Semantic Scene Graph
```

---

## Unified Scene Graph

```text
Application Window
│
├── Navigation
├── Sidebar
├── Main Editor
│   ├── Code Block
│   ├── Button
│   └── Terminal Panel
└── Toast Notification
```

The AI no longer cares whether nodes came from DOM or OCR.

---

## Fusion Node Types

| Source        | Node Type               |
| ------------- | ----------------------- |
| DOM           | Native UI Node          |
| OCR           | Vision UI Node          |
| Accessibility | Semantic Attribute Node |
| Cursor        | Interaction Node        |
| Keyboard      | Workflow Node           |

---

## Unified Node Metadata

```ts
interface UnifiedSceneNode {
  nodeId: string;
  source: SceneNodeSource;
  semanticType: string;
  children: string[];
}
```

---

## Fusion Priority Rules

| Source Combination    | Winner                             |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| DOM + OCR Same Region | DOM                                |
| OCR Only              | OCR                                |
| Accessibility + DOM   | Accessibility augments DOM         |
| OCR + Cursor          | OCR layout with cursor interaction |

---

## Why Fusion Matters

Enables:

* Browser tutorials.
* Desktop tutorials.
* Mixed tutorials.
* Browser inside desktop apps.
* Embedded webviews.

All become searchable and editable.

---

## Engineering Rules

1. Scene Graph Fusion never duplicates semantic nodes.
2. DOM nodes always retain original semantic IDs.
3. OCR nodes receive vision-specific semantic IDs.
4. AI consumes the unified graph only.

---
