# 20.03 Timeline Composition Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **All independent timelines become one synchronized production timeline.**

Timeline Composer is TryLipi's equivalent of an NLE (Non-Linear Editor) timeline engine.

---

## Timeline Composition Pipeline

```text
Cursor Timeline
Camera Timeline
Zoom Timeline
Effects Timeline
Caption Timeline
Audio Timeline
      │
Timeline Composer
      │
Master Composition Timeline
```

---

## Timeline Hierarchy

```text
Master Timeline
│
├── Visual Timeline
│
├── Audio Timeline
│
├── Interaction Timeline
│
├── AI Timeline
│
└── Metadata Timeline
```

---

## Timeline Synchronization Rules

| Timeline | Sync Source          |
| -------- | -------------------- |
| Cursor   | Semantic timestamps  |
| Camera   | Semantic events      |
| Zoom     | Focus transitions    |
| Captions | Word timestamps      |
| Audio    | Speech timeline      |
| Effects  | Animation timestamps |

---

## Frame Mapping

```text
Timestamp

00:12.340

↓

Frame Number

740

↓

Composition State
```

Every timestamp resolves to one deterministic frame.

---

## Timeline Segments

Supports segmentation for:

* Chapters.
* Scenes.
* Workflows.
* Export chunks.
* Replay segments.

---

## Timeline Metadata

```ts
interface CompositionTimeline {
  frameRate: 60 | 120;
  durationUs: number;
  segments: TimelineSegment[];
}
```

---

## Timeline Editing Rules

Timeline edits generate a new composition graph version.

Previous render graph remains immutable.

---

## Engineering Rules

Timeline Composer is deterministic and version-controlled.

---

# 20.04 Render Graph Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Every frame is produced from a dependency graph instead of imperative rendering logic.**

This is the heart of TryLipi's rendering engine.

---

## Render Graph Architecture

```text
Render Graph
│
├── Background Node
├── Window Node
├── Recording Node
├── Cursor Node
├── Annotation Node
├── Caption Node
├── Webcam Node
└── Overlay Node
```

Each node depends on timeline state.

---

## Dependency Graph

```text
Cursor Timeline

↓

Cursor Node

↓

Annotation Node

↓

Overlay Node
```

Dependencies guarantee correct ordering.

---

## Node Categories

| Node             | Responsibility      |
| ---------------- | ------------------- |
| Source Node      | Recording frames.   |
| Effect Node      | Cursor glow, blur.  |
| Composition Node | Merge layers.       |
| Audio Node       | Timeline audio.     |
| Export Node      | Final output frame. |

---

## Render Graph Lifecycle

```text
Timeline Frozen

↓

Graph Built

↓

Dependencies Resolved

↓

Frame Rendering Begins
```

---

## Incremental Graph Updates

Only affected nodes rebuild.

Example:

```text
Caption Edited

↓

Caption Node Updated

↓

Overlay Node Updated

↓

No Cursor Re-render Needed
```

---

## Graph Metadata

```ts
interface RenderGraphNode {
  nodeId: string;
  nodeType: RenderNodeType;
  dependencies: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Render graph updates are dependency-aware and incremental.

---

# 20.05 Layer Composition Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Every visible element is rendered as an independent compositing layer.**

---

## Layer Stack

```text
Composition Stack
│
├── Background
├── Window Frame
├── Recording
├── Cursor
├── Spotlight
├── Highlights
├── Arrows
├── Captions
├── Webcam
├── CTA Overlay
└── Branding
```

---

## Layer Ordering Rules

| Layer       | Z Index |
| ----------- | ------- |
| Background  | 0       |
| Window      | 1       |
| Recording   | 2       |
| Cursor      | 3       |
| Effects     | 4       |
| Annotations | 5       |
| Captions    | 6       |
| Webcam      | 7       |
| Overlay     | 8       |

Ordering is deterministic.

---

## Blend Modes

Supports:

| Blend      | Usage               |
| ---------- | ------------------- |
| Normal     | Default UI.         |
| Multiply   | Shadows.            |
| Screen     | Glow.               |
| Overlay    | Highlights.         |
| Soft Light | Background effects. |

---

## Alpha Composition

Supports:

* Transparent overlays.
* Glass morphism.
* Shadows.
* Blur masks.
* Gradient masks.

---

## Safe Area Composition

Layers avoid platform UI overlays automatically.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface CompositionLayer {
  layerId: string;
  zIndex: number;
  blendMode: BlendMode;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Composition layers remain independent until final frame merge.

---

# 20.06 GPU Frame Scheduler

## Mission Statement

> **The renderer should maximize GPU throughput without breaking timeline determinism.**

---

## Scheduler Architecture

```text
Composition Timeline

↓

Frame Scheduler

↓

GPU Queue

↓

Rendered Frames
```

---

## Scheduler Responsibilities

| Responsibility    | Description                  |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Frame Queue       | Build render queue.          |
| Dependency Check  | Wait for required nodes.     |
| GPU Batch Builder | Batch similar render passes. |
| Cache Lookup      | Skip cached frames.          |
| Retry Engine      | Recover failed frame.        |

---

## Frame Scheduling Pipeline

```text
Frame Requested

↓

Dependencies Ready?

↓

GPU Queue

↓

Render Pass

↓

Frame Cache
```

---

## Render Pass Categories

| Pass          | Purpose                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------- |
| Geometry Pass | Shapes and layout.        |
| Blur Pass     | Blur shaders.             |
| Shadow Pass   | Window shadows.           |
| Cursor Pass   | Cursor rendering.         |
| Overlay Pass  | Captions and annotations. |

---

## Cache Strategy

Frames reuse cached outputs when:

* Timeline unchanged.
* Effects unchanged.
* Audio unchanged.
* Camera unchanged.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface FrameSchedulerState {
  queuedFrames: number;
  cachedFrames: number;
}
```

---

## Performance Targets

| Operation          | Target       |
| ------------------ | ------------ |
| Frame Scheduling   | Under 1 ms   |
| Cache Lookup       | Under 0.2 ms |
| GPU Batch Creation | Under 3 ms   |

---

## Engineering Rules

Scheduler preserves frame ordering regardless of GPU batching.

---

# 20.07 Deterministic Replay Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Preview is mathematically identical to export.**

Replay Runtime guarantees creator trust.

---

## Replay Architecture

```text
Timeline Version

↓

Replay Runtime

↓

Frame Validator

↓

Preview Frame

↓

Export Frame
```

---

## Replay Validation Pipeline

```text
Frame Generated

↓

Replay Hash

↓

Export Hash

↓

Match?
```

---

## Replay Hashing

Each frame stores:

* Timeline Version.
* Graph Version.
* Layer Version.
* Render Hash.

---

## Replay Metadata

```text
Frame 1040

Timeline Version 18

Render Hash A91F23
```

---

## Replay Guarantees

| Guarantee    | Description         |
| ------------ | ------------------- |
| Same Cursor  | Same coordinates.   |
| Same Zoom    | Same interpolation. |
| Same Caption | Same timing.        |
| Same Audio   | Same alignment.     |
| Same Effects | Same easing curve.  |

---

## Drift Detection

Detects:

* Missing layer.
* Timing mismatch.
* Audio drift.
* Frame mismatch.
* Cache corruption.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ReplayValidationResult {
  frameHash: string;
  isDeterministic: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Replay validation runs before encoding begins.

# 20.09 Acceptance Principles

## Timeline Tests

* All timelines synchronized.
* Frame mapping deterministic.
* Timeline edits create new graph version.

### Graph Tests

* Dependency ordering correct.
* Incremental updates work.
* Node invalidation localized.

### Layer Tests

* Layer ordering preserved.
* Blend modes deterministic.
* Safe areas respected.

### Scheduler Tests

* Cached frames reused.
* GPU batching correct.
* Failed frame retried.

### Replay Tests

* Preview hash equals export hash.
* Cursor identical.
* Audio aligned.
* Captions identical.

---

# 20.10 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.1)

1. Export Rendering Engine builds videos from semantic timelines—not preview pixels.
2. Timeline Composer merges all visual, audio and AI timelines into one immutable composition timeline.
3. Render Graph defines dependency-aware rendering for every frame.
4. Layer Composition Runtime renders independent visual layers before final composition.
5. GPU Frame Scheduler batches rendering work while preserving deterministic frame ordering.
6. Deterministic Replay guarantees preview and export produce identical frames.
7. Timeline freezing prevents AI recomputation during export.
8. Frame caches are dependency-aware and reusable across exports.
9. Replay hashes validate rendering correctness before encoding begins.
10. Chapter 20.1 establishes TryLipi's production-grade rendering runtime powering every exported video.

# 20.21 Video Encoding Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The encoder converts deterministic rendered frames into production-quality videos optimized for every creator platform.**

Rendering produces **RGBA composition frames**.

Encoding converts those frames into efficient video formats while preserving:

* Visual fidelity.
* Audio synchronization.
* Captions.
* Alpha channels.
* Metadata.
* AI chapter information.

Encoding is **never responsible for visual decisions** — only compression and packaging.

---

## Rendering vs Encoding

### Rendering Runtime

```text
Semantic Timeline

↓

GPU Frames (RGBA)
```

### Encoding Runtime

```text
RGBA Frames

↓

Video Codec

↓

Container

↓

Final Export
```

The renderer creates pixels.

The encoder compresses pixels.

---

## Encoding Responsibilities

| Runtime               | Responsibility                   |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Video Encoder         | Encode rendered frames.          |
| Audio Encoder         | Encode narration/music/SFX.      |
| Muxer                 | Merge audio + video.             |
| Metadata Writer       | Chapters, subtitles, thumbnails. |
| Export Bundle Builder | Final production asset.          |

---

## Encoding Principles

1. Never re-render frames.
2. Preserve deterministic timestamps.
3. Audio/video remain sample-accurate.
4. Multiple export formats share one render output.
5. Metadata is embedded whenever supported.
6. Progressive export supported.
7. Resume interrupted exports.

---

# 20.31 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.2)

1. Video Encoding Engine converts rendered RGBA frames into production-ready video containers.
2. WebCodecs is the primary hardware-accelerated browser encoder whenever available.
3. FFmpeg WASM and native FFmpeg provide advanced codec, alpha and container support.
4. Audio Muxing Engine synchronizes narration, microphone, music and sound effects with semantic timestamps.
5. Export Profiles configure codecs, resolutions and bitrates for different creator platforms.
6. Thumbnail Engine generates hero frames, GIF previews and storyboard strips using semantic importance scores.
7. Export Metadata Builder packages subtitles, chapters, thumbnails, documentation and knowledge metadata alongside videos.
8. Encoding runtime never modifies render timing or semantic event ordering.
9. Production bundles are immutable artifacts containing every export asset.
10. Chapter 20.2 establishes TryLipi's production-grade encoding pipeline supporting browser, desktop and cloud exports.

# 20.31 Cloud Rendering Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Rendering should scale from a 30-second Instagram Reel to a 4-hour 4K developer tutorial without changing the creator experience.**

Local rendering is ideal for quick exports.

Cloud rendering handles:

* Long recordings.
* 4K / 8K exports.
* Multi-language dubbing.
* AI-heavy videos.
* Team collaboration.
* Batch rendering.

The creator clicks **Export** — TryLipi decides the best rendering strategy.

---

## Rendering Modes

| Mode                 | Use Case                                |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Local Browser Render | Short creator videos.                   |
| Local Desktop Render | Long tutorials using local GPU.         |
| Hybrid Render        | Browser prepares assets, cloud renders. |
| Cloud Render         | Large or collaborative exports.         |
| Distributed Render   | Multi-GPU rendering.                    |

---

## Export Decision Engine

```text
Creator Clicks Export
        │
Render Planner
        │
├── Local GPU
├── Hybrid GPU
├── Cloud GPU
└── Distributed Cluster
```

---

## Rendering Design Principles

1. Creator never manages infrastructure.
2. Rendering is resumable.
3. Every render is deterministic.
4. Failed chunks are recoverable.
5. Multi-device rendering supported.
6. GPU resources allocated dynamically.
7. Cost optimization built into scheduling.

---

# 20.32 Distributed Cloud Rendering Architecture

## Mission Statement

> **Every export becomes a distributed render job composed of immutable render bundles.**

---

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Export Request
      │
Render Planner
      │
Render Bundle Storage
      │
Render Queue
      │
GPU Worker Cluster
      │
Chunk Encoder Workers
      │
Asset Merger
      │
Final Export Bundle
```

---

## Cloud Components

```text
Cloud Rendering Platform
│
├── API Gateway
├── Render Planner
├── Job Scheduler
├── Render Queue
├── GPU Workers
├── Encoder Workers
├── Merge Workers
├── Asset Storage
└── Notification Service
```

---

## Render Bundle Contents

```text
Render Bundle
│
├── Timeline Metadata
├── Render Graph
├── Audio Timeline
├── Captions
├── Chapters
├── Knowledge Graph
├── Export Profile
└── Preset Assets
```

Workers never receive raw editor state.

---

## Stateless Worker Design

Every worker receives:

* Bundle.
* Chunk range.
* Export profile.
* Render version.

Workers remain stateless.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface CloudRenderBundle {
  renderJobId: string;
  bundleVersion: number;
  exportProfileId: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Cloud workers only consume immutable render bundles.

---

# 20.33 Render Queue & Job Scheduler

## Mission Statement

> **Render jobs should be prioritized, resumable and observable.**

---

## Queue Architecture

```text
Export Requests
      │
Priority Queue
      │
Scheduler
      │
GPU Worker Assignment
```

---

## Queue Types

| Queue              | Purpose           |
| ------------------ | ----------------- |
| Preview Queue      | Fast previews.    |
| Creator Queue      | Standard exports. |
| High Quality Queue | 4K/8K exports.    |
| Batch Queue        | Multiple exports. |
| Enterprise Queue   | Team rendering.   |

---

## Job States

| State     | Description        |
| --------- | ------------------ |
| Queued    | Waiting.           |
| Preparing | Bundles uploading. |
| Rendering | GPU active.        |
| Encoding  | Chunk encoding.    |
| Merging   | Final composition. |
| Completed | Export ready.      |
| Failed    | Needs retry.       |
| Cancelled | User cancelled.    |

---

## Scheduler Responsibilities

* Allocate GPUs.
* Balance workloads.
* Retry failures.
* Predict completion.
* Optimize queue latency.

---

## Priority Rules

| Priority | Examples                |
| -------- | ----------------------- |
| Highest  | Preview export.         |
| High     | Creator manual export.  |
| Medium   | Scheduled batch export. |
| Low      | Archive exports.        |

---

## Scheduler Metadata

```ts
interface RenderJobState {
  renderJobId: string;
  priority: RenderPriority;
  estimatedCompletionSeconds: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Scheduler decisions never affect deterministic render output.

---

# 20.34 Chunk Rendering Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Large videos render in parallel without visual seams or audio drift.**

---

## Chunk Architecture

```text
30 Minute Video
      │
Chunk Planner
      │
Chunk 1
Chunk 2
Chunk 3
Chunk 4
      │
Chunk Encoder
      │
Chunk Merge
```

---

## Chunk Strategy

| Chunk Type     | Example             |
| -------------- | ------------------- |
| Fixed Duration | Every 60 seconds.   |
| Chapter-Based  | Split by chapters.  |
| Workflow-Based | Split by workflows. |
| Adaptive       | GPU memory aware.   |

---

## Chunk Metadata

```text
Chunk 03

Start Frame 7200

End Frame 10800

Timeline Version 18
```

---

## Boundary Synchronization

Chunk boundaries include overlap frames.

```text
Chunk A
██████████░░

Chunk B
░░██████████
```

Overlap prevents transition artifacts.

---

## Audio Chunk Strategy

Audio overlaps:

* Crossfades.
* Narration continuity.
* Music continuity.

No audible seams.

---

## Chunk Metadata Interface

```ts
interface RenderChunk {
  chunkId: string;
  startFrame: number;
  endFrame: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Chunk boundaries preserve animation easing and audio continuity.

---

# 20.35 Distributed GPU Worker Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **GPU workers render independent frame ranges while preserving identical output.**

---

## Worker Architecture

```text
Render Queue

↓

GPU Worker

↓

Frame Renderer

↓

Chunk Encoder

↓

Asset Upload
```

---

## Worker Lifecycle

```text
Receive Bundle

↓

Load Assets

↓

Render Frames

↓

Encode Chunk

↓

Upload Result
```

---

## Worker Types

| Worker           | Responsibility     |
| ---------------- | ------------------ |
| Render Worker    | GPU composition.   |
| Encode Worker    | Codec encoding.    |
| Merge Worker     | Final assembly.    |
| Thumbnail Worker | Preview assets.    |
| Subtitle Worker  | Caption packaging. |

---

## GPU Resource Allocation

| Resource       | Usage                 |
| -------------- | --------------------- |
| VRAM           | Composition textures. |
| Compute Queue  | Shader execution.     |
| Encoder Queue  | Hardware encoding.    |
| Transfer Queue | Asset upload.         |

---

## Worker Health Checks

Workers continuously report:

* GPU utilization.
* VRAM usage.
* Temperature (native/cloud).
* Frame throughput.
* Failure count.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface GPUWorkerState {
  workerId: string;
  activeChunkId: string;
  gpuUtilizationPercent: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Workers render deterministic frame ranges independently.

---

# 20.36 Render Recovery & Retry Engine

## Mission Statement

> **No creator should lose a 45-minute render because frame 19,842 failed.**

---

## Recovery Architecture

```text
Worker Failure

↓

Chunk Retry Planner

↓

New Worker Assigned

↓

Resume Rendering
```

---

## Failure Categories

| Failure          | Recovery              |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Worker Crash     | Retry chunk.          |
| GPU Timeout      | Move worker.          |
| Network Failure  | Resume upload.        |
| Encoding Failure | Restart encoder only. |
| Merge Failure    | Retry merge stage.    |

---

## Retry Strategy

```text
Attempt 1

↓

Attempt 2

↓

Different GPU

↓

Fallback Runtime
```

---

## Checkpoint System

Every chunk stores:

* Render progress.
* Encoded bytes.
* Audio progress.
* Validation hashes.

---

## Resume Export

User closes browser.

Cloud continues rendering.

User returns.

Progress restored.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface RenderRecoveryState {
  retryCount: number;
  checkpointFrame: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery always resumes from immutable checkpoints.

---

# 20.37 Render Diagnostics & Performance Analytics

## Mission Statement

> **Creators and engineers should understand render performance in real time.**

---

## Diagnostics Dashboard

```text
Render Dashboard
│
├── Progress
├── ETA
├── FPS
├── GPU Usage
├── Memory Usage
├── Chunk Status
├── Retry Count
└── Output Size
```

---

## Performance Metrics

| Metric          | Purpose              |
| --------------- | -------------------- |
| Frames Rendered | Progress.            |
| FPS Rendered    | Throughput.          |
| GPU Utilization | Performance.         |
| VRAM Usage      | Resource planning.   |
| Encoder Speed   | Encoding throughput. |
| Upload Speed    | Cloud upload.        |

---

## Timeline Diagnostics

Example:

```text
Chapter 4

Rendering

Chunk 7

96% Complete

ETA 42 Seconds
```

---

## AI Render Diagnostics

Detects:

* Expensive blur layers.
* Heavy shadows.
* Large webcam overlays.
* Caption density.
* Animation hotspots.

Suggests optimization.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface RenderDiagnostics {
  renderFPS: number;
  gpuMemoryMB: number;
  etaSeconds: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Diagnostics never modify render output.

---

# 20.40 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 20.3)

1. Cloud Rendering executes immutable render bundles using distributed GPU workers.
2. Render Queue prioritizes preview, creator, batch and enterprise export jobs independently.
3. Chunk Rendering splits long recordings into deterministic overlapping render segments.
4. Distributed GPU Workers render frame ranges without sharing mutable rendering state.
5. Recovery Engine resumes failed renders from checkpoints instead of restarting exports.
6. Diagnostics provide real-time visibility into rendering throughput, GPU utilization and ETA.
7. Export Infrastructure packages media assets, captions, chapters, documentation and knowledge metadata together.
8. Local, hybrid and cloud rendering produce identical deterministic outputs.
9. Every production export is reproducible from its render bundle and timeline version.
10. Chapter 20 completes TryLipi's Export Rendering Engine—the production-grade rendering, encoding and cloud export infrastructure powering browser, desktop and enterprise video creation.

# 21.01 AI Orchestration Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **TryLipi should behave like one intelligent AI system even though dozens of specialized models power it internally.**

This chapter defines the **AI Operating System** of TryLipi.

Every AI feature—from OCR to documentation generation—uses this orchestration layer.

Instead of calling models directly...

TryLipi sends semantic tasks into a routing runtime that chooses the best execution strategy.

---

## Traditional AI Application

```text
Frontend

↓

Gemini API

↓

Response
```

Every feature is tightly coupled to one provider.

---

## TryLipi AI Operating System

```text
Creator Action

↓

AI Task Runtime

↓

Routing Engine

↓

Capability Graph

↓

Context Builder

↓

Model Adapter

↓

AI Provider
```

Every AI provider becomes interchangeable.

---

## Core Responsibilities

| Runtime          | Responsibility                   |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Model Registry   | Maintain available AI models.    |
| Routing Engine   | Select the optimal model.        |
| Capability Graph | Know model capabilities.         |
| Prompt Builder   | Generate structured prompts.     |
| Context Builder  | Assemble semantic context.       |
| Task Planner     | Break large AI jobs into stages. |
| Adapter Layer    | Standardize provider APIs.       |

---

## AI Design Principles

1. Features never directly call AI providers.
2. Routing decisions are deterministic.
3. Context is semantic—not transcript-only.
4. Providers are interchangeable.
5. AI tasks are versioned.
6. Prompt templates are reusable.
7. AI execution is observable.

---

## AI Lifecycle

```text
Semantic Task

↓

Task Planner

↓

Context Builder

↓

Routing Engine

↓

Model Execution

↓

Structured Result
```

---

# 21.02 AI Operating System Architecture

## Mission Statement

> **Every AI feature executes inside one unified orchestration runtime.**

---

## High-Level Architecture

```text
TryLipi AI Runtime
│
├── Task Registry
├── Routing Engine
├── Capability Graph
├── Context Builder
├── Prompt Builder
├── Model Registry
├── Adapter Layer
├── Execution Runtime
└── Response Validator
```

---

## Runtime Flow

```text
User Action

↓

Semantic Task

↓

Context Builder

↓

Prompt Builder

↓

Routing Engine

↓

Model Adapter

↓

AI Provider

↓

Validator

↓

Result
```

---

## AI Runtime Layers

```text
AI Operating System
│
├── Semantic Task Layer
├── Context Layer
├── Prompt Layer
├── Routing Layer
├── Execution Layer
├── Validation Layer
└── Analytics Layer
```

Each layer has a single responsibility.

---

## AI Runtime Responsibilities

| Layer            | Responsibility            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| Task Layer       | Define AI job.            |
| Context Layer    | Fetch semantic knowledge. |
| Prompt Layer     | Construct prompt payload. |
| Routing Layer    | Choose execution model.   |
| Execution Layer  | Invoke provider.          |
| Validation Layer | Validate JSON/schema.     |
| Analytics Layer  | Track latency and cost.   |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface AIOrchestrationRuntime {
  taskId: string;
  routingVersion: number;
  executionMode: AIExecutionMode;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

AI Runtime is provider-independent and task-centric.

* Store supported modalities.

```text
OCR
```

# 21.04 AI Capability Graph Engine

## Mission Statement

> **The routing engine understands capabilities—not provider names.**

Capability Graph separates **what** is needed from **who** provides it.

---

## Capability Graph Architecture

```text
AI Capability Graph
│
├── Vision
├── OCR
├── JSON Generation
├── Translation
├── Speech Recognition
├── Speech Synthesis
├── Embeddings
├── Long Context
└── Image Generation
```

---

## Capability Relationships

```text
Scene Understanding
│
├── Vision
├── OCR
└── JSON Output
```

A task maps to required capabilities.

---

## Capability Metadata

| Capability   | Description          |
| ------------ | -------------------- |
| Vision       | Understand pixels.   |
| OCR          | Read text.           |
| JSON         | Structured output.   |
| Audio Input  | Understand speech.   |
| Audio Output | Generate narration.  |
| Embedding    | Vector generation.   |
| Translation  | Language conversion. |

---

## Capability Resolution

```text
Task

Scene Understanding

↓

Capabilities Needed

Vision
OCR
JSON
```

Routing uses capabilities—not model names.

---

## Capability Interface

```ts
interface AICapability {
  capabilityId: string;
  modality: AIInputModality;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Capabilities are reusable semantic building blocks across AI tasks.

---

# 21.05 AI Routing Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Every AI task is routed to the most appropriate model automatically.**

This is the decision engine of TryLipi.

---

## Routing Architecture

```text
Semantic Task

↓

Routing Rules

↓

Capability Matching

↓

Cost Rules

↓

Latency Rules

↓

Model Selection
```

---

## Routing Inputs

| Signal                | Purpose                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Task Type             | Documentation, OCR, etc. |
| Context Size          | Small vs large context.  |
| Required Capabilities | Vision, audio, JSON.     |
| Cost Budget           | Optimize spending.       |
| Latency Target        | Fast vs quality.         |
| Export Mode           | Offline vs realtime.     |

---

## Routing Example

| Task                | Routing Decision        |
| ------------------- | ----------------------- |
| OCR                 | OCR model.              |
| Scene Understanding | Vision model.           |
| Tutorial Script     | Long-context LLM.       |
| Translation         | Translation model.      |
| AI Voice            | Speech synthesis model. |

---

## Routing Strategies

| Strategy        | Use Case                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------- |
| Fastest         | Preview generation.        |
| Cheapest        | Background indexing.       |
| Highest Quality | Final tutorial generation. |
| Balanced        | Creator default mode.      |

---

## Multi-Step Routing

```text
Documentation Task

↓

Planner Model

↓

Retriever

↓

Writer Model

↓

Validator Model
```

Multiple AI models cooperate.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface AIRoutingDecision {
  taskId: string;
  selectedModelId: string;
  routingReason: RoutingReason;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Routing decisions are deterministic given identical inputs and routing version.

---

# 21.06 Prompt Builder Runtime

Prompt Builder standardizes AI interactions.

```text
Semantic Context

Prompt Template

↓

Prompt Builder
```

# 21.07 Context Builder Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **AI receives only the semantic context it needs for the task.**

Context Builder is responsible for assembling knowledge before inference.

---

## Context Sources

```text
Knowledge Graph
Scene Graph
Workflow Timeline
Project Memory
Recording Timeline
Documentation Graph
      │
Context Builder
```

---

## Context Layers

| Context               | Source                |
| --------------------- | --------------------- |
| Scene Context         | Scene Graph           |
| Workflow Context      | Workflow Runtime      |
| Project Context       | Project Memory        |
| Code Context          | Code Scene Runtime    |
| UI Context            | UI Recognition Engine |
| Documentation Context | Chapter Graph         |

---

## Context Compression

Instead of sending an entire recording...

Context Builder sends:

* Current workflow.
* Relevant entities.
* Current chapter.
* Neighboring steps.

---

## Retrieval Example

```text
Task

Explain JWT Middleware

↓

Retrieve

Workflow

Authentication

↓

Retrieve

jwt.ts

middleware.ts

auth.routes.ts
```

Only relevant context enters the prompt.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface AIContextBundle {
  workflowId?: string;
  entityIds: string[];
  chapterIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Context Builder retrieves semantic entities instead of raw transcript windows whenever possible.

---

# 21.08 AI Task Planner & Inference Pipeline

## Mission Statement

> **Large AI jobs are decomposed into deterministic execution plans.**

---

## Planning Pipeline

```text
Semantic Task

↓

Task Planner

↓

Execution Plan

↓

Inference Jobs

↓

Aggregation

↓

Validation
```

---

## Planner Responsibilities

| Responsibility      | Description                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Split Tasks         | Large recordings into stages.  |
| Dependency Planning | OCR before documentation.      |
| Parallel Planning   | Independent jobs concurrently. |
| Aggregation         | Merge outputs.                 |
| Retry Planning      | Retry failed stages only.      |

---

## Example Documentation Plan

```text
Documentation Generation
│
├── Detect Chapters
├── Retrieve Code Context
├── Generate Markdown
├── Generate Screenshots
├── Generate API Docs
└── Validate Output
```

---

## Parallel Execution Example

```text
Recording

↓

OCR

Scene Understanding

Transcription

↓

Documentation Builder
```

Independent AI jobs execute concurrently.

---

## Inference Job Metadata

```ts
interface AIInferenceJob {
  jobId: string;
  dependencyJobIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Result Validation

Validators verify:

* JSON schema.
* Markdown structure.
* Missing entities.
* Hallucination guards.
* Chapter consistency.

---

## Engineering Rules

Inference plans are DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs) instead of sequential AI calls.

---

# 21.09 Runtime AI APIs

## Runtime APIs

| API                   | Purpose                       |

```ts
interface AIOrchestrationAPI {

}
```

## Runtime Events

```text
task.created
context.built
prompt.generated

```

---

## Engineering Rules

AI APIs expose semantic task execution independently from provider implementations.

---

# 21.10 Acceptance Principles

## Routing Tests

* OCR routed correctly.
* Vision tasks routed correctly.
* Documentation routed correctly.

### Context Tests

* Workflow context retrieved.
* Project memory injected.
* Scene graph retrieved correctly.

### Prompt Tests

* Output schema respected.
* Template version applied.
* Context compression works.

### Planner Tests

* Independent jobs parallelized.
* Dependencies honored.
* Validation executed.

---

# 21.11 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 21.1)

1. AI Model Orchestration Runtime is the operating system for every AI feature inside TryLipi.
2. Features communicate through semantic AI tasks instead of provider-specific APIs.
3. Model Registry maintains immutable metadata describing every available AI model and capability.
4. Capability Graph separates task requirements from provider implementations.
5. Routing Engine selects models using capabilities, context size, latency targets and cost strategy.
6. Prompt Builder generates versioned structured prompts from reusable templates.
7. Context Builder assembles semantic knowledge from Scene Graph, Workflow Graph, Project Memory and Knowledge Graph.
8. Task Planner decomposes complex AI features into deterministic inference DAGs with dependency-aware execution.
9. Validation Runtime verifies structured outputs before downstream AI systems consume them.
10. Chapter 21.1 establishes TryLipi's AI Operating System—the orchestration layer connecting every AI model into one coherent platform.

# 21.21 AI Memory Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **AI should remember knowledge, not repeatedly re-read recordings.**

This chapter introduces TryLipi's **persistent semantic memory architecture**.

Without memory:

* Every AI request becomes expensive.
* Context windows explode.
* Latency increases.
* Costs grow rapidly.

With memory:

* AI retrieves only relevant semantic knowledge.
* Previously computed understanding is reused.
* Costs decrease dramatically.
* Long recordings remain searchable.

---

## AI Without Memory

```text id="qzcklm"
Recording

↓

Entire Transcript Sent

↓

LLM

↓

Answer
```

Every request sends thousands of unnecessary tokens.

---

## TryLipi Memory Runtime

```text id="8gqgjy"
Recording

↓

Knowledge Graph

↓

Semantic Memory

↓

Retriever

↓

Compressed Context

↓

LLM
```

Memory replaces transcript replay.

---

## Memory Responsibilities

| Runtime             | Responsibility                         |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Recording Memory    | Entire recording knowledge.            |
| Project Memory      | Repository, files, workflows.          |
| Conversation Memory | AI conversations with creator.         |
| Retrieval Memory    | Frequently accessed semantic entities. |
| Prompt Cache        | Prompt reuse.                          |
| Embedding Cache     | Vector reuse.                          |

---

## Memory Design Principles

1. Memory stores semantic entities.
2. Retrieval happens before generation.
3. Memory is immutable per recording version.
4. Context is assembled dynamically.
5. Cached knowledge expires through versioning.
6. Retrieval is deterministic.
7. Memory minimizes token usage.

---

# 21.22 Multi-Layer Memory Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Different memories serve different AI tasks.**

TryLipi uses layered memory instead of one giant conversation history.

---

## Memory Architecture

```text id="dd9vjl"
AI Memory Runtime
│
├── Recording Memory
├── Workflow Memory
├── Project Memory
├── Conversation Memory
├── User Preference Memory
├── Cache Memory
└── Embedding Memory
```

---

## Memory Hierarchy

```text id="3zkjvt"
Recording Memory
│
├── Chapters
├── Workflows
├── Files
├── UI Components
├── Commands
├── APIs
└── Concepts
```

---

## Memory Types

### Recording Memory

Stores:

* Scene Graph.
* Workflow Graph.
* Knowledge Graph.
* Chapters.
* AI summaries.

### Project Memory

Stores:

* Repository.
* Branch.
* Environment variables.
* Dependencies.
* Frameworks.

### Conversation Memory

Stores:

* Previous AI questions.
* Creator preferences.
* Active editing session.
* Follow-up context.

### Cache Memory

Stores reusable AI outputs.

---

## Memory Lifetimes

| Memory              | Lifetime                         |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Recording Memory    | Permanent for recording version. |
| Project Memory      | Recording session.               |
| Conversation Memory | Workspace session.               |
| Prompt Cache        | Versioned cache.                 |
| Embedding Cache     | Until graph version changes.     |

---

## Metadata

```ts id="dg1nsn"
interface AIMemoryState {
  recordingMemoryVersion: number;
  projectMemoryVersion: number;
  cacheVersion: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Memory layers are isolated and independently versioned.

---

# 21.23 Semantic Retrieval Engine

## Mission Statement

> **AI retrieves only the knowledge required to answer the current task.**

Retrieval is powered by semantic entities—not raw text.

---

## Retrieval Pipeline

```text id="9owftk"
User Task

↓

Intent Classifier

↓

Retriever

↓

Knowledge Graph

↓

Context Bundle
```

---

## Retrieval Sources

| Source              | Used For               |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Knowledge Graph     | Concepts & entities.   |
| Scene Graph         | UI understanding.      |
| Workflow Graph      | Process understanding. |
| Project Memory      | Repository context.    |
| Documentation Graph | Markdown retrieval.    |
| Code Graph          | Source code context.   |

---

## Retrieval Strategies

### Entity Retrieval

Example:

```text id="4mimly"
JWT Middleware

↓

Entity

jwt.ts

↓

Workflow

Authentication
```

### Workflow Retrieval

Returns related workflow entities.

### Neighbor Retrieval

Returns previous/next chapter context.

### Dependency Retrieval

Returns imported files and APIs.

---

## Multi-Hop Retrieval

```text id="xeyxtq"
Deploy Backend

↓

Vercel

↓

Environment Variables

↓

MongoDB URI
```

Multiple relationships retrieved automatically.

---

## Retrieval Metadata

```ts id="hwp6jn"
interface RetrievalBundle {
  entityIds: string[];
  workflowIds: string[];
  relatedChapterIds: string[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Retriever prioritizes semantic relationships over keyword matching.

# 21.25 Context Compression Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Compress semantic context before sending it to expensive AI models.**

This is one of TryLipi's biggest cost-saving systems.

---

## Compression Pipeline

```text id="khjlwm"
Retriever

↓

Context Builder

↓

Context Compressor

↓

LLM Context
```

---

## Compression Layers

| Layer                | Purpose                             |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Entity Compression   | Replace verbose descriptions.       |
| Workflow Compression | Summarize completed workflow.       |
| Chapter Compression  | Keep current chapter only.          |
| Code Compression     | Include only relevant functions.    |
| UI Compression       | Include interacted components only. |

---

## Example Compression

### Raw Context

```text id="wkdltm"
15-minute transcript

35,000 tokens
```

### Compressed Context

```text id="vmhll8"
Authentication Workflow

jwt.ts

middleware.ts

POST /login

420 tokens
```

Huge reduction.

---

## Compression Rules

1. Remove duplicate entities.
2. Keep dependency chain.
3. Preserve semantic IDs.
4. Preserve chronology when required.
5. Never remove referenced entities.

---

## Metadata

```ts id="qpnx42"
interface CompressedContext {
  originalTokenCount: number;
  compressedTokenCount: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Compression happens after retrieval—not before.

---

# 21.26 AI Cache & Response Reuse Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Never pay twice for identical semantic work.**

Caching dramatically reduces latency and AI costs.

---

## Cache Architecture

```text id="mmjlwm"
AI Task

↓

Cache Key Builder

↓

Semantic Cache

↓

Hit?

↓

LLM
```

---

## Cache Layers

| Cache             | Scope              |
| ----------------- | ------------------ |
| Prompt Cache      | Prompt hash.       |
| Retrieval Cache   | Retrieval bundle.  |
| Embedding Cache   | Vector generation. |
| Response Cache    | Final AI output.   |
| Translation Cache | Language output.   |
| OCR Cache         | OCR blocks.        |

---

## Cache Key Strategy

Cache key includes:

* Task ID.
* Context version.
* Prompt version.
* Model version.
* Recording version.

---

## Cache Invalidation

Triggers include:

* Timeline edits.
* Prompt version changes.
* Model version changes.
* Recording version changes.

---

## Cache Metadata

```ts id="abp76x"
interface SemanticCacheEntry {
  cacheKey: string;
  modelVersion: string;
  responseVersion: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Cache entries are immutable and version-aware.

---

# 21.27 Token Optimization & Batching Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Minimize token usage without reducing semantic quality.**

This chapter formalizes TryLipi's AI cost optimization strategy.

---

## Optimization Pipeline

```text id="4e2hjc"
Semantic Tasks

↓

Task Grouper

↓

Batch Builder

↓

Context Compressor

↓

LLM
```

---

## Batching Strategies

### Workflow Batch

Group related workflow analysis.

### OCR Batch

Analyze multiple OCR regions together.

### Translation Batch

Translate multiple captions together.

### Conversation Batch

Analyze multiple conversations together.

---

## Token Reduction Techniques

| Technique             | Benefit                        |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Context Compression   | Massive reduction.             |
| Prompt Reuse          | Repeated prompts avoided.      |
| Entity References     | Replace repeated descriptions. |
| Shared System Prompts | Sent once per batch.           |
| Semantic IDs          | Compact references.            |

---

## Batch Metadata

```ts id="6ixxiz"
interface BatchInferenceRequest {
  taskIds: string[];
  sharedContextVersion: number;
}
```

---

## Cost Savings Examples

| Strategy            | Expected Reduction  |
| ------------------- | ------------------- |
| Prompt Cache        | High reduction.     |
| Context Compression | High reduction.     |
| Embedding Reuse     | High reduction.     |
| Batch OCR           | Moderate reduction. |
| Batch Translation   | Moderate reduction. |

---

## Engineering Rules

Batching groups semantically compatible tasks only.

---

# 21.31 Acceptance Principles

## Memory Tests

* Recording memory persists.
* Project memory isolated.
* Conversation memory updates correctly.

### Retrieval Tests

* Entity retrieval works.
* Workflow retrieval works.
* Dependency retrieval works.

### Cache Tests

* Prompt cache hit.
* OCR cache hit.
* Cache invalidates correctly.

### Optimization Tests

* Compression ratio measured.
* Batch requests generated.
* Cost estimator accurate.

---

# 21.32 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 21.2)

1. AI Memory Runtime stores semantic knowledge instead of repeatedly processing recordings.
2. Recording, Project, Conversation and Cache memories are isolated and independently versioned.
3. Semantic Retrieval retrieves entities, workflows and chapters before AI generation.
4. Embedding Infrastructure indexes semantic entities into namespace-aware vector stores.
5. Context Compression minimizes token usage while preserving semantic dependencies.
6. Cache Runtime reuses prompts, embeddings, OCR results, translations and AI responses through versioned cache keys.
7. Token Optimization batches semantically compatible AI tasks and removes duplicated context.
8. Latency Optimization uses speculative retrieval, cache warmup and parallel inference without changing outputs.
9. AI Cost Engine estimates token usage and routing budgets before model execution.
10. Chapter 21.2 establishes TryLipi's AI Memory & Optimization Runtime—the foundation for scalable, low-cost, low-latency AI execution.

# 21.31 AI Reliability Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **TryLipi should continue working even when an AI provider fails, becomes slow, or changes behavior.**

AI infrastructure must be **provider-independent, fault-tolerant, observable, and measurable**.

Creators should never know which provider handled a request.

The orchestration runtime guarantees:

* Reliable AI execution.
* Automatic fallback.
* Consistent output schemas.
* Streaming responses.
* Cost-aware routing.
* Quality monitoring.

---

## AI Reliability Pipeline

```text
Semantic Task

↓

Routing Engine

↓

Provider Adapter

↓

Reliability Runtime

↓

Validation Runtime

↓

Creator Response
```

---

## Reliability Responsibilities

| Runtime              | Responsibility                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Provider Abstraction | Hide provider-specific APIs.    |
| Retry Runtime        | Recover transient failures.     |
| Fallback Runtime     | Switch providers automatically. |
| Validation Runtime   | Validate structured responses.  |
| Monitoring Runtime   | Track health & latency.         |
| Evaluation Runtime   | Measure output quality.         |

---

## Reliability Principles

1. Never expose provider-specific logic to features.
2. Failures are recoverable whenever possible.
3. Responses must satisfy schemas.
4. Streaming is first-class.
5. Monitoring is built into every inference.
6. Quality is continuously evaluated.
7. Infrastructure supports future AI providers.

---

# 21.32 Provider Abstraction Layer

## Mission Statement

> **Every AI provider implements one common TryLipi AI interface.**

This layer isolates business logic from vendor SDKs.

---

## Provider Architecture

```text
TryLipi AI Runtime
        │
Provider Adapter Layer
        │
├── Provider A Adapter
├── Provider B Adapter
├── Provider C Adapter
├── Local Model Adapter
└── Experimental Adapter
```

No feature imports provider SDKs directly.

---

## Adapter Responsibilities

| Adapter          | Responsibility                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Authentication   | Provider credentials.           |
| Request Builder  | Convert unified request format. |
| Response Parser  | Normalize output.               |
| Streaming Parser | Stream normalized tokens.       |
| Error Mapper     | Normalize provider errors.      |

---

## Unified Request Flow

```text
AI Task

↓

Unified Request

↓

Provider Adapter

↓

Provider Response

↓

Normalized Response
```

---

## Unified Response Format

```ts
interface AIResponse {
  responseId: string;
  output: unknown;
  usage: TokenUsage;
}
```

Every provider returns identical runtime objects.

---

## Provider Capabilities

Each adapter declares:

* Supported modalities.
* Max context.
* Streaming support.
* JSON support.
* Vision support.
* Audio support.

---

## Adapter Versioning

```ts
interface ProviderAdapterVersion {
  adapterId: string;
  apiVersion: string;
}
```

Adapters evolve independently.

---

## Engineering Rules

Provider adapters are the only layer allowed to understand vendor-specific request/response formats.

---

# 21.33 Reliability & Fallback Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **AI failures should degrade gracefully instead of breaking creator workflows.**

---

## Reliability Architecture

```text
Inference Request

↓

Health Check

↓

Primary Provider

↓

Retry?

↓

Fallback Provider

↓

Validator
```

---

## Failure Categories

| Failure                | Recovery Strategy  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ |
| Timeout                | Retry.             |
| Rate Limit             | Backoff + retry.   |
| Provider Unavailable   | Fallback provider. |
| Invalid JSON           | Validation retry.  |
| Partial Stream Failure | Resume stream.     |

---

## Retry Strategy

```text
Attempt 1

↓

Exponential Backoff

↓

Attempt 2

↓

Fallback Provider

↓

Failure Event
```

---

## Retry Policies

| Task             | Retry Count |
| ---------------- | ----------- |
| OCR              | 2           |
| Documentation    | 2           |
| Translation      | 3           |
| Voice Generation | 2           |
| Embeddings       | 1           |

---

## Fallback Routing Example

```text
Documentation Task

↓

Primary LLM

↓

Unavailable

↓

Fallback LLM

↓

Schema Validation
```

Creator receives one consistent response.

---

## Health Monitoring

Provider health includes:

* Availability.
* Latency.
* Error rate.
* Success rate.
* Streaming stability.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ReliabilityState {
  retryAttempt: number;
  providerHealth: ProviderHealthState;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Fallback decisions preserve output schema compatibility.

---

# 21.34 Streaming Inference Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Long AI responses should appear immediately instead of waiting for completion.**

Streaming powers:

* Documentation generation.
* Tutorial generation.
* AI chat.
* Translation.
* Narration previews.

---

## Streaming Architecture

```text
AI Provider

↓

Streaming Adapter

↓

Chunk Normalizer

↓

Streaming Runtime

↓

UI Renderer
```

---

## Streaming Lifecycle

```text
Inference Started

↓

Token Stream

↓

Partial Validation

↓

UI Updates

↓

Completed
```

---

## Stream Types

| Stream             | Example                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| Text Stream        | Documentation.           |
| Markdown Stream    | README generation.       |
| JSON Stream        | Structured AI outputs.   |
| Caption Stream     | Live captions.           |
| Translation Stream | Multi-language captions. |

---

## Incremental Markdown Rendering

```text
# Authentication

↓

## Step 1

↓

Paragraph

↓

Code Block

↓

Checklist
```

Documentation appears progressively.

---

## Stream Buffer

Buffer responsibilities:

* Merge partial tokens.
* Repair Markdown boundaries.
* Validate JSON chunks.
* Preserve ordering.

---

## Stream Metadata

```ts
interface AIStreamChunk {
  sequenceNumber: number;
  isFinalChunk: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Streaming output is normalized before UI rendering.

---

# 21.35 AI Safety & Validation Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Every AI response must satisfy structural, semantic and safety validation before reaching creators.**

This runtime protects downstream systems.

---

## Validation Pipeline

```text
AI Response

↓

Schema Validation

↓

Semantic Validation

↓

Safety Validation

↓

Output Runtime
```

---

## Validation Layers

| Layer              | Responsibility             |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| Schema Validator   | JSON structure.            |
| Markdown Validator | Heading/code formatting.   |
| Entity Validator   | Referenced entities exist. |
| Workflow Validator | Workflow consistency.      |
| Citation Validator | Knowledge references.      |
| Safety Validator   | Unsafe outputs.            |

---

## Schema Validation

Example:

```text
Documentation Output

↓

Required Sections

✓ Title

✓ Steps

✓ Summary

✓ Metadata
```

---

## Semantic Validation

Checks:

* Missing workflow IDs.
* Missing chapter references.
* Invalid UI entities.
* Missing code entities.

---

## Hallucination Guard

The validator rejects outputs that reference:

* Unknown files.
* Unknown workflows.
* Unknown APIs.
* Unknown chapters.

Only retrieved entities are valid.

---

## Safety Categories

| Category             | Runtime Action     |
| -------------------- | ------------------ |
| Invalid JSON         | Retry.             |
| Missing Entity       | Retry retrieval.   |
| Unsafe Markdown      | Reject section.    |
| Broken Code Block    | Repair.            |
| Unsupported Language | Retry translation. |

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ValidationReport {
  schemaPassed: boolean;
  semanticPassed: boolean;
  safetyPassed: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Validation executes before caching AI responses.

# 21.40 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 21.3)

1. Provider Abstraction isolates TryLipi features from vendor-specific AI SDKs.

7. Production AI Infrastructure supports feature flags, A/B experiments, rate limiting and provider rollouts without changing feature code.
8. AI infrastructure is horizontally scalable and resilient to provider outages.
9. Every AI response is traceable through routing version, prompt version, retrieval version and provider adapter version.
10. Chapter 21 completes TryLipi's AI Model Orchestration Runtime—the enterprise AI operating system powering all multimodal intelligence across recording, editing, documentation, search and future autonomous creator workflows.

# 08A.01 Pixel Tracking Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Pixel Tracking is the visual intelligence layer that understands movement directly from pixels, even when DOM information is unavailable.**

This chapter introduces the **Pixel Tracking Runtime**, arguably the most important visual tracking system inside TryLipi.

It allows the camera to understand:

* Buttons moving while scrolling.
* Videos playing inside websites.
* Mobile apps without DOM access.
* PDFs.
* Images.
* Canva.
* Figma.
* VS Code.
* Terminal windows.
* Native desktop applications.
* Games.
* Any arbitrary screen recording.

Unlike DOM tracking, Pixel Tracking works **everywhere**.

---

## Why Pixel Tracking Exists

### DOM Tracking Works Here

* Chrome websites.
* React apps.
* HTML elements.
* Browser UI.

### DOM Tracking Completely Fails Here

* Figma Canvas.
* Canva Canvas.
* VS Code Editor.
* Terminal.
* PDF Viewer.
* Image Viewer.
* Mobile Emulator.
* Native Windows App.
* Video Player.
* Zoom Meeting.
* Photoshop.
* Blender.
* Unity.

Pixel Tracking becomes the universal fallback.

---

## DOM vs Pixel Tracking

| DOM Tracking             | Pixel Tracking             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| Knows HTML elements.     | Knows visual pixels.       |
| Requires browser access. | Works on any pixels.       |
| Perfect IDs.             | Visual feature IDs.        |
| Lightweight.             | GPU vision processing.     |
| Browser only.            | Browser + Desktop + Cloud. |

---

## Pixel Tracking Responsibilities

| Runtime              | Responsibility                   |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Feature Detector     | Detect stable visual landmarks.  |
| Optical Flow Engine  | Measure movement between frames. |
| Landmark Tracker     | Maintain landmark identity.      |
| Confidence Engine    | Measure tracking quality.        |
| Motion Graph Builder | Store pixel motion timeline.     |
| Pixel Cache          | Reuse tracked landmarks.         |

---

## Core Design Principles

1. Pixel tracking is provider-independent.
2. Works without DOM.
3. GPU accelerated.
4. Deterministic.
5. Runs in realtime.
6. Robust to scrolling.
7. Robust to scaling.
8. Robust to animation.
9. Robust to partial occlusion.
10. Every tracked landmark has confidence.

---

## Pixel Tracking Lifecycle

```text
Captured Frame

↓

Feature Detection

↓

Landmark Extraction

↓

Optical Flow

↓

Motion Estimation

↓

Confidence Update

↓

Motion Timeline
```

Pixel tracking creates a **pixel motion graph** used by Smart Zoom.

---

# 08A.02 Pixel Tracking Runtime Architecture

## Mission Statement

> **Every captured frame produces a structured graph of visual landmarks and motion vectors.**

---

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Screen Capture Engine
        │
Captured Frames
        │
Pixel Tracking Runtime
        │
├── Feature Detector
├── Landmark Tracker
├── Optical Flow Engine
├── Motion Vector Generator
├── Confidence Runtime
└── Motion Graph Builder
```

---

## Runtime Pipeline

```text
Frame N

↓

Feature Detection

↓

Landmarks

↓

Frame N+1

↓

Optical Flow

↓

Motion Vectors

↓

Updated Landmarks
```

Every pair of frames updates tracked pixels.

---

## Pixel Runtime Layers

```text
Pixel Tracking Runtime
│
├── Frame Preprocessor
├── Image Pyramid Builder
├── Feature Detector
├── Feature Descriptor
├── Optical Flow Engine
├── Landmark Matcher
├── Confidence Engine
├── Motion Graph Builder
└── Cache Runtime
```

Each layer has a single responsibility.

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Layer              | Responsibility                |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Frame Preprocessor | Prepare frame textures.       |
| Pyramid Builder    | Multi-scale processing.       |
| Feature Detector   | Detect landmarks.             |
| Descriptor Builder | Encode landmark appearance.   |
| Optical Flow       | Estimate movement.            |
| Matcher            | Match features across frames. |
| Confidence Engine  | Validate matches.             |
| Motion Graph       | Timeline of movement.         |

---

## Frame Processing Flow

```text
RGBA Frame

↓

Luminance Conversion

↓

Gaussian Pyramid

↓

Feature Detection

↓

Tracking Runtime
```

The runtime always preprocesses frames before tracking.

---

## Runtime Metadata

```ts
interface PixelTrackingRuntime {
  runtimeVersion: number;
  frameRate: number;
  pyramidLevels: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Pixel Tracking Runtime is deterministic for identical frame sequences.

---

# 08A.03 Feature Detection Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Stable visual landmarks are the anchors of every camera movement.**

Feature Detection finds pixels worth tracking.

---

## What Is a Feature?

A feature is a visually distinctive point that remains identifiable.

Examples:

* Button corner.
* Icon corner.
* Text intersection.
* Checkbox.
* Avatar eye.
* Window corner.
* Folder icon.
* Cursor hotspot.

---

## Feature Detection Pipeline

```text
Frame

↓

Grayscale

↓

Edge Detection

↓

Corner Detection

↓

Feature Descriptor

↓

Landmark
```

---

## Feature Categories

| Feature       | Example             |
| ------------- | ------------------- |
| Corner        | Button corner.      |
| Edge          | Toolbar edge.       |
| Blob          | Notification badge. |
| Texture       | Code editor text.   |
| Icon Shape    | GitHub logo.        |
| Text Anchor   | "Deploy" button.    |
| Cursor Anchor | Pointer hotspot.    |

---

## Multi-Scale Detection

```text
Original Image

↓

1x Features

↓

0.5x Features

↓

0.25x Features

↓

Feature Merge
```

Allows tracking during zoom.

---

## Feature Descriptor Runtime

Each landmark stores:

* Position.
* Scale.
* Orientation.
* Appearance vector.
* Descriptor hash.

---

## Descriptor Metadata

```ts
interface PixelFeatureDescriptor {
  featureId: string;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  orientation: number;
}
```

---

## GPU Feature Extraction

Runs inside WebGPU.

Parallel extraction for thousands of features.

---

## Feature Density Rules

| Region      | Target Density |
| ----------- | -------------- |
| Toolbar     | High           |
| Buttons     | High           |
| Text Blocks | Medium         |
| Background  | Low            |
| Blank Area  | Ignore         |

---

## Engineering Rules

Features must be stable across neighboring frames.

---

# 08A.04 Optical Flow Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Measure how every tracked pixel moves between frames.**

Optical Flow is the heart of motion estimation.

---

## Optical Flow Philosophy

Instead of comparing objects...

Compare **pixel movement**.

```text
Frame A

●

↓

Frame B

●→
```

Movement becomes vectors.

---

## Optical Flow Pipeline

```text
Frame N

↓

Landmarks

↓

Frame N+1

↓

Motion Estimation

↓

Motion Vectors
```

---

## Motion Vector Runtime

Every feature stores:

* Delta X.
* Delta Y.
* Velocity.
* Confidence.
* Rotation estimate.

---

## Multi-Level Optical Flow

```text
Image Pyramid

↓

Coarse Motion

↓

Fine Motion

↓

Subpixel Refinement
```

Allows fast and accurate tracking.

---

## Types of Motion

| Motion      | Example        |
| ----------- | -------------- |
| Translation | Scroll.        |
| Rotation    | Rotate canvas. |
| Scale       | Zoom webpage.  |
| Perspective | Window resize. |
| Affine      | Transform UI.  |

---

## Motion Graph

```text
Landmark A

Frame 1

↓

Frame 2

↓

Frame 3

↓

Frame 4
```

Motion history becomes part of timeline metadata.

---

## Motion Metadata

```ts
interface MotionVector {
  featureId: string;
  deltaX: number;
  deltaY: number;
  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Motion vectors are calculated before zoom prediction.

---

# 08A.05 Pixel Landmark Tracking Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Landmarks persist across hundreds or thousands of frames while the screen changes.**

---

## Landmark Lifecycle

```text
Feature Appears

↓

Tracking ID Created

↓

Motion Updated

↓

Confidence Updated

↓

Tracking Ends
```

---

## Tracking IDs

Each landmark gets a permanent runtime identifier.

```text
Landmark-2481

Button Corner

Frame 120–890
```

---

## Landmark Graph

```text
Landmark Graph
│
├── Position Timeline
├── Velocity Timeline
├── Scale Timeline
├── Visibility Timeline
└── Confidence Timeline
```

---

## Landmark State Machine

| State     | Meaning               |
| --------- | --------------------- |
| New       | Newly detected.       |
| Active    | Successfully tracked. |
| Lost      | Temporarily missing.  |
| Recovered | Found again.          |
| Expired   | Removed.              |

---

## Landmark Matching

Matching considers:

* Descriptor similarity.
* Distance threshold.
* Motion prediction.
* Scale prediction.
* Rotation prediction.

---

## Landmark Metadata

```ts
interface PixelLandmark {
  landmarkId: string;
  trackingState: TrackingState;
  visibilityScore: number;
}
```

---

## Motion Timeline Example

```text
Frame 100

Button

↓

Frame 110

Moved Down

↓

Frame 120

Moved Down Again
```

Timeline becomes reusable by Smart Zoom.

---

## Engineering Rules

Landmarks survive scrolling whenever confidence remains above threshold.

---

# 08A.06 Pixel Confidence Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Every tracked landmark has a measurable confidence score used by downstream AI systems.**

Confidence prevents camera jitter.

---

## Confidence Architecture

```text
Landmark

↓

Similarity Score

↓

Motion Consistency

↓

Visibility Score

↓

Confidence
```

---

## Confidence Inputs

| Signal                | Contribution |
| --------------------- | ------------ |
| Descriptor Similarity | High         |
| Motion Prediction     | High         |
| Scale Consistency     | Medium       |
| Rotation Consistency  | Medium       |
| Visibility            | High         |
| Pixel Quality         | Medium       |

---

## Confidence Lifecycle

```text
Feature Detected

95%

↓

Scroll

90%

↓

Blur

82%

↓

Occlusion

48%
```

Confidence decreases as uncertainty grows.

---

## Confidence Thresholds

| Score    | Action              |
| -------- | ------------------- |
| 90–100   | Lock tracking.      |
| 75–89    | Stable tracking.    |
| 50–74    | Soft tracking.      |
| 30–49    | Candidate recovery. |
| Below 30 | Tracking lost.      |

---

## Confidence Recovery

```text
Lost Landmark

↓

Nearby Search

↓

Descriptor Match

↓

Recovered
```

Recovery happens in Part 08A.3.

---

## Confidence Metadata

```ts
interface PixelTrackingConfidence {
  landmarkId: string;
  confidenceScore: number;
  recoveryCandidate: boolean;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera movement only locks onto landmarks above confidence threshold.

---

# 08A.07 Runtime Pixel APIs

## Runtime APIs

| API                          | Purpose                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `detectPixelFeatures()`      | Detect landmarks.        |
| `buildFeatureDescriptors()`  | Encode features.         |
| `computeOpticalFlow()`       | Generate motion vectors. |
| `trackLandmarks()`           | Update landmark graph.   |
| `updateTrackingConfidence()` | Update confidence score. |
| `buildMotionGraph()`         | Store motion timeline.   |

---

## Runtime Interface

```ts
interface PixelTrackingAPI {
  gpuAccelerated: boolean;
  supportsRealtimeTracking: boolean;
}
```

---

## Runtime Events

```text
pixel.features.detected
landmark.created
opticalflow.updated
landmark.updated
confidence.updated
motiongraph.updated
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Pixel APIs expose deterministic motion tracking independent of zoom and camera systems.

---

# 08A.08 Acceptance Principles

## Feature Detection Tests

* Detect UI corners.
* Detect icons.
* Detect text anchors.
* Ignore blank regions.

### Optical Flow Tests

* Track scrolling.
* Track zooming.
* Track animated UI.
* Track canvas movement.

### Landmark Tests

* Persistent tracking IDs.
* Stable motion history.
* Visibility timeline maintained.

### Confidence Tests

* Confidence decreases during blur.
* Confidence recovers after visibility returns.
* Lost landmarks trigger recovery pipeline.

---

# 08A.09 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 08A.1)

1. Pixel Tracking Runtime is the universal visual tracking engine for DOM and non-DOM environments.
2. Feature Detection identifies stable visual landmarks across every captured frame.
3. Optical Flow computes deterministic pixel motion vectors between neighboring frames.
4. Pixel Landmarks persist across scrolling, scaling and animation using runtime tracking IDs.
5. Motion Graph stores landmark movement as timeline metadata reusable by Smart Zoom and Camera Pan.
6. Confidence Engine scores every tracked landmark using descriptor similarity, motion consistency and visibility.
7. Pixel Tracking is GPU accelerated and operates independently from AI provider infrastructure.
8. Pixel Tracking never depends on HTML, React or browser DOM metadata.
9. Every downstream camera system consumes Motion Graphs instead of raw pixel movement.
10. Chapter 08A.1 establishes the foundation for Persistent Object Tracking, Zoom Prediction and Visual Saliency AI.

# 08A.21 Persistent Object Tracking Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Pixel landmarks become persistent visual objects that survive scrolling, animation, resizing, zooming and long recordings.**

Chapter **08A.1** tracked *pixels*.

Chapter **08A.2** tracks *objects built from pixels.*

An object may exist for thousands of frames while continuously updating its geometry.

Examples include:

* Button
* Icon
* Card
* Avatar
* Image
* Toolbar
* Terminal Window
* VS Code Tab
* Cursor Hover Target
* Floating Tooltip
* Modal Window

The object becomes a first-class entity inside TryLipi.

---

## Pixel vs Object Tracking

| Pixel Tracking       | Persistent Object Tracking        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Tracks landmarks.    | Tracks complete UI objects.       |
| Point-based.         | Bounding-box based.               |
| Motion vectors only. | Motion + geometry + identity.     |
| Frame-to-frame.      | Timeline-to-timeline persistence. |
| Local confidence.    | Object confidence history.        |

---

## Why Object Tracking Matters

Without persistent tracking:

* Zoom jitters.
* Camera loses buttons while scrolling.
* Blur masks detach.
* Callouts drift.
* AI annotations break.

Persistent tracking guarantees cinematic stability.

---

## Object Lifecycle

```text
Visual Object Appears

↓

Object Initialized

↓

Bounding Box Locked

↓

Movement Updates

↓

Visibility Changes

↓

Tracking Maintained

↓

Object Ends
```

---

## Responsibilities

| Runtime              | Responsibility                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Object Builder       | Convert landmarks into objects. |
| Bounding Box Runtime | Maintain geometry.              |
| Motion Estimator     | Update object movement.         |
| Geometry Tracker     | Track scale/rotation.           |
| Timeline Builder     | Store object history.           |
| Confidence Runtime   | Object stability score.         |

---

## Design Principles

1. Objects have stable IDs.
2. Geometry updates continuously.
3. Objects survive scrolling.
4. Objects survive zoom.
5. Objects survive resizing.
6. Motion is deterministic.
7. Camera follows objects—not pixels.

---

# 08A.22 Object Tracking Runtime Architecture

## Mission Statement

> **The runtime converts pixel landmarks into persistent tracked entities with geometry and timeline history.**

---

## High-Level Architecture

```text
Pixel Tracking Runtime
        │
Landmark Graph
        │
Object Tracking Runtime
        │
├── Landmark Clustering
├── Object Builder
├── Bounding Box Runtime
├── Motion Runtime
├── Geometry Runtime
├── Timeline Runtime
└── Confidence Runtime
```

---

## Runtime Pipeline

```text
Landmarks

↓

Cluster Similar Landmarks

↓

Object Candidate

↓

Geometry Builder

↓

Object Tracker

↓

Timeline Storage
```

---

## Runtime Layers

```text
Persistent Object Tracking Runtime
│
├── Object Initializer
├── Bounding Box Generator
├── Geometry Tracker
├── Scroll Tracker
├── Timeline Recorder
├── Visibility Runtime
├── Confidence Runtime
└── Cache Runtime
```

---

## Object Runtime State

| State      | Description               |
| ---------- | ------------------------- |
| Candidate  | Newly detected object.    |
| Active     | Successfully tracked.     |
| Stable     | High confidence tracking. |
| Hidden     | Temporarily invisible.    |
| Recovering | Searching nearby.         |
| Expired    | Removed permanently.      |

---

## Object Metadata

```ts
interface PersistentTrackedObject {
  objectId: string;
  objectType: VisualObjectType;
```

## Engineering Rules

Object Tracking Runtime is built entirely on Pixel Tracking Runtime outputs.

Bounding boxes become the anchor for:

* Smart Zoom.

* AI Highlights.
* Documentation Screenshots.

```text
Refinement
```

```text
├── Toolbar

├── Editor
```

# 08A.24 Scale, Rotation & Perspective Tracking Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Objects remain locked even while their size, orientation or perspective changes.**

## Geometry Tracking Pipeline

```text

↓

↓

↓
```

## Types of Geometry Changes

| Scale Down       | Window resized.           |
| Rotation         | Canvas rotated.           |
| Perspective Warp | Image transformed.        |

---

## Scale Tracking Runtime

Example:

```text
Frame 50

Button Width = 120

↓

Frame 90

Button Width = 145
```

Tracking continues without ID change.

## Rotation Tracking

Objects store orientation.

Examples:

* Rotated canvas.
* Whiteboard.

* Image editor.

## Perspective Tracking

# 08A.25 Scroll Tracking & Viewport Motion Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Objects continue tracking while entire screens move underneath the viewport.**

Scrolling is the hardest visual tracking problem in browser recordings.

## Scroll Tracking Architecture

```text
↓

↓

↓
```

```text
↓
```

| Scroll Delta X | Horizontal movement. |

| Inertia        | Smooth movement.     |
| Elastic Scroll | Mobile browsers.     |

## Sticky Element Runtime

Detects elements that do **not** move during scroll.

Examples:

* Navigation bar.
* Floating action button.
* Cookie banner.
* Toolbar.

---

## Infinite Scroll Runtime

Supports:

* Lazy-loaded lists.
* Long documentation.
* GitHub README.
* Notion pages.
* Chat conversations.

New content becomes tracked automatically.

# 08A.29 Acceptance Principles

## Bounding Box Tests

* Stable button tracking.
* Nested object tracking.
* Padding adapts correctly.

### Geometry Tests

* Scale tracking preserved.
* Rotation preserved.
* Perspective preserved.

### Scroll Tests

* Sticky elements remain fixed.
* Infinite scroll tracked.
* Lazy-loaded content tracked.

### Timeline Tests

* Object birth/death stored.
* Visibility history stored.
* Hover/click events stored.

### GPU Tests

* 60 FPS tracking at 1080p.
* Parallel object updates.
* Stable memory usage.

---

# 08A.30 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 08A.2)

1. Persistent Object Tracking converts pixel landmarks into stable visual entities with permanent tracking IDs.
2. Bounding Box Engine continuously updates object geometry for Smart Zoom, Camera Pan and AI annotations.
3. Objects preserve identity through translation, scaling, rotation and perspective transformations.
4. Scroll Tracking compensates viewport motion before optical flow refinement, allowing stable tracking during scrolling.
5. Sticky UI elements and infinite-scroll content receive specialized tracking behavior.
6. Object Timeline records geometry, visibility, confidence and interaction history across the recording.
7. GPU Tracking Pipeline performs large-scale parallel object tracking using WebGPU compute passes.
8. Geometry updates never create new object identities unless explicitly reinitialized by recovery runtime.
9. Object Tracking outputs reusable timeline metadata consumed by Smart Zoom, Visual Saliency and AI Tutorial Generation.
10. Chapter 08A.2 establishes the persistent object layer that enables cinematic camera tracking across arbitrary browser and desktop recordings.

# 08A.31 Object Reidentification Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **A tracked object should regain its identity after temporarily disappearing from the screen.**

This is the difference between **basic object tracking** and **production-quality tracking**.

Objects disappear because of:

* Fast scrolling.
* Popups covering buttons.
* Context menus.
* Window switches.
* Browser zoom.
* Lazy loading.
* Animations.
* Temporary blur.
* Partial clipping.
* Multi-monitor transitions.

The runtime must recognize:

> *"This is still the same object."*

---

## Why Reidentification Matters

### Without Reidentification

```text id="c4gk8r"
Button Visible

↓

Scroll

↓

Button Leaves Screen

↓

Returns

↓

NEW Object ID
```

Camera jumps.

Annotations break.

Zoom resets.

---

### With Reidentification

```text id="shxygn"
Button Visible

↓

Hidden

↓

Recovered

↓

Same Object ID
```

Everything stays attached.

---

## Reidentification Responsibilities

| Runtime            | Responsibility                |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Identity Matcher   | Match previous objects.       |
| Appearance Matcher | Compare visual descriptors.   |
| Spatial Predictor  | Predict likely location.      |
| Temporal Predictor | Predict return window.        |
| Recovery Validator | Confirm identity restoration. |

---

## Identity Design Principles

1. IDs survive temporary disappearance.
2. Recovery uses multiple signals.
3. Recovery confidence is measurable.
4. Recovery is deterministic.
5. Multiple candidate matches supported.
6. Recovery never duplicates IDs.
7. Timeline continuity preserved.

---

## Reidentification Lifecycle

```text id="9f0h17"
Object Lost

↓

Recovery Candidate Search

↓

Descriptor Matching

↓

Geometry Validation

↓

Identity Restored
```

---

| Scale Consistency        | Medium     |

| Scroll Offset Prediction | High       |
| Semantic Context         | High       |

---

```text id="6upghu"
Lost Descriptor

```

```text id="ujlpdv"
Candidate A

94%

73%

21%
```

Timeline remains continuous.

# 08A.33 Occlusion Handling Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Objects continue existing even when partially or fully hidden behind other UI elements.**

Occlusion handling is essential for:

* Dropdown menus.
* Modals.
* Notifications.
* Context menus.
* Floating tooltips.
* Sticky headers.
* Cursor overlap.
* Window overlap.

---

## Occlusion Architecture

```text id="j6shn2"
Tracked Object

↓

Visibility Estimator

↓

Occlusion Detector

↓

Prediction Runtime

↓

Recovered Object
```

---

## Occlusion Types

| Type                | Example                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Partial Occlusion   | Tooltip covering button.       |
| Full Occlusion      | Modal covers content.          |
| Temporary Occlusion | Cursor covers icon.            |
| Scroll Occlusion    | Sticky navbar overlaps button. |
| Window Occlusion    | Browser partially covered.     |

---

## Visibility Runtime

```text id="tpkxrz"
Object Area

↓

Visible Pixels

↓

Hidden Pixels

↓

Visibility Score
```

---

## Occlusion Prediction

When visibility decreases:

* Predict hidden geometry.
* Predict motion continuation.
* Keep object active.
* Reduce confidence.

---

## Hidden Geometry Runtime

Stores predicted:

* Center.
* Size.
* Velocity.
* Rotation.
* Scale.

---

## Visibility Metadata

```ts id="0rvxcm"
interface VisibilityState {
  visiblePercentage: number;
  occludedPercentage: number;
}
```

---

## Confidence During Occlusion

| Visibility | Tracking Mode      |
| ---------- | ------------------ |
| 100%       | Locked             |
| 70–99%     | Stable             |
| 40–69%     | Predicted          |
| 10–39%     | Recovery Candidate |
| Below 10%  | Hidden             |

---

## Engineering Rules

Occluded objects remain alive until expiration threshold is exceeded.

---

# 08A.36 Recovery & Failure Handling Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Tracking failures should recover automatically before camera movement breaks.**

---

## Failure Pipeline

```text id="ytbsxf"
Tracking Confidence Drops

↓

Recovery Runtime

↓

Template Matching

↓

Descriptor Matching

↓

Recovered

OR

Expired
```

---

## Failure Categories

| Failure       | Recovery               |
| ------------- | ---------------------- |
| Fast Scroll   | Motion prediction.     |
| Heavy Blur    | Template matching.     |
| Occlusion     | Visibility prediction. |
| Window Resize | Geometry prediction.   |
| Theme Change  | Appearance update.     |
| Zoom Change   | Scale recovery.        |

---

## Recovery Strategies

### Strategy 1 — Motion Prediction

Predict likely position.

### Strategy 2 — Descriptor Matching

Search nearby features.

### Strategy 3 — Template Matching

Visual similarity recovery.

### Strategy 4 — Semantic Recovery

Use object type and UI relationships.

---

## Failure State Machine

```text id="o7h9lc"
Stable

↓

Confidence Drops

↓

Searching

↓

Recovered

↓

Stable
```

or

```text id="5ubwdp"
Searching

↓

Timeout

↓

Expired
```

---

## Recovery Timeout Runtime

Objects expire after configurable timeout.

Different object classes use different thresholds.

---

## Metadata

```ts id="cckfqk"
interface TrackingFailureReport {
  failureReason: TrackingFailureReason;
  recoveryStrategy: RecoveryStrategy;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Recovery attempts execute before object expiration.

---

# 08A.39 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 08A.3)

1. Persistent Object Tracking preserves object identity across temporary disappearance and long recordings.
2. Reidentification Runtime restores object identity using appearance, motion, geometry and semantic context.
3. Occlusion Handling predicts hidden geometry while maintaining object timeline continuity.
4. Template Matching provides visual recovery when motion estimation becomes unreliable.
5. Pixel Cache stores reusable descriptors, templates, geometry and confidence history for efficient tracking.
6. Recovery Runtime executes deterministic recovery strategies before expiring tracked objects.
7. Tracking failures degrade gracefully through prediction, template matching and semantic recovery.
8. Object timelines remain continuous across recovery events without creating duplicate identities.
9. Pixel Tracking infrastructure operates independently of DOM metadata and supports browser, desktop and cloud recordings.
10. Chapter 08A completes TryLipi's Pixel Tracking & Persistent Object Tracking Engine—the visual foundation for cinematic zooming, camera movement, saliency detection and AI-generated tutorials.
