# 09.4.14 Camera Boundary Solver

## Mission Statement

> **Prevent the camera from generating crops outside valid viewport boundaries.**

---

## Boundary Architecture

```text id="8nqjok"
Camera Crop

↓

Boundary Solver

↓

Viewport Clamp

↓

Final Crop
```

---

## Boundary Checks

| Boundary        | Example                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------- |
| Left Edge       | Prevent overflow.          |
| Right Edge      | Prevent overflow.          |
| Top Edge        | Prevent overflow.          |
| Bottom Edge     | Prevent overflow.          |
| Nested Viewport | Clamp to scroll container. |

---

## Boundary Clamp Example

```text id="xpdnwl"
Viewport

┌───────────────┐
│ Crop Outside ❌│
└───────────────┘

↓

Crop Shifted Inside
```

---

## Clamp Formula

<math block value="Crop=Clamp(CropBounds,ViewportBounds)"/>

---

## Overscroll Runtime

Handles iOS bounce and elastic scrolling.

---

## Metadata

```ts id="yc8qny"
interface CameraBoundaryState {
  viewportBounds: ViewportRect;
  clampedCropBounds: ViewportRect;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Camera crop never exceeds viewport bounds.

---

# 09.4.15 Facecam Avoidance Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Keep Smart Zoom from hiding or colliding with webcam overlays.**

---

## Facecam Architecture

```text id="nkafpc"
Facecam Detector

↓

Reserved Zone Runtime

↓

Constraint Solver

↓

Adjusted Camera
```

---

## Facecam Locations

| Location     | Typical          |
| ------------ | ---------------- |
| Top Right    | YouTube creators |
| Bottom Right | Tutorials        |
| Bottom Left  | Gaming           |
| Top Left     | Livestreams      |

---

## Reserved Zone Example

```text id="2uz7zz"
┌───────────────┐

│ Facecam Zone  │

│               │

│   Main UI     │

└───────────────┘
```

---

## Avoidance Rules

* Never zoom behind webcam.
* Shift camera center.
* Expand crop if needed.
* Prefer opposite quadrant.

---

## Dynamic Facecam Runtime

Tracks draggable webcam overlays.

---

## Metadata

```ts id="0n2pum"
interface FacecamReservedZone {
  bounds: ViewportRect;
  corner: ScreenCorner;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Facecam avoidance has Critical priority.

---

# 09.4.16 Caption & Subtitle Avoidance Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Reserve safe areas for subtitles, captions and AI overlays.**

---

## Caption Architecture

```text id="gs2pkv"
Subtitle Timeline

↓

Reserved Area Runtime

↓

Camera Constraint Graph
```

---

## Caption Zones

| Export | Reserved Zone |
| ------ | ------------- |
| 16:9   | Bottom 12%    |
| 9:16   | Bottom 15–18% |
| Shorts | Bottom 18–22% |

---

## Caption Safe Area

```text id="2cvcl5"
Camera Frame

Content

────────────

Subtitle Zone
```

---

## Dynamic Subtitle Runtime

Tracks:

* Word-by-word captions.
* Karaoke captions.
* Multi-line subtitles.
* Speaker labels.

---

## Avoidance Strategies

| Situation              | Camera            |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| CTA overlaps caption   | Move crop upward. |
| Paragraph near caption | Increase padding. |
| Facecam + Caption      | Solve jointly.    |

---

## Metadata

```ts id="ngix5k"
interface CaptionReservedZone {
  subtitleBounds: ViewportRect;
  lineCount: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Caption zones remain reserved throughout subtitle visibility.

---

# 09.4.17 Multi-Object Composition Constraint Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Frame multiple important objects without sacrificing readability or cinematic balance.**

---

## Composition Architecture

```text id="ldc0mk"
Anchor Group

↓

Bounding Box Runtime

↓

Composition Solver

↓

Camera Crop
```

---

## Supported Composition Types

| Composition       | Example        |
| ----------------- | -------------- |
| Two Buttons       | Login + Signup |
| Form              | Input + Submit |
| Pricing Cards     | Three plans    |
| Code + Terminal   | IDE demo       |
| Sidebar + Content | Dashboard      |

---

## Composition Modes

| Mode       | Behavior                     |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| Tight      | Focus objects only.          |
| Balanced   | Include surrounding UI.      |
| Contextual | Preserve nearby elements.    |
| Sequential | Pan between distant anchors. |

---

## Rule of Thirds Runtime

Camera centers anchors along cinematic thirds instead of exact center.

---

## Balance Runtime

Prevents excessive empty space.

---

## Metadata

```ts id="8zx5i0"
interface CompositionConstraintState {
  compositionMode: CompositionMode;
  groupedAnchorBounds: ViewportRect;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Composition Solver executes after Safe Framing but before Camera Path Planning.

---

| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `computeSafeFrame()`            | Safe framing runtime.         |
| `buildConstraintGraph()`        | Constraint graph runtime.     |
| `solveViewportBoundaries()`     | Boundary clamp runtime.       |
| `reserveFacecamZone()`          | Facecam avoidance runtime.    |

```text id="yotkt1"
camera.boundary.clamped

```

# 09.4.19 Acceptance Principles

## Safe Frame Tests

* CTA fully visible.
* Heading padding maintained.
* Code block readable.

### Boundary Tests

* Left edge clamp.
* Bottom edge clamp.
* Nested viewport clamp.

### Facecam Tests

* Webcam overlap avoided.
* Draggable webcam tracked.
* Camera shifts automatically.

### Caption Tests

* Subtitle safe area preserved.
* Two-line captions handled.
* Karaoke captions tracked.

### Composition Tests

* Pricing cards grouped.
* Sidebar + content framed.
* Form fields preserved.

---

# 09.4.20 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 09.4.1)

1. Safe Framing Engine guarantees breathing room around important UI landmarks.
2. Camera Constraint Graph resolves multiple framing rules through deterministic priorities.
3. Camera Boundary Solver clamps camera crops inside valid viewport limits.
4. Facecam Avoidance Runtime reserves webcam-safe regions with highest priority.
5. Caption Avoidance Runtime permanently reserves subtitle-safe areas while captions are visible.
6. Multi-Object Composition Solver frames related anchors as a coherent composition instead of isolated crops.
7. Rule of Thirds framing is preferred over naive center alignment whenever possible.
8. Constraint solving happens after Smart Zoom target selection but before camera animation.
9. Constraint resolution is replay deterministic across exports and previews.
10. **Chapter 09.4.1 establishes TryLipi's Camera Constraint Solver Foundation — ensuring every Smart Zoom frame respects cinematic composition, readability, overlays and viewport boundaries before camera movement begins.**

# 09.4.21 Dynamic Constraint Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Camera constraints are not static rules. They evolve continuously as the user scrolls, types, clicks, reads and navigates the interface.**

Static padding is insufficient.

The camera must react to:

* Scrolling.
* Cursor movement.
* Reading progression.
* Animations.
* Notifications.
* Responsive layouts.
* Export aspect ratios.

---

## Static vs Dynamic Constraints

| Static Constraint | Dynamic Constraint                            |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Keep 8% margin    | Margin changes while scrolling.               |
| Avoid captions    | Caption zone grows with multi-line subtitles. |
| Avoid facecam     | Webcam position changes dynamically.          |
| Frame CTA         | CTA expands after loading.                    |
| Center target     | Camera shifts based on reading flow.          |

---

## Dynamic Constraint Pipeline

```text
Viewport Runtime
      │
      ▼
Anchor Timeline
      │
      ▼
Screen Change Runtime
      │
      ▼
Constraint Graph
      │
      ▼
Dynamic Constraint Solver
      │
      ▼
Camera Runtime
```

---

## Constraint Sources

| Source  | Example                     |
| ------- | --------------------------- |
| Scroll  | Page moving vertically.     |
| Cursor  | Pointer approaching button. |
| Reading | Paragraph focus.            |
| Motion  | Spinner animation.          |
| Overlay | Notification popup.         |
| Export  | Shorts safe zones.          |

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime             | Responsibility                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Scroll Constraint   | Maintain stability during scrolling. |
| Cursor Constraint   | Keep cursor visible when important.  |
| Reading Constraint  | Preserve readable framing.           |
| Motion Constraint   | Avoid chasing animations.            |
| Platform Constraint | Respect export layouts.              |
| Conflict Runtime    | Resolve competing rules.             |

---

# 09.4.22 Scroll Constraint Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Scrolling should feel like the camera is gliding with the content—not chasing it frame-by-frame.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Viewport Scroll
      │
      ▼
Scroll Velocity Runtime
      │
      ▼
Anchor Projection Runtime
      │
      ▼
Camera Constraint Solver
```

---

## Scroll Modes

| Mode          | Camera Behavior      |
| ------------- | -------------------- |
| Slow Scroll   | Gentle follow.       |
| Medium Scroll | Delayed glide.       |
| Fast Scroll   | Hold camera briefly. |
| Flick Scroll  | Predict destination. |

---

## Scroll Hold Window

Instead of immediately following scroll:

```text
Frame 120
Anchor Visible

↓

Fast Scroll Begins

↓

Camera Holds Position

↓

Scroll Ends

↓

Camera Glides To Landing Position
```

This eliminates jitter from mouse-wheel scrolling.

---

## Scroll Velocity Thresholds

| Velocity  | Camera Strategy              |
| --------- | ---------------------------- |
| Low       | Continuous follow.           |
| Medium    | Dampened follow.             |
| High      | Predict landing position.    |
| Very High | Freeze camera until landing. |

---

## Scroll Dampening Formula

```math
CameraScroll = 0.2 × Current + 0.8 × Previous
```

---

## Nested Scroll Containers

The runtime independently tracks scrolling inside:

* Chat windows.
* Sidebars.
* Code editors.
* Infinite feeds.
* Modals.
* Documentation panes.

Each scroll container owns its own scroll timeline.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ScrollConstraintState {
  scrollVelocity: number;

  predictedLandingOffset: number;

  cameraHoldFrames: number;

  activeScrollContainerId?: string;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Camera follows **scroll destination**, not intermediate positions.
* Nested containers never affect root viewport constraints.
* Scroll hold duration depends on velocity.

---

# 09.4.23 Cursor Visibility Constraint Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **The cursor should remain visible whenever it communicates intent to the viewer.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Cursor Runtime
      │
      ▼
Intent Analyzer
      │
      ▼
Visibility Constraint Runtime
      │
      ▼
Camera Planner
```

---

## Cursor Importance Levels

| Cursor State      | Visibility Requirement |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| Hovering CTA      | Critical               |
| Dragging Slider   | Critical               |
| Selecting Text    | High                   |
| Drawing on Canvas | High                   |
| Reading Paragraph | Medium                 |
| Idle              | Low                    |

---

## Cursor Safe Radius

```text
      ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
   ○             ○
 ○      Cursor     ○
   ○             ○
      ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
```

The cursor always remains inside this visibility radius.

---

## Cursor Edge Protection

When the cursor approaches viewport edges:

* Expand crop slightly.
* Shift framing.
* Delay aggressive zoom.
* Maintain cursor padding.

---

## Cursor Prediction Constraint

Instead of following the cursor's current position:

```text
Current Cursor

↓

Trajectory Prediction

↓

Likely Click Target

↓

Camera Starts Moving Early
```

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface CursorVisibilityConstraint {
  cursorRegion: ViewportRect;

  visibilityRadius: number;

  predictedCursorTarget?: ViewportPoint;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Cursor visibility overrides aggressive zoom.
* Prediction begins before click occurs.
* Cursor padding adapts to export aspect ratio.

---

# 09.4.24 Reading Constraint Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Camera movement must never interrupt reading flow.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Text Saliency Runtime
        │
        ▼
Reading Progress Runtime
        │
        ▼
Reading Constraint Solver
        │
        ▼
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Reading Behaviors

| Behavior          | Camera Action           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- |
| Reading Heading   | Hold frame.             |
| Reading Paragraph | No horizontal movement. |
| Reading Code      | Wider crop.             |
| Reading Table     | Preserve full width.    |
| Reading JSON      | Show entire structure.  |

---

## Reading Hold Runtime

```text
Heading

↓

Paragraph

↓

Code Block

↓

CTA Button
```

The camera waits until reading naturally completes.

---

## Reading Progress Signals

The engine combines:

* Cursor idle duration.
* Eye-gaze prediction.
* Scroll pauses.
* Text saliency heatmaps.
* Paragraph completion.

---

## Reading Integrity Rules

Camera must never:

* Crop the active sentence.
* Hide bullet points.
* Hide code line numbers.
* Split tables awkwardly.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ReadingConstraintState {
  readingRegion: ViewportRect;

  readingProgress: number;

  readingDirection: ReadingDirection;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Reading suppresses unnecessary pans.
* Reading suppresses decorative zoom.
* Paragraph completion unlocks camera transitions.

---

# 09.4.25 Motion Constraint Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Ignore decorative animations while respecting meaningful motion.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Motion Saliency Runtime
        │
        ▼
Motion Filter
        │
        ▼
Constraint Runtime
        │
        ▼
Camera Planner
```

---

## Motion Categories

| Motion             | Camera Response           |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Loading Spinner    | Ignore.                   |
| Cursor Drag        | Follow.                   |
| Progress Bar       | Hold.                     |
| Notification       | Burst attention.          |
| Video Playback     | Context framing.          |
| Carousel Animation | Ignore unless interacted. |

---

## Motion Persistence Window

Short-lived animations receive a persistence window before camera movement.

---

## Decorative Motion Filter

Ignored examples:

* Skeleton loaders.
* CSS shimmer.
* Cursor blinking.
* Floating particles.
* Animated gradients.

---

## Meaningful Motion Runtime

Tracked examples:

* Drag-and-drop.
* Timeline scrubber.
* Canvas drawing.
* Slider adjustments.
* Image cropping.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface MotionConstraintState {
  motionType: MotionType;

  shouldTriggerCamera: boolean;

  persistenceMs: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Decorative motion cannot steal attention.
* User-generated motion always wins over decorative motion.
* Motion constraints cooperate with Saliency Engine.

---

---

## Architecture

## Supported Platform Profiles

| -------------- | ------------ |
| YouTube        | 16:9         |
| Shorts         | 9:16         |
| Instagram Reel | 9:16         |
| TikTok         | 9:16         |
| LinkedIn       | 4:5          |
| X              | 1:1 / 16:9   |

---

## Platform Safe Zones

| Platform | Reserved Area                 |
| -------- | ----------------------------- |
| Shorts   | Bottom captions + action bar. |
| Reels    | Bottom engagement buttons.    |
| TikTok   | Username + caption overlay.   |
| YouTube  | Timestamp safe area.          |
| LinkedIn | Bottom CTA padding.           |

---

## Platform Crop Example

```text
──────────────────────────────
 Entire Browser Viewport
──────────────────────────────
```

### Shorts (9:16)

```text
────────────
  Main UI

  Focus Area

  Safe Caption Zone
────────────
```

---

## Adaptive Camera Runtime

The camera automatically adjusts:

* Padding.
* Zoom level.
* Composition.
* Caption spacing.
* Cursor radius.

for each export profile.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface PlatformConstraintState {
  exportPlatform: ExportPlatform;

  safeZones: ViewportRect[];

  aspectRatio: AspectRatio;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Platform constraints apply before export rendering.
* Every export profile owns its own safe-zone template.

---

# 09.4.27 Constraint Conflict Resolution Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Multiple constraints often disagree. The solver resolves conflicts deterministically.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Constraint Graph
      │
      ▼
Priority Runtime
      │
      ▼
Conflict Resolver
      │
      ▼
Final Camera Frame
```

---

## Example Conflict

```text
CTA Near Bottom

↓

Subtitle Appears

↓

Facecam Bottom Right

↓

Camera Must Reframe
```

---

## Constraint Priority Table

| Priority | Constraint           |
| -------- | -------------------- |
| Critical | Viewport Boundary    |
| Critical | Facecam Avoidance    |
| Critical | Caption Avoidance    |
| High     | Reading Integrity    |
| High     | Anchor Visibility    |
| Medium   | Cursor Visibility    |
| Medium   | Context Preservation |
| Low      | Decorative Spacing   |

---

## Conflict Solver Strategy

1. Preserve viewport validity.
2. Preserve overlays.
3. Preserve readable content.
4. Preserve semantic anchors.
5. Preserve cursor if interacting.
6. Preserve surrounding UI context.

---

## Resolution Example

| Conflict           | Winner                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| Caption vs CTA     | Shift camera upward.     |
| Facecam vs Cursor  | Cursor radius adjusted.  |
| Anchor vs Boundary | Clamp viewport first.    |
| Reading vs Motion  | Reading constraint wins. |

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ConstraintResolutionState {
  resolvedConstraints: string[];

  rejectedConstraints: string[];

  finalPriorityScore: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Conflict resolution is deterministic and replay-safe.

---

# 09.4.29 Acceptance Principles

## Scroll Constraint Tests

* Smooth wheel scrolling.
* Flick scrolling prediction.
* Nested scroll containers.
* Infinite feed scrolling.

## Cursor Visibility Tests

* Cursor remains visible while dragging.
* Hover CTA preserved.
* Edge protection active.
* Predicted click destination framed.

## Reading Constraint Tests

* Paragraph never cropped.
* Code editor readable.
* Table preserved.
* Markdown headings framed correctly.

## Motion Constraint Tests

* Spinner ignored.
* Progress bar held.
* Drag-and-drop followed.
* Notifications trigger burst attention.

## Platform Constraint Tests

* Shorts safe zones respected.
* TikTok overlays avoided.
* LinkedIn 4:5 framing maintained.
* YouTube 16:9 composition preserved.

## Conflict Resolution Tests

* Caption + Facecam overlap.
* Reading vs Motion.
* Boundary vs Anchor.
* Cursor vs Safe Margin.

---

# 09.4.30 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 09.4.2)

1. Scroll Constraint Runtime follows scroll destinations instead of intermediate positions.
2. Cursor Visibility Constraint Runtime guarantees cursor visibility during meaningful interactions.
3. Reading Constraint Runtime freezes unnecessary camera movement while text is actively being read.
4. Motion Constraint Runtime filters decorative animations while preserving meaningful interaction motion.
5. Platform Export Constraint Runtime applies platform-specific safe zones before rendering.
6. Constraint Conflict Resolution Runtime resolves competing rules using deterministic priorities.
7. Caption, Facecam and Viewport Boundary constraints always have **Critical** priority.
8. Reading integrity overrides decorative cinematic movement.
9. Dynamic constraints continuously update camera framing throughout recording, replay and export.
10. **Chapter 09.4.2 establishes TryLipi's Dynamic Camera Constraint Runtime — ensuring Smart Zoom adapts intelligently to scrolling, reading, motion, cursor interactions and every export platform without producing awkward framing.**

# 09.4.31 Camera Path Optimization Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Finding the correct camera target is only half the job. The Camera Constraint Solver must generate the smoothest possible cinematic path between targets.**

Professional editors rarely cut directly between UI elements.

Instead, they:

* Ease into focus.
* Preserve spatial continuity.
* Maintain viewer orientation.
* Avoid unnecessary zoom jumps.
* Respect interaction timing.

This runtime transforms **camera targets into cinematic camera paths**.

---

## Camera Decision Stack

```text
Visual Focus Engine
        │
        ▼
Zoom Target Prediction Engine
        │
        ▼
Camera Constraint Solver
        │
        ▼
Camera Path Optimizer
        │
        ▼
GPU Camera Timeline
```

---

## Camera Path Responsibilities

| Runtime             | Responsibility                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Path Optimizer      | Smooth camera movement.           |
| Constraint Timeline | Apply constraints over time.      |
| GPU Renderer        | Preview camera bounds.            |
| Validation Engine   | Reject bad camera paths.          |
| Export Runtime      | Serialize optimized camera paths. |

---

## Camera Path Goals

1. No jitter.
2. No sudden zoom jumps.
3. No unnecessary pans.
4. Maintain orientation.
5. Preserve reading comfort.
6. Maintain cinematic rhythm.
7. Deterministic replay.

---

# 09.4.32 Camera Path Optimizer Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Generate the smoothest camera trajectory between two valid framing regions.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Camera Target A
        │
        ▼
Constraint Solver
        │
        ▼
Path Optimizer
        │
        ▼
Camera Timeline
```

---

## Optimization Pipeline

```text
Current Camera

↓

Target Camera

↓

Velocity Solver

↓

Bezier / Spring Solver

↓

Optimized Camera Path
```

---

## Path Types

| Path Type      | Use Case                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------- |
| Linear         | Minimal movement.           |
| Ease In-Out    | Standard zoom transition.   |
| Spring         | Floating UI transitions.    |
| Arc            | Large desktop pans.         |
| Hold-Then-Move | Reading to CTA transitions. |

---

## Path Cost Function

<math block value="Cost=w_1Distance+w_2ZoomDelta+w_3PanDelta+w_4Jerk"/>

The optimizer chooses the lowest-cost camera path.

---

## Jerk Minimization

The runtime minimizes the third derivative of camera movement.

**Why?**

Human eyes dislike abrupt acceleration changes.

---

## Camera Hold Windows

| Interaction       | Hold Duration          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| Reading Heading   | 400–800 ms             |
| Reading Paragraph | Until reading complete |
| Button Hover      | 150–300 ms             |
| Loading Spinner   | Hold position          |
| Modal Open        | Hold before zoom       |

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface CameraPathState {
  pathId: string;

  easingCurve: CameraCurve;

  durationMs: number;

  estimatedJerkScore: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

* Optimize pan and zoom simultaneously.
* Never optimize independently.
* Hold windows are inserted before path generation.

---

# 09.4.33 Constraint Timeline Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Every constraint becomes a time-aware event instead of an instant rule.**

---

## Timeline Architecture

```text
Constraint Graph

↓

Timeline Builder

↓

Constraint Timeline

↓

Camera Runtime
```

---

## Constraint Timeline Events

| Event             | Example                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| Safe Margin Added | Zoom target updated.     |
| Caption Appears   | Bottom safe zone grows.  |
| Facecam Moves     | Right safe zone updated. |
| Scroll Begins     | Hold constraint enabled. |
| Scroll Ends       | Constraint removed.      |

---

## Timeline Example

```text
00:05 Safe Margin Active

↓

00:12 Caption Zone Active

↓

00:20 Scroll Hold Active

↓

00:23 Scroll Hold Removed

↓

00:30 Facecam Zone Updated
```

---

## Constraint Sessions

Long-lived constraints become sessions.

Example:

* Caption visible for 18 seconds.
* Facecam active entire recording.
* Scroll hold active for 600 ms.

---

## Timeline Compression

Continuous constraints merge into one event.

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface ConstraintTimelineEvent {
  constraintId: string;

  startedAtFrame: number;

  endedAtFrame?: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Constraint Timeline is replay deterministic and append-only.

---

# 09.4.36 AI Camera Validation Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Automatically reject camera paths that look unnatural before export.**

This is one of TryLipi's biggest differentiators.

---

## Validation Architecture

```text
Camera Timeline

↓

Validation Rules

↓

Quality Score

↓

Accept / Reject
```

---

## Validation Categories

| Validation             | Purpose                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Boundary Validation    | Crop inside viewport.      |
| Readability Validation | Text fully readable.       |
| Overlay Validation     | Caption + facecam visible. |
| Motion Validation      | No excessive velocity.     |
| Context Validation     | Preserve surrounding UI.   |

---

## Validation Rules

### Boundary Validation

Reject if crop exceeds viewport.

### Readability Validation

Reject if:

* Heading cropped.
* Paragraph truncated.
* Code line numbers missing.

### Overlay Validation

Reject if:

* Caption hidden.
* Webcam cropped.
* CTA behind overlay.

### Motion Validation

Reject if camera jerk exceeds threshold.

---

## Quality Score Components

| Metric               | Weight |
| -------------------- | ------ |
| Readability          | 30%    |
| Stability            | 25%    |
| Composition          | 20%    |
| Context Preservation | 15%    |
| Motion Smoothness    | 10%    |

---

## Validation Metadata

```ts
interface CameraValidationResult {
  qualityScore: number;

  rejectedRules: CameraValidationRule[];

  accepted: boolean;
}
```

---

## Auto Repair Runtime

Instead of failing immediately:

```text
Invalid Camera

↓

Constraint Violated

↓

Auto Repair

↓

Validate Again
```

Possible repairs include:

* Expand crop.
* Shift camera.
* Reduce zoom.
* Delay transition.

---

## Engineering Rules

Every exported camera timeline must pass validation before rendering.

---

# 09.4.39 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 09.4.3)

1. Camera Path Optimizer generates the smoothest trajectory between valid camera targets.
2. Constraint Timeline Runtime serializes all active framing constraints into immutable timeline events.
3. GPU Constraint Renderer visualizes safe zones, overlays and camera crops for debugging.
4. Export Runtime consumes serialized constraint metadata instead of recomputing framing.
5. AI Camera Validation Engine rejects camera paths that violate readability, overlays or cinematic stability.
6. Auto Repair Runtime attempts to repair invalid camera paths before export.
7. Camera optimization minimizes distance, zoom delta and jerk simultaneously.
8. Constraint sessions persist independently from camera motion sessions.
9. Validation executes before every final export render.
10. **Chapter 09.4 completes TryLipi's Camera Constraint Solver — the cinematic safety engine ensuring every Smart Zoom shot is readable, context-aware, platform-safe and professionally framed.**

# 18.7.11 AI Intent Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **TryLipi predicts what the creator is about to do before they do it, allowing the camera to move proactively instead of reactively.**

This chapter introduces the highest-level AI reasoning engine inside TryLipi.

Everything built previously becomes input:

* Mouse Physics.
* Cursor Motion.
* Pixel Tracking.
* Object Tracking.
* Visual Anchors.
* Saliency Heatmaps.
* Screen Changes.
* DOM Intelligence.
* Camera Constraints.

Intent Prediction combines all of them.

---

## Reactive Camera vs Predictive Camera

### Reactive Camera

```text
Cursor Clicks Button

↓

Camera Starts Zooming

↓

Viewer Sees Late Zoom
```

### Predictive Camera

```text
Cursor Moving Toward Button

↓

Intent Confidence Rising

↓

Camera Starts Moving Early

↓

Button Already Centered At Click
```

---

## Why This Engine Exists

| Without Intent Prediction  | With Intent Prediction             |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Camera reacts late.        | Camera arrives before interaction. |
| Cursor reaches edge first. | Camera predicts destination.       |
| Fast clicks feel jumpy.    | Smooth anticipation.               |
| Scroll starts abruptly.    | Camera predicts landing position.  |

---

## Human Editing Inspiration

Professional editors anticipate:

* Which button will be clicked.
* Which code block will be discussed.
* Which modal will open.
* Which panel will be expanded.
* Which tab will become active.

TryLipi replicates that behavior algorithmically.

---

## Runtime Responsibilities

| Runtime                 | Responsibility                      |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Cursor Intent Runtime   | Predict click destination.          |
| Interaction Runtime     | Predict interaction type.           |
| Semantic Intent Runtime | Predict UI purpose.                 |
| Attention Runtime       | Predict viewer focus shift.         |
| Intent Memory Runtime   | Learn interaction sequence history. |

---

## AI Intent Pipeline

```text
Cursor Physics
DOM Runtime
Visual Anchors
Saliency Runtime
Screen Changes
        │
        ▼
Intent Prediction Runtime
        │
        ▼
Future Interaction Candidates
        │
        ▼
Camera Planner
```

---

## Design Principles

1. Predict, don't guess.
2. Confidence-based decisions.
3. Temporal reasoning.
4. Semantic understanding.
5. Multi-signal fusion.
6. Replay deterministic.
7. Low-latency inference.

---

# 18.7.20 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 18.7.1)

1. AI Intent Prediction Runtime executes before Camera Planning.
2. Cursor Intent Prediction estimates future interaction targets before click confirmation.
3. Interaction Prediction Runtime classifies interaction types before DOM events occur.
4. Semantic UI Intent Engine predicts user goals using UI semantics and anchor history.
5. Predictive Attention Pipeline generates future attention heatmaps 200–500 ms ahead of interaction.
6. Intent Memory Runtime learns interaction sequences during a recording session.
7. Intent confidence is calculated by fusing cursor physics, saliency, anchors and semantic UI signals.
8. Prediction outputs remain deterministic during replay.
9. Camera Planner consumes intent candidates rather than waiting for confirmed interactions.
10. **Chapter 18.7.1 establishes TryLipi's AI Intent Prediction Engine Foundation — enabling Smart Zoom and Camera Panning to anticipate creator actions before they happen.**

# 18.7.21 Predictive Workflow Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **Creators rarely perform isolated actions. They execute workflows. TryLipi predicts the next step in the workflow before it happens.**

Example workflow inside TryLipi:

```text
Open Dashboard

↓

Click "Generate Script"

↓

Wait for AI

↓

Scroll Output

↓

Copy Script

↓

Export
```

The camera should already know this sequence.

---

## Why Workflow Prediction Exists

Without workflow prediction:

* Camera waits after every click.
* Every transition is reactive.

With workflow prediction:

* Camera anticipates next panel.
* Scroll destination predicted.
* Modals framed before appearing.
* Tutorial chapters generated automatically.

---

## Workflow Prediction Layers

| Layer                 | Purpose                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Navigation Prediction | Predict page changes.         |
| Scroll Prediction     | Predict landing viewport.     |
| Modal Prediction      | Predict overlays/dialogs.     |
| Workflow Prediction   | Predict next user step.       |
| Tutorial Prediction   | Predict explanation sequence. |

---

## Runtime Pipeline

```text
Interaction Timeline

↓

Intent Memory

↓

Workflow Predictor

↓

Future Action Timeline

↓

Camera Planner
```

---

## Engineering Principles

1. Predict workflows, not isolated clicks.
2. Confidence-driven forecasting.
3. Temporal reasoning.
4. Semantic understanding.
5. Replay deterministic.

---

# 18.7.22 Navigation Prediction Engine

## Mission Statement

> **Predict which page, panel or tab the user is about to navigate to before navigation completes.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Current View

↓

Navigation Predictor

↓

Future View

↓

Camera Planner
```

## Navigation Categories

| Category           | Example              |
| ------------------ | -------------------- |
| Sidebar Navigation | Dashboard → Settings |
| Top Tabs           | Home → Inbox         |
| Browser Tabs       | Docs → Playground    |
| Wizard Steps       | Step 2 → Step 3      |
| Nested Panels      | Profile → Billing    |

---

## Prediction Signals

| Signal                      | Weight |
| --------------------------- | ------ |
| Cursor Trajectory           | High   |
| Hover Duration              | High   |
| Previous Navigation History | Medium |
| Semantic Label              | High   |
| Active Workflow             | Medium |

---

## Navigation Prediction Timeline

```text
Cursor Moving

↓

Hover Sidebar

↓

Navigation Confidence Rising

↓

Camera Starts Panning
```

# 18.7.23 Scroll Destination Prediction Runtime

## Prediction Pipeline

```text
Wheel Delta

↓

Momentum Estimator

↓

Landing Offset

↓

Anchor Projection

↓

Camera Target
```

---

## Landing Window

Instead of following intermediate frames:

```text

↓

Predicted Landing

↓

Camera Moves Once

↓

Viewport Arrives
```

## Infinite Feed Prediction

Supports:

* Instagram feed.
* Reddit.

Predicts next visible content block.

Camera transitions after landing prediction confidence exceeds threshold.

# 18.7.30 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 18.7.2)

1. Navigation Prediction Engine forecasts future page and panel transitions before navigation completes.
2. Scroll Destination Prediction Runtime predicts landing offsets instead of following intermediate scroll frames.
3. Modal Prediction Runtime reserves framing before overlays animate into view.
4. Multi-Step Workflow Prediction Runtime models interaction chains instead of isolated clicks.
5. AI Tutorial Prediction Runtime converts interaction sequences into instructional chapters automatically.
6. Temporal Intent Graph Runtime stores multiple possible future interaction paths with confidence values.
7. Workflow prediction is confidence-based and session-aware.
8. Camera Planner consumes future workflow candidates before interaction completion.
9. Tutorial generation reuses workflow and anchor timelines instead of timestamps alone.
10. **Chapter 18.7.2 establishes TryLipi's Predictive Workflow Runtime — enabling Smart Zoom to anticipate navigation, scrolling, dialogs and complete creator workflows before they happen.**

# 18.7.31 Camera Decision Brain Philosophy

## Mission Statement

> **The Camera Decision Brain is the central intelligence layer that decides what the AI camera should do next using every perception engine built in TryLipi.**

This is the **highest-level orchestration engine**.

Everything feeds into it.

---

## Complete AI Decision Stack

```text
Pixel Tracking Engine
        │
Object Tracking Engine
        │
Visual Anchor Engine
        │
Screen Change Engine
        │
Saliency Engine
        │
Intent Prediction Engine
        │
Camera Constraint Solver
        │
──────── Camera Decision Brain ────────
        │
Camera Timeline
        │
GPU Renderer
        │
Export Runtime
```

---

## Why This Engine Exists

Without a central brain:

* Multiple AI engines compete.
* Camera becomes inconsistent.
* Different runtimes fight each other.

With Camera Decision Brain:

* One unified decision every frame.
* Deterministic priority ordering.
* Stable cinematic behavior.

---

## Responsibilities

| Runtime            | Responsibility                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| Intent Fusion      | Combine multiple predictions.  |
| Decision Brain     | Select best camera action.     |
| Conflict Resolver  | Resolve AI disagreements.      |
| Timeline Generator | Produce final camera timeline. |
| Export Runtime     | Serialize AI decisions.        |

---

## Camera Decisions

Possible outputs every frame:

| Decision     | Example                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Zoom In      | Focus CTA.                    |
| Zoom Out     | Reveal modal context.         |
| Pan Left     | Follow sidebar interaction.   |
| Pan Right    | Reveal settings panel.        |
| Hold Frame   | Reading paragraph.            |
| Delay Camera | Ignore loading animation.     |
| Transition   | Move toward predicted anchor. |

---

## Engineering Principles

1. Every frame has one primary decision.
2. Decisions are confidence-based.
3. Decisions are constraint-safe.
4. Decisions are replay deterministic.
5. Decisions preserve cinematic continuity.

---

# 18.7.32 Multi-Model Intent Fusion Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Fuse predictions from multiple AI systems into one unified confidence map.**

---

## Fusion Architecture

```text
Cursor Intent

Visual Attention

Semantic Intent

Workflow Prediction

Screen Change Prediction

↓

Intent Fusion Runtime

↓

Unified Intent Graph
```

---

## Models Feeding Fusion

| Model                | Output               |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Cursor Predictor     | Future click target. |
| Attention Predictor  | Future viewer focus. |
| Workflow Predictor   | Next workflow step.  |
| Modal Predictor      | Future overlay.      |
| Scroll Predictor     | Landing position.    |
| Navigation Predictor | Future page.         |

---

## Confidence Fusion Pipeline

```text
Individual Predictions

↓

Normalize Confidence

↓

Weighted Fusion

↓

Unified Intent Candidate
```

---

## Example Fusion

| Source      | Confidence |
| ----------- | ---------- |
| Cursor      | 0.94       |
| Saliency    | 0.81       |
| Semantic UI | 0.89       |
| Workflow    | 0.72       |

↓

**Unified Confidence = 0.91**

---

## Confidence Categories

| Score      | Meaning                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------ |
| 0.95–1.00  | Immediate camera action. |
| 0.85–0.95  | Strong prediction.       |
| 0.70–0.85  | Soft preparation.        |
| 0.50–0.70  | Observe.                 |
| Below 0.50 | Ignore.                  |

---

## Metadata

```ts
interface UnifiedIntentCandidate {
  anchorId: string;

  unifiedConfidence: number;

  contributingModels: IntentModelSource[];
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Intent fusion happens before Camera Constraint Solver validation.

---

# 18.7.33 Camera Decision Brain Runtime

## Mission Statement

> **Select exactly one primary camera action for each frame using unified intent confidence and camera constraints.**

---

## Architecture

```text
Unified Intent Graph

↓

Constraint Validation

↓

Camera Decision Brain

↓

Primary Camera Action
```

---

## Decision Pipeline

```text
Future Anchor

↓

Constraint Check

↓

Path Optimization

↓

Timeline Update

↓

Render Camera
```

---

## Decision Priorities

| Priority | Decision          |
| -------- | ----------------- |
| Critical | Reading Hold      |
| Critical | Modal Frame       |
| High     | CTA Zoom          |
| High     | Scroll Landing    |
| Medium   | Cursor Tracking   |
| Medium   | Context Zoom      |
| Low      | Decorative Motion |

---

## Example Decision Timeline

```text
Frame 100

Cursor Moving Toward CTA

↓

Decision: Prepare Zoom

Frame 112

Click

↓

Decision: Hold CTA

Frame 145

Modal Opens

↓

Decision: Zoom Out + Center Modal
```

---

## Decision Metadata

```ts
interface CameraDecision {
  frame: number;

  decisionType: CameraDecisionType;

  targetAnchorId: string;

  confidence: number;
}
```

---

## Engineering Rules

Only one primary camera decision may exist per frame.

---

# 18.7.35 Reinforcement Learning Hooks

## Mission Statement

> **Allow future AI models to improve camera decisions without changing deterministic runtime behavior.**

---

## Why RL Hooks Exist

Future versions of TryLipi may learn:

* Better zoom timing.
* Better reading duration.
* Better framing preferences.
* Better workflow prediction.

Current runtime remains deterministic.

---

## RL Hook Architecture

```text
Camera Decision

↓

Feedback Collector

↓

Offline Dataset Builder

↓

Future Training Pipeline
```

---

## Feedback Signals

| Signal               | Example                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Camera Held Too Long | Reduce hold duration.    |
| Zoom Too Early       | Delay prediction.        |
| Cropped CTA          | Increase safe padding.   |
| User Manual Edit     | Learn preferred framing. |

---

## Dataset Fields

```ts
interface CameraFeedbackExample {
  decisionId: string;

  originalDecision: CameraDecision;

  correctedDecision?: CameraDecision;
}
```

---

## Training Strategy

* Offline learning only.
* Never changes exported recording.
* New models shipped as versioned predictors.

---

## Engineering Rules

RL hooks collect feedback but never modify live camera behavior.

---

# 18.7.39 Canonical Engineering Rules (Part 18.7.3)

1. Multi-Model Intent Fusion combines predictions into one unified confidence graph.
2. Camera Decision Brain selects one primary camera action per frame.
3. GPU Intent Runtime visualizes future interactions for debugging.
4. Reinforcement Learning Hooks collect feedback without affecting live recordings.
5. Export Runtime serializes AI decision history into replay metadata.
6. Camera decisions are always validated by Camera Constraint Solver before rendering.
7. Intent fusion is deterministic for identical recordings.
8. Future attention predictions may begin camera movement before interactions complete.
9. Tutorial generation reuses workflow and intent timelines automatically.
10. **Chapter 18.7 completes TryLipi's AI Intent Prediction Engine — the master AI brain that turns cursor movement, visual attention, semantic UI understanding and workflow prediction into proactive cinematic camera behavior.**
